@lAddBundleExecutable@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddBundleExecutable@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: Adds a bundle executable to a runtime‑dependency set. If the set already contains one, it records an error via the helper and signals failure; otherwise it succeeds.

@lAddInstallRuntimeDependenciesGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lAddInstallRuntimeDependenciesGenerator.body: The routine registers generators for installing runtime‑only dependencies, library dependencies, and Apple framework dependencies. It first checks whether the target uses DLLs or Apple frameworks, gathers the relevant configuration list, and then creates a runtime‑dependency generator with appropriate include/exclude filters. Afterwards it creates a library‑dependency generator, and if the platform is Apple it also creates a framework‑dependency generator. Flags are set to indicate which dependency type was installed.

@lArchToolsetHelper::[lambda_0]::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchToolsetHelper::[lambda_0]::operato.body: The function reads a JSON value, applies the contained configuration to a preset, updates the supplied state object, and returns true if the operation succeeded (otherwise false).

@lArchToolsetHelper::[lambda_0]@kArchToo.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchToolsetHelper::[lambda_0]@kArchToo.body: The lambda examines the incoming JSON `value`. If it’s absent or null, it clears the output fields, marks the strategy as null, and returns success. If the value is a string, it copies that string into the output value field, clears the strategy, and signals success. For an object value it delegates to a helper routine. Any other type triggers a preset error and returns failure.

@lArchToolsetHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchToolsetHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The helper constructs a small validator that, when invoked, examines a JSON value and fills a `ConfigurePreset` instance. It first clears the target fields if the value is missing, then distinguishes three accepted formats: a plain string (directly assigned to the value field), an object (validated via a pre‑built `JSONHelperBuilder` instance), or an unexpected type that triggers an error. The returned lambda returns `true` on success and `false` otherwise, leaving the optional strategy field unset when no strategy is supplied.

@lArchToolsetStrategyHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lArchToolsetStrategyHelper@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The helper inspects a JSON string value: if it equals “set” or “external”, it assigns the corresponding enum value to the optional output and returns success; otherwise it reports an error and returns failure.

@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::ActionMap@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::ActionMap@k.body: The `ActionMap` constructor performs a move‑construction: it takes an rvalue reference to another `ActionMap` and efficiently transfers ownership of its internal data structures into the new instance, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.

@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::ActionMap@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::ActionMap@k.body: Creates a new `ActionMap` instance by copying the internal mapping structure from the supplied source instance (the unnamed reference). It performs a shallow copy of the underlying key/value collections so that the new map shares the same mapping data until modified.

@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::ActionMap@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::ActionMap@k.body: The `ActionMap()` function acts as the entry point for setting up the internal mapping that the argument parser uses to resolve command‑level actions. When invoked it typically creates (or retrieves) an `ActionMap` instance, populates it with the known action handlers, and makes that mapping available for the rest of the parsing logic.

@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to an `ActionMap`, moves its contents into the current object, and returns a reference to that object, allowing chained assignments such as `a = b = c;`.

@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::operator=@k.body: The overloaded assignment operator copies all key/value pairs from the supplied map into the current instance, then returns a reference to the updated object. It performs a self‑check to avoid self‑assignment issues and preserves the map’s internal structure.

@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::~ActionMap@.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ActionMap::~ActionMap@.body: The `~ActionMap` function initializes and returns the internal map that associates action identifiers with their corresponding handler objects. It constructs the mapping used throughout the program to resolve a given action name to its implementation.

@lArgumentParser::AsParseResultPtr@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::AsParseResultPtr@k_ZN1.body: It accepts a reference to any type that is **not** a subclass of `ParseResult`. The return type is enabled only when that condition holds, yielding a pointer type (`ParseResult*`). Inside the function body, it simply returns `nullptr`. In other words, the template produces a `nullptr` of type `ParseResult*` for any type that isn’t a `ParseResult`, while disabling the overload when the argument already derives from `ParseResult`.

@lArgumentParser::Base::Base@k_ZN14Argum.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Base::Base@k_ZN14Argum.body: It creates a new object by taking the ownership of another instance: it copies the internal state via move semantics so the new instance takes over the resources of the source without copying them.

@lArgumentParser::Base::Base@k_ZN14Argum.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Base::Base@k_ZN14Argum.body: The `Base` function is a copy constructor that accepts a `const Base&` parameter (though the formal parameter name is omitted in the snippet) and constructs a new instance from the supplied object. It performs the standard copy‑semantics for the `Base` type.

@lArgumentParser::Base::Base@k_ZN14Argum.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Base::Base@k_ZN14Argum.body: The `Base()` function is the constructor for the `Base` class. It performs the minimal bookkeeping necessary to bring an instance into a usable state—allocating its internal storage, setting default values, and inserting the object into any framework‑wide registries or lookup tables that the surrounding code expects to exist.

@lArgumentParser::Base::Bind@k_ZN14Argum.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::Base::Bind@k_ZN14Argum.body: The `Bind` routine registers a keyword‑action pair: it forwards the name and action to `MaybeBind`, expects a successful insertion, and discards the returned flag (the `static_cast<void>` is a no‑op).

@lArgumentParser::MaybeEmpty::MaybeEmpty.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::MaybeEmpty::MaybeEmpty.body: MaybeEmpty checks whether a provided container contains any elements and returns a boolean flag accordingly.

@lArgumentParser::NonEmpty::NonEmpty@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::NonEmpty::NonEmpty@k_Z.body: NonEmpty validates that the supplied entity is not empty before any further processing.

@lArgumentParser::NonEmpty::NonEmpty@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::NonEmpty::NonEmpty@k_Z.body: Checks whether a given collection/value contains any elements and returns a simple boolean indicator.

@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::MaybeRepo.author: AI Short Overview
@lArgumentParser::ParseResult::MaybeRepo.body: If the parse result is empty (no errors recorded), the function returns false; otherwise it concatenates the stored keyword‑error pairs into a single string, issues a fatal error via the cmMakefile, and returns true.

@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTC1ET_19cmListFileBacktra.author: AI Short Overview
@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTC1ET_19cmListFileBacktra.body: The constructor creates a `BT` instance by moving the supplied value into the `Value` base and the supplied back‑trace into the `Backtrace` base, using defaults when none are supplied.

@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTINSt7__cxx1112basic_stri.author: AI Short Overview
@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTINSt7__cxx1112basic_stri.body: The function is a constructor that accepts a constant reference to a BT instance whose underlying string type is std::basic_string<char>. It copies the internal data from the argument to the new object, effectively cloning the contained string representation.

@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTISt4pairINSt7__cxx1112ba.author: AI Short Overview
@lBT::BT@k_ZN2BTISt4pairINSt7__cxx1112ba.body: The public `BT` function accepts a reference to a `BT`‑wrapped pair consisting of a `std::basic_string<char>` and a `bool`. It unpacks the pair, extracts the string and boolean flag, and performs whatever transformation or lookup the surrounding code requires—typically returning a value or side effect based on the flag.

@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The `CMakeFiles` public function is a constructor that accepts an rvalue reference to a `CMakeFiles` instance. It’s used to efficiently transfer ownership of an existing `CMakeFiles` object into a new instance, typically to initialise or configure file‑generation settings for a project.

@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The constructor stores a reference to a file‑API, records the supplied version, builds paths for the module directory, source, and build directories, and records whether the build tree is distinct from the source tree. The final `static_cast<void>` is a no‑op that silences the unused‑variable warning.

@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The constructor copies the contents of an existing `CMakeFiles` instance into a new one, preserving the current state of file collections and any configuration flags. It is used whenever a duplicate make‑file configuration is needed without altering the original instance.

@lCMakeFiles::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110C.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::Dump@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_110C.body: The Dump function aggregates the state of a CMakeFiles instance into a JSON object: it serializes the collection of paths, the associated inputs, and—only if present—the set of globs‑dependent entries, then returns that object.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpGlobDependent@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpGlobDependent@k_ZN12_G.body:
The function serialises a `cmGlobCacheEntry` into a JSON‐style object.  
It builds a `Json::Value` object, copies the `Expression` field into the `"expression"` key, and conditionally adds boolean flags (`"recurse"`, `"listDirectories"`, `"followSymlinks"`) if the corresponding flags are set. If `Relative` is non‑empty it is added under the `"relative"` key. Finally it appends every entry in `Files` to a JSON array stored under `"paths"`. The constructed object is returned.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpGlobsDependent@k_ZN12_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpGlobsDependent@k_ZN12_.body: Iterates over the cached glob entries of the current CMake instance and builds a JSON array containing the per‑glob serialization produced by `DumpGlobDependent(entry)`—effectively serialising the dependent data for each global entry into a JSON array.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpInput@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpInput@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The function receives a file path, then builds a JSON‐style object that flags whether the file lies under the CMake module directory, outside the top source or build trees (external), or whether it is a generated out‑of‑source file. It also normalises the path to a relative form when appropriate, before returning that object.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpInputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpInputs@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The routine gathers a list of file‑paths by walking through each local generator attached to the current global CMake instance. For every generator it pulls the associated makefile, enumerates that file’s list of source files, and appends each path (after serializing it with `DumpInput`) into a JSON array that it finally returns.

@lCMakeFiles::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::DumpPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: This method builds a JSON object containing two key‑value pairs: “source” set to the value of the `TopSource` member and “build” set to the value of the `TopBuild` member. It then returns that object.

@lCMakeFiles::~CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.author: AI Short Overview
@lCMakeFiles::~CMakeFiles@k_ZN12_GLOBAL_.body: The `~CMakeFiles` function initializes and registers file‑level objects used throughout the project. It processes a list of file descriptors, allocates the corresponding internal structures, and links them into the global registry so that downstream components can query, read, or modify the files without duplicating creation logic. It returns a status code indicating success or failure of the file‑building phase.

@lCheckIncludeGuardIsSet@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheckIncludeGuardIsSet@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__.body: The routine walks up the directory hierarchy, examining each directory’s state for a property named by the supplied string. If it finds that property at any level (current or an ancestor), it returns true; otherwise it falls back to false after exhausting the chain.

@lCheck_Numeric_Character@p@l./Source/Cu.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_Numeric_Character@p@l./Source/Cu.body: Checks whether a given character is a digit, a plus/minus sign, or the locale‑specific decimal point, returning TRUE when it matches any of those.

@lCheck_Numeric_Field@p@l./Source/Curses.author: AI Short Overview
@lCheck_Numeric_Field@p@l./Source/Curses.body: Parse the field’s string, optionally strip a leading sign, read digits and an optional decimal point, then convert it to a double; if the value lies between the supplied low/high limits (respecting precision) it normalizes the field buffer with a formatted string and returns TRUE, otherwise returns FALSE.

@lCopy_Numeric_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lCopy_Numeric_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The function allocates a new `numericARG` block, copies the struct pointed to by `argp` into it, and returns the new pointer (or `NULL` if allocation fails). It also contains a typo in the `malloc` argument (`numericARG` instead of `numericARG`) and never frees the allocated memory, leading to a leak.

@lCreateInstallFileSetGenerator@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lCreateInstallFileSetGenerator@k_ZN12_G.body: This function creates a `cmInstallFileSetGenerator` configured for a specific file‑set target. It determines the appropriate message‑level using `helper.Makefile` and then constructs the generator with the target’s name, the file set, destination path, and the permission/​configuration options supplied in `args`. The returned `unique_ptr` owns the fully configured generator.

@lCreateInstallFilesGenerator@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lCreateInstallFilesGenerator@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The function forwards the supplied arguments to an overload that also receives the destination path obtained from `args.GetDestination()`. It constructs and returns a `cmInstallFilesGenerator` instance configured with the provided makefile, file list, command arguments, and whether program files are to be treated specially.

@lCreateInstallFilesGenerator@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lCreateInstallFilesGenerator@k_ZN12_GLO.body: Creates a unique‑owned `cmInstallFilesGenerator` instance configured for the current install operation. The routine first determines the appropriate message verbosity by calling `cmInstallGenerator::SelectMessageLevel` with the supplied `cmMakefile`. It then passes the supplied file list, destination path, program flag, and all arguments extracted from `cmInstallCommandArguments`—permissions, configurations, component, exclude flag, rename flag, optional flag—along with the command’s back‑trace, to the `cmInstallFilesGenerator` constructor via `cm::make_unique`. The result is a `std::unique_ptr<cmInstallFilesGenerator>` ready to produce the install files.

@lCreateInstallTargetGenerator@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCreateInstallTargetGenerator@k_ZN12_GL.body: The routine creates a new install generator for a target, configuring it with the supplied destination, permissions, and optional settings (like whether the component is a name‑link). It records the generator on the target and returns a unique‑pointer to that instance.

@lCreateInstallTargetGenerator@k_ZN12_GL.author: AI Short Overview
@lCreateInstallTargetGenerator@k_ZN12_GL.body: Creates a `cmInstallTargetGenerator` for a build target, forwarding the supplied parameters—including the destination path, force‑opt flag, and whether to use a name link—to an overloaded helper that actually constructs the generator.

@lEmptyBinaryDirectory@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lEmptyBinaryDirectory@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body: The function first validates that the supplied path is long enough and that the directory exists. If the directory contains a `CMakeCache.txt` file, it attempts to delete the contents repeatedly, retrying up to five times with short pauses. It reports success as `true`; otherwise it returns the error message via the `err` reference and indicates failure.

@lFree_Numeric_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lFree_Numeric_Type@p@l./Source/CursesDi.body: The routine safely deallocates a heap‑allocated object: it receives a void pointer, verifies that it is non‑null, and invokes `free()` to release the memory. This lightweight helper is typically used as a uniform deallocation hook wherever dynamic objects of varying types are freed.

@lGetIncludeGuardVariableName@k_ZN12_GLO.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetIncludeGuardVariableName@k_ZN12_GLO.body: The function generates a unique include‑guard identifier by hashing the supplied file path with MD5 and wrapping the hash in a static prefix/suffix pair (`__INCGUARD_…__`).

@lGetIndexArg@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111GetInd.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetIndexArg@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111GetInd.body: Accepts a string argument, tries to parse it to a long value, and on failure consults the policy state: in WARN mode it emits a warning and continues with the legacy path, in OLD it silently ignores, and in NEW it returns false. If parsing succeeds, it casts the parsed value to int, assigns it to *idx, and returns true. The cast may truncate values beyond the int range.

@lGetList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17GetListERKN.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetList@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_17GetListERKN.body: The function fetches a string‑representation of a variable from a `cmMakefile` via `GetListString`. If that fails or the string is empty it returns an optional containing an empty `cmList`; otherwise it builds and returns a list populated from the string (the final containment check is effectively a no‑op).

@lGetListString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113GetL.author: AI Short Overview
@lGetListString@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_113GetL.body: GetListString looks up a variable in a makefile; if the variable exists it writes its value into `listString` and returns true, otherwise it returns false.

@lGhsMultiGpj::GetGpjTag@k_ZN11GhsMultiG.author: AI Short Overview
@lGhsMultiGpj::GetGpjTag@k_ZN11GhsMultiG.body: The function receives an enum value representing a GPJ type, looks it up in a static array of string tags, and returns the corresponding tag string (or an empty string when the type isn’t in the list).

@lGhsMultiGpj::WriteGpjTag@k_ZN11GhsMult.author: AI Short Overview
@lGhsMultiGpj::WriteGpjTag@k_ZN11GhsMult.body: The routine calls the helper `GetGpjTag` to retrieve a C‑string that identifies the requested `gpjType` and then streams that string followed by a newline into the supplied `std::ostream`.

@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleAppendCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine expands a list variable name to its current string value, then appends the supplied items (starting from the third argument onward) to that list within the internal makefile representation, and records the change in the makefile’s definition map. If no items are supplied, it exits early without altering the makefile.

@lHandleDirectoryMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleDirectoryMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body:
The function parses a list of arguments for the directory‑install command.  
It interprets keywords such as DESTINATION, TYPE, PATTERN, REGEX, EXCLUDE, PERMISSIONS, OPTIONAL, MESSAGE_NEVER, and permission arguments, building a set of directories to install.  
While parsing it tracks whether a pattern or regex rule is active, applies the corresponding permissions, and accumulates any exclusion flags.  
After validating the arguments it creates an `cmInstallDirectoryGenerator` with the accumulated data, registers the component name with the global generator, and returns success or an appropriate error status.

@lHandleExportAndroidMKMode@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleExportAndroidMKMode@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The function parses and validates the arguments for an Android‑Makefile export command. It ensures a destination is provided, checks that the supplied file name is a plain “.mk” file (no path, no invalid extension), and that the export name can be safely mapped to a file. If everything checks out, it retrieves the matching export set from the makefile’s export set map and installs an Android‑MK export generator for that set. If any check fails, it records an error in the status object and returns false.

@lHandleExportMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleExportMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The function parses command‑line arguments for an “EXPORT” install mode, validates that all required options (destination, file name, and optional parameters such as permissions or component names) are supplied and well‑formed, and then creates an export‑install generator that writes the export configuration to the appropriate file in the build tree.

@lHandleFilesMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleFilesMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_115Ha.body: The function `HandleFilesMode` processes a list of file‑names supplied on the command‑line for the *FILES* mode of a CMake installation. It parses the arguments, validates that no unknown options were passed, checks that any requested type is allowed, and ensures that a single file is being renamed when the –RENAME flag is used. It rejects any file that was generated by an `export()` command (those cannot be installed directly), finalizes the arguments, and then registers the files with the global generator, adding any specified component names. If any of these checks fails, an error is recorded in `status` and the function returns false.

@lHandleFilterCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleFilterCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The function first validates the number of arguments, reports an error if any required part (list name, operator, mode, or pattern) is missing, then resolves the requested filter mode (INCLUDE or EXCLUDE). It fetches the named list, applies the supplied regex pattern under the chosen filter, and records the resulting list definition in the makefile before returning success or failure.

@lHandleFindCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleFindCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The routine parses a `FIND` invocation: it pulls the list name and variable to define from the arguments, looks up the named list, and writes the variable a string of the element’s index (or `‑1` if not found). If the list is missing, it simply defines the variable as `‑1`.

@lHandleGetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleGetCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116H.body: The function checks that at least three arguments are supplied, resolves the named list via `GetList`, validates each index argument with `GetIndexArg`, retrieves the corresponding items from that list, and finally registers the concatenated result in the makefile under the supplied variable name. If any step fails it reports an error via `cmExecutionStatus`.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.body: The `ArgVectors` function is a move‑constructor that creates a new `ArgVectors` instance from an existing one. It simply takes an rvalue reference (`ArgVectors&&`) and constructs a new object by moving the underlying data, enabling efficient transfer of argument vectors without copying. This is used in places like `cmInstallCommand.cxx` where existing vectors need to be re‑used or passed on without cost.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.body: The constructor performs a deep copy of an existing `ArgVectors` instance. It is invoked when a new command object needs to replicate the argument list of an already‑created command—typically during the install‑command workflow (see line 1298 of *cmInstallCommand.cxx*). By copying the internal vector representation, it guarantees that subsequent operations on the new instance are isolated from the original.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.body: The `ArgVectors` function parses a command‑line argument string and returns a vector of the individual arguments after stripping quotes and handling escape sequences. It is used throughout the codebase wherever a command line must be tokenized for further processing—for example, in `cmInstallCommand.cxx` when the installer needs to split the raw install command into its constituent options and operands. The function relies on a simple loop that splits on whitespace while respecting quoted substrings, and it produces a `std::vector<std::string>` that callers can iterate over or query for the presence of specific flags.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::Ar.body: Creates and returns a vector of argument objects that the cmInstallCommand module consumes during installation processing.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::[l.body: Returns a `std::unique_ptr<cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGenerator>` for the supplied target and command arguments. The function instantiates a new `cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGenerator` (using the provided arguments) and hands it back as a uniquely‑owned pointer, allowing callers to own and safely destroy the generator without manual cleanup. This helper is invoked in various code paths that construct runtime‑artifact generators for a given target.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode::[l.body: Creates a `cmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGenerator` wrapped in a `std::unique_ptr`, passing the target name, destination path, permissions, configurations, component data, message level, exclusion flags, optional settings, and the backtrace from the helper.

@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleImportedRuntimeArtifactsMode@k_Z.body: The function parses command‑line options for installing imported runtime artifacts, distinguishing libraries, runtime-only files, frameworks, and bundled executables. It validates each target’s type (executable, shared‑library, or module), creates a suitable install generator for the specific artifact type, registers those generators with the global generator, and records any runtime‑dependency sets required for the current host platform.

@lHandleInsertCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleInsertCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine parses an INSERT sub‑command: it validates the supplied arguments, resolves the target list (creating a new one if absent), parses the numeric index, and then inserts the succeeding arguments at that position in the list. After a successful insertion it updates the makefile definition, returning true; on parsing or runtime failure it reports an error in the status object and returns false.

@lHandleJoinCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleJoinCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_117.body: The function validates the argument count, retrieves the named list via `GetList`, and if the list is present, defines a makefile variable whose value is the list joined with the supplied glue string; if the list is absent, it defines the variable as an empty string. It returns `false` only when the argument count is wrong, otherwise `true`.

@lHandleLengthCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandleLengthCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: The routine implements the “LENGTH” sub‑command that expects two arguments: a list name and a target variable name. It first verifies that exactly two arguments are supplied; if not, it records an error on the makefile and returns `false`. When the argument count is correct, the routine resolves the list name via `GetList`. It then records the list’s current size (or zero if the list is missing) under the supplied variable name by calling `AddDefinition` on the makefile. If this succeeds, the function returns `true`.

@lHandlePackageInfoMode::[lambda_0]::ope.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePackageInfoMode::[lambda_0]::ope.body: The function provides a string representation of the object—typically used for logging or debugging.

@lHandlePackageInfoMode::[lambda_0]@kHan.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePackageInfoMode::[lambda_0]@kHan.body:
The lambda builds a file‑name string by concatenating `pkgNameOnDisk` with an optional suffix.  
If `appendix` is empty it returns `"pkgNameOnDisk.cps"`, otherwise it returns `"pkgNameOnDisk-appendix.cps"`.  
The function captures no external variables and uses `cmStrCat` to concatenate.

@lHandlePackageInfoMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePackageInfoMode@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N.body: The function implements the “PACKAGE_INFO” sub‑command of CMake. When called it first verifies that the experimental feature is enabled; if not, it reports the sub‑command as unknown and aborts. It then parses the supplied arguments, checking for duplicates, missing values, and mutual exclusivity (e.g. APPENDIX vs. VERSION, APPENDIX vs. DEFAULT_TARGETS, etc.). After validation, it builds the package file name (optionally lower‑casing and appending an APPENDIX when supplied) and selects the destination directory. @lHandlePopBackCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.author: AI Short Overview
@lHandlePopBackCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_.body:

Any remaining variable names after the list empties are undef­ined. If the list was empty from the start, all following variable names are undef­ined. The function always returns `true` after performing the removal/assignment logic.

@l__errno_location@k__errno_location.body: `__errno_location` provides the address of the thread‑local storage that holds the C library’s `errno` value. The function returns a pointer to that location so callers can read or modify `errno` safely in a multithreaded context.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.body: Returns a standard iterator for a container by forwarding the underlying iterator type.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.body: The function __normal_iterator is a helper that produces a simple iterator interface over a collection of strings. It accepts a reference to a __normal_iterator object parameterized with a const pointer to a string and a vector of strings, and forwards the underlying traversal logic to the standard iterator types, allowing client code to range‑over the contained strings without exposing internal details. The implementation typically maps to the begin()/end() pattern on the underlying vector, yielding a lightweight wrapper for idiomatic iteration.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.body: The function `__normal_iterator` is a public helper that produces an iterator over a sequence of `const char*` elements. When invoked, it wraps the raw character array into a lightweight iterator that supplies each element as a `std::basic_string<char>` view. This abstraction lets callers walk through raw string data uniformly without exposing the underlying storage details, ensuring a consistent iteration interface across the codebase.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::__normal.body: The function creates an iterator that yields `std::basic_string<char>` pointers over a `std::vector<std::basic_string<char>>`. It can be used to traverse a container for algorithms requiring normal iteration semantics.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: Returns a reference to the stored value so callers can treat the object like a raw pointer without changing its internal state.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: The `operator++` overload implements the postfix‑increment behavior for a `__normal_iterator`. When invoked, it returns a copy of the current iterator value (representing the element before the move) and then advances the underlying iterator so that subsequent uses of the returned iterator refer to the element that follows the original one.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: The `operator++()` of `__normal_iterator` increments the underlying iterator (or its internal position) and returns a reference to the iterator instance itself, enabling fluent chaining of increments in expressions.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: The overload adds an integral offset to the iterator, moving it forward by that many positions, and returns the modified iterator for chaining.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: This overload produces a new `__normal_iterator` that points to the element `difference` positions ahead in the underlying container. It simply adds the given offset to the iterator’s internal pointer/position and returns the resulting iterator.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: The public `operator->()` overload returns a pointer to the underlying object, enabling `obj->member` syntax to access members of that object while preserving const‑ness. It must not alter the state of the current instance and should never yield a dangling or `nullptr`. Use it only when you need arrow‑style member access on a wrapper or proxy that forwards to an internal member.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: It returns a new `__normal_iterator` that’s positioned a given number of steps before the current iterator – effectively stepping the iterator back by the supplied difference.

@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::__normal_iterator::operator.body: It copies the supplied iterator’s internal state into the current instance (typically via a move‑style assignment) and then returns a reference to the updated object.

@l__gnu_cxx::operator!=@k_ZN9__gnu_cxxne.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::operator!=@k_ZN9__gnu_cxxne.body: The operator overload returns true when the two normal_iterator instances do not refer to the same element; otherwise it returns false. It works by comparing the underlying iterator members (or the wrapped elements) of each instance.

@l__gnu_cxx::operator==@k_ZN9__gnu_cxxeq.author: AI Short Overview
@l__gnu_cxx::operator==@k_ZN9__gnu_cxxeq.body: The `operator==` template for `__normal_iterator` performs a value‑equality comparison: it returns `true` if both iterator instances wrap the same underlying iterator and belong to the same container, otherwise `false`. It typically implements this by comparing the stored iterator pointers or references (e.g. comparing `iterator_` member values).

@l_nc_Internal_Validation@k_nc_Internal_.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Internal_Validation@k_nc_Internal_.body: The routine performs an internal validation step for a form. It first synchronizes the form’s buffer, then checks whether the current field is marked as required or not permitted by the *O_PASSOK* flag. If the check fails, it runs the type‐specific validator; failure causes an immediate FALSE return. On success it clears the required flag, marks the field as changed, and propagates that change to any linked fields before exiting with TRUE.

@l_nc_Refresh_Current_Field@k_nc_Refresh.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Refresh_Current_Field@k_nc_Refresh.body:
The routine refreshes the part of the form that represents the current field.  
It verifies that the form and its window exist, then if the field is public it either copies the field’s window buffer (for scrollable or multiline fields) or simply marks the entire window as needing refresh.  
Finally it restores the original window state and positions the form cursor.

@l_nc_Set_Current_Field@k_nc_Set_Current.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Set_Current_Field@k_nc_Set_Current.body: The routine validates the incoming arguments, updates the form’s current field pointer, reallocates a new window for that field (creating a padded or derived window as needed), refreshes the visual display—including justification and visibility handling—and resets the form’s cursor and top‑row positions before returning success.

@l_nc_Set_Form_Page@k_nc_Set_Form_Page@f.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Set_Form_Page@k_nc_Set_Form_Page@f.body:
Updates the form’s current page and redraws only the fields on that page that have the O_VISIBLE flag.  
If a specific field is supplied, it becomes the current field; otherwise the first field of the new page is made active.  
The routine returns the status of any field‑display operation (or E_OK if all succeeded).

@l_nc_Synchronize_Attributes@k_nc_Synchr.author: AI Short Overview
@l_nc_Synchronize_Attributes@k_nc_Synchr.body: Synchronizes a field’s display state with its containing form: it validates the field, then if the field is active it updates the buffer, sets window attributes, clears the window, and either realigns justifications or copies the field buffer to the form window. If the field isn’t active it simply displays the field. It also tags the field as needing a full redraw.

@labort@kabort.author: AI Short Overview
@labort@kabort.body: Abnormal termination of the current execution context: it immediately shuts down the process and triggers any registered cleanup handlers before exiting, typically invoked after detecting a fatal error that cannot be recovered.

@laddFilesToItsSourceGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBA.author: AI Short Overview
@laddFilesToItsSourceGroups@k_ZN12_GLOBA.body: The function walks through the supplied file paths, tokenizes each path (appending a prefix if supplied), creates or retrieves a source‑group for that token chain via the makefile, and then registers the file in that group. If any group cannot be created, it records an error message and aborts the operation, signalling failure; otherwise it completes and returns success.

@latof@katof.author: AI Short Overview
@latof@katof.body: Converts a null‑terminated C‑string into a `double`, returning the numeric value represented by that string.

@latoi@katoi.author: AI Short Overview
@latoi@katoi.body: Converts a null‑terminated C string to an int by parsing an optional sign followed by decimal digits until a non‑digit is encountered; if the string contains no valid digits it returns 0.

@lcheckArgumentsPreconditions@k_ZL27chec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckArgumentsPreconditions@k_ZL27chec.body: The function validates the presence and correctness of the three expected command‑line arguments – prefix, tree, and regex – by delegating each check to the shared helper `checkSingleParameterArgumentPreconditions`. It returns true only if all three helpers succeed, propagating any error message back through the supplied `errorMsg` reference.

@lcheckSingleParameterArgumentPreconditi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcheckSingleParameterArgumentPreconditi.body: The function receives an argument name, a parsed‑arguments map, and a string to receive an error message. It looks up the argument in the map; if found it ensures the argument has exactly one value. If that check fails, it writes a descriptive error into errorMsg and returns false, otherwise it returns true.

@lclearerr@kclearerr.author: AI Short Overview
@lclearerr@kclearerr.body: Clears the error flag of the supplied FILE stream, resetting its state so that subsequent I/O calls on that stream behave normally.

@lclose@kclose.author: AI Short Overview
@lclose@kclose.body: The function attempts to close an underlying resource identified by the integer argument and returns a status code indicating success or failure.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: Returns a `string_view` that covers the passed‐in array up to, but not including, its terminating `'\0'`.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: It returns the supplied string view unchanged.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: It returns a `string_view` that is directly constructed from the supplied `String` argument. The function is a static member of `AsStringView<String>` and simply forwards the call to the `String` instance’s `view()` method, yielding a lightweight view of the string without copying its contents.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: The function simply creates a `string_view` that refers to the supplied string; it returns that view without copying the string data.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: The `view` helper simply turns a raw C‑string into a `string_view` – it constructs the view from the supplied pointer and returns it unchanged, exposing the underlying string data directly.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: It returns a `string_view` unchanged, acting as a straight pass‑through identity operation.

@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::AsStringView::view@k_ZN2cm12AsStri.body: Creates a string_view over the single character supplied.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: This function accepts a reference to a const char array of size N and returns an `std::string` constructed from that array, dropping the trailing null terminator.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: It returns a default‑constructed string view – essentially an empty string – for a `nullptr` argument.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: Returns a `std::string` that represents the value stored in a `StringOpPlus<L, R>` instance.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: It simply returns the input string unchanged—acting as a trivial identity function.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: The function wraps a C‑style string into a `String` instance, returning an empty `String` when passed a null pointer; otherwise it copies the null‑terminated sequence into a new string object.

@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::IntoString::into_string@k_ZN2cm10I.body: Creates a one‑character string from the supplied character.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ENS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ENS.body: Creates a `String` instance from a `static_string_view` by forwarding the view and a private‑mode flag to the primary constructor. The `explicit` keyword guarantees that a `static_string_view` cannot be implicitly converted to a `String`; the call to `String(s, Private())` supplies the view and a private‑only flag to the underlying implementation.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EON.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EON.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference to a `std::string` and a private‑tag parameter. It allocates a new string via `std::make_shared`, stores that pointer in `string_`, and then builds a `view_` that references the underlying buffer of the stored string (its data pointer and size).

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.body: The constructor creates a new `String` by taking ownership of the internal buffer and view from the supplied rvalue reference `s`. It copies `s.string_` into `string_` and copies `s.view_` into `view_`, then clears `s.view_` to a default-constructed string view.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOS.body: This private constructor simply delegates to the base class’s move constructor: it takes an r‑value reference, flags the operation as noexcept, and uses an initializer‑list to invoke `String(std::move(s))`, leaving the body empty.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EOT.body: This constructor accepts any type `T` that satisfies the `IntoString` trait. It forwards the argument to `IntoString<T>::into_string`, then forwards that string to a private constructor that actually builds the `String` instance.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EPK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1EPK.body: Constructs a `String` object from a C‑style string and a size argument by delegating to the `std::string` constructor.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.body: The declaration declares a noexcept copy‑constructor that is defaulted, letting the compiler generate a trivial copy operation that simply copies the internal string data without throwing exceptions.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ERK.body: Creates a new string that looks at the original string’s internal buffer. It copies the base string reference (`string_`), and then sets its internal view to start at `s.data()+pos` and span at most `count` characters—clipped to the remaining length of `s`. If `count` is left as `npos`, the view extends to the end of `s`.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.body: The constructor takes an `std::initializer_list<char>` (a braced list of characters), creates a temporary `std::string` from that list, and then delegates to the primary `String` constructor that accepts a `std::string`. This forwards the constructed string directly to the underlying string representation.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.body: The constructor takes a `std::string_view`, constructs a `std::string` from it, and forwards that string along with a `Private()` marker to a delegating constructor that initializes the internal representation. It enforces explicit construction to avoid unintended implicit conversions.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ESt.body: The constructor simply assigns the supplied `string_view` to the `view_` member, acting as a private factory that lets only trusted code create an instance.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ET_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1ET_.body: Constructs a `String` from any input iterator range. It simply forwards the `[first, last)` range to the `String(std::string(first, last))` constructor, delegating the actual construction to that overload.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Emc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Emc.body: Creates a string that consists of `n` copies of the character `c` by delegating the construction to the `std::string`‑based constructor.

@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::String@k_ZN2cm6StringC1Ev.body: The function creates a new string instance with no initial content, providing a clean‑start for subsequent usage.

@lcm::String::at@k_ZNK2cm6String2atEm@f..author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::at@k_ZNK2cm6String2atEm@f..body: The `at` member simply forwards a const‑indexed access to the underlying `view_` container: given a position `pos`, it calls `view_.at(pos)` and returns the resulting character. Because the member is marked `const`, it guarantees not modifying the object, and any bounds violation that `view_.at` performs will propagate as an exception to the caller.

@lcm::String::back@k_ZNK2cm6String4backE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::back@k_ZNK2cm6String4backE.body: The method retrieves and returns the last character stored in the underlying view, guaranteeing no exceptions and preserving const‑ness.

@lcm::String::begin@k_ZNK2cm6String5begi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::begin@k_ZNK2cm6String5begi.body: The function simply forwards the request for the first position of the underlying sequence. It guarantees no exception is thrown (notably marked `noexcept`) and returns a const‑iterator that cannot be used to modify the container, ensuring read‑only access.

@lcm::String::borrow@k_ZN2cm6String6borr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::borrow@k_ZN2cm6String6borr.body: Creates a new `String` instance from the supplied `string_view` and tags the resulting object as private.

@lcm::String::c_str@k_ZN2cm6String5c_str.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::c_str@k_ZN2cm6String5c_str.body: The `c_str` member returns a raw `const char*` pointing at the internal buffer that stores the string data. It first obtains the internal pointer, and if it is `nullptr` simply returns that value. If the string is not null‑terminated it converts the internal representation into a standard `std::string` in order to obtain a proper terminator and then returns that pointer. This guarantees callers receive a null‑terminated C‑string that can safely be accessed one byte past the end.

@lcm::String::cbegin@k_ZNK2cm6String6cbe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::cbegin@k_ZNK2cm6String6cbe.body: It forwards to the container’s underlying `begin()` and yields a `const_iterator` that points to the very first element. The function is marked `noexcept`, so callers can call it without worry about exception safety, and the member is `const` so it can be invoked on read‑only instances.

@lcm::String::cend@k_ZNK2cm6String4cendE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::cend@k_ZNK2cm6String4cendE.body: Returns a read‑only iterator that refers to the logical end of the internal sequence, letting callers traverse the data without modifying the underlying container.

@lcm::String::clear@k_ZN2cm6String5clear.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::clear@k_ZN2cm6String5clear.body: Assigns an empty string literal to the instance.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: The member template `compare` is enabled only when `T` can be viewed as a string view (via `AsStringView<T>::value`). It forwards the argument to `AsStringView<T>::view`, then delegates to the stored `view_`’s own `compare` member, returning an `int` that reflects the lexical ordering of the two string views.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body:
The function forwards a comparison request to the underlying `view_` object: it simply returns the result of `view_.compare(pos1, count1, s)`.  
This member is `const`, so it guarantees not to modify the object. The return value follows the usual convention for comparison functions—negative if the target is less than the argument, zero if equal, positive otherwise. No extra logic is performed in this wrapper; it merely delegates the call to the encapsulated view implementation.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: The method forwards the comparison request to its underlying view object, passing along the provided position and lengths of the substrings to be compared. It relies on the view’s own `compare` routine to produce and return the integer comparison result.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: The function forwards its arguments to the underlying view_ object’s compare method and returns that comparison result.

@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::compare@k_ZNK2cm6String7co.body: This member simply forwards a substring‑comparison to its underlying view: it compares the segment of the stored view from `pos1` of length `count1` with the segment of the provided `string_view` from `pos2` of length `count2`, returning the integer result of that comparison.

@lcm::String::copy@k_ZNK2cm6String4copyE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::copy@k_ZNK2cm6String4copyE.body: This member forwards a request to the underlying view to copy a segment starting at position `pos` of length `count` into the buffer pointed to by `dest`, returning the number of bytes actually written.

@lcm::String::crbegin@k_ZNK2cm6String7cr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::crbegin@k_ZNK2cm6String7cr.body: It returns a const‑reverse iterator that points to the container’s last element, letting you traverse it in reverse order without changing the underlying data (the call is noexcept and guarantees no side‑effects).

@lcm::String::crend@k_ZNK2cm6String5cren.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::crend@k_ZNK2cm6String5cren.body: It returns a const reverse iterator that represents the one‑past‑the‑first element of the container.

@lcm::String::data@k_ZNK2cm6String4dataE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::data@k_ZNK2cm6String4dataE.body: Returns a pointer to the underlying data buffer without modifying the object; the call is marked `noexcept` and `const`, so it guarantees no state change or exception propagation.

@lcm::String::empty@k_ZNK2cm6String5empt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::empty@k_ZNK2cm6String5empt.body: Returns a `bool` that tells whether the internal `view_` container has no elements, delegating the check to `view_`’s own `empty()` implementation. The method is `const` and marked `noexcept`, guaranteeing no state mutation or exception is thrown.

@lcm::String::end@k_ZNK2cm6String3endEv@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::end@k_ZNK2cm6String3endEv@.body: The member returns a constant iterator that refers to the underlying view’s logical end. It’s declared `noexcept`, guaranteeing the call will not throw, and as a `const` member it doesn’t alter the object’s state. The function simply forwards the `view_.end()` iterator, so it can be used safely in noexcept contexts while ensuring no modification of the underlying container.

@lcm::String::erase@k_ZN2cm6String5erase.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::erase@k_ZN2cm6String5erase.body: The `erase` function removes a substring of the requested length starting at a given index, throwing an exception if the start index lies outside the current string. It builds a new string that contains the prefix before that region and the suffix after it, then replaces the original string with that new content via a move assignment. This way it preserves data integrity while ensuring the returned reference points to the updated string.

@lcm::String::find@k_ZNK2cm6String4findE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::find@k_ZNK2cm6String4findE.body: find returns the index of the first occurrence of the supplied argument in the underlying string view by converting the argument into a string view and delegating to the underlying view’s find operation.

@lcm::String::find@k_ZNK2cm6String4findE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::find@k_ZNK2cm6String4findE.body: The `find` member simply forwards a string-search request to the encapsulated view object and returns the resulting index (or `npos` if not found). It performs a const‑qualified lookup with no side‑effects.

@lcm::String::find_first_not_of@k_ZNK2cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::find_first_not_of@k_ZNK2cm.body: The function returns the first index in the stored string after a given start position that does not contain any character from a provided set, converting the argument to a string view via AsStringView and delegating the search to the underlying view’s `find_first_not_of` implementation.

@lcm::String::find_first_not_of@k_ZNK2cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::find_first_not_of@k_ZNK2cm.body: The method returns the index of the first character after a given position that is not contained in a supplied list of characters, delegating the actual lookup to its internal view.

@lcm::String::find_first_of@k_ZNK2cm6Str.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::find_first_of@k_ZNK2cm6Str.body: The template is a const member that accepts any type convertible to a `string_view`. It forward‑constructs a temporary `string_view` from the argument (via `AsStringView<T>::view`), then delegates the search to the underlying `view_` object’s `find_first_of` method, returning its result.

@lcm::String::find_first_of@k_ZNK2cm6Str.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::find_first_of@k_ZNK2cm6Str.body: The member returns the position of the first occurrence of the substring `s` in the internal string view, starting the search at the supplied offset and scanning at most `count` characters. If `s` isn’t found, it yields the special value `npos`. The function simply forwards the call to the encapsulated `view_` object.

@lcm::String::find_last_not_of@k_ZNK2cm6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm::String::find_last_not_of@k_ZNK2cm6.body: The template resolves at compile‑time: if `T` can be viewed as a string, it forwards the argument to the underlying `view_`’s `find_last_not_of` routine and returns whatever that routine returns. @lcm::String::find_last_not_of@k_ZNK2cm6.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmBinUtilsLinuxELFObjdumpGetRuntimeDep.body: The function executes the “objdump” utility to gather dependency information for a specified ELF file. @lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::GetFileDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::GetFileDep.body: The method walks through every candidate file name, attempts to resolve it against the current executable and loader context, and if it resolves to a real file that is not excluded, it pulls that file’s metadata (including its own rpaths) and registers the file in the archive. When a dependency is newly discovered, the routine also recursively scans its own lib list using the accumulated rpaths. If any resolution fails or metadata is missing, the function aborts early, flagging the overall dependency resolution as unsuccessful.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::GetFileInf.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveDep.author: AI Short Overview

It sets the `resolved` flag appropriately and verifies that the resulting path is absolute before returning success.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveExe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveExe.body: The routine first verifies that the supplied executable path string isn’t empty. If it is empty, it clears the resolved flag and returns true. Otherwise it substitutes the first 16 characters of the target name with the executable path, then checks whether the resulting path exists on disk; if it does, it sets the resolved flag to true, otherwise to false, and returns true in either case.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveLoa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveLoa.body: The routine substitutes the first 12‑character placeholder in the input name with the supplied loader path, then tests whether that constructed path actually exists on disk. If the path string is empty or the constructed path fails the existence test, it marks the dependency unresolved; otherwise it records it resolved.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveRPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ResolveRPa.body: The routine walks through each directory supplied in *rpaths*. For every candidate it forms a candidate file name by substituting the first six characters of the supplied *name* with the current rpath. It then checks whether the resulting path has a special prefix: if it begins with “@loader_path/” it delegates resolution to `ResolveLoaderPathDependency`; if it begins with “@executable_path/” it delegates to `ResolveExecutablePathDependency`. If neither special prefix applies, the routine falls back to a simple file‑existence test. When a file is found it assigns that path to the output reference, marks the dependency as resolved, and returns success. The function itself always returns `true` (unless a delegated resolution fails), so the caller must rely on the `resolved` flag to know whether a suitable path was actually found.

@lcmBinUtilsMacOSMachOLinker::ScanDepend.author: AI Short Overview

If no metadata is available, it immediately reports failure.

@lcmCMakePath::Absolute@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: The method appends a new path component to the internal Path member, normalizing directory separators to forward‑slashes via `generic_string()`, and then returns the updated instance by reference.

@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: Adds the supplied path to the current instance and returns a reference to that instance, enabling fluent method chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Append@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: This overload accepts any type `Source` that satisfies the `enable_if_pathable` trait. @lcmCMakePath::Assign@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Assign@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: It assigns a value to the internal `Path` member by forwarding the incoming argument, then returns `*this` to allow fluent chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::Assign@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: Adds the supplied `path` to the current object's `Path` string and returns a reference to the modified instance.

@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: `Concat` appends the given `source` to the internal path object via `operator+=`, then returns a reference to the current instance, enabling fluent chaining of path segments while being constrained by `enable_if_pathable` to guarantee that the supplied type is indeed path‑compatible.

@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Concat@k_ZN11cmCMakePath6.body: The function appends the provided string view to the existing internal path and then returns the modified instance, enabling chained calls on the same object.

@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: Formats a string‑view path by constructing a `std::string` and delegating to the overload that operates on a `std::string`, then returns the formatted result.

@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::FormatPath@k_ZN11cmCMakeP.body: The routine cleans a Windows‑style path string: it replaces backslashes with forward slashes, strips the “//?/” long‑name marker, and rewrites leading “UNC” prefixes into a single leading slash. It returns the trimmed, forward‑slash path.

@lcmCMakePath::GenericString@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GenericString@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: Returns a string obtained by delegating to the `Path` member’s `generic_string()` implementation.

@lcmCMakePath::GenericWString@k_ZNK11cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GenericWString@k_ZNK11cmC.body: The function returns a `std::wstring` that represents the underlying path in a wide‑character string form. It simply forwards the request to the `generic_wstring()` method of the `Path` member, guaranteeing that the returned string is immutable (the function is marked `const`).

@lcmCMakePath::GetExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.body: This function returns the file‑extension string stored in the internal `Path` object.

@lcmCMakePath::GetFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: This const member simply forwards to the underlying path object’s `filename()` method, returning the last component of the stored path. If the path ends with a separator or contains no filename component, the returned string will be empty.

@lcmCMakePath::GetNarrowStem@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetNarrowStem@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: It returns the first part of the path’s stem up to the first dot – if one exists – otherwise it yields the entire stem unchanged.

@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: The function copies the internally stored path, normalises it to the native filesystem representation, and writes that string into the supplied `path` reference.

@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetNativePath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: The `GetNativePath` member collects the internal path string, normalises it, and writes it into the supplied reference. On Windows, if the resulting path is an absolute path that would exceed the legacy `MAX_PATH` limit, it rewrites the path to a “prefixed” form (`\\?\…` or `\\?\UNC\…`) so that the path can be passed to Windows APIs that accept extended‑length paths.

@lcmCMakePath::GetParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: It returns a `cmCMakePath` that represents the parent directory of the current instance, allowing callers to traverse up the hierarchy without mutating the original path.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.body: Returns a relative path by delegating to the underlying `Path` object's `relative_path()` method.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.body: Retrieves the root‐level directory stored in the current object by delegating to the encapsulated Path instance; the method is `const`, guaranteeing no modification of internal state.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: It forwards the request to the wrapped `Path` object and returns the value produced by `Path.root_name()`. The function is marked `const`, guaranteeing that no internal state is altered during the call.

@lcmCMakePath::GetRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: Returns the root path stored in the internal `Path` object, simply forwarding `Path.root_path()` without mutating any state.

@lcmCMakePath::GetStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body:
cmCMakePath GetStem() const { return this->Path.stem(); }  

This member function returns the base component of the stored path by delegating to `Path.stem()` and wraps it in a `cmCMakePath` result.

@lcmCMakePath::GetWideExtension@k_ZNK11c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::GetWideExtension@k_ZNK11c.body: The function extracts the substring that follows the last dot in the current path’s filename. If the filename is empty, “.”, or “..”, it yields an empty path object. It identifies the first dot that is not a leading dot; when such a dot exists it returns a string view of the remaining characters as a new path instance. If no dot is found it falls back to an empty path.

@lcmCMakePath::HasExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasExtension@k_ZNK11cmCMa.body: Delegates the check to `Path.has_extension()`, returning `true` if the underlying path contains an extension.

@lcmCMakePath::HasFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasFileName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: Returns true if the underlying path object contains a file name; it simply proxies the result of `Path.has_filename()` without modifying any state.

@lcmCMakePath::HasParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasParentPath@k_ZNK11cmCM.body: Returns whether the underlying `Path` object reports a parent path, simply forwarding the result of its `has_parent_path()` call.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRelativePath@k_ZNK11cm.body: Checks whether the internal `Path` instance contains a relative component and returns that result as a boolean.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRootDirectory@k_ZNK11c.body: Checks whether the stored `Path` object reports having a root‑level component and returns that result.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRootName@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: The function forwards a check to the underlying `Path` object: it returns `true` when that object reports the presence of a root name, and `false` otherwise.

@lcmCMakePath::HasRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasRootPath@k_ZNK11cmCMak.body: It checks whether the stored path includes a root component, allowing callers to detect absolute paths.

@lcmCMakePath::HasStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::HasStem@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: The method simply forwards to the underlying Path object, returning true when that object reports it contains a stem.

@lcmCMakePath::IsAbsolute@k_ZNK11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::IsAbsolute@k_ZNK11cmCMake.body: The function `IsAbsolute()` simply forwards to `Path.is_absolute()` and returns that boolean result.

@lcmCMakePath::IsEmpty@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::IsEmpty@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: This function simply returns the result of the internal `Path.empty()` call: it returns `true` when the `Path` string is empty, and `false` otherwise. The call is marked `noexcept` so it cannot throw.

@lcmCMakePath::IsPrefix@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::IsPrefix@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: The method walks through both path strings element‑by‑element. When the current object’s path runs out of its elements or the next element in the argument path diverges, the loop stops. If the current object’s path has been exhausted (or the next element in the argument path is an empty string) before the argument path ends, the method returns true; otherwise false.

@lcmCMakePath::IsRelative@k_ZNK11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::IsRelative@k_ZNK11cmCMake.body: Returns whether the wrapped Path instance reports its path as relative.

@lcmCMakePath::Native@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::NativeWString@k_ZNK11cmCM.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::Normal@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.body: The method computes a path that is lexically proximate to a supplied base path by calling the internal `lexically_proximate` helper, then normalises Windows‐style backslashes to forward slashes before returning the resulting path string.

@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Proximate@k_ZNK11cmCMakeP.body: It forwards a `Source` that is convertible to a filesystem path to the path‑specific `Proximate` overload. The template is enabled only when `Source` satisfies `enable_if_pathable`, ensuring compile‑time type safety.

@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: Computes the relative path between the current path and the supplied `base` path, returning a new path instance that represents that relative position.

@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::Relative@k_ZNK11cmCMakePa.body: The template creates a relative path by converting the supplied `base` value to a `filesystem::path` and then delegating to the existing `Relative` overload that accepts a path. The `enable_if_pathable<Source>` guard ensures only types that can be converted to a `filesystem::path` compile. The function simply returns the result of the underlying `Relative` call.

@lcmCMakePath::RemoveExtension@k_ZN11cmC.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceExtension@k_ZN11cm.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.body: Replace the path’s filename component with the supplied `filename` value, then return the current object for chaining.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceFileName@k_ZN11cmC.body: Replaces the current filename component of the internal path (if one exists) with the supplied argument and returns the modified instance.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.body: The function forwards the supplied `extension` to an overload that accepts a `string_view`, effectively performing a “wide‑extension” replacement on the current path and returning the updated path.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.body: This template forwards a call to `ReplaceWideExtension` on the current object, accepting any type that satisfies the `enable_if_pathable` constraint and returning the resulting `cmCMakePath&`.

@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::ReplaceWideExtension@k_ZN.body: The method strips an existing extension from the current path (if one is present), then appends the supplied string (prefixed with a dot when missing), and finally updates the internal path with the new filename.

@lcmCMakePath::String@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::String@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath.body:
It returns a copy of the underlying path string. Since the method is `const`, it guarantees the object can’t be modified during the call.  
The implementation simply forwards to `Path.string()`, so it relies on whatever string representation `Path` provides.  
Because it returns a `std::string` by value, callers incur a copy each time; if `Path` holds a large string this can be a performance hit.  
A potential pitfall is the naming: `String()` shadows the standard `std::string` type, which can be confusing when reading code.

@lcmCMakePath::WString@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::WString@k_ZNK11cmCMakePat.body: The function simply returns the current path as a wide‑character string, delegating to the underlying `Path::wstring()` implementation. It is read‑only (const), so no state changes occur.

@lcmCMakePath::begin@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::begin@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath5.body: The function constructs an `iterator` that holds a reference to the `cmCMakePath` instance and points to the first element of its internal `Path` container. It simply returns this iterator.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: `cmCMakePath` is a noexcept constructor that simply forwards a `cm::filesystem::path` argument to its base class `Path` via a move‑semantic initialization (`Path(std::move(path))`). No extra logic or side‑effects are performed.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: Creates a `Path` instance from a null‑terminated C string. @lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body:
`cmCMakePath` is a small utility type that represents a filesystem path.  
- It stores the path string internally.  
- It has a defaulted copy constructor (`cmCMakePath(const&) = default;`).  
- The object exposes an `Append()` member that returns a new `cmCMakePath` with the supplied component appended, making it easy to chain path fragments (e.g., `"compiler_depend.make"` in the examples).

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: The function creates a `Path` object by formatting the input string with `FormatPath` using the specified format (defaulting to the generic format) and then passes the result to the base `Path` constructor, all within a noexcept context.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: The template creates a `Path` instance from any type that is move‑convertible to a path. It forwards the source (via `std::move`) to `FormatPath` with the supplied formatting option (defaulting to `generic_format`), and constructs the `Path` object from that result. The `enable_if_move_pathable<Source>` constraint guarantees the template participates only when the source type can be moved into a path-compatible representation.

@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCMakePath::cmCMakePath@k_ZN11cmCMake.body: Creates a new `cmCMakePath` object with its default state. The default constructor is noexcept, so no exceptions are thrown during construction, and it can be invoked simply via a default‐constructed instance (`cmCMakePath{}` or `return cmCMakePath{}`).

@lcmCMakePath::end@k_ZNK11cmCMakePath3en.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCMakePath::iterator::iterator@k_ZN11.author: AI Short Overview
