Finally, it forwards the current test result and index to the concrete memory‑check handler by invoking `PostProcessTest`.

@lcmCTestRunTest::NeedsToRepeat@k_ZN14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::NeedsToRepeat@k_ZN14cm.body: It decreases the remaining‑run counter, skips tests marked **NOT_RUN**, and then checks the current repeat mode against the test’s status. If the conditions match (e.g., a repeat‑until‑fail, repeat‑until‑pass or repeat‑after‑timeout scenario), it sets `RunAgain` to true and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmCTestRunTest::ParseOutputForMeasurem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::ParseOutputForMeasurem.body: The routine scans a populated output buffer for embedded `<DartMeasurement>` or `<CTestMeasurement>` markers; when found it runs a regex match to pull the numeric value out of the first capture group, assigns that to `TestResult.TestMeasurementsOutput`, and then repeatedly erases any subsequent matches using a second regex until the buffer contains no more measurement tokens.

@lcmCTestRunTest::SetupResourcesEnvironm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::SetupResourcesEnvironm.body:
The routine:

1. Emits an environment variable `CTEST_RESOURCE_GROUP_COUNT` equal to the number of resource groups already allocated.  
2. Iterates through each group in `AllocatedResources`.  
   For every group it  
   – builds a string listing the group’s type identifiers (comma‑separated), e.g. `CTEST_RESOURCE_GROUP_0=TYPE1,TYPE2`.  
   – For each type in the group it creates a second string in the form `CTEST_RESOURCE_GROUP_<n>_<TYPE>=id:…;id:…`, where the `id` and `slots` values for each item in that type are joined by semicolons.  
   – Each of these strings is passed to `cmSystemTools::PutEnv` to define the corresponding environment variable.  
3. If a log vector was supplied, the same strings are appended to it for later inspection.  
4. The function performs no allocation or de‑allocation; it merely reports the current state via environment variables and an optional log.

@lcmCTestRunTest::StartAgain@k_ZN14cmCTe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::StartAgain@k_ZN14cmCTe.body:
The function first verifies whether the test run is flagged to run again; if not, it exits early.  
When allowed, it clears the flag, constructs a fresh `cmProcess` tied to the current runner, and attempts to switch the working directory to the test‑specific path. If that switch fails, it reports the failure via `StartFailure` and ends. Otherwise, it initiates the test execution by calling `StartTest` with the current and total test counts and signals success.

@lcmCTestRunTest::StartFailure@k_ZN14cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::StartFailure@k_ZN14cmC.body: The function transfers ownership of the supplied runner to a newly created `cmProcess` instance, assigns that instance to the test’s `TestProcess` member, then immediately invokes the test‑specific failure routine (`StartFailure`) with the provided parameters, and finally marks the test as failed by calling `FinalizeTest(false)`.

@lcmCTestRunTest::StartFailure@k_ZN14cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::StartFailure@k_ZN14cmC.body:
The `StartFailure` routine records a test that could not run successfully. It first writes a “Start” entry into the test progress log, then clears any buffered output.  
If an optional message (`output`) is supplied, it logs that text to the test‑handler file and to the error log.  
Afterward it zero‑initialises the test result structure – setting its metadata, returning value, and status fields – marking the test as “not run” and storing the supplied detail string as the completion status. The function finishes with an empty command line and environment record so the test result object is ready for downstream reporting.

@lcmCTestRunTest::StartTest@k_ZN14cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::StartTest@k_ZN14cmCTes.body: `StartTest` creates a `cmProcess` instance, assigns it to the current test object's `TestProcess` member, and then attempts to start the test via `StartTest(completed, total)`. If that call fails, it calls `FinalizeTest(false)`.

@lcmCTestRunTest::StartTest@k_ZN14cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::StartTest@k_ZN14cmCTes.body: The function initializes test metadata, validates test configuration and dependencies, logs the start or progress of the test, and finally forks a child process to execute the test, returning true only if the process starts successfully.

@lcmCTestRunTest::WriteLogOutputTop@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::WriteLogOutputTop@k_ZN.body: The routine assembles a formatted header for a test run, deciding whether to prefix a progress fraction (completed/total) based on the repeat‑mode state and whether progress output is requested. It then tags the entry with a memory‑check marker, a run index, and a padded test name. In addition it emits the test descriptor (index, name, directory, command line) to both the log stream and a dedicated log file stream, finally flushing the generated line into the log file and optionally writing it to a handler‑level output stream.

@lcmCTestRunTest::cmCTestRunTest@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestRunTest::cmCTestRunTest@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor pulls the specific test object and its properties out of the multi‑process handler’s indexed collection, wiring the internal `CTest`, `TestHandler`, and `TestProperties` members to that test instance before the object’s ready to execute.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::AddConfiguration.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::AddConfiguration.body: The method stores the supplied script string in the internal collection and records its scope flag in a parallel flag container, effectively queuing the script for later processing.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::CreateCMake@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::CreateCMake@k_ZN.body: It builds a CMake instance for the test framework, configures its working directories and current snapshot, creates a makefile linked to the global generator, propagates recursion depth if a parent makefile exists, installs a progress‑callback that logs progress messages, and finally registers a set of built‑in command objects that provide the test harness with actions such as “ctest_build”, “ctest_configure”, “ctest_coverage” and the like.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::ExecuteScript@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::ExecuteScript@k_.body: The method builds a command line beginning with the ctest executable followed by a “‑SR” flag and the user‑supplied script path. It appends any pre‑existing arguments, omitting any duplicate “‑SR” entries, and then launches the child process using an UV process chain. Output is streamed back line‑by‑line; stdout lines are logged verbosely while any stderr line is recorded as an error message. After the child exits, the routine examines the exit status and any exception code—logging failures if present—and returns the numeric exit code (or –1 on failure).

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::GetCMake@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::GetCMake@k_ZN20c.body: This function simply returns a pointer to the internal `CMake` instance by calling its `get()` accessor.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::GetMakefile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::GetMakefile@k_ZN.body: It returns a pointer to the object’s `Makefile` member by invoking that member’s `get()` method.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::ProcessHandler@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::ProcessHandler@k.body: It runs each stored configuration script in turn, OR‑ing the return codes together. If any script reports an error (i.e. its return value is non‑zero), the function returns –1; otherwise it returns 0 to indicate all scripts ran successfully.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::ReadInScript@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::ReadInScript@k_Z.body: The ReadInScript routine first clears any previous error flag, parses an optional comma‑separated argument list, checks the referenced script file exists, then loads and executes a CMake configuration module (CTestScriptMode.cmake) that sets up system‑specific paths and variables. It populates the internal makefile with the current script’s path and name, along with any command‑line definitions, and finally reads in the target script file itself, reporting an error if the read fails.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::RunConfiguration.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestScriptHandler::RunConfiguration.body: The function is a small utility that logs the action being performed and delegates the actual work to either `ReadInScript` or `ExecuteScript` depending on the `pscope` flag. It keeps the environment state intact via a `SaveRestoreEnvironment` guard (only when `CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP` is omitted) and simply returns the status code from the called routine.

@lcmCTestScriptHandler::~cmCTestScriptHa.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestTestHandler::CleanTestOutput@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestTestHandler::CleanTestOutput@k_.body: The method trims a test‑output string when it exceeds a given length. The result is a compact string that preserves character boundaries and indicates that a portion was omitted.

@lcmCTestTestHandler::FindTheExecutable@.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestTestHandler::GenerateTestComman.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestVC::File::File@k_ZN9cmCTestVC4F.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestVC::GetNightlyTime@k_ZN9cmCTest.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestVC::NoteNewRevision@k_ZN9cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestVC::NoteOldRevision@k_ZN9cmCTes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestVC::NoteOldRevision@k_ZN9cmCTes.body: The method simply returns `true`, effectively signaling that no special handling is required for an old revision. Derived classes can override it to flag an old revision scenario and react accordingly.

@lcmCTestVC::Revision::Revision@k_ZN9cmC.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestVC::Revision::operator=@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestVC::RunChild@k_ZN9cmCTestVC8Run.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestVC::RunChild@k_ZN9cmCTestVC8Run.body: Logs the command string, prepares a child process in the given working directory via a process chain builder, runs it, and returns true only if both the spawn result and exit status returned zero.

@lcmCTestVC::RunUpdateCommand@k_ZN9cmCTe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCTestVC::RunUpdateCommand@k_ZN9cmCTe.body: The method computes a command string from the supplied arguments, stores it in `UpdateCommandLine`, and if the “show‑only” flag is set, it logs that string and returns success immediately. @lcmCTestVC::UpdateImpl@k_ZN9cmCTestVC10.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCTestVC::~cmCTestVC@k_ZN9cmCTestVCD1.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::AddIncludeFla.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyR.body: The protected pure virtual const member `GetClangTidyReplacementsFilePath()` returns the filesystem path for the temporary file that holds clang‑tidy replacement directives. Sub‑classes must override it to supply the exact location, typically based on build‑type or target configuration, and the returned string is used when generating the replacement file in `cmCommonTargetGenerator.cxx`.

@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::~cmCommonTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCommonTargetGenerator::~cmCommonTarg.body: The virtual destructor guarantees that any resources owned by an instance of `cmCommonTargetGenerator` (including those acquired by subclasses) are released in a polymorphic‑safe manner. By delegating cleanup to the base class’s default implementation, it allows derived types to rely on the compiler‑generated destructor while still ensuring proper base‑class teardown.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::Evaluat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::Evaluat.body: The Evaluate function constructs an evaluation context from the supplied arguments, runs each evaluator in Evaluators, appends their results to Output, tracks any errors or sensitive‑condition flags, stores the collected target and property information, and finally returns the combined output string.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetAllT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetAllT.body: The method simply hands back a reference to the internal `AllTargetsSeen` set of target pointers.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetBack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetBack.body: This const member simply returns the stored `Backtrace` member by value. It does not modify any state and has no side‑effects, making it safe to call from any context.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadC.body: The function simply returns the value of the `HadContextSensitiveCondition` flag stored in the object. Because it’s marked `const`, it guarantees that calling this accessor will not alter any internal state.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadH.body: Returns the flag indicating whether the head‑sensitive condition is set.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetHadL.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetInpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetInpu.body: Retrieves a read‑only reference to the internal member variable `Input`. Because the method is marked `const`, callers cannot modify the object through the returned reference. The function merely returns the stored string; it performs no side‑effects or allocations.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetMaxL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetMaxL.body: Finds the entry in the `MaxLanguageStandard` map for the supplied target; if a match exists, assigns that map‑value to the supplied `mapping` reference.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSeen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSeen.body: The `GetSeenTargetProperties()` function simply returns a const reference to the internal `SeenTargetProperties` set, letting callers read the current set of property names that have been seen without permitting modification. It’s a straightforward accessor that preserves immutability of the underlying collection.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetSour.body: Returns the set of source‑sensitive targets that belong to the current instance.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::GetTarg.body: This member simply hands back a constant reference to the internal `DependTargets` container, letting callers read the current target set without permitting direct modification of the set itself. Since the returned reference points to the same underlying `std::set`, any changes to the pointed‑to objects (e.g. mutating a `cmGeneratorTarget` instance) will still affect the internal state, so callers must respect ownership semantics. The function guarantees read‑only access but does not perform defensive copying, so no defensive copy or deep‑clone is performed.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetEval.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetEval.body: Sets the internal flag that determines whether evaluation logic should run during the build‑system phase—assigning the incoming boolean to the class’s `EvaluateForBuildsystem` member.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetQuie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::SetQuie.body: The method simply assigns the supplied boolean value to the instance’s `Quiet` member, toggling the object’s quiet mode on or off.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.body: The constructor parses the supplied expression string, tokenizes it using the internal lexer, stores whether the expression requires evaluation, and if evaluation is needed, runs the parser to populate the internal evaluators from the token list. It also optionally creates a profiling entry when the CMAKE_BOOTSTRAP flag is not defined.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::cmCompi.body: The constructor `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression(cmCompiledGeneratorExpression const&) = delete;` forbids copying any instance of `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression`. This guarantees that objects are managed exclusively and that accidental implicit copy‑semantics cannot occur.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::operato.body: The `operator=` overload assigns a given `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression` to the current instance—typically updating the internal expression state—and then returns a reference to `*this` so that calls can be chained.

@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::~cmComp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCompiledGeneratorExpression::~cmComp.body: The destructor `~cmCompiledGeneratorExpression()` cleanly deallocates internal resources and finalizes any runtime state associated with a compiled generator expression. It guarantees no lingering handles or dangling pointers persist once an instance is destroyed, ensuring the expression’s lifecycle ends safely.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Compute@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Compute@k_ZN2.body: Runs Tarjan’s algorithm to discover strongly‑connected components, then rebuilds the internal component‑graph to match the newly‑found component count, and finally invokes TransferEdges() to wire the edges into that graph.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponentG.body: This accessor simply returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored graph object, allowing callers to inspect the component graph without mutating it.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponentM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponentM.body: The function provides read‑only access to the internal list of component identifiers. By returning a const reference, it avoids copying the vector and guarantees that callers cannot modify the underlying data. Because the function is itself marked const, it can be safely invoked on const instances of the owning class. The implementation is essentially a single‑line getter that preserves encapsulation while offering efficient read‑only access.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponents.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::GetComponents.body: The `GetComponents` member simply returns the internal `Components` container by reference, letting callers read the stored list of `NodeList` objects without copying the entire vector.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Tarjan@k_ZN23.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::Tarjan@k_ZN23.body: The function initializes the Tarjan‑DFS machinery and then iterates over every vertex of the input graph. For each vertex that has not yet been marked, it triggers a recursive visit routine (TarjanVisit) that performs a depth‑first search, pushes nodes onto a stack, and records low‑link values so that when backtracking detects a root of a strongly connected component it can be extracted and stored in TarjanComponents. The routine works by resetting the per‑run state (TarjanWalkId, TarjanIndex, TarjanStack) before each new start so that the component identification logic is self‑contained across iterations.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TarjanEntry::.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TarjanEntry::.body: The destructor for `TarjanEntry` releases any internal bookkeeping (e.g., clears adjacency lists, resets counters) and ensures the instance is left in a clean state before being de‑allocated.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TarjanVisit@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TarjanVisit@k.body:
The function performs a depth‑first traversal of a node within the input graph, marking the node with the current walk identifier, recording its entry time, and adding it to a stack.  
While recursing on each outgoing edge it skips neighbours that have already been reached by a previous walk (they belong to a different component).  
During backtracking it updates the candidate root of the current node when a neighbour’s root has an earlier visit index.  
When the node’s root points back at itself, a new component is completed: the stack is unwound until that node, all popped nodes are assigned to the newly‑found component, and the component’s node list is sorted.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TransferEdges.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::TransferEdges.body: Iterates over every vertex in the original graph. For each outgoing edge, the routine checks whether the adjacent vertex lies in a different Tarjan component. If so, it records that inter‑component link in the component‑level graph, preserving the edge’s strong/weak status and back‑trace information.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::cmComputeComp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::cmComputeComp.body: `cmComputeComponentGraph` is a constructor that merely stores the supplied graph in an internal member (`InputGraph`). It accepts a constant reference, ensuring no accidental modifications to the original graph, and leaves the rest of the class uninitialized until further setup is performed.

@lcmComputeComponentGraph::~cmComputeCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeComponentGraph::~cmComputeCom.body: When invoked, `~cmComputeComponentGraph` cleans up the internal state of a `cmComputeComponentGraph` instance. It frees any allocated resources, finalizes internal structures, and ensures that the object is left in a clean state ready for destruction.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.body: The function takes a target that depends on another target (dependee). It looks up the link‑interface of that dependent target for the current build configuration, then for each library in that interface it registers a new dependency on the target that is doing the build. The library is added only once (the set tracks duplicates). When a library is added it also records the back‑trace of where that link came from, so that information can be emitted later. The function then recurses on any nested interfaces that those libraries themselves bring in, adding their objects and libraries in turn. The result is a target that has all the transitive link, object and source file dependencies wired in.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddInterfaceDe.body: The routine records an interface dependency between a “depender” and a dependent target. It first resolves both targets from the internal list, then checks whether the dependent target is a self‑exported executable; if it is, it drops the link. If the target is still valid, it inserts two `cmLinkItem`s into the supplied set – one marking the dependency as a “real” link and the other as a “virtual” link (the boolean flag distinguishes the kind). Finally it recurses on the same routine for the child back‑trace, passing the current back‑trace, the user configuration string, and the emitted set, thereby propagating the dependency chain until no further links remain.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddObjectDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddObjectDepen.body: The routine registers an object‑library dependency for a target: it obtains the library name from the source file, resolves the corresponding link item, and inserts the item into the dependency set if it hasn't been recorded yet. Afterward it validates that the target’s type is one of the allowed executable or library kinds; otherwise it emits a fatal error and aborts.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.body: The routine registers a new dependency edge in the internal dependency graph. It first checks whether the *dependee* belongs to the build system; if not, it walks the dependee’s utility items, recursively adding those as dependencies. When the dependee is part of the system, it looks up its index in the map, asserts the lookup succeeded, and finally inserts a back‑edge into the graph data structure.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::AddTargetDepen.body: The routine locates the dependent target from the instance’s target list, verifies that the dependency is valid (issuing a fatal error if it isn’t found), and if the dependent target is a non‑exporting executable it is ignored. When the checks pass it forwards the information to the internal helper that actually registers the dependency.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CheckComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CheckComponent.body: The function scans each non‑trivial component of the graph. For each component it first confirms that no cycles are permitted; if that flag is set it immediately reports a problem. It then verifies that every node in the component targets a static library; any deviation triggers a complaint and causes the function to return false. If all components satisfy these conditions, the routine returns true.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectDepends.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectDepends.body: The `CollectDepends` routine first initializes the adjacency list for every target by resizing an internal graph to match the target count, then iteratively invokes `CollectTargetDepends` for each target index to populate that target’s outgoing dependency list. This builds the internal dependency graph used for later resolution or scheduling.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.body: It clears the SideEffects list, resizes it to the size of InitialGraph, and for each node index invokes CollectSideEffectsForTarget with a set of already‑visited nodes to gather side‑effect information.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectSideEff.body: The routine performs a depth‑first traversal of a dependency graph. It marks each node as visited, then appends the node’s own custom and language side‑effects to its target’s effect lists. After that, it recursively processes each outgoing edge, merging the successor nodes’ side‑effects into the current node’s collections so that when the recursion unwinds every target’s side‑effects set contains the full closure of effects reachable from that node.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargetD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargetD.body: The routine walks through every build‑configuration of the current target and records every library, object file, and utility that the target requires. It skips self‑references, deduplicates items, and uses `AddTargetDepend`, `AddInterfaceDepends`, and `AddObjectDepends` to register each dependency in the target’s dependency graph.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargets.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::CollectTargets.body: Collects every target from each local generator, assigns it an index in the internal list, and appends it to the target collection vector.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComplainAboutB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComplainAboutB.body: The routine walks the graph of a cycle component, collects the names of every target in that component together with the intra‑component dependencies that caused the cycle, and appends explanatory text about why a strong dependency cycle cannot be broken (e.g. global flags or missing static‑library constraints). When finished it calls `cmSystemTools::Error` to surface the message.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::Compute@k_ZN22.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::Compute@k_ZN22.body:
The function orchestrates a multi‑stage graph‑building routine:  
1. It gathers targets and their dependencies, then optionally dumps the resulting initial graph.  
2. It constructs a component graph from that graph; if any component fails verification the routine aborts immediately.  
3. It collects side‑effects, builds an intermediate graph, and again verifies the resulting components.  
4. Finally it resolves the final dependency graph, optionally prints it, and returns success only when all verification steps succeed.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeFinalDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeFinalDe.body: The routine builds the final dependency graph: it linearizes intra‑component edges, records each component’s head, and then rewires inter‑component edges so that component tails point to the heads of the components they depend on, returning success unless a cycle is detected.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeInterme.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::ComputeInterme.body: The function clears and resizes an intermediate graph to match the size of the initial graph. It then iterates over each vertex, retrieves the corresponding target, and if that target is not a static or object library it simply copies the initial edge list into the intermediate list. If the target is one of those types, it checks for an “OPTIMIZE_DEPENDENCIES” property; when that flag is on it calls OptimizeLinkDependencies to potentially trim the edge list, otherwise it keeps the original edges. This prepares the intermediate graph for subsequent processing.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayCompone.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayCompone.body: The function prints a list of all strongly connected components in the given graph. It iterates over each component, outputting its index and the names of the targets that belong to it.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayGraph@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplayGraph@k.body: The `DisplayGraph` method outputs a human‑readable layout of the dependency graph to `stderr`. It iterates over each target, prints the target’s name and then lists every outgoing edge, indicating for each dependent target whether the dependency is strong or weak.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplaySideEff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::DisplaySideEff.body: It iterates over the stored side‑effects for each target, outputting the target name followed by any custom command or language‑specific side‑effects that influence that target.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::GetTargetDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::GetTargetDirec.body: The routine looks up the target’s index, retrieves the corresponding adjacency list from the final graph, and for each edge it inserts the dependent target into the supplied set while copying the edge’s type, cross‑flag, and back‑trace information.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::IntraComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::IntraComponent.body: The function walks a graph of edges belonging to a single component, using a depth‑first traversal. It first blocks re‑visiting nodes (the `visited` guard prevents infinite loops). When a node is first reached, it records a strong intra‑component edge in `FinalGraph`, recursing on all incident edges that belong to the same component (`cmap[j] == c` and are “strong”). After all descendants are processed, the current node is appended to a linked list of intra‑component edges: if a predecessor already exists it is added; otherwise that node becomes the tail of the component. The function returns `true` only when all recursion paths succeed, otherwise `false` is returned to signal a cycle or inconsistency.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::OptimizeLinkDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::OptimizeLinkDe.body: The routine walks through the supplied edge list, emitting every edge that is marked strong unchanged, and for the remaining edges it expands the dependency graph by pulling in any targets that have recorded “side‑effect” records—both custom‑command side‑effects and any language‑specific side‑effects that the caller cares about. For each such target it inserts a corresponding graph edge (once per target) into the output list, ensuring that a target is only added a single time even if referenced by multiple input edges.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::cmComputeTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::cmComputeTarge.body: The constructor stores the passed `cmGlobalGenerator` instance, retrieves the CMake instance, and pulls two global properties—`GLOBAL_DEPENDS_DEBUG_MODE` and `GLOBAL_DEPENDS_NO_CYCLES`—into the `DebugMode` and `NoCycles` members for later use.

@lcmComputeTargetDepends::~cmComputeTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmComputeTargetDepends::~cmComputeTarg.body: The destructor of `cmComputeTargetDepends` performs the standard clean‑up steps for the class: it releases any owned resources, clears the internal structures that track target dependencies, and resets any state flags so that the object ends in a clean state. Because it is declared `= default`, no custom cleanup logic is present beyond what the compiler supplies.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::IsTrue@k_ZN20cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::IsTrue@k_ZN20cmC.body: The function consumes a list of expanded command arguments and, through a fixed sequence of handler routines (each handling a specific precedence level), it repeatedly collapses the argument list until only a single Boolean remains or an error is detected. If any handler fails it emits an error message and returns false; otherwise it returns the Boolean value of the sole remaining argument.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::cmConditionEvalu.body: The constructor stores a reference to the supplied `cmMakefile` and a moved‑copy of the provided `cmListFileBacktrace`, and pulls the current status of policy CMP‑0139 from the makefile for later checks.

@lcmConditionEvaluator::~cmConditionEval.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConditionEvaluator::~cmConditionEval.body: The `~cmConditionEvaluator` function takes a condition string and a context map, parses the condition into an abstract syntax tree, then evaluates the tree against the supplied context to return a boolean result. It supports logical operators (`&&`, `||`), comparison operators (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`), and nested parentheses, handling missing keys by treating them as false.

@lcmConfigureLog::BeginEvent@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::BeginEvent@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The function prepares a log entry by first ensuring the logger is initialized, then writes a separator line, increases indentation, records the event kind, and finally appends the back‑trace and verification checks associated with the supplied `cmMakefile` object.

@lcmConfigureLog::BeginLine@k_ZN14cmConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::BeginLine@k_ZN14cmConf.body: The function writes a number of two‑space pairs equal to the current indentation level into the stream and returns that stream reference.

@lcmConfigureLog::BeginObject@k_ZN14cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::BeginObject@k_ZN14cmCo.body: The function writes the supplied key followed by “:”, ends the current line, and then increments the internal indentation counter.

@lcmConfigureLog::EndEvent@k_ZN14cmConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EndEvent@k_ZN14cmConfi.body: The method simply decrements the `Indent` counter (after asserting it is non‑zero) and thus signals the end of the current nested logging level.

@lcmConfigureLog::EndLine@k_ZN14cmConfig.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EndLine@k_ZN14cmConfig.body: When invoked, `EndLine` simply inserts a newline into the internal output stream—effectively terminating the current log entry and flushing any pending output to the stream.

@lcmConfigureLog::EndObject@k_ZN14cmConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EndObject@k_ZN14cmConf.body: The routine simply decrements the current indentation level after ensuring it’s non‑zero.

@lcmConfigureLog::EnsureInit@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::EnsureInit@k_ZN14cmCon.body: Ensures that the internal log stream is opened once: if already opened it returns immediately. When opening, it constructs the full file path, opens the file in append mode, sets the opened flag, writes a separator line, and then starts a new event‑object section.

@lcmConfigureLog::IsAnyLogVersionEnabled.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::IsAnyLogVersionEnabled.body: The method scans two sorted vectors of version IDs in tandem and returns true as soon as a common element is found; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteBacktrace@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteBacktrace@k_ZN14c.body: Collects back‑trace entries from a `cmMakefile` instance, normalises each file path to be relative to the project root (skipping any entries whose name is empty or the special “deferred” line), and stores the resulting strings in a vector. Finally, the vector is passed to `WriteValue` to record the back‑trace data.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteChecks@k_ZN14cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteChecks@k_ZN14cmCo.body: The function checks whether any check‑in‑progress messages exist for the given `cmMakefile`. If none, it returns immediately. Otherwise it opens a “checks” section, iterates over the messages in reverse order, writes each one prefixed with a dash via the `Encoder`, and finally closes the section.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteEscape@k_ZN14cmCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteEscape@k_ZN14cmCo.body: The `WriteEscape` method serializes a single byte into its hexadecimal escape form (`"\xHH"`) and streams it to the configured output. It formats the byte into a temporary buffer using `snprintf`, then, if the conversion succeeds, writes that buffer to the underlying stream. The routine assumes the buffer length of six characters suffices for any single‑byte escape and relies on the stream’s `write` method to consume that data safely.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteLiteralTextBlock@.body: Writes the key and its value in a literal‑style block: it prints the key, starts a new line, indents the value, then scans the value string. For each character it emits either the raw byte (for printable ASCII) or an escape sequence (for tabs, newlines, backslashes, and any non‑printable bytes, including multi‑byte UTF‑8 characters). It ends the line after the block and restores the previous indentation level.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: When invoked, the function appends the supplied key followed by “: null” to the internal output buffer and finalises the line by calling `EndLine()`.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The `WriteValue` method writes a key‑value pair to the logger: it starts a new line, outputs the key followed by a colon and space, encodes the value into the internal stream using the encoder, and then finalizes the line.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body:
The function iterates over a supplied map and writes its entries to an output stream.  
If a key consists solely of letters, digits, hyphen or underscore (matching `rawKeyChars`), the key‑value pair is written directly via `WriteValue`.  
Otherwise, it writes the key and value in a quoted form: first the key is escaped with the encoder, then a colon and space, and finally the escaped value.  
The routine wraps the whole sequence in a JSON‑style object, beginning with `BeginObject(key)` and ending with `EndObject()`.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The method starts an object with the supplied key, iterates over the vector, writes each string prefixed by a dash into the stream via the encoder, and then finalises the object.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: The function writes a key/value pair to the log. It takes a string_view key and a bool value, converts the bool to the literal strings “true” or “false”, and appends them to the log line by calling BeginLine and EndLine.

@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::WriteValue@k_ZN14cmCon.body: Writes a key and integer value to the log buffer by formatting them as a single line.

@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14c.body: This constructor initializes the configuration object by moving in a directory string and a list of log‑file versions. It guarantees that the special version number 1 is present in the list—adding it if necessary—then creates a new JSON stream writer via `Json::StreamWriterBuilder` and assigns that writer to the internal encoder.

@lcmConfigureLog::~cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConfigureLog::~cmConfigureLog@k_ZN14.body: When an instance of `cmConfigureLog` is destroyed, the destructor checks whether the object was opened. If so, it performs cleanup by calling `EndObject()` and emits a trailing ellipsis to indicate the end of its logging session.

@lcmConstStack::Empty@k_ZNK12cmConstStac.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Empty@k_ZNK12cmConstStac.body: The `Empty()` member function reports whether the container contains any elements. In practice it simply tests whether the underlying size/count is zero and returns true when there are none, false otherwise.

@lcmConstStack::Pop@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Pop@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.body: The `Pop()` method removes and returns the top entry of a stack. As a `const` member, it returns a copy of that entry without altering the internal state of the stack. In the code base it’s invoked to peel successive back‑trace frames: each call to `Pop()` yields the current frame and discards it, allowing the calling code to walk back through a recorded trace.

@lcmConstStack::Push@k_ZNK12cmConstStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Push@k_ZNK12cmConstStack.body: The `Push` member inserts a value onto the current stack and returns a new `Stack` instance containing that value at the top. The method does not modify the original stack; instead it creates a fresh stack (or a copy) that has the supplied value added on top‑of‑stack, which callers can then use for further back‑trace operations.

@lcmConstStack::Top@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::Top@k_ZNK12cmConstStack3.body: The `Top()` member simply returns a const reference to the current top element of the underlying container. It lets callers inspect (but not modify) the most recent item without altering the stack’s state.

@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.body: `cmConstStack` provides a lightweight, read‑only stack abstraction that is constructed from a collection of elements. It encapsulates the underlying storage and exposes a constant‑time interface for accessing the stored items, enabling callers to work with a stack‑like container without mutating the underlying data.

@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.body: cmConstStack initializes a read‑only stack instance by forwarding its arguments to the underlying base constructor, then exposing a const‑access wrapper for stack operations.

@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.body: The protected member simply exposes a read‑only view of the internal constant stack; it returns a const reference to the internal container so callers cannot modify it while still allowing code paths that need the underlying data to access it safely.

@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmConstStack::cmConstStack@k_ZN12cmCon.body: The protected `cmConstStack` function supplies constant access to a stack structure, typically employed via the `using cmConstStack::cmConstStack;` statement. It is referenced in `cmFindPackageStack.h` (around line 28) to provide read‑only stack operations.

@lcmCreateTestSourceList@k_Z22cmCreateTe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCreateTestSourceList@k_Z22cmCreateTe.body:
cmCreateTestSourceList parses a vector of argument strings to generate a test‑driver source list.  
It extracts optional EXTRA_INCLUDE and FUNCTION arguments, treats the remaining items as test source files, sanitizes each filename into a unique C‑compatible function name, and creates forward declarations and a function‑map string.  
The function registers these pieces in the makefile object, writes the test‑driver source file from a template, and finally populates a source‑list definition in the makefile before returning the success status.

@lcmCryptoHash::HashFile@k_ZN12cmCryptoH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::HashFile@k_ZN12cmCryptoH.body: Computes the binary hash of a given file path by delegating to ByteHashFile and then turning the resulting byte array into a string representation before returning it.

@lcmCryptoHash::HashString@k_ZN12cmCrypt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::HashString@k_ZN12cmCrypt.body: Hashes a string input into a hexadecimal string representation.

@lcmCryptoHash::cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCry.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCry.body: The constructor maps the chosen algorithm to its internal identifier, then immediately invokes the underlying hash‑initialisation routine to set up the internal context object that will drive the hashing operation.

@lcmCryptoHash::~cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCryptoHash::~cmCryptoHash@k_ZN12cmCr.body: This destructor releases the cryptographic hash context by calling `rhash_free` on the internal `CTX` pointer, ensuring any allocated resources are cleaned up before the object is destroyed.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::GetValueAsBool@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::GetValueAsBool@k_Z.body: It returns true when the widget’s `Value` field equals the string “ON”; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN18.body: When a user presses Enter or Space while the widget is focused, the method flips the widget’s internal boolean value (true ↔ false), updates the widget’s visual state via `touchwin`/`wrefresh`, and signals that the input was handled by returning true; any other key press falls through and returns false.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::SetValueAsBool@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::SetValueAsBool@k_Z.body: Sets the widget’s display to match the supplied Boolean. When `value` is true it writes “ON” and, if color support is present, applies the `BoolOn` color pair to both foreground and background of the field. When `value` is false it writes “OFF” and, if colors are available, applies the `BoolOff` pair instead. If color support is absent, only the text changes.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.body: The declaration marks the copy‑constructor of `cmCursesBoolWidget` as deleted, so any attempt to copy an instance of the widget will be rejected by the compiler.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::cmCursesBoolWidget.body: The constructor initializes a boolean‑style widget: it assigns the `BOOL` type, applies default foreground/background if the terminal lacks color support, disables the static flag on its field, and sets the initial value to `false`.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents copying or assigning a `cmCursesBoolWidget` instance. It guarantees that objects of this type cannot be copied or reassigned, enforcing immutability of the widget’s internal state.

@lcmCursesBoolWidget::~cmCursesBoolWidge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesBoolWidget::~cmCursesBoolWidge.body: The virtual destructor of `cmCursesBoolWidget` cleans up all resources owned by the widget—destroying any internal UI components, unregistering event handlers, and releasing any dynamically allocated memory before the object is discarded.

@lcmCursesColor::HasColors@k_ZN13cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesColor::HasColors@k_ZN13cmCurse.body: When the program compiles with `HAVE_CURSES_USE_DEFAULT_COLORS` defined, the method simply forwards the result of `has_colors()` to the caller; if that macro is not defined, it always returns `false`. The function therefore reports whether the curses library was built with support for colors or not.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.body:
The constructor signature  

```cpp
cmCursesFilePathWidget(cmCursesFilePathWidget const&) = delete;
```  

declares a deleted copy constructor for the `cmCursesFilePathWidget` type, so any attempt to copy an instance of this widget will be rejected at compile‑time.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::cmCursesFilePa.body: This constructor forwards the requested size and coordinates to its base class and then marks the widget’s type field as `cmStateEnums::FILEPATH`.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::operator=@k_ZN.body: The copy‑assignment operator is explicitly deleted, so any attempt to assign one `cmCursesFilePathWidget` instance to another will be a compile‑time error.

@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::~cmCursesFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesFilePathWidget::~cmCursesFileP.body: The destructor `~cmCursesFilePathWidget()` is responsible for cleaning up any state held by a `cmCursesFilePathWidget`. When an instance goes out of scope or is explicitly deleted, this function will be invoked. It performs the necessary teardown of resources allocated by the widget (for example dynamic buffers, handles to terminal widgets, or observers) and ensures that its base class `cmCursesPathWidget` is properly destructed as well. It guarantees that no lingering handles or memory leaks remain after the widget is destroyed.

@lcmCursesForm::GetForm@k_ZN12cmCursesFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::GetForm@k_ZN12cmCursesFo.body: It returns the stored pointer in the object—i.e., the value of its internal `Form` member.

@lcmCursesForm::LogMessage@k_ZN12cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesForm::LogMessage@k_ZN12cmCurse.body: The function writes the supplied string to a global debug stream only when a global debug flag is true; if the flag is false it exits without action.

@lcmCursesMainForm::PrintKeys@k_ZN16cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesMainForm::PrintKeys@k_ZN16cmCu.body: The PrintKeys routine writes a help‑text line of shortcuts to the screen. It first checks that the terminal’s size is sufficient; if the current widget can render its own key hints it hands off to that widget. Otherwise it prints a fixed set of key‑bindings such as “Show log output”, “Configure”, “Generate”, “Toggle advanced mode”, “Help”, “Quit”, plus a page counter if paging is active. The routine ends by positioning the form cursor back to the form’s current location.

@lcmCursesPathWidget::~cmCursesPathWidge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesPathWidget::~cmCursesPathWidge.body: ~cmCursesPathWidget implements a widget that presents filesystem paths in a curses‑based UI. It extends cmCursesStringWidget to provide editable path strings, handles key navigation (e.g., arrow keys for directory traversal), supports history and auto‑completion, and emits signals when the current path changes for integration with other parts of the application.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetString@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetString@k_ZN20.body: It returns a pointer to the underlying string value stored in the widget by delegating to its `GetValue()` method.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetValue@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::GetValue@k_ZN20c.body: The `GetValue` method simply returns the widget’s internal string buffer. It calls the helper `field_buffer` with the widget’s `Field` member and an offset of `0`, yielding a `const char*` that points to the current content.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN.body: Handles keyboard events for a string field in a curses‑based UI: it first checks whether the widget is in edit mode and whether the pressed key should toggle that mode (Enter, 'i', Escape, Tab, arrow keys, etc.). It then invokes the appropriate form_driver operations to move the cursor, delete characters, or jump fields, refreshes the window, and returns true if the key was handled or false otherwise.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnReturn@k_ZN20c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnReturn@k_ZN20c.body: When the widget is in edit mode the routine clears its stored string, switches off the edit flag, and tells the form to refresh its field buffers; otherwise it turns on edit mode, records the current field content, and notifies the form that a key has been printed.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnTab@k_ZN20cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnTab@k_ZN20cmCu.body: The function is the widget’s hook for the Tab key. It receives a form and a curses window but ignores them; in practice it would trigger any code that should run when the widget is active and the user presses Tab (e.g., moving focus or sending a form‑level command).

@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnType@k_ZN20cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::OnType@k_ZN20cmC.body: The `OnType` method simply forwards the key code it receives to the underlying form driver for the form contained in the `cmCursesMainForm` instance. It ignores the `WINDOW*` parameter and relies on `form_driver(fm->GetForm(), key)` to dispatch the input to the form’s input handler.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN20.body: The `PrintKeys` method verifies that the terminal window is wide enough to display its interface; if the widget is in edit mode it clears the bottom of the screen and prints a short instruction line that tells the user to press **Enter** to confirm or **Esc** to cancel, and then returns `true`. If the widget is not in edit mode it simply returns `false`.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::SetString@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::SetString@k_ZN20.body: The method simply forwards the supplied string to the underlying `SetValue` routine, thereby updating the widget’s internal value with the new text.

@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesStringWidget::cmCursesStringWi.body: Initialises a string‑widget with the supplied geometry, marks it as non‑editable, sets its type to STRING, and applies a colour scheme—using the colour pair if the terminal supports colours, otherwise falling back to normal/standout. The field is finally marked non‑static.

@lcmCursesWidget::GetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::GetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.body: It returns a pointer to the internal string that holds the widget’s value. The pointer points to a read‑only const character array (the string’s data).

@lcmCursesWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN14cmCu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::HandleInput@k_ZN14cmCu.body: The `HandleInput` function is a pure virtual interface that widgets implement to process a key press or other input event. It receives the event key, the form that owns the widget, and a pointer to the curses window that the widget draws into, and returns `true` if the widget consumed the event (preventing further propagation) or `false` if the event should be passed on. This method is invoked by the form’s input dispatch loop (e.g., in `cmCursesMainForm::HandleInput`), where the current focused widget receives the key event and may react accordingly.

@lcmCursesWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN14cmCurs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::PrintKeys@k_ZN14cmCurs.body: The function `PrintKeys` is a virtual member that simply returns `false`. It performs no other computation or side‑effects.

@lcmCursesWidget::SetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::SetValue@k_ZN14cmCurse.body: The method assigns the supplied string to the widget’s internal Value member and then pushes that data into the associated field buffer via `set_field_buffer`, casting the string’s contents to a mutable `char*` pointer.

@lcmCursesWidget::cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor creates a ncurses field with the supplied geometry, stores a pointer to the widget instance in the field’s user‑pointer, turns off the auto‑skip option for that field, and initializes the internal page counter to zero.

@lcmCursesWidget::~cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCursesWidget::~cmCursesWidget@k_ZN14.body: The destructor checks whether the `Field` pointer is non‑null, releases the associated memory with `free_field`, and then clears the pointer to prevent dangling references.

@lcmCustomCommand::GetCodegen@k_ZNK15cmC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommand::GetCodegen@k_ZNK15cmC.body: This const member simply returns the current value of the `Codegen` flag, exposing whether code generation is enabled.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCC@k_ZNK2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetCC@k_ZNK2.body: The function `GetCC()` returns a constant reference to the `cmCustomCommand` object stored in `this->CC`. It simply dereferences `CC` and returns the referenced command without modifying it.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetDepends@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetDepends@k.body: It returns a const reference to the internal `Depends` vector, exposing the collection of dependency strings held by the instance without copying or modifying the data.

@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetUtilities.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmCustomCommandGenerator::GetUtilities.body: Returns a constant reference to the internal set that holds the utilities (a collection of BT pairs keyed by string).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: Sets the internal line counter to the supplied 64‑bit value.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: The function simply returns the value stored in the `Id` member, guaranteeing no exceptions will be thrown.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: Returns the current validity flag held by the object.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: It returns the stored line number, guaranteeing no exceptions and preserving constness.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: The method simply flips an internal validity flag: calling it clears the current “valid” status, marking the instance as invalid. It runs without throwing exceptions (marked noexcept).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: Creates a source‑breakpoint instance by initializing its internal state from an existing breakpoint instance via a move‑like operation, efficiently transferring ownership of the underlying data.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: The function `cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint(const cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint &unnamed)` is a copy‑constructor that initializes a new `cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint` object from an existing instance. It is invoked in several places of the codebase—for example, whenever the debugger’s breakpoint needs to be replicated or passed to a function that requires a fresh copy.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerSourceBreakpoint.body: The constructor stores the supplied breakpoint identifier and source line number in the object’s members, preparing the breakpoint instance for later matching against the current execution point during a debugging session.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerStackFrame::GetL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerStackFrame::GetL.body: Returns the current source‑code line number associated with the current stack frame. The function is `const noexcept`, so it does not modify any state and guarantees no exception is thrown. It returns the value of the `Line()` member of the `Function` object stored in the frame.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerStackFrame::GetM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerStackFrame::GetM.body:
The method simply returns the stored pointer to the `Makefile` object.  
It is marked `const` and `noexcept`, indicating it doesn't modify the object and guarantees no exceptions on normal execution.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::AddSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::AddSu.body: This method appends a non‑null `cmDebuggerVariables` instance to the internal `SubVariables` collection, ensuring that only valid pointers are stored.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetEn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetEn.body: This method assigns the supplied boolean to the `EnableSorting` member.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetIg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetIg.body: This method assigns the supplied flag to the internal `IgnoreEmptyStringEntries` member, which determines whether empty‑string entries are skipped during subsequent operations.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariables::SetVa.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda builds a `std::vector<cmDebuggerVariableEntry>` by iterating over a `list` of items, appending each entry with a key formatted as `"[<index>]"` and the item’s `Value`, and finally returns the filled vector.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda captures a target object and returns a vector of key/value pairs describing its deployment characteristics—install path, platform flags (AIX, Android, Apple frameworks, DLLs), export status, import visibility, configuration scope, name, runtime path, and target type.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The lambda creates a vector of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry` objects by iterating over a collection named `values`. @lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The function builds a `cmDebuggerVariables` object populated with key‑value pairs exposed by a `cmGlobalGenerator`. It pulls standard target names and flags from the generator, packs them into a vector of `cmDebuggerVariableEntry`, and attaches them to the newly‑created variable set. If the generator has an “InstallComponents” list, the function recursively creates a sub‑variable set for those components and appends it under the “InstallComponents” key. Finally, it configures the variable set to ignore empty strings and tags the variable set with the generator’s name before returning the shared pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a new cmDebuggerVariables object populated with the test’s name, style and expansion lists, then attaches sub‑variables for the test’s command and properties. If the supplied test is null, it simply returns a null pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a cmDebuggerVariables instance that contains the file‑set’s name, type, and visibility string. It also recursively attaches sub‑variables for any sub‑directories or sub‑files. If the supplied fileSet pointer is null, the function simply returns an empty shared pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a shared pointer to a top‑level cmDebuggerVariables instance that holds sub‑variables for each non‑empty entry; if the entry list is empty the function simply returns a null pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a new `cmDebuggerVariables` object only when the caller supplied values, fills its internal vector with entries named by indexed keys (`[0]`, `[1]`, …), assigns a string containing the count of entries to the value field, turns off sorting, and returns the shared pointer (or `nullptr` if the set was empty).

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: The function checks whether the supplied list is empty; if so it returns an empty pointer. Otherwise it constructs a new `cmDebuggerVariables` instance, populating its internal list of entries by iterating over the supplied items and tagging each entry with an index in brackets. It then stores the total count as the variable’s value, turns off automatic sorting, and returns the populated shared pointer.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a shared‑pointer to a new cmDebuggerVariables instance when the supplied list of tests is non‑empty. It first verifies that the vector is not empty; if it is, the function returns an empty shared pointer. It then constructs a new cmDebuggerVariables object with the given name and type flag, and iterates over each test in the vector, recursively calling CreateIfAny on each test’s name and sub‑test list to build a tree of sub‑variables. After adding all children, it stores the count of tests as the variable’s value (using `std::to_string(tests.size())`) and returns the constructed object.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.body: Creates a composite debugger variable object that aggregates target‑specific data by iterating over the supplied targets and adding each target’s attributes (paths, flags, and resource lists) as sub‑variables.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview

Otherwise it constructs a new variable instance using `make_shared`, then iterates over each file set, recursively calling `CreateIfAny` for that file set’s name and adding the resulting sub‑variables via `AddSubVariables`. The final pointer is returned.

@lcmDebugger::cmDebuggerVariablesHelper:.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDefinitions::GetInternal@k_ZN13cmDef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDefinitions::GetInternal@k_ZN13cmDef.body: Recursively walks the definition stack, returning the first matching definition it encounters. If none is found and `raise` is true, the function inserts the resolved definition into the current frame before returning it.

@lcmDefinitions::HasKey@k_ZN13cmDefiniti.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDefinitions::HasKey@k_ZN13cmDefiniti.body: The function iterates through a range of stack iterators—from `begin` to `end`—checking each element’s map for the supplied key. If the key is found in any of those maps, it returns `true`; otherwise, after exhausting the range, it returns `false`.

@lcmDefinitions::MakeClosure@k_ZN13cmDef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDefinitions::MakeClosure@k_ZN13cmDef.body: MakeClosure walks a range of stack frames, building a new `cmDefinitions` that contains only those symbols that are actually defined in the examined frames. It keeps a set of names that were seen but not defined (`undefined`), and skips any key that is already present in the resulting map. The algorithm stops when it encounters a key that has already been filled in `closure.Map`; otherwise it inserts the entry if `mi.second.Value` is true, otherwise notes it as undefined. The result is a compact closure that contains every entry from the stack that is defined and not overwritten by a later definition.

@lcmDefinitions::Raise@k_ZN13cmDefinitio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDefinitions::Raise@k_ZN13cmDefinitio.body: The `Raise` function simply forwards its arguments to the internal helper `GetInternal`, passing along the supplied key and stack range. It invokes `GetInternal` with the final boolean argument set to `true`, which signals that the caller expects the operation to *raise* (or trigger) the requested action – effectively “raising” a definition or similar event.

@lcmDefinitions::Set@k_ZN13cmDefinitions.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDefinitions::Unset@k_ZN13cmDefinitio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDefinitions::Unset@k_ZN13cmDefinitio.body: The `Unset` method assigns a new default‑constructed value (`Def()`) to the map entry keyed by `key`. If the key doesn’t already exist in `Map`, the subscript operator inserts a new entry; otherwise it simply overwrites the existing value with a default‑constructed one. This effectively resets the stored value for that key to the default state.

@lcmDepends::cmDepends@k_ZN9cmDependsC1E.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDepends::~cmDepends@k_ZN9cmDependsD1.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDependsFortran::ConsiderModule@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDependsFortran::CopyModule@k_ZN16cmD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::CopyModule@k_ZN16cmD.body: Copies the requested Fortran module file to the destination stamp file, adding a “.mod” suffix when needed and looking up both upper‑case and lower‑case paths before copying; it returns true only when the copy succeeds and false otherwise.

@lcmDependsFortran::Finalize@k_ZN16cmDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::Finalize@k_ZN16cmDep.body:
The `Finalize` routine orchestrates the end‑of‑build bookkeeping for a Fortran target.  
- It scans the module registry (`LocateModules`).  
- It collects the directories where stamps and module files live (`stamp_dir`, `mod_dir`).  
- It checks for the legacy‑spelling of the intrinsic‑module flag and uses the current flag if present.  
- For every object in `Internal->ObjectInfo` it emits a dependency record to the two output streams, passing along whether intrinsic modules are being built.  
- It then records the list of modules that the target provides into a small “fortran.internal” file, and finally writes a tiny cleanup script that will delete the generated modules and their stamp files.  
- If any step fails it propagates `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmDependsFortran::FindModule@k_ZN16cmD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::FindModule@k_ZN16cmD.body: The routine builds both the upper‑case and lower‑case variants of the requested module name, then iterates over each directory in the instance’s include path, trying to locate a file matching either variant. If a match is found, the full path is returned via the reference parameter and the function reports success; otherwise it signals failure.

@lcmDependsFortran::LocateModules@k_ZN16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::LocateModules@k_ZN16.body: LocateModules() iterates over the internal map of object information, clearing and inserting entries into the internal dependency tables. It then reconciles these entries against local and remote module definitions, loading supplemental module data from the makefile as necessary. The routine returns true only when every required module is successfully matched; otherwise it reports an error and returns false.

@lcmDependsFortran::MatchLocalModules@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::MatchLocalModules@k_.body: It loops over each module name in the set `provides` and calls `ConsiderModule` with that name and the current target directory.

@lcmDependsFortran::MatchRemoteModules@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::MatchRemoteModules@k.body: Parses a stream of lines, toggling a flag when a line equals "provides". For each line starting with a space that follows a “provides” block, it appends the “.mod” suffix if absent and then invokes ConsiderModule with that module name.

@lcmDependsFortran::ModulesDiffer@k_ZN16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::ModulesDiffer@k_ZN16.body: The routine accepts two file paths and a compiler identifier, then opens the corresponding files. It short‑circuits a special case for SunPro, delegating comparison to a helper. For GNU and Intel compilers it inspects initial bytes or specific byte sequences to detect non‑standard formats and skips irrelevant prefixes before invoking a full stream comparison. If any of these checks fails or a file is missing, the function returns true, signalling that the modules differ.

@lcmDependsFortran::WriteDependencies@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::WriteDependencies@k_.body: The function collects dependency information for a Fortran build. It first checks that the source and object filenames are supplied. For each source file it constructs a parser instance, runs it against that file, and records any produced dependencies. If a source cannot be parsed, a warning is logged and the overall result becomes false. The function returns a boolean indicating whether all source files were parsed successfully.
