@lcmDependsFortran::WriteDependenciesRea.body:
The function orchestrates the generation of makefile dependency rules for a Fortran object:

- It records the source file and includes, optionally using long‑line syntax if supported.
- It enumerates required modules, adding a rule that forces the target to depend on the module’s stamp file (or on the module file itself if the stamp is unavailable).
- When the target provides modules, it adds a copy‑module rule: it creates a stamp file, triggers the `cmake_copy_f90_mod` helper, and marks the stamp file as a prerequisite for the object. It also writes the final touch rule that updates the stamp file after the object is built.

@lcmDependsFortran::cmDependsFortran@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::cmDependsFortran@k_Z.body: The constructor simply wires up a Fortran‑specific dependency helper. It configures the include‑search path, pulls the list of Fortran target definitions from the current makefile, parses each `NAME=VALUE` definition into a bare symbol name and registers it in the internal definitions set, and finally stores the compiler id and sub‑module separator values for later use.

@lcmDependsFortran::cmDependsFortran@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::cmDependsFortran@k_Z.body: The public constructor creates a fresh cmDependsFortran instance, initializing its internal state to the default empty configuration so the object can subsequently register and manage Fortran module dependencies.

@lcmDependsFortran::~cmDependsFortran@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortran::~cmDependsFortran@k_.body: The destructor `~cmDependsFortran` is a public virtual member that the compiler generates automatically (using `= default`). It performs the usual cleanup for any derived objects that override this destructor, ensuring proper destruction of all member sub‑objects.

@lcmDependsFortranInternals::CreateObjec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortranInternals::CreateObjec.body: The function looks up a key in the internal map. If the key isn’t present it creates a new entry, stores the supplied source string in that entry’s `Source` field, and finally returns a reference to the stored `cmFortranSourceInfo` object. It guarantees that after the call the caller can use the returned reference to read or modify the object’s information without having to duplicate it.

@lcmDependsFortranInternals::cmDependsFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortranInternals::cmDependsFo.body: Receives an instance of `cmDependsFortranInternals` plus an unnamed argument, stitches the internal dependency graph, and returns the resolved dependency mapping.

@lcmDependsFortranInternals::cmDependsFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortranInternals::cmDependsFo.body: The routine consumes a reference to a `cmDependsFortranInternals` object, extracts its stored internal‑dependency entries, and registers them in the project‑wide dependency graph. It iterates over the internal dependency list, adds each entry to the global registry (updating reference counts, ensuring uniqueness, and linking any dependent sub‑components), and finally marks the internal dependencies as resolved for the current build context.

@lcmDependsFortranInternals::cmDependsFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortranInternals::cmDependsFo.body: The public function `cmDependsFortranInternals` serves as a helper that, given a Fortran module (or a context in the build graph), returns the collection of internal components that the module depends on. It walks the internal dependency tree, gathering the relevant internal symbols that need to be linked or built before the target is usable. This function is invoked by other parts of the code to resolve internal linkage information for Fortran modules.

@lcmDependsFortranInternals::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortranInternals::operator=@k.body: The public `operator=` function performs an assignment‑like operation on a `cmDependsFortranInternals` instance. It accepts a temporary or reference (`cmDependsFortranInternals && [unnamed]`) and copies the necessary internal state into `*this`. The function returns a reference to the current object (`*this`) so that chained assignments remain usable. This allows the object to be used with standard assignment syntax while internally updating its internal representation of Fortran dependency data.

@lcmDependsFortranInternals::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortranInternals::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator copies the internal state of a source `cmDependsFortranInternals` into the current object, performing a member‑wise copy (including any dynamically allocated resources) and returns a reference to the updated object so calls can be chained. It typically guards against self‑assignment to avoid corrupting data.

@lcmDependsFortranInternals::~cmDependsF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsFortranInternals::~cmDependsF.body: `~cmDependsFortranInternals()` is a public entry point used by the build system to expose a snapshot of internal dependency metadata. When invoked, it pulls together the mapping between Fortran modules and their internal linkage requirements, returning a lightweight descriptor that callers can query or cache. The function itself performs essentially a read‑only lookup—no side‑effects, making it safe to call from any component that needs to reason about internal Fortran inter‑dependencies.

@lcmDependsJava::CheckDependencies@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJava::CheckDependencies@k_ZN1.body: The function `CheckDependencies` is intended to verify that the dependencies listed in a file or stream are valid. It accepts an input stream, a file name string, and a reference to a `DependencyMap` that should be filled with the valid dependency entries. In its current form the implementation is a stub: it simply returns `true`, indicating success without performing any real checks.

@lcmDependsJava::WriteDependencies@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJava::WriteDependencies@k_ZN1.body: The function only verifies that the supplied set of source file names contains at least one non‑empty entry; if the set is empty or its first element is an empty string it logs an error and returns false, otherwise it simply returns true.

@lcmDependsJava::cmDependsJava@k_ZN13cmD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJava::cmDependsJava@k_ZN13cmD.body: `cmDependsJava` is a copy‑constructor that has been explicitly marked as deleted (`= delete`). This declaration prevents any implicit or explicit copy construction of the type, so attempts to copy an instance (e.g., `auto b = a;` or passing by value) will fail at compile time. @lcmDependsJava::cmDependsJava@k_ZN13cmD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJava::cmDependsJava@k_ZN13cmD.body: The function `cmDependsJava()` checks the current build environment for Java support and initializes the corresponding dependency flags so that subsequent modules can safely rely on Java‑specific functionality.

@lcmDependsJava::operator=@k_ZN13cmDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJava::operator=@k_ZN13cmDepen.body: The deleted copy‑assignment operator (`operator=`) forbids assigning one `cmDependsJava` object to another. Its signature returns a reference, but because it’s marked `= delete`, any attempt to use it results in a compile‑time error.

@lcmDependsJava::~cmDependsJava@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDependsJava::~cmDependsJava@k_ZN13cm.body:
The `~cmDependsJava()` is a virtual destructor that overrides a base‑class destructor.  
When a `cmDependsJava` instance is destroyed, this function runs automatically, allowing the class to release any allocated resources, close sockets or files, and otherwise perform any necessary cleanup before the object’s memory is reclaimed.

@lcmDocumentationEntry::cmDocumentationE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationEntry::cmDocumentationE.body: The constructor implements a move‑style transfer: it takes an rvalue reference to another `cmDocumentationEntry` instance and initializes the new object by adopting the source’s internal state (members, etc.) without copying each component. This allows efficient in‑place construction while ensuring that the original instance is left in a valid, typically empty, state.

@lcmDocumentationEntry::cmDocumentationE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationEntry::cmDocumentationE.body: The constructor creates a new `cmDocumentationEntry` by copying the contents of an existing instance. It takes a constant reference to another `cmDocumentationEntry` and copies its internal state—such as identifiers, titles, descriptions, or any nested metadata—into the newly constructed object. This allows callers to clone a documentation entry or use an existing entry as a template for a new instance.

@lcmDocumentationEntry::cmDocumentationE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationEntry::cmDocumentationE.body: `cmDocumentationEntry()` constructs and registers a documentation entry object. It pulls data from a `cmDocumentationEntry` struct, fills in metadata (such as identifiers, timestamps, and source locations), and then stores the resulting record in the system’s documentation registry so other modules can query or display it.

@lcmDocumentationEntry::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDocumentationEntry::operator=@k_ZN20.body: Assigns an rvalue of type `cmDocumentationEntry` to the object, moving its internal state into the target instance and then returning a reference to that instance.

@lcmDocumentationEntry::operator=@k_ZN20.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDocumentationEntry::~cmDocumentation.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmDurationTo@k_Z12cmDurationToRKNSt6ch.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmDurationTo@k_Z12cmDurationToRKNSt6ch.body:
Converts a `cmDuration` value to the requested type `T` while guarding against overflow or underflow.  
If the source duration exceeds the representable range of `T`, the function clamps the result to the nearest `std::chrono::duration<T>::max()` or `min()` value.  
Otherwise, it performs a `duration_cast` to `std::chrono::duration<T, std::ratio<1>>` and returns the underlying count as a value of type `T`.

@lcmExecutionStatus::GetBreakInvoked@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::GetBreakInvoked@k_Z.body: This method simply exposes the internal flag `BreakInvoked`, returning its current value. It allows callers to query whether the break condition has already been triggered.

@lcmExecutionStatus::GetContinueInvoked@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::GetContinueInvoked@.body: The method returns the current value of the internal flag **ContinueInvoked**, indicating whether the “Continue” operation has already been triggered. It performs no side‑effects—just reads and returns that flag.

@lcmExecutionStatus::GetExitCode@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::GetExitCode@k_ZNK17.body: It retrieves the stored exit code, returning the value if present or –1 when the optional is empty.

@lcmExecutionStatus::GetMakefile@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::GetMakefile@k_ZN17c.body: It returns a reference to the internal `Makefile` member without copying it.

@lcmExecutionStatus::GetReturnInvoked@k_.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExecutionStatus::GetReturnVariables@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::GetReturnVariables@.body: Returns a const reference to the internal vector of strings, exposing the stored variable list for read‑only inspection without copying the contents.

@lcmExecutionStatus::HasExitCode@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExecutionStatus::SetBreakInvoked@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::SetBreakInvoked@k_Z.body: Marks the internal flag indicating a break has been requested by setting it to true.

@lcmExecutionStatus::SetContinueInvoked@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::SetContinueInvoked@.body: SetContinueInvoked marks that a continue action has already been triggered by setting its internal flag to true, allowing subsequent code paths to recognize that the continue has been processed. @lcmExecutionStatus::SetError@k_ZN17cmEx.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExecutionStatus::SetExitCode@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExecutionStatus::SetReturnInvoked@k_.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExecutionStatus::cmExecutionStatus@k.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExecutionStatus::~cmExecutionStatus@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExecutionStatus::~cmExecutionStatus@.body: ~cmExecutionStatus cleans up internal status information before the object goes out of scope. @lcmExpandedCommandArgument::GetValue@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::GetValue@k_.body: Returning a reference allows the caller to inspect the stored string without copying it, and the const qualifier guarantees no change to the object’s internal state.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.body: The constructor initializes a `cmExpandedCommandArgument` instance by storing the supplied string in its internal `Value` member and recording whether the argument should be treated as quoted via the `Quoted` flag.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::cmExpandedC.body: The routine constructs an expanded representation of command‑line arguments, unfolding any shorthands or references so that downstream components receive a fully resolved view of the options.

@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::~cmExpanded.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpandedCommandArgument::~cmExpanded.body: The function produces a fully expanded argument object from a raw command‑line argument string. @lcmExperimental::HasSupportEnabled@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExperimental::HasSupportEnabled@k_ZN.body: Checks whether a given feature is enabled in a `cmMakefile`. It pulls a feature‑specific record with `DataForFeature`, pulls the current definition from the makefile, and compares that value to the feature’s unique identifier (`Uuid`). If the values match, it marks the feature as enabled. When a feature becomes enabled for the first time, it emits an author‑warning message and flips a flag in the record so the warning is only issued once. The function finally returns the enabled flag.

@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GenerateIm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GenerateIm.body: The function first checks whether the file should be opened in append mode; if not, it writes a predefined header via `GenerateImportHeaderCode`. Then it creates a `stringstream` to collect the body of the import file and calls `GenerateMainFile` to fill that buffer. Finally it streams the buffer’s contents to the supplied output stream and returns the success flag from the main‑file generation step.

@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GenerateIm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GenerateIm.body: The function writes the contents that make up an import‑header file (e.g. header guards, include directives, namespace declarations, and any boiler‑plate required by the generator) into the supplied `std::ostream` so that the generated header can be emitted as part of the build process.

@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GenerateIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GenerateIn.body: The function walks the supplied property map and emits a series of “LOCAL_” directives that describe the compile options, link libraries, include directories and link flags that an Android‑style build system will apply to a library or executable target. It distinguishes static and shared libraries, prefixes relative paths with “‑l” when necessary, and records whether a pre‑built static library requires C++ support. The output it generates is a make‑file fragment that the target’s build tool can consume to wire up its dependencies.

@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GetGenerat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GetGenerat.body:

The function’s signature is:

```cpp
virtual GenerateType GetGenerateType() const = 0;
```

where `GenerateType` is an enum or similar type used by the framework to distinguish generator kinds. All implementations must maintain const‑correctness, returning the enum value without side effects.

@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GetImportP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::GetImportP.body: The function returns a string literal formed by concatenating a predefined import prefix with a trailing slash. The returned view references the string literal `"$(_IMPORT_PREFIX)/"` without allocating new memory.

@lcmExportAndroidMKGenerator::cmExportAn.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportCMakeConfigGenerator::GetFileS.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportCMakeConfigGenerator::GetFileS.author: AI Short Overview

In the exporter workflow it is queried when building a CMake configuration file; the concrete implementation typically collects all file paths stored in the target’s file‑set and formats them into a CMake‑compatible list. The base class supplies no logic, so subclasses must provide the actual mapping logic.

@lcmExportCMakeConfigGenerator::~cmExpor.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateCxxModu.author: AI Short Overview

A concrete implementation takes a constant reference to a string (typically a module name or path) and writes the necessary configuration entries into the appropriate output buffers, ensuring that the resulting configuration satisfies the specifications expected by downstream code such as the export‑file generator.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportC.body: The `GenerateImportConfig` method delegates the actual rendering of an import‑configuration file to the helper `GenerateImportTargetsConfig`. It accepts an output stream and a configuration string, then invokes the helper with the original configuration plus a computed suffix (via `PropertyConfigSuffix`). This facilitates generating the appropriate import‑targets section for a given configuration without duplicating logic.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportF.body: Write an import file to the provided stream and return true on success; derived classes implement the concrete format.

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GenerateImportT.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetCxxModulesDi.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportFileGenerator::GetImportPrefix.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::C.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.body: The routine assembles a small CMake include file in the C++ modules directory. If the file stream fails it reports an error and returns false; otherwise it returns true.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.body: Collects the export targets, emits the code blocks for importing them, generating the interface properties, file‑sets, and any configuration‑specific imports, and finally writes checks for missing targets, returning a Boolean success flag.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.body: Returns the dash `-` character that the class uses as the separator between elements of a configuration‑file name. The method is marked `protected virtual`, so derived classes can override it, and `const` guarantees it cannot modify object state.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.body: It returns a glob string composed of the stored base path, a single‑character wildcard, and the file extension.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.body: The function simply proxies a call to an internal helper (`IEGen`) and returns the resulting string. @lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.body: The protected virtual method builds a list of directory strings for a target’s file set. It iterates over the target’s generator configs, evaluates the destination expression for each, prefixes non‑absolute paths with the import prefix, and for context‑sensitive generators adds a configuration marker. It rejects unsupported C++ module file‑sets with context‑sensitive entries, then joins the collected directory strings with spaces before returning the result.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::G.body: The routine walks through the provided `cmFileSet`, enumerating all directory and file entries for each configuration listed in the target’s generator. For each entry it evaluates the target path, escapes it for CMake syntax, and appends it to a list of result strings, wrapping them in quotes when needed. If any part of the set is context‑sensitive while the configuration set contains more than one config, it emits a fatal error and returns an empty string. Finally it joins all collected path strings with a space separator and returns the resulting string.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::L.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::L.body: The routine outputs a CMake fragment that first enumerates the files matching a configured glob under `${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}`. It then loops through that list, issuing an `include()` for each file and finally cleans up the temporary loop variables.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::c.body: The `cmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator` function is responsible for creating the export‑metadata files that `cmake` will install. It walks through the current configuration’s export list, writes the appropriate `ExportSet` files in the install tree, and ensures that all exported targets will be correctly discovered by downstream `cmake` invocations.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::c.body: The constructor merely forwards the passed `iegen` to the base class `cmExportInstallFileGenerator` and performs any minimal setup required for the derived generator.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::c.body: This constructor creates a new `cmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator` by copying the internal state of an existing instance. It copies configuration options, path settings, and any logger or context objects needed to emit CMake files for an export‑install target. The new instance is ready to generate the appropriate CMake configuration once invoked.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::o.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::o.body: The assignment operator accepts an rvalue reference to another cmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator, transfers its internal state (e.g., mapping of config entries) into the current instance, and returns a reference to the updated object. If the source object has an invalid internal state, the operation may throw an exception; otherwise it performs a shallow copy of the underlying data structures.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::o.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::o.body: The assignment operator copies all internal configuration data from the supplied instance into the current object, updating its state to match that of the source without re‑initialising resources.

@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::~.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator::~.body: The `~cmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator` routine orchestrates the generation of a CMake configuration file during an export‑install operation. It gathers the build‑time settings captured in the `cmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator` class, serializes them into a CMake‑style script (often a `cmakefile.cmake`), and writes that script to the destination path specified by the export configuration. It is invoked by higher‑level installers to ensure the generated CMake file is present in the exported package so consuming projects can immediately consume the build configuration.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetConfi.body: `GetConfigFileNameSeparator` is a protected pure virtual member that returns the single‑character separator used when constructing a configuration file name. Implementations in derived classes supply the specific separator (e.g., ‘_’, ‘-’, etc.) that the rest of the system consumes to assemble file names. The function is const, ensuring it does not modify object state, and being pure virtual guarantees each concrete implementation must provide its own separator definition.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::GetConfi.body: The function declares a pure virtual const member that returns a `std::string` representing a file‑glob pattern used to locate configuration‑import files. Implementations supply the specific glob string that callers use to locate the appropriate files during installation.

@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::~cmExpor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportInstallFileGenerator::~cmExpor.body: The destructor finalizes the export file generator, releasing allocated resources and ensuring all associated file‑generation subsystems are properly shut down.

@lcmExportSet::AddTargetExport@k_ZN11cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSet::AddTargetExport@k_ZN11cmE.body: Adds a newly created target export to the internal collection, transferring ownership of the passed `std::unique_ptr<cmTargetExport>` into the internal vector.

@lcmExportSetMap::operator[]@k_ZN14cmExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExportSetMap::operator[]@k_ZN14cmExp.body: The operator overload looks up an entry by name; if it’s missing it inserts a new default‑constructed export‑set using that key, and finally returns a reference to the stored set.

@lcmExprParserHelper::Error@k_ZN18cmExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::Error@k_ZN18cmExpr.body: Captures the current buffer position and stores a message consisting of the supplied string plus that position in parentheses into the `ErrorString` member.

@lcmExprParserHelper::GetError@k_ZN18cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::GetError@k_ZN18cmE.body:
The member function returns a C‑style pointer to the internal string that holds the error text, exposing the raw buffer directly.  
It simply forwards the internal string’s `c_str()` result, so the caller receives a pointer into the object’s own storage.  

**Key points to note**  
- The returned pointer is only valid while the object remains alive and its string buffer is unchanged.  
- Because the pointer is raw, the caller must not attempt to modify the string through it.  
- The function is a trivial getter; it doesn’t perform any copying or ownership transfer.

@lcmExprParserHelper::GetResult@k_ZNK18c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::GetResult@k_ZNK18c.body: Returns the stored result value without modifying any state.

@lcmExprParserHelper::GetWarning@k_ZNK18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::GetWarning@k_ZNK18.body: The function returns a reference to the `WarningString` member. It is a `const` member function, so it promises not to modify the object. It returns the stored warning string by reference, avoiding a copy.

@lcmExprParserHelper::LexInput@k_ZN18cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::LexInput@k_ZN18cmE.body: The method pulls up to maxlen bytes from an internal input stream, advancing an internal position pointer. It updates a line counter whenever a newline is consumed and returns the count of bytes actually read (or 0 if the buffer is exhausted). It falls back to a single newline character when the input source runs out of data.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParseString@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParseString@k_ZN18.body: The function takes an input string and a verbosity flag, initializes an internal scanner state, runs the parser on the string, and stores the parsing result. If parsing fails it records an error message; otherwise it reports the parsed result when verbosity is enabled.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.body: This constructor creates a new instance by performing a member‑wise copy of the source object. It copies each member (including any owned resources) so that the new instance owns its own independent state, preserving the original object's invariants without sharing mutable resources.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::Parser.body: ParserType() returns the parser type used by the system, typically inferred from configuration or input. It allows the rest of the code to select the appropriate parsing strategy at runtime.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::operat.body: The `operator=` function implements the copy‑assignment operator for `ParserType`. It takes a const reference to another `ParserType` instance, copies the internal state of that object into the current instance, and returns a reference to the current object (`*this`). This allows callers to write `obj1 = obj2;` to replace the contents of `obj1` with those of `obj2`.

@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::~Parse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::ParserType::~Parse.body: Returns a parser instance that matches the requested format string – the routine performs a simple lookup of the format type and constructs the concrete parser object that knows how to read that data.

@lcmExprParserHelper::Print@k_ZN18cmExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::Print@k_ZN18cmExpr.body: Print writes the supplied string to an output stream, prefixed by the place argument.

@lcmExprParserHelper::SetError@k_ZN18cmE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::SetError@k_ZN18cmE.body: Assigns the supplied string to the internal member variable ErrorString, using std::move to avoid an unnecessary copy.

@lcmExprParserHelper::SetResult@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::SetResult@k_ZN18cm.body: Assigns the supplied 64‑bit integer to the helper’s internal `Result` field, replacing whatever value was previously stored. The method is a straightforward setter that does no validation or side‑effects beyond the assignment.

@lcmExprParserHelper::UnexpectedChar@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::UnexpectedChar@k_Z.body: The routine records a warning that the current input character is not accepted, appending a message that includes the current buffer index and the offending character to the warning log.

@lcmExprParserHelper::cmExprParserHelper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::cmExprParserHelper.body: The function is a copy‑constructor for `cmExprParserHelper`. It accepts a constant reference to another helper instance and duplicates its internal parser state (tokens, bindings, etc.) so the new object starts with the same configuration as the source.

@lcmExprParserHelper::cmExprParserHelper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::cmExprParserHelper.body: Initializes the helper’s internal state by setting `FileLine` to –1, `FileName` to nullptr, and `Result` to 0.

@lcmExprParserHelper::operator=@k_ZN18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::operator=@k_ZN18cm.body: Performs a deep copy of all internal data members from the source object to the target, ensuring the helper’s internal state is fully duplicated while maintaining any required ownership semantics.

@lcmExprParserHelper::~cmExprParserHelpe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExprParserHelper::~cmExprParserHelpe.body: The `~cmExprParserHelper()` function is a destructor that automatically releases any resources owned by a `cmExprParserHelper` instance. When an object of that class goes out of scope or is explicitly destroyed, this destructor is invoked to clean up its internal state.

@lcmExpr_yyerror@k_ZL14cmExpr_yyerrorPvP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyerror@k_ZL14cmExpr_yyerrorPvP.body: The function simply forwards a supplied error string to the scanner’s error‑handling routine—invoking `cmExpr_yyget_extra(yyscanner)->Error(message)`.

@lcmExpr_yyget_extra@k_Z18cmExpr_yyget_e.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyget_extra@k_Z18cmExpr_yyget_e.body: The function takes a `yyscan_t` pointer, casts it to the internal `yyguts_t` struct, and returns the `yyextra` member. It assumes the caller supplies a valid scanner object; passing a null or corrupted pointer would lead to a crash. It also expects the `yyguts_t` definition to expose the `yyextra` field, otherwise the compiler will reject the cast.

@lcmExpr_yylex@k_Z12cmExpr_yylexPN18cmEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yylex@k_Z12cmExpr_yylexPN18cmEx.body: The routine scans the input buffer character‑by‑character, following a deterministic automaton encoded in the tables (yy_accept, yy_chk, yy_nxt, etc.). When a recognised token is found it returns a token code such as exp_NUMBER, exp_PLUS, exp_OR, etc. It also handles buffer switches and end‑of‑file conditions, restoring the scanner state if a buffer boundary is crossed.

@lcmExpr_yyparse@k_Z14cmExpr_yyparsePv@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExpr_yyparse@k_Z14cmExpr_yyparsePv@f.body: The function is a hand‑crafted, table‑driven LALR parser that reads tokens from a scanner, maintains a state stack and a semantic value stack, and performs shifting, reducing, and error recovery. It uses tables (`yypact`, `yytable`, etc.) to decide actions, shifts tokens onto the stacks, reduces according to grammar rules, executes semantic actions, and handles syntax errors with a backtracking routine. The core loop reads a lookahead token when needed, decides the action, shifts or reduces, and after a rule is applied it updates the state stack and proceeds to the next token until it reaches the final state or encounters an unrecoverable error.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Ge.body: The `Generate()` member is an abstract entry point that concrete subclasses must implement. When invoked it is expected to produce the necessary output (e.g., write a configuration file, emit build scripts, etc.) and signal completion, but the base class itself contains no logic.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Op.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::Op.body: The `Open` method is a virtual entry point for initializing an external‑makefile project; in its current form it does nothing except returning `false`, effectively marking the operation as unsupported or unimplemented in this code path.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator::cm.body: `cmExternalMakefileProjectGenerator` orchestrates the creation of a Makefile for an external project by pulling together the project’s target information, variable context, and project file settings. It queries the project configuration, pulls any legacy generator settings, and writes out a makefile that the external tool can consume. The routine ultimately produces an output file that the build system will invoke to build that project’s sources.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The function appends the supplied string to the internal list of supported global generators. It simply stores the string reference for later use in the generator‑factory logic.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorFact.body: The function is a simple const accessor that returns a copy of the internal `SupportedGlobalGenerators` member, which is a `std::vector<std::string>` holding the names of the global generators supported by this factory.

@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExternalMakefileProjectGeneratorSimp.body: The constructor simply forwards the supplied name and documentation string to the base factory class, establishing a new *Simple* external‑makefile project‑generator factory instance.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendAll.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendAll.body: The function walks through every target produced by the supplied local generators, emitting a rule for each one into the output stream. It distinguishes global targets (only from the main binary directory), utility targets (skipping the nightly/continuous/experimental variants), and the various executable/library classes (adding a “/fast” alias as well), while guarding against duplicate entries and ensuring proper compiler and makefile context for each appended target.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::AppendTar.body: The `AppendTarget` routine serialises a target into the generator’s output stream. For each source file belonging to the target it collects compile‑flags, defines, and include paths, stripping flag tokens via a regular‑expression sweep. It then emits a JSON‑style record containing the target’s name, its build command (produced by `BuildMakeCommand`), working directory and a file‑regex pattern. Depending on the global generator it prefixes the record with either a Ninja build file (`build.ninja`) or a Makefile name. The record is appended to the output stream, joining multiple targets into a single file.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::BuildMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::BuildMake.body: BuildMakeCommand assembles a shell‑invocation string for the chosen build system. It prefixes the make executable, appends the `‑f` flag with the (possibly escaped) makefile name, and finally appends the target name. The branch logic chooses different quoting/escaping conventions per generator type (e.g. NMake, Ninja, or MinGW), and uses `ConvertToOutputPath` to generate a path that the specific tool can consume. The routine returns that fully‑qualified command string.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeDe.body: ComputeDefines collects and merges preprocessor definitions for the current build target. It pulls the language and build‑type setting from the source file, constructs an expression interpreter, then pulls in generic and target‑specific compile definitions that are stored in the source file’s properties. Those definitions are evaluated, appended to a set, and finally concatenated into a single string that is returned for use in the build process.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeFl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeFl.body: The function assembles a string of compiler flags for a source object by: determining the source’s language (falling back to C when none is provided), appending the corresponding explicit language flag first; then invoking the generator’s `GetTargetCompileFlags` to fill in any build‑type‑specific defaults; finally evaluating and appending any `COMPILE_FLAGS` or `COMPILE_OPTIONS` values defined on the source file through the generator expression interpreter. The result, a single string of flags, is returned.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::ComputeIn.body: ComputeIncludes walks the source file’s properties to pull any explicit include directories, merges them with the project‑wide include paths defined in the makefile, and finally stitches the resulting paths into a single flag string that is used by the build system to pass‑through to the compiler.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreateNew.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreateNew.body: The routine generates a Sublime project file: it opens the output stream, writes a JSON‑like structure listing the source‑root relative path as a “folder” entry, then serialises every target’s include directories into a “build_systems” array, and finally emits any env‑variable mappings from `CMAKE_SUBLIME_TEXT_2_ENV_SETTINGS`. If the relative output path is empty it defaults to “./”. It also skips writing the build‑folder entry when `ExcludeBuildFolder` is true.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreatePro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::CreatePro.body: It gathers the binary directory and project name from the first generator, assembles the full path to a *.sublime-project* file in that directory, and then forwards that path to CreateNewProjectFile for the actual file creation.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Generate@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Generate@.body: The `Generate` function first fetches the flag `CMAKE_SUBLIME_TEXT_2_EXCLUDE_BUILD_TREE` to decide whether build‑tree files should be excluded, then pulls the global environment settings under the key `CMAKE_SUBLIME_TEXT_2_ENV_SETTINGS`. With those settings in hand it loops through every project in the global generator’s project map and calls `CreateProjectFile` for each entry, producing a Sublime‑Text 2 project file for that sub‑project.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::GetFactor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::GetFactor.body:
The function creates a single shared factory for the *Sublime Text 2* generator.  
When the factory has no global generators configured, it registers a set of default Makefile generators (MinGW, NMake, Ninja, and Unix), conditionally on the platform. It then returns a pointer to that configured factory instance.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Open@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::Open@k_ZN.body: The `Open` function verifies that a required executable is available, then either reports that the target file already exists (in a dry‑run) or launches the executable with the generated project file. If the executable or its cache entry is missing, the function immediately returns `false`. In a dry‑run it merely checks for the file’s existence; otherwise it runs the command `sublime-project` with the project file path. The caller is responsible for handling any return value to determine success.

@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmExtraSublimeTextGenerator::cmExtraSu.body: The constructor for `cmExtraSublimeTextGenerator` simply initializes the internal flag `ExcludeBuildFolder` to `false`. This flag controls whether the class will skip generating text for the build‑output directory.

@lcmFileAPI::AddProjectQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::AddProjectQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function validates the requested `ObjectKind` against supported type‑and‑version constraints. If the combination is invalid (unsupported kind or minor version higher than the defined limit) it returns `false`; otherwise, if this query is not already recorded in `TopQuery.Known`, it appends it, sets `QueryExists` to true, and returns `true`.

@lcmFileAPI::AddReplyIndexObject@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::AddReplyIndexObject@k_ZN9cm.body: `AddReplyIndexObject` takes an `Object` reference, checks whether the reply has already been registered, and if not it builds the object, writes it to disk and records the resulting entry in the reply‑index map, returning the corresponding `Json::Value`.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMake@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMake@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: The method composes a JSON object that describes the current CMake installation: it records the tool’s version, the full paths to the CMake binaries (CMake, CTest, and CPack), the root directory, and the JSON representation of the global generator. The constructed object is then returned.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMakeFiles@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCMakeFiles@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The method builds a JSON representation of CMake files by calling a dumper, setting the kind string, and for objects with version 1 it calls BuildVersion. If the object’s version doesn’t match, it returns early (the code comment indicates this case is unreachable).

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCache@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCache@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: BuildCache creates a JSON value by dumping the current cache, annotating the object kind and, if the object’s version is 2, filling the version field using BuildVersion; otherwise the function simply returns the constructed cache.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReply@k_ZN9cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReply@k_ZN9cmFil.body: The function builds a JSON reply for a client query. It starts by creating a base reply from the directory‑level query, then conditionally inserts the specific query JSON. If an error string is present it replaces the query section with an error representation; otherwise it adds any provided client or request data and finally appends a collection of per‑request responses generated by the helper method. The fully populated JSON value is returned.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponse@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponse@k_.body: The function checks the request for an error; if one is present, it builds an error reply using `BuildReplyError`; otherwise it appends an index object via `AddReplyIndexObject` and returns the resulting JSON value.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponses@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientReplyResponses@k.body: The function first checks if the request list contains an error flag; if present it immediately builds and returns an error reply. Otherwise it initializes an empty JSON array and iterates over each request, appending a built reply object per request. The result is a JSON array of per‑request reply values.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequest@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequest@k_ZN9cmF.body: The routine takes a JSON request, confirms required fields, maps the “kind” string to an internal enum, parses any provided version tokens, and then delegates to a kind‑specific builder helper to populate the resulting `ClientRequest`.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCMakeFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCMakeFile.body: The method scans the supplied list of requested versions, picks the first entry whose major number equals 1 and whose minor number is at most the predefined threshold (CMakeFilesV1Minor), assigns that major number to the client request’s Version field, and if no such entry exists, records an error via NoSupportedVersion.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCache@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCache@k_Z.body: The routine walks the supplied version list, picks the first entry whose major part is 2 and whose minor part is at most the cached minor threshold, assigns that major value to the request’s `Version`. If no entry satisfies the condition, it tags the request with an error string produced by `NoSupportedVersion`.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCodeModel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestCodeModel.body: The function scans the supplied list of requested `RequestVersion` values. It stores the first one whose major part equals 2 and whose minor part does not exceed the defined maximum (`CodeModelV2Minor`). If no such version is found, it marks an error in the request object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestConfigure.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestConfigure.body: It iterates over the supplied version list, picks the first entry whose major is 1 and whose minor does not exceed the constant `ConfigureLogV1Minor`, assigns that value to the request’s `Version` field, and if no such entry exists it marks the request with a `NoSupportedVersion` error.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestInternalT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestInternalT.body: The routine scans the supplied `versions` list, picks the first entry whose major version is 1 or 2 with a minor no greater than the corresponding internal‑test thresholds, and assigns that major value to `r.Version`. If none of the requested versions satisfy that criterion, it records an error via `NoSupportedVersion(versions)`.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestToolchain.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequestToolchain.body: The function iterates over the supplied version list, picks the first entry that satisfies a major‑number constraint (major = 1 and minor ≤ ToolchainsV1Minor), and assigns that major value to the request’s `Version` field. If no such entry is found, it records an error via `NoSupportedVersion`.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequests@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildClientRequests@k_ZN9cm.body: The method accepts a JSON value expected to be an array. It first checks for null and array types, returning an error message if the checks fail. When valid, it reserves space in a vector for each array element and iteratively constructs individual client requests by delegating to the private `BuildClientRequest` helper, finally returning the populated vector.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildCodeModel@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildCodeModel@k_ZN9cmFileA.body: The `BuildCodeModel` routine serialises a given object into a JSON value. It first creates a base model via `cmFileAPICodemodelDump`, tags it with the object’s kind, and then injects a `version` field. If the input object's version field equals `2`, it delegates to `BuildVersion(2, CodeModelV2Minor)` to fill in the rest; otherwise the function simply returns the partially‑filled model. The conditional block guarantees that only a supported version path is taken; the “unreachable” return is a defensive fallback that should never execute.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildConfigureLog@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildConfigureLog@k_ZN9cmFi.body: The function pulls in a `cmFileAPIConfigureLogDump` result for the current object, tags that entry with the object’s kind name, and then adds a `version` field only when the object's version is `1`; otherwise it simply returns the partially‑filled JSON. It ends by returning the JSON value that has been populated with the kind and optional version information.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildInternalTest@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildInternalTest@k_ZN9cmFi.body: It builds a JSON object for an internal test. It sets a “kind” field from the object’s kind name and attaches a “version” field. If the object’s version equals 2, it uses a helper that builds a version‑2 test; otherwise it falls back to the version‑1 helper. The function finally returns the constructed test object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildObject@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildObject@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.body: Returns a JSON value that represents the passed `Object`. The helper inspects the `ObjectKind` of the object and forwards the construction to the corresponding `Build*` routine, returning the JSON value produced by that specific builder.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildReply@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildReply@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: BuildReply iterates over the query’s known and unknown collections, inserting each known object via AddReplyIndexObject into the reply JSON, and for each unknown name it inserts an error entry via BuildReplyError.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyError@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyError@k_ZN9cmFile.body: BuildReplyError simply constructs a JSON object that contains the provided error message under the key `"error"` and returns that object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyIndex@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildReplyIndex@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function gathers reply data for all known query clients. It creates a JSON object that records the current CMake version, compiles a reply for the top‑level query and for each registered client query, then serialises the list of generated objects into the “objects” array before returning the assembled JSON object.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildToolchains@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildToolchains@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function creates a JSON representation of a toolchain for a given object, populating the “kind” field with the object’s type string, inserting a “version” field that is only produced when the object’s version equals 1, and finally returning the composed JSON value.

@lcmFileAPI::BuildVersion@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::BuildVersion@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: The function creates a JSON value containing the supplied major and minor numbers and returns that value.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQuery::ClientQuery@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQuery::ClientQuery@k_.body: ClientQuery takes an rvalue reference of a ClientQuery object, extracts the query parameters, runs the associated query‑handling logic (including any required validation or lookup), and then returns the appropriate result or status indication for that request.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQuery::ClientQuery@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQuery::ClientQuery@k_.body: The constructor duplicates an existing `ClientQuery` instance, copying all its member values into the new object so that the new query mirrors the original state.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQuery::ClientQuery@k_.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQuery::~ClientQuery@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQuery::~ClientQuery@k.body: The `~ClientQuery` function is a public entry point that takes a `ClientQuery` structure as its input, orchestrates the necessary validation and lookup logic against the underlying data store, and then returns the composed result set back to the caller. It essentially wires together the various helper utilities that parse, validate, and execute the query before handing back a clean, consumable response.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::ClientQuer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::ClientQuer.body: The constructor takes an rvalue reference (`ClientQueryJson&&`) and initializes a new `ClientQueryJson` object by moving the contents of the source object into the new instance.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::ClientQuer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::ClientQuer.body: Creates a new `ClientQueryJson` instance by copying the contents of an existing instance passed by reference.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::ClientQuer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::ClientQuer.body: The `ClientQueryJson()` routine builds a JSON payload containing the client’s query parameters (client‑ID, target file, and any filters). It then sends this payload to the API endpoint that resolves the request and returns the requested data. The surrounding code uses this JSON to drive the query logic in other parts of the system.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::operator=@.body: Moves an rvalue of ClientQueryJson into the current instance, transferring its contents while leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::operator=@.body: The assignment operator copies the entire state from another `ClientQueryJson` into the current instance, performing a member‑wise deep copy of all query parameters.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::~ClientQue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientQueryJson::~ClientQue.body: The function takes a `ClientQueryJson` instance and emits a JSON string that faithfully represents all required fields while gracefully flagging missing or malformed data—effectively preparing the query payload for downstream API consumption.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.body: The move constructor initializes a new `ClientRequest` by transferring ownership of the source’s data members without deep copying, ensuring the original instance is left in a valid state.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.body:
The declaration defines a copy constructor for the `ClientRequest` struct.  
It takes a const reference to another `ClientRequest` instance and uses that reference to initialize the new object with the same internal state.  
In practice, it is invoked whenever a request object needs to be duplicated, for example in the code around line 105 of `cmFileAPI.h`.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::ClientReques.body: The function constructs and returns a `ClientRequest` instance populated with the request’s metadata (client ID, operation type, context flags, etc.) that is passed further into the API layer for processing.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::operator=@k_.body: The operator= overload allows a temporary `ClientRequest` to be moved into an existing instance, copying or transferring its internal state and returning a reference to the modified object.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::operator=@k_.body: `operator=` implements the copy‑assignment operator for `ClientRequest`. It copies all data members from the source object into the current one, performs a self‑assignment guard, and returns a reference to `*this` so that the operator can be chained. The implementation is straightforward: check for self‑assignment, copy each field (including any nested objects or pointers), and finally return the updated object.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::~ClientReque.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequest::~ClientReque.body: Builds a new `ClientRequest` instance, populating its mandatory fields (client ID, request type, any payload data) and returns a reference to the freshly‑in‑itialised object.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.body: The constructor initializes a new `ClientRequests` instance by moving the underlying vector of requests from an existing instance, transferring ownership of the request elements without copying them.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.body: The copy‐constructor simply creates a new `ClientRequests` instance that contains the same sequence of `ClientRequest` objects as the source instance. It forwards the copy operation to the underlying `std::vector<ClientRequest>` base, so the new object inherits the current vector’s contents and any internal bookkeeping (size, capacity, etc.) unchanged.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::ClientReque.body: ClientRequests is a constructor for a class that inherits from std::vector<ClientRequest>, thereby providing a dynamic array of ClientRequest objects. When invoked, it constructs an initially empty vector ready to hold incoming client requests, enabling further operations such as insertion, removal or enumeration of requests throughout the system.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator for `ClientRequests` moves all elements from the supplied temporary (rvalue) into the current object, replacing its vector contents and returning a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::operator=@k.body: The operator takes another ClientRequests instance and copies its underlying vector into the current object, returning a reference to the updated instance. This copies the entire request list efficiently, assuming no self‑assignment scenario and no external side‑effects beyond the standard vector assignment.

@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::~ClientRequ.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ClientRequests::~ClientRequ.body: The destructor `~ClientRequests()` simply cleans up the `ClientRequests` collection, ensuring any resources owned by the `vector` base are released when an instance of `ClientRequests` goes out of scope.

@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixHash@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixHash@k_ZN9cmFi.body: The routine takes a file path, runs a SHA‑3‑256 hash on the file contents, then truncates the resulting hex string to exactly 20 characters (padding with zeros if necessary) before returning it.

@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixTime@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ComputeSuffixTime@k_ZN9cmFi.body: Creates a string of the current moment in a compact “YYYY‑MM‑DDTHH‑MM‑SS‑mmmm” format: it pulls the now‑time in milliseconds, converts it to seconds, builds a timestamp object, and appends the millisecond fraction zero‑padded to four digits before returning the string.

@lcmFileAPI::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK9cmFi.body: Returns the internal CMake instance pointer, exposing it as read‑only so callers cannot modify the underlying state.

@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions::[l.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions::[l.body: Captures a reference to a `versions` collection and, for a supplied `Query`, iterates over its `Known` objects. Whenever an object’s `Kind` equals `ConfigureLog`, its `Version` is appended to the captured list.

@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::GetConfigureLogVersions@k_Z.body: The function scans the top‑level query and each client query for objects whose kind is ConfigureLog, extracts their version identifiers into a vector, sorts that vector, removes any duplicates, and returns the resulting sorted list.

@lcmFileAPI::LoadDir@k_ZN9cmFileAPI7Load.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::LoadDir@k_ZN9cmFileAPI7Load.body: Retrieves all file names in a given directory (excluding the special entries “.” and “..”), loads them into a vector, sorts the vector in ascending order, and returns that sorted list.

@lcmFileAPI::MaybeJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::MaybeJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.body: If the incoming `Json::Value` represents an object or an array, the method creates a new JSON object containing a single member `jsonFile`, whose value is the filename returned by `WriteJsonFile`. It then returns that object. If the value is not an object or array, the method simply returns the original value unchanged.

@lcmFileAPI::NoSupportedVersion@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::NoSupportedVersion@k_ZN9cmF.body:
The function builds an error‑message string.  
It starts with “no supported version specified”; if the supplied vector contains any `RequestVersion` entries, it appends “among:” followed by a space‑separated list of each version’s major.minor pair. The resulting string is returned.

@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.body: The `Object(Object&&)` constructor is a move constructor: it takes an rvalue reference to another `Object` instance and transfers (moves) the internal state of that instance into the new one.

@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.body: The constructor takes another instance by reference and duplicates its internal state into the new object, ensuring that all owned resources are correctly replicated so the new instance starts in the same configuration as the source.

@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Object::Object@k_ZN9cmFileA.body: Object() is a public constructor that initializes a new instance of the Object struct. It takes no parameters and sets up the default state for that instance. The implementation is elsewhere in the codebase, but the interface signals that it creates the object and performs any necessary initialization steps.

@lcmFileAPI::Object::operator=@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Object::operator=@k_ZN9cmFi.body: The move‑assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another instance, moves its internal resources into the current object (typically by swapping or moving member variables), then returns `*this`. It should guard against self‑assignment, release any owned resources before the move, and keep the object in a valid state afterward.

@lcmFileAPI::Object::operator=@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Object::operator=@k_ZN9cmFi.body: The operator assigns the contents of the RHS object into the LHS object and returns a reference to the object itself.

@lcmFileAPI::Object::~Object@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Object::~Object@k_ZN9cmFile.body: ~Object() is a public destructor that releases resources held by an instance of the `Object` struct, ensuring any dynamically allocated members are properly freed before the object is discarded.

@lcmFileAPI::ObjectKindName@k_ZN9cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ObjectKindName@k_ZN9cmFileA.body: The `ObjectKindName` helper returns a C‑string identifier that matches the underlying `ObjectKind` enumeration. It uses a compile‑time constant array and casts the enum value to an index, yielding a `const char*` that corresponds to the enum element’s textual name. This allows callers to obtain a readable name for a given kind without any runtime lookup logic.

@lcmFileAPI::ObjectName@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ObjectName@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: It builds a string that combines the object’s kind name with “‑v” and its version number, then returns that string.

@lcmFileAPI::Query::Query@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Query::Query@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: It efficiently creates a new Query instance by moving the resources from an existing temporary Query object—no copy operations are performed.

@lcmFileAPI::Query::Query@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Query::Query@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: This constructor creates a new `Query` instance by copying the state from another `Query` object passed by const reference.

@lcmFileAPI::Query::Query@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Query::Query@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: The `Query` public function acts as the primary entry point for retrieving data. It validates the supplied parameters, forwards the request to the underlying data‑access layer, and then returns the extracted result set—typically a collection of domain objects or an error code—ready for the caller to consume in the surrounding workflow.

@lcmFileAPI::Query::operator=@k_ZN9cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Query::operator=@k_ZN9cmFil.body: It forwards the contents of a temporary `Query` into the current instance, performs the usual move‑assignment semantics, and returns a reference to the updated object.

@lcmFileAPI::Query::operator=@k_ZN9cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Query::operator=@k_ZN9cmFil.body: The operator= function assigns a new Query object to the current one by copying all of its member data and then returns a reference to the assigned object, allowing chaining of assignments.

@lcmFileAPI::Query::~Query@k_ZN9cmFileAP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::Query::~Query@k_ZN9cmFileAP.body: ~Query constructs or retrieves a Query object, packing search parameters into a ready‑to‑use Query struct that other components invoke to perform file‑based data retrieval.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadClient@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadClient@k_ZN9cmFileAPI10.body: The ReadClient routine builds the path to the client’s query folder, loads the file list, and for each file it marks whether it’s a known JSON query or tries to read it—on‑failure the file name is stored in an “unknown” list.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadClientQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadClientQuery@k_ZN9cmFile.body: The function loads a JSON file specific to a client, validates that the file’s root is an object, pulls out the optional “client” value, and then fills the `ClientQueryJson` structure with the request list by delegating to `BuildClientRequests`.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: The routine opens the specified file, loads its entire contents into a contiguous buffer, and hands that buffer to a JSON parser. On any read‑or‑parse failure it clears the output value and records an explanatory message before returning false.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadQueries@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadQueries@k_ZN9cmFileAPI1.body: The routine first verifies that either the standard query directory or an optional user‑supplied one exists; if neither is found it exits immediately. It then loads all query filenames from the existing directories into a single vector (adding the user‑specific list after the system list). It loops over that list, and for each entry: if the name starts with “client‑”, it dispatches to the dedicated client reader; otherwise it tries to parse the query into the top‑level query object. Parsing failures result in the filename being stored in a separate “unknown” collection.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadQuery@k_ZN9cmFileAPI9Re.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadQuery@k_ZN9cmFileAPI9Re.body: The function parses a string in the form `<kind>-<ver>`, verifies that the `<kind>` matches one of the supported `ObjectKind` values and that the `<ver>` string matches the only allowed version for that kind. If both checks succeed it constructs an `Object` with the corresponding `Kind` and `Version`, appends it to `objects` and returns `true`. If the string is malformed, unknown, or the version mismatches, it returns `false`.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersion@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersion@k_ZN9cmF.body: The function extracts a version from a JSON value: it validates that the major field is present and numeric, treats the optional minor field if supplied, builds a RequestVersion struct with those values, appends it to the result vector, and returns a success flag while reporting any malformed input via the error string.

@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersions@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReadRequestVersions@k_ZN9cm.body: The function parses a JSON‐style version list. It first checks whether the supplied `version` node is an array; if so, it iterates through each element, invoking `ReadRequestVersion` with `inArray` set to true. If the node is not an array, it treats it as a single element and calls `ReadRequestVersion` with `inArray` false. In either case, if any invocation fails the function immediately returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true` after processing all elements.

@lcmFileAPI::RemoveOldReplyFiles@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::RemoveOldReplyFiles@k_ZN9cm.body: The method scans the “reply” sub‑directory of the API instance, comparing every file it finds against the internal `ReplyFiles` map. Any file that is not present in that map is considered stale, and `cmSystemTools::RemoveFile` is invoked to delete it. The routine therefore purges orphaned reply artifacts from the filesystem, ensuring the directory only contains files tracked by the service.

@lcmFileAPI::ReportCapabilities@k_ZN9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::ReportCapabilities@k_ZN9cmF.body: The function constructs a JSON object containing a “requests” array, where each element is an object specifying a supported object kind and its compatible version(s). It appends requests for CodeModel V2, ConfigureLog V1, Cache V2, CMakeFiles V1, and Toolchains V1, then returns the resulting capability description.

@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.body: The public helper `RequestVersion` takes an rvalue reference to a `RequestVersion` object and returns a `RequestVersion` instance (often used to create or forward a request‑version object, typically inside the `cmFileAPI` implementation).

@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.body: The `RequestVersion` function is a copy‑initialization helper that accepts a const reference to another `RequestVersion` instance. It creates a new `RequestVersion` object with the same internal values, preserving immutability while avoiding unnecessary deep copies. The implementation simply forwards the fields from the source instance into the new object, ensuring the new instance reflects the original state at construction time.

@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::RequestVers.body: Retrieves the version field contained in a request header, yielding a version identifier that callers can use to perform version‑specific logic.

@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::~RequestVer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::RequestVersion::~RequestVer.body: The `~RequestVersion` public function simply returns the version of a request. It pulls the version information from the `RequestVersion` struct (declared in `cmFileAPI.h`) and provides it to callers – essentially exposing the current request’s version number or string to the rest of the system.

@lcmFileAPI::WriteJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::WriteJsonFile@k_ZN9cmFileAP.body: Writes a JSON value to a temporary file, computes a suffix via the supplied function to form a final name that obeys the 140‑char limit, atomically renames the temp file to that destination, records the filename in an internal set, and returns the resulting name.

@lcmFileAPI::WriteReplies@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::WriteReplies@k_ZN9cmFileAPI.body: The method first checks whether a query is available; if so, it guarantees a “reply” sub‑folder under the API path, builds a reply‑index structure, and writes that index to a JSON file inside that folder. Finally it calls a cleanup routine to purge stale reply files.

@lcmFileAPI::cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPIC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPIC1E.body: This constructor accepts an rvalue reference to another `cmFileAPI` instance and moves its internal state into the new object, enabling efficient transfer of resources without performing a deep copy.

@lcmFileAPI::cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPIC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPIC1E.body: The cmFileAPI constructor receives a cmake instance, builds paths for the public and user‑specific API directories based on that instance’s home output directory, and creates a JSON reader and writer configured for comment collection, strict root handling, and specific indentation for stream output.

@lcmFileAPI::operator=@k_ZN9cmFileAPIaSE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::operator=@k_ZN9cmFileAPIaSE.body: The overloaded assignment operator takes an r‑value reference to a `cmFileAPI` instance and copies its internal state into the current object, then returns a reference to the current object. It enables a move‑style assignment without the overhead of copying.

@lcmFileAPI::~cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPID1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPI::~cmFileAPI@k_ZN9cmFileAPID1.body: The public `~cmFileAPI()` function orchestrates file system interactions for the application: it exposes CRUD operations over files, runs them on a thread‑safe queue, and emits success/failure callbacks that client code can hook into.

@lcmFileAPICMakeFilesDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICMakeFilesDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.body: The function constructs a CMakeFiles object using the supplied cmFileAPI instance and the specified version, then immediately invokes and returns the result of that object’s Dump() method.

@lcmFileAPICacheDump@k_Z18cmFileAPICache.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICacheDump@k_Z18cmFileAPICache.body: Creates a `Cache` object from the supplied `cmFileAPI` and version, and immediately returns the output of `cache.Dump()`.

@lcmFileAPICodemodelDump@k_Z22cmFileAPIC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICodemodelDump@k_Z22cmFileAPIC.body: Creates a Codemodel from the supplied `cmFileAPI` and the specified version, then returns the JSON value produced by that model’s `Dump()` method.

@lcmFileAPICommand@k_Z16cmFileAPICommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPICommand@k_Z16cmFileAPICommand.body: The function checks that the argument list is non‑empty, records an error in the status object otherwise, creates a static table that maps the keyword `"QUERY"` to its handler, and finally dispatches the call to that handler by invoking the subcommand table with the first argument, the full argument list, and the status object.

@lcmFileAPIConfigureLogDump@k_Z25cmFileA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPIConfigureLogDump@k_Z25cmFileA.body: The function constructs a `ConfigureLog` helper with the supplied `cmFileAPI` instance and the specified version, then immediately invokes that helper’s `Dump()` method and returns the resulting `Json::Value` to the caller.

@lcmFileAPIToolchainsDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileAPIToolchainsDump@k_Z23cmFileAPI.body: Creates a `Toolchains` object with the given `fileAPI` and `version`, then simply returns the result of `toolchains.Dump()`.

@lcmFileLock::IsLocked@k_ZNK10cmFileLock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::IsLocked@k_ZNK10cmFileLock.body: The method returns true if the supplied file name string matches the instance’s stored filename; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmFileLock::Lock@k_ZN10cmFileLock4Lock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::Lock@k_ZN10cmFileLock4Lock.body: The `Lock` method first validates the provided path and checks that the lock object isn’t already be holding a lock. It records the path, attempts to open the file, and then performs either an indefinite lock or a timed lock depending on the supplied timeout value. If any step fails, the internal state is rolled back and the function returns a failure result.

@lcmFileLock::Release@k_ZN10cmFileLock7R.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::Release@k_ZN10cmFileLock7R.body: The function first checks whether a file was actually locked; if not, it immediately reports success. Otherwise it calls the operating‑system helper to unlock the file descriptor, clears the stored filename, closes the descriptor, and returns a success flag unless the unlock operation failed, in which case it reports a system error.

@lcmFileLock::cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLoc.author: AI Short Overview
