@lcmFileLock::cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLoc.body: The `cmFileLock` constructors obtain an exclusive lock on a file identified by a path during construction and automatically release the lock when the object is destroyed, ensuring that any operations performed while the object is alive do not interfere with other processes that might try to access the same file.

@lcmFileLock::~cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLock::~cmFileLock@k_ZN10cmFileLo.body:
When a `cmFileLock` object is destroyed, its destructor checks whether the `Filename` member is empty.  
If it isn’t, the object calls its `Release()` method to drop the lock, discards the returned `cmFileLockResult` value (the static‑cast line does nothing useful), and asserts that the release succeeded (`IsOk()` must be true).

@lcmFileLockPool::IsAlreadyLocked@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::IsAlreadyLocked@k_ZNK1.body:
The routine scans the internal collections of **function‑level**, **file‑level**, and the single **process‑level** scopes.  
It iterates through each collection, queries the scope for a lock on the supplied filename, and immediately returns `true` if any scope reports the file as already locked; if none do, it returns `false`.

@lcmFileLockPool::LockFileScope@k_ZN14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::LockFileScope@k_ZN14cm.body: Checks if the requested file is already locked; if so, it returns an “already‑locked” status. Otherwise, it verifies that there is at least one file‑scope in the pool and then delegates the lock request to the most recent scope, returning that scope’s result.

@lcmFileLockPool::LockFunctionScope@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::LockFunctionScope@k_ZN.body:
The function first checks if the requested file is already locked; if so, it immediately returns an “already‑locked” result.  
If there are no function scopes registered, it returns a “no‑function” result.  
Otherwise it forwards the lock request to the most recently added scope (the back of the `FunctionScopes` vector) and returns that scope’s result.

@lcmFileLockPool::LockProcessScope@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::LockProcessScope@k_ZN1.body:
The function first checks whether the requested file is already locked by the current process.  
If it is, it immediately returns a result representing the “already locked” state.  
Otherwise, it forwards the lock request to its `ProcessScope` helper, passing the file name and timeout, and returns the resulting lock status.

@lcmFileLockPool::PopFileScope@k_ZN14cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PopFileScope@k_ZN14cmF.body: The method removes the most recently added scope from the pool, asserting that at least one scope is present before performing the pop.

@lcmFileLockPool::PopFunctionScope@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PopFunctionScope@k_ZN1.body: Removes the most‑recently added function scope from the internal stack, after first verifying that the stack is not empty.

@lcmFileLockPool::PushFileScope@k_ZN14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PushFileScope@k_ZN14cm.body: PushFileScope appends a new file‑scope entry into the internal collection.

@lcmFileLockPool::PushFunctionScope@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::PushFunctionScope@k_ZN.body: The method adds a new, default‑constructed entry to the `FunctionScopes` container of the pool instance. It simply pushes a fresh scope onto the internal stack, preparing the pool to track a new function context.

@lcmFileLockPool::Release@k_ZN14cmFileLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::Release@k_ZN14cmFileLo.body: The method iterates through each registered scope in `FunctionScopes` and `FileScopes`, invoking their `Release` routines for the supplied filename. If any scope reports a non‑OK result, the function immediately returns that error. Only when all scope releases succeed does it finally call `ProcessScope.Release` and return its outcome.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.body: The function `operator()` is a const member that takes a reference to a `cmFileLock` object and returns a `bool`. It performs whatever checks or actions are required by the surrounding code—most likely inspecting the passed‑in lock object and determining a success/failure condition for whatever operation that the lock is meant to guard.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.body: Checks whether a specific file is locked by calling `IsLocked` on the provided lock object.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::IsAlreadyLo.body: This const member scans the internal `Locks` vector for the given file name. It invokes `std::any_of` with a lambda that queries each `cmFileLock` via its `IsLocked` method, returning a single boolean that signals whether the file is already locked in the pool.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Lock@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Lock@k_ZN14.body: The function tries to acquire an exclusive lock on the named file for the lifetime of the current `ScopePool` instance. It creates a `cmFileLock` object, calls its `Lock` method with the supplied filename and timeout, and if the lock succeeds it stores the lock in the pool’s internal `Locks` container before returning an “ok” result. If the lock attempt fails, it simply propagates the failure result back to the caller.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Release@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::Release@k_Z.body:
Iterates over the collection of file‑locks stored in the pool.  
If it encounters a lock that currently owns the specified filename, it invokes that lock’s `Release()` method and returns its outcome immediately.  
When no matching lock is found, the routine simply reports success (e.g., `MakeOk()`), indicating the file was already unlocked or never locked.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.body: This constructor performs a move‑construction of a `ScopePool` object. It is marked `noexcept`, indicating that it guarantees no exceptions during the move and that the standard library can use it in exception‑safe contexts. The `= default;` definition delegates the actual implementation to the compiler, ensuring the compiler generates an efficient, implicitly generated move constructor that correctly transfers all member state without any extra copying or allocation.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::ScopePool@k.body: The constructor simply creates a new `ScopePool` instance using the compiler‑generated default constructor. No additional logic or resource allocation is performed; any members that exist are left at their default‑value state.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::operator=@k.body: Moves the lock set from the temporary `other` into the current pool, guarding against self‑assignment and marking the operation noexcept. It then returns a reference to the modified pool.

@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::~ScopePool@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::ScopePool::~ScopePool@.body: When a `ScopePool` object goes out of scope, the destructor is invoked to clean up its internal state—releasing any acquired locks and freeing associated resources before the object is destroyed.

@lcmFileLockPool::cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14c.body: The constructor prepares the internal lock‑pool data structures, allocating any needed resources and establishing the initial lock‑tracking state that the pool will use to coordinate file‑level locking during runtime.

@lcmFileLockPool::~cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockPool::~cmFileLockPool@k_ZN14.body: The `~cmFileLockPool` destructor cleans up the pool’s internal data structures, ensuring that any pending file‑level locks held by the pool are released and that the pool’s resources are properly freed before the object is destroyed.

@lcmFileLockResult::IsOk@k_ZNK16cmFileLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::IsOk@k_ZNK16cmFileLo.body: Returns true if the internal `Type` value equals `OK`; otherwise returns false.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeAlreadyLocked@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeAlreadyLocked@k_.body: The function constructs and returns a `cmFileLockResult` object that signifies an “already‑locked” condition; its status field is set to the predefined `ALREADY_LOCKED` value and its accompanying numeric indicator is zero.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeNoFunction@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeNoFunction@k_ZN1.body: Creates a `cmFileLockResult` that signals “no function” by returning the `NO_FUNCTION` status and a zero‑error flag.

@lcmFileLockResult::MakeOk@k_ZN16cmFileL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::MakeOk@k_ZN16cmFileL.body: The `MakeOk` method constructs and returns a `cmFileLockResult` instance representing a successful operation: it sets the status field to `OK` and the error code to `0`.

@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::cmFileLockResult@k_Z.body: The constructor creates a new instance from an existing one by copying all of its internal state (e.g., lock identifiers, status flags, and any associated metadata). It performs a shallow copy of primitive data members, and for complex members it performs a deep copy or move‑semantics to preserve resource ownership semantics. This guarantees that the newly‑constructed object is fully independent while still reflecting the same lock state as the source object.

@lcmFileLockResult::~cmFileLockResult@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileLockResult::~cmFileLockResult@k_.body: The function returns a `cmFileLockResult` object that reports whether the file‑locking operation succeeded and, if not, supplies an error message.

@lcmFileSet::AddDirectoryEntry@k_ZN9cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::AddDirectoryEntry@k_ZN9cmFi.body: Adds a directory string to the internal collection by moving it into `DirectoryEntries`.

@lcmFileSet::AddFileEntry@k_ZN9cmFileSet.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::AddFileEntry@k_ZN9cmFileSet.body: The method takes a `BTree<std::string>` parameter and appends it to the `FileEntries` container using move semantics to avoid copying the entire object. It performs no other logic—simply enqueues the argument into the internal list.

@lcmFileSet::ClearDirectoryEntries@k_ZN9.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::ClearDirectoryEntries@k_ZN9.body: The `ClearDirectoryEntries` method clears the internal collection that tracks directory entries, effectively resetting the file set to an empty state. It simply calls the container’s `clear()` routine, ensuring all stored entries are removed and any associated resources are released.

@lcmFileSet::ClearFileEntries@k_ZN9cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::ClearFileEntries@k_ZN9cmFil.body: The method simply invokes the container’s `clear()` routine, which removes every element from the `FileEntries` member so the set becomes empty.

@lcmFileSet::CompileDirectoryEntries@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::CompileDirectoryEntries@k_Z.body: Iterates through each directory entry, parses each of its contained expressions into compiled generator objects using the stored back‑trace context, and collects those objects into a result vector that is returned.

@lcmFileSet::CompileFileEntries@k_ZNK9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::CompileFileEntries@k_ZNK9cm.body: The method walks through the stored `FileEntries` entries, and for each entry it parses each individual string in the associated list into a `cmGeneratorExpression`. The resulting expression objects are collected into a vector of `unique_ptr` objects and returned.

@lcmFileSet::CopyEntries@k_ZN9cmFileSet1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::CopyEntries@k_ZN9cmFileSet1.body: Merges the directory and file entries from another file set into the current instance by appending their vectors.

@lcmFileSet::EvaluateDirectoryEntries@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::EvaluateDirectoryEntries@k_.body: This method iterates over a collection of compiled generator expressions, resolves each entry’s directory path relative to the current source directory, and then collapses that path. It records each resolved path in a cache along with an optional file‑ID. For every new entry it checks against all previously‑added directories to ensure that no two entries form a sub‑directory relationship; if such a conflict is found it reports a fatal error and returns an empty vector. The function finally returns a vector of the unique, collapsed directory strings that survive these checks.

@lcmFileSet::EvaluateFileEntry@k_ZNK9cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::EvaluateFileEntry@k_ZNK9cmF.body: The function evaluates a list of file expressions against a set of allowed base directories. It resolves each expression to an absolute path, normalizes it, and verifies that the file resides inside one of the supplied directories. If a file falls outside those directories it reports a fatal error and aborts; otherwise it records the file under its relative directory in the provided map.

@lcmFileSet::GetDirectoryEntries@k_ZNK9c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetDirectoryEntries@k_ZNK9c.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored list of directory entries, allowing callers to inspect the contents without being able to alter them.

@lcmFileSet::GetFileEntries@k_ZNK9cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetFileEntries@k_ZNK9cmFile.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored vector of string‑based entries, exposing the collection without copying or altering the underlying data.

@lcmFileSet::GetName@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetName@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the stored name, letting callers read the string without copying or modifying it.

@lcmFileSet::GetType@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetType@k_ZNK9cmFileSet7Get.body: The function returns the stored type string; it is a trivial accessor that never modifies the object. It simply returns a reference to the internal member `Type`, guaranteeing that the returned value is read‑only and that no copy of the string is performed.

@lcmFileSet::GetVisibility@k_ZNK9cmFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::GetVisibility@k_ZNK9cmFileS.body: A simple, read‑only accessor that returns the current value of the instance’s visibility flag.

@lcmFileSet::IsValidName@k_ZN9cmFileSet1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::IsValidName@k_ZN9cmFileSet1.body: The function verifies whether a given string matches a specific regular‑expression pattern. It creates a single, static `RegularExpression` instance with the pattern `"^[a-z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$"`; the pattern requires the string to start with a lowercase letter or digit, followed by zero or more alphanumeric or underscore characters. It returns `true` if the entire string satisfies that pattern, otherwise `false`.

@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.body: The `cmFileSet` constructor takes an rvalue reference to another `cmFileSet` instance and moves its internal file‑descriptor set into the new object, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state.

@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.body: Creates a cmFileSet instance by storing a reference to the supplied cmake object and initializing the internal fields Name, Type and Visibility.

@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetC1E.body: The `cmFileSet` function is a copy‑constructor/assignment‑like helper that takes another `cmFileSet` instance (passed by const‑reference) and copies its internal state into the current object. It’s primarily used to initialize or re‑initialize a `cmFileSet` from an existing one while preserving the underlying file‑set representation.

@lcmFileSet::~cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetD1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSet::~cmFileSet@k_ZN9cmFileSetD1.body:
The `~cmFileSet()` function is the destructor for the `cmFileSet` class.  
When invoked it performs any required cleanup for the file‑set instance—closing file handles, freeing allocated buffers, and erasing any internal state so that subsequent operations do not operate on dangling resources.

@lcmFileSetTypeCanBeIncluded@k_Z26cmFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSetTypeCanBeIncluded@k_Z26cmFile.body: The function compares the supplied string against the literal `"HEADERS"` and returns `true` only when the strings match exactly; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmFileSetVisibilityFromName@k_Z27cmFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSetVisibilityFromName@k_Z27cmFil.body:
The function maps a string view to one of the three visibility enums.  
If `name` matches “INTERFACE”, “PUBLIC”, or “PRIVATE”, it returns the corresponding enum value; otherwise it logs a fatal‑error message and falls back to `Private`.

@lcmFileSetVisibilityIsForInterface@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSetVisibilityIsForInterface@k_Z3.body: The function checks whether the supplied visibility value is considered “for an interface” (i.e. Interface or Public) and returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmFileSetVisibilityIsForSelf@k_Z28cmFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSetVisibilityIsForSelf@k_Z28cmFi.body: It returns true only when the visibility value is `Private` or `Public`; for any other value (including `Interface`) it returns false.

@lcmFileSetVisibilityToName@k_Z25cmFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFileSetVisibilityToName@k_Z25cmFileS.body:
The function receives a `cmFileSetVisibility` value and returns the corresponding string view by dispatching a `switch` on the enum:  
- `Interface` → `"INTERFACE"_s`  
- `Public` → `"PUBLIC"_s`  
- `Private` → `"PRIVATE"_s`  

If the value is none of these, it returns an empty string view.

@lcmFindFile@k_Z10cmFindFileRKSt6vectorI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindFile@k_Z10cmFindFileRKSt6vectorI.body: The function forwards the supplied argument list and status reference to a helper object that performs the search and returns its success flag.

@lcmFindFileCommand::cmFindFileCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindFileCommand::cmFindFileCommand@k.body: This constructor registers the command “find_file” with the base class, sets it to treat a resolved result as a file path by enabling `IncludeFileInPath` and marking the variable type as `cmStateEnums::FILEPATH`.

@lcmFindNot@k_Z9cmFindNotRKT_RKT0_@f./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindNot@k_Z9cmFindNotRKT_RKT0_@f./So.body: `cmFindNot` returns a const iterator pointing to the first element in the provided range that differs from the value `t`. It simply forwards the range’s begin and end iterators to `std::find_if` with a lambda that checks inequality, yielding an iterator past the matching element. The implementation relies on the range providing `begin()`/`end()` and a `const_iterator` type that matches the range’s internal iterator type.

@lcmFindPackageCall::cmFindPackageCall@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageCall::cmFindPackageCall@k.body: The constructor creates a new `cmFindPackageCall` instance by moving the internal state from the supplied temporary object, ensuring that all owned resources are transferred without duplication.

@lcmFindPackageCall::cmFindPackageCall@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageCall::cmFindPackageCall@k.body: Creates a `cmFindPackageCall` instance from an existing one. It accepts a constant reference to another `cmFindPackageCall` (the unnamed parameter) and produces a new object that captures the same call‑context information for later use.

@lcmFindPackageCall::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageCall::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The operator= function copies the internal state of a supplied `cmFindPackageCall` instance into the current object, returning a reference to that instance to allow fluent chaining of call‑construction steps.

@lcmFindPackageCall::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageCall::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The assignment operator copies the package‑level data from the source `cmFindPackageCall` into the target object, preserving any existing internal bookkeeping. It simply assigns the source’s `name`, `version`, and `required` fields to the current instance and returns `*this`.

@lcmFindPackageCall::~cmFindPackageCall@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageCall::~cmFindPackageCall@.body: The `~cmFindPackageCall` function is the entry point that performs the lookup of a package based on a call name. It parses the supplied package identifier, interacts with the internal package registry to resolve the package metadata, and finally returns a pointer (or reference) to the corresponding package object. Internally it also flags any errors in the lookup path (e.g., missing package, ambiguous names, or version conflicts) so the caller can react accordingly.

@lcmFindPackageStack::cmFindPackageStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageStack::cmFindPackageStack.body: The routine constructs a new `cmFindPackageStack` instance by taking ownership of an existing stack object (via rvalue reference). It wires up the internal representation of that stack—primarily the list of packages and their dependency relationships—so that the rest of the code can query the stack for the next package to process. The implementation is referenced in the project at line 25 of `cmFindPackageStack.h`, where the class definition and the constructor are declared.

@lcmFindPackageStack::cmFindPackageStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageStack::cmFindPackageStack.body:
The routine extracts the internal package‑stack from a `cmFindPackageStack` instance.  
It takes a constant reference to the stack object, validates that the object is properly initialized, and returns a reference to the internal vector (or list) that holds the resolved package identifiers. The function is used by other components to query the current package stack without modifying it.

@lcmFindPackageStack::cmFindPackageStack.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPackageStack::cmFindPackageStack.body: The `cmFindPackageStack` function performs the package‑resolution logic: it scans the project’s package list, resolves each package’s dependencies, pushes resolved packages onto a stack, and finally returns that stack for use elsewhere in the build system.

@lcmFindPathCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::InitialPass@k_ZN17c.body: The function first sets the internal path‑name flag to “INCLUDE”, then parses the supplied argument list. If parsing fails it returns false. It turns on debug mode based on the variable name, and if the header was already resolved it normalises the cached result and returns true. Otherwise it performs a header search, stores the string result, and finally returns true.

@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFindPathCommand::cmFindPathCommand@k.body: The constructor creates a cmFindPathCommand instance, initializing its internal state: the path‑environment variable is set to “INCLUDE”, the flag to include a file is cleared, and it stores a brief documentation string plus the variable type designation (PATH).

@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.body: The function is a thin wrapper that forwards a move‑only `cmFortranCompiler` instance to the underlying compiler machinery—initializing any internal state needed before invoking the compiler’s entry point.

@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.body: A copy constructor that duplicates the internal state of an existing `cmFortranCompiler` instance—copying its configuration, language settings, and any internal state used during compilation.

@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranCompiler::cmFortranCompiler@k.body: The `cmFortranCompiler()` function serves as a thin façade around the system’s Fortran compiler interface. Internally it resolves the compiler configuration, forwards the compilation request to the underlying Fortran engine, and propagates the resulting error or success status back to the caller. This abstraction keeps the rest of the codebase decoupled from the specific compiler command‑line flags or build options, enabling easier swapping or unit‑testing of the compiler stage without touching higher‑level logic.

@lcmFortranCompiler::~cmFortranCompiler@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranCompiler::~cmFortranCompiler@.body: The `cmFortranCompiler` function parses a Fortran source file, performs semantic analysis against the language’s type system, and emits an intermediate representation (IR) for subsequent code generation. It integrates with the build system to drive the full compilation pipeline and exposes error diagnostics back to the caller.

@lcmFortranFile::cmFortranFile@k_ZN13cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranFile::cmFortranFile@k_ZN13cmF.body: This routine takes an open file stream, a buffer state flag, and a string identifier, and writes a Fortran‑style header into the stream—primarily recording the buffer state and the supplied string in a format that downstream code can parse.

@lcmFortranFile::cmFortranFile@k_ZN13cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranFile::cmFortranFile@k_ZN13cmF.body: Handles opening and parsing a Fortran source file; it reads the file into a buffer, tokenizes the contents, and returns a structured representation (e.g., a parse tree) for downstream processing.

@lcmFortranFile::~cmFortranFile@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranFile::~cmFortranFile@k_ZN13cm.body: The function `~cmFortranFile()` creates a Fortran‑style file for the project: it gathers the necessary header data, writes the formatted code blocks into the file, and returns a status flag indicating whether the operation succeeded.

@lcmFortranLexer_GetCurrentBuffer@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranLexer_GetCurrentBuffer@k_Z31c.body: The routine simply interprets the supplied scanner handle as the internal scanner structure and returns the active buffer flag via the `YY_CURRENT_BUFFER` macro.

@lcmFortranModuleAppendUpperLower@k_ZL31.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranModuleAppendUpperLower@k_ZL31.body: The function parses a Fortran module file name, detects whether it ends with “.mod”, “.sub” or “.smod”, isolates the base part before the extension, converts that base to upper‑case, and appends the original extension back. It stores this upper‑case string in `mod_upper` and preserves the original full name in `mod_lower`.

@lcmFortranParser_Error@k_Z21cmFortranPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_Error@k_Z21cmFortranPa.body: The function assigns an error message to the parser’s Error field, falling back to a generic “unknown error” string when no message is supplied.

@lcmFortranParser_FilePop@k_Z23cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_FilePop@k_Z23cmFortran.body: The routine removes the most recently opened file from the parser’s internal file stack, closes its file handle, and restores the lexer’s input buffer to the next file on the stack, ensuring the lexer continues scanning the previous source file.

@lcmFortranParser_FilePush@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_FilePush@k_Z24cmFortra.body: The routine opens the named file, creates a new lexer buffer for it, switches the lexer to that buffer, and pushes the resulting file object onto the parser’s internal stack. It returns `true` only when the file is opened and the buffer switch succeeds; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmFortranParser_GetInInterface@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_GetInInterface@k_Z30cm.body: The function simply returns the current value of the parser’s `InInterface` flag, indicating whether the parser is currently parsing an interface section.

@lcmFortranParser_GetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_GetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.body: The function retrieves the current value of the `OldStartcond` field from a `cmFortranParser` instance and returns that integer directly.

@lcmFortranParser_Input@k_Z21cmFortranPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_Input@k_Z21cmFortranPa.body: It reads the next chunk from the file at the top of the parser’s stack into the supplied buffer, updates a flag if the final byte read was a newline, and, if the file ends without a trailing newline, inserts one before returning the number of bytes read.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleDefine@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleDefine@k_Z26cmFort.body:
The function registers a new macro name into the parser’s macro set unless the parser is currently inside a pre‑processor false branch.  
If `InPPFalseBranch` is false, the supplied macro string is added to the `PPDefinitions` set; otherwise it is ignored.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleElif@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleElif@k_Z24cmFortra.body: `cmFortranParser_RuleElif` is a helper that participates in processing preprocessor directives for an `elif` form of an `#if` block. It examines whether the current parser position is inside a branch that has already been skipped due to a preceding false condition (the stack `SkipToEnd` is non‑empty and its top is `true`). If no other false‑branch flag (`InPPFalseBranch`) is set, it flips that flag to indicate that from this point forward the parser is now inside a false branch that will be bypassed until the corresponding `#endif`. This enables subsequent parsing stages to recognise that code inside this branch should not be tokenised further.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleElse@k_Z24cmFortra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleElse@k_Z24cmFortra.body: The function updates the parser’s flag `InPPFalseBranch` to reflect whether the current directive is inside a false pre‑processing branch. It first exits immediately if the parser is already inside a nested false branch (i.e. `InPPFalseBranch > 1`). Otherwise, it sets the flag to 1 when the top of the `SkipToEnd` stack is true, or to 0 otherwise.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleEndif@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleEndif@k_Z25cmFortr.body: It removes the most recent skip‑target from the parser’s stack and, when the parser is inside a false pre‑processor block, it decrements the counter that tracks nested false branches.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleIf@k_Z22cmFortranP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleIf@k_Z22cmFortranP.body: When the parser sees a `#if` directive it calls this routine. It records that a new pre‑processor branch has begun by pushing `false` onto the `SkipToEnd` stack, so that subsequent parsing logic knows the current block should not be skipped until the matching `#endif` is reached. This function therefore sets up the state that the parser will use to properly handle nested `#if`, `#elif`, and `#else` directives.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfdef@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfdef@k_Z25cmFortr.body: This routine signals the parser that a new pre‑processor branch has begun. It updates a stack that tracks whether the current branch should be ignored and adjusts a counter tracking nested false branches: if the parser already sat in a false branch, the counter is incremented; otherwise it either marks the start of a new false branch (when the macro is unknown) or simply flags the current branch to be skipped.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfndef@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleIfndef@k_Z26cmFort.body: The routine marks the beginning of a new pre‑processor branch by pushing a flag onto parser‑>SkipToEnd. It then checks whether the parser is already inside a false branch; if so, it increments a counter. If not, it looks up the macro name in PPDefinitions; if found, it marks the branch as false, otherwise it signals that the current branch should be skipped by setting the top of SkipToEnd to true.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleInclude@k_Z27cmFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleInclude@k_Z27cmFor.body: This routine processes an `#include` directive. It first aborts if the current pre‑processor branch is inactive, then verifies that there is an open file by asserting the file stack is non‑empty. Using the directory of the file at the stack’s top, it attempts to resolve the named file relative to that directory. If the file is found, its full path is recorded in the parser’s include set and the file is pushed onto the parsing stack so that its contents will be parsed inline. If the file cannot be located, the routine simply returns without error.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleLineDirective@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleLineDirective@k_Z3.body: The function processes a #line directive from a Fortran source file. It ignores directives that refer to built‑in placeholders (like `<built‑in>` or `<command‑line>`). For real file names it normalises backslashes to forward slashes, converts Windows‑style separators to Unix style, and, when the file can be found, records the file name in the parser’s include set.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleModule@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleModule@k_Z26cmFort.body: The function records a module name as a provided module in the parser’s internal list unless the parser is currently in a pre‑processor false branch or inside an interface block; if the parser is in an interface, it adds the lower‑cased name to the parser’s provided‑module set.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmodule@k_Z29cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmodule@k_Z29cmF.body: The routine records a submodule dependency: it normalises the module and sub‑module names to lowercase, then inserts the canonical module requirement (`module_name.mod`) and the corresponding provided submodule (`module_name@submodule_name.smod`) into the parser’s `Info` containers. It only executes this bookkeeping when the parser is not already inside a false‑branch of a preprocessing conditional.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmoduleNested@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleSubmoduleNested@k_.body: The function registers a nested‑submodule relationship in the parser’s internal dependency graph. It first normalizes all names to lower‑case, then records that the parent module’s submodule is a requirement (`Info.Requires`) and that the nested submodule is a provision (`Info.Provides`). If the parser is currently in a false positive‑preprocessing branch, the operation is skipped.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleUndef@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleUndef@k_Z25cmFortr.body: If the parser is not inside a false pre‑processor branch, the routine checks the parser’s macro definition table for the supplied name. When that name appears in the map it is erased, thereby removing the macro from future expansions.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleUse@k_Z23cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleUse@k_Z23cmFortran.body: The function registers a module dependency: it first checks whether the parser is in a pre‑processor false branch; if not, it normalises the supplied module name to lower‑case and inserts it into the parser’s `Requires` set.

@lcmFortranParser_RuleUseIntrinsic@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_RuleUseIntrinsic@k_Z32.body: When the parser hits a “use intrinsic” directive it simply normalises the supplied module name to lowercase and records that module in its intrinsic set, provided the current parse state isn’t already flagged as a false‑branch.

@lcmFortranParser_SetInInterface@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_SetInInterface@k_Z30cm.body: When called, the function checks a flag (`InPPFalseBranch`) on the parser. If that flag is set, the function exits immediately, leaving `InInterface` unchanged. Otherwise it writes the supplied boolean into `parser->InInterface`. The method is a simple conditional setter that only changes the interface‑state when the parser is not in the special false‑branch state.

@lcmFortranParser_SetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_SetOldStartcond@k_Z31c.body: The function assigns the supplied integer value to the parser’s `OldStartcond` member.

@lcmFortranParser_StringAppend@k_Z28cmFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_StringAppend@k_Z28cmFo.body: The function simply appends the supplied character to the parser’s current token string.

@lcmFortranParser_StringEnd@k_Z25cmFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_StringEnd@k_Z25cmFortr.body: The routine simply hands back the underlying C‑string pointer for the parser’s current token string. It just accesses the parser’s `TokenString` field and returns the raw character array via `c_str()`.

@lcmFortranParser_StringStart@k_Z27cmFor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_StringStart@k_Z27cmFor.body: Resets the parser’s token buffer so the next string token starts with an empty string.

@lcmFortranParser_s::FindIncludeFile@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::FindIncludeFile@k_Z.body: The function first checks whether the given include name already specifies a full path; if so, it verifies the file exists and returns that path. If not, it searches first in the directory of the including file, then iteratively through the configured include‑path list, assigning the first matching file path it finds to the output string and signalling success. If no match is found in any of those locations, the function reports failure.

@lcmFortranParser_s::ModName@k_ZNK17cmFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::ModName@k_ZNK17cmFo.body: The function generates a module filename by concatenating the supplied module identifier with the suffix “.mod”.

@lcmFortranParser_s::SModName@k_ZNK17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::SModName@k_ZNK17cmF.body: The function builds a module name string. It uses a default “.mod” extension unless a custom extension is supplied. If the separator string is empty, it returns the sub‑name followed by that extension; otherwise it concatenates the base module name, the separator, the sub‑name, and the extension.

@lcmFortranParser_s::cmFortranParser_s@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::cmFortranParser_s@k.body:
Creates a parser instance wired to a specific compiler.  
The constructor takes the compiler, a list of include paths, a set of macro definitions and a reference to source‑level info.  
During construction it flags that the parser is not currently inside an interface block, clears any pending pre‑processor false‑branch counter, and hooks up the lexical scanner by calling the generated lexer‑initialisation routine.  
Finally it constructs a dummy buffer (never actually read) to use as the fall‑back buffer when the input stack is exhausted, and switches the scanner to that buffer.

@lcmFortranParser_s::~cmFortranParser_s@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranParser_s::~cmFortranParser_s@.body: The destructor simply releases the internal scanner by calling `cmFortran_yylex_destroy` on the stored `Scanner` member before the `cmFortranParser_s` instance is deallocated.

@lcmFortranSourceInfo::cmFortranSourceIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranSourceInfo::cmFortranSourceIn.body: Retrieves metadata about a Fortran source object—returning a lightweight struct that exposes file‑path, line‑range, and associated parsed nodes, enabling callers to locate and inspect the original source without re‑parsing it.

@lcmFortranStreamContainsSequence@k_ZL31.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranStreamContainsSequence@k_ZL31.body: The function scans a text stream for a particular sequence of characters. It reads each character sequentially; whenever a read character matches the next expected character in the given sequence it advances the match counter. If a mismatch occurs it drops back to the start of the sequence. When the counter reaches the sequence length it returns true; otherwise if the stream ends early it returns false.

@lcmFortranStreamsDiffer@k_ZL22cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortranStreamsDiffer@k_ZL22cmFortran.body: The function reads characters from both streams one‑by‑one until a difference is found or until both streams hit end‑of‑file together. If it reaches the end of both streams at the same time, it concludes the streams are identical and returns false. If any mismatch or an early end‑of‑file occurs, it breaks out of the loop and returns true, indicating the streams differ.

@lcmFortran_yy_create_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_create_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.body: Creates a new buffer state object, allocates space for the internal character buffer (with an extra 2‑byte guard area), marks the buffer as owned, and invokes yy_init_buffer() to fill the buffer from the supplied file. If any allocation fails, it aborts with a fatal error. The function then returns the populated buffer state.

@lcmFortran_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z26cmFort.body: The routine tears down a previously‑allocated scanner buffer. It first verifies that the supplied buffer pointer is non‑null, then clears the global indicator that this buffer is the active one. After that it frees the internal character array if the buffer was owned by the scanner and finally frees the buffer structure itself, returning control to the caller.

@lcmFortran_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z29cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z29cmF.body: The routine replaces the scanner’s current buffer with the one supplied in `new_buffer`. It first pushes the current buffer onto an internal stack (implicitly via `yyensure_buffer_stack`), writes the current buffer’s contents back to the hold‑area if a buffer was previously active, then installs the new buffer’s state pointers. Finally it marks that a buffer switch has taken place (`yyg->yy_did_buffer_switch_on_eof = 1`).

@lcmFortran_yyerror@k_ZL17cmFortran_yyer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyerror@k_ZL17cmFortran_yyer.body: Retrieves the parser instance stored in the scanner’s extra data and passes the supplied error string to the parser’s error‑handling routine.

@lcmFortran_yyget_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyget_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.body: The function simply pulls the `yyextra` field out of the scanner state structure. It receives a `yyscan_t` handle, casts it to the internal `yyguts_t` struct, and returns the stored `yyextra` value.

@lcmFortran_yylex@k_Z15cmFortran_yylexP1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yylex@k_Z15cmFortran_yylexP1.body: cmFortran_yylex initializes the lexical analyzer on its first call, then repeatedly reads characters from the input buffer, uses the state transition tables to recognize tokens, and on acceptance restores the matched text and fires the corresponding action code (which handles Fortran string literals, comments, preprocessor directives, and simple operators). It also manages buffer switches and EOF conditions, returning token codes to the parser.

@lcmFortran_yylex_destroy@k_Z23cmFortran.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yylex_destroy@k_Z23cmFortran.body: This routine tears down a yyscanner instance. It walks up the internal buffer stack, deleting every buffer record until none remain. Then it frees the buffer‑stack array, the start‑condition stack, and finally re‑initializes the global state for the next scan. At the end it deallocates the scanner struct itself, clearing the pointer and returning success.

@lcmFortran_yylex_init@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yylex_init@k_Z20cmFortran_yy.body: This function accepts a pointer to a global state structure, validates the pointer, allocates a fresh `yyguts_t` block, zero‑initializes it, and then hands the freshly‑allocated structure over to the detailed init routine (`yy_init_globals`). If allocation fails or the pointer is null, it sets `errno` accordingly and returns an error code.

@lcmFortran_yyparse@k_Z17cmFortran_yypar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyparse@k_Z17cmFortran_yypar.body: The `yyparse` routine drives a hand‑written LALR parser: it keeps a state stack, a semantic value stack, and a look‑ahead token. On each shift it reads the next token from the scanner, updates the state using the parsing tables, and pushes the semantic value onto the stack. When a rule matches it pops the required number of symbols, executes the semantic action (which may call helper routines such as `cmFortranParser_Rule…`), and then pushes the resulting value onto the stack. Errors trigger a recovery loop that pops states until a state that can shift an error token is found, after which normal parsing continues. At end of input or on explicit accept/abort the routine cleans up both stacks, releases any allocated buffers, and returns an error count or success flag.

@lcmFortran_yyset_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yyset_extra@k_Z21cmFortran_y.body: The routine simply records a user‑supplied extra token in the scanner’s internal context by casting the opaque handle to the concrete `yyguts_t` struct and assigning the value to the internal `yyextra` member.

@lcmFortran_yystype::cmFortran_yystype@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yystype::cmFortran_yystype@k.body: The constructor creates a new `cmFortran_yystype` object by copying all of the fields from the supplied instance, performing a shallow copy of the member values.

@lcmFortran_yystype::cmFortran_yystype@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yystype::cmFortran_yystype@k.body: `cmFortran_yystype` is the semantic‑value type used by the parser. It bundles the data that the lexer returns for each token—usually an integer code, a string value, or a user‑defined value (e.g., a symbol table entry). The struct is pushed onto the parsing stack during semantic actions so that later productions can access the exact value that has been parsed, and the parser can drop it on the stack after it’s no longer needed.

@lcmFortran_yystype::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yystype::operator=@k_ZN17cmF.body: The `operator=` overload assigns every member of the right‑hand operand to the corresponding member of the current object, then returns a reference to *this*. It performs a straightforward member‑wise copy and does not perform any validation or side‑effects.

@lcmFortran_yystype::~cmFortran_yystype@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFortran_yystype::~cmFortran_yystype@.body: The `~cmFortran_yystype` function simply returns the type‐specific `cmFortran_yystype` struct used by the parser, providing a lightweight interface for retrieving the current parsing state.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch@k_ZN.body: The private pure‑virtual `ArgumentsMatch` takes a `cmListFileFunction const&` and returns `true` only when the arguments supplied in that instance satisfy the expected signature; otherwise it returns `false`. Sub‑classes override it to provide the concrete matching logic, and this helper is used in parts such as the call site in *cmFunctionBlocker.h* to validate arguments before proceeding.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName@k_ZN.body: The pure virtual member must be overridden by every concrete subclass to supply the literal text that marks the end of its corresponding command. It returns a `string_view` representing that terminal keyword or token used during parsing or code generation.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::GetStartingContext@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::GetStartingContext@.body: The method returns a constant reference to the `StartingContext` member, allowing callers to read the context without permitting any mutation of the underlying object.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN17cmFunc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN17cmFunc.body: The `Replay` member re‑executes a set of `cmListFileFunction` objects supplied in a vector. In practice, a subclass implements the exact replay logic – e.g. applying each function to an internal data structure – and returns `true` if all calls succeed or `false` on any failure. Because the function is pure virtual, every concrete subclass must override it, ensuring that the class‑specific replay behaviour is supplied while keeping the interface uniform.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::StartCommandName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::StartCommandName@k_.body: The function supplies the command string that identifies the concrete command implementation; concrete classes must override it to return the specific command name.

@lcmFunctionBlocker::~cmFunctionBlocker@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmFunctionBlocker::~cmFunctionBlocker@.body: When a `cmFunctionBlocker` object is destroyed, this virtual destructor runs to release any held resources, allowing derived types to override cleanup behaviour.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::addToCurrentP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::addToCurrentP.body: The function grabs the last dependency object in the `Content` list and, based on the helper’s current state, appends the supplied string either to the last rule in that dependency’s `rules` vector (if the vector is non‑empty) or to the last path in its `paths` vector. If the `Content` list is empty, or the relevant vector is empty, the function exits early. If the helper is in the `Failed` state it immediately returns without modification.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newDependency.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newDependency.body: The routine switches the helper’s state to *Dependency* and guarantees the current content entry has a trailing empty path entry—adding a new placeholder string whenever the last path slot is missing or already non‑empty.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newEntry@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newEntry@k_ZN.body: If the current state is `Rule` and there is at least one rule already present in the last element of `Content`, the helper immediately switches to the `Failed` state and returns. Otherwise, it marks the state as `Rule`, appends a new element to `Content`, and calls `newRule()` to initialize that entry.

@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newRuleOrDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfileLexerHelper::newRuleOrDepe.body: The method checks the current helper state and dispatches to the corresponding routine: when the state equals Rule it calls newRule(), otherwise when it equals Dependency it calls newDependency(). It assumes no other state values are possible; if an unexpected state appears nothing will be invoked.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_create_buffer@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_create_buffer@k_Z29cmG.body: Creates a new buffer structure, allocates memory for the internal buffer and its bookkeeping, sets the buffer length, marks the buffer as owned by the parser, calls the helper to fill it with file data, and finally returns a handle to the caller.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_delete_buffer@k_Z29cmG.body: The routine clears and frees a buffer that belongs to the scanner: if the buffer is already null it exits; otherwise it clears the current‑buffer flag when applicable, frees the internal char array only when it was allocated by the system, and finally releases the buffer structure itself. It safeguards against double frees by inspecting the ownership flag before calling the deallocation helper.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z28cmGc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_flush_buffer@k_Z28cmGc.body: The routine clears the buffer’s contents, writes two sentinel bytes that force the scanner to transition to its end‑of‑buffer state and then jam state, resets all counters and flags to their start‑state values, and if this buffer is the active one, it forces a re‑initialisation of the scanning state.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_init_buffer@k_ZL27cmGc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_init_buffer@k_ZL27cmGc.body: The `yy_init_buffer` routine wires up a new scanner buffer: it clears the internal buffer, assigns the supplied `FILE*` as the source, marks the buffer as ready to fill, and records whether the file is a terminal to flag interactive mode. If the buffer being initialized isn’t the current one, the line‑number and column counters are re‑seeded to the start of a file. Finally, the routine restores the system’s `errno` value after its internal work.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_load_buffer_state@k_ZL.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_load_buffer_state@k_ZL.body: The function copies the current lexical buffer status into a `yyguts_t` structure: it sets `yy_n_chars` to the number of characters in the active buffer, records the current buffer pointer into `yy_c_buf_p` and `yytext_ptr`, stores the input file pointer in `yyin`, and captures the first character into `yy_hold_char`. This snapshot allows the scanner to resume correctly after a context change.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z27cmGcc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_buffer@k_Z27cmGcc.body: The function verifies that the supplied raw buffer has enough space for the end‑of‑buffer markers, allocates a `yy_buffer_state` structure, populates its fields (size, position, flags for interactive mode, etc.), switches the scanner to this new buffer with `yy_switch_to_buffer`, and returns the initialized buffer pointer.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z26cmGccD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_bytes@k_Z26cmGccD.body: This function allocates a temporary buffer that contains the supplied byte stream followed by two sentinel markers (the custom `YY_END_OF_BUFFER_CHAR`), then hands that buffer over to `yy_scan_buffer`. It marks the resulting buffer object as “our buffer”, allowing the caller to discard it safely after parsing is finished.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_string@k_Z27cmGcc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_scan_string@k_Z27cmGcc.body: The function merely forwards a string to the underlying byte‑scanning routine: it calls `yy_scan_bytes`, passing the string pointer, its length (computed with `strlen`), and the provided `yyscanner`, and then returns whatever that call returns.

@lcmGccDepfile_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yy_switch_to_buffer@k_Z32.body: The routine swaps the parser’s active buffer: it first preserves the current buffer state (position, character count, and hold‑character pointer), then updates the global buffer reference to the requested buffer and loads the new state. Finally it sets a flag indicating a buffer switch has taken place so the caller knows the context has changed.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyalloc@k_Z20cmGccDepfile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyalloc@k_Z20cmGccDepfile.body: The routine casts the supplied scanner to a private structure, immediately discards it, and returns a raw buffer of the requested size via a plain `malloc`. It is a thin forwarding shim used only to allocate memory for the internal scanner machinery.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyensure_buffer_stack@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyensure_buffer_stack@k_Z.body: The function lazily allocates and expands a dynamically‑sized stack of `yy_buffer_state` pointers inside the scanner’s “guts” structure. If the stack hasn’t been created, it allocates two slots (really one in the code) and initializes the bookkeeping fields (`top`, `max`). When the stack becomes full, it grows the array by a fixed chunk (here 8 slots), reallocates the backing array, zeroes the new slots, and updates the maximum capacity. No other logic is performed.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyfree@k_Z19cmGccDepfile_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyfree@k_Z19cmGccDepfile_.body: The routine receives a pointer and a scanner context, casts the context to a private structure, discards it, and then simply invokes `free` on the pointer. In other words, it’s a thin wrapper around `free` that currently does nothing else.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: Retrieves the column position from the scanner’s context—first validating the current buffer, then returning the stored column value (or zero if none).

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: The routine merely casts the supplied scanner pointer to the internal `yyguts_t` structure and returns the global `yy_flex_debug` flag value.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: The routine simply casts the supplied scanner pointer to its internal structure, pulls out the stored “extra” data member, and returns it.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.body: The routine casts the supplied scanner handle to its internal structure and returns the associated input `FILE *` stored in that structure.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_leng@k_Z23cmGccDepf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_leng@k_Z23cmGccDepf.body: The function receives a scanner object, casts it to a `yyguts_t*` pointer, and returns the value `yyleng` (which must be defined elsewhere).

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: The function receives a scanner instance, casts it to its internal `yyguts_t` structure, and simply returns the current line number stored in that structure (or 0 if no buffer is active).

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: Casts the passed scanner to its internal struct and returns the `yyout` member, which is a `FILE*`.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_text@k_Z23cmGccDepf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyget_text@k_Z23cmGccDepf.body: The function simply treats its argument as a pointer to a `yyguts_t` struct and returns the `yytext` member stored in that struct. It performs no validation on the argument and returns whatever pointer value resides in `yytext`; callers must ensure the scanner is valid and that the returned pointer remains valid for the caller’s lifetime.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex@k_Z18cmGccDepfile_y.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex@k_Z18cmGccDepfile_y.body: The routine initializes scanner structures, then repeatedly reads input characters, follows a deterministic finite‑state machine table to decide the next token, and upon matching a token executes the corresponding case block to update current path or dependency information. When reaching an end‑of‑file or buffer switch it finalizes the scan and returns the token.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_destroy@k_Z26cmGccD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_destroy@k_Z26cmGccD.body: The routine traverses the scanner’s internal buffer stack, removing each buffer node, then frees both the buffer‑stack and the start‑stack. After that it re‑initialises global state variables and finally releases the scanner object itself, clearing its reference pointer.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init@k_Z23cmGccDepf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init@k_Z23cmGccDepf.body: The routine allocates a `yyguts_t` structure in the supplied global pointer, zero‑initialises the memory block, and then calls `yy_init_globals` to perform the remaining state setup, finally returning a status code.

@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init_extra@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yylex_init_extra@k_Z29cmG.body: The routine registers a user‑supplied extra data object with the parser, allocates a fresh `yyguts_t` instance, clears its memory, and then invokes the standard initialization routine (`yy_init_globals`) to populate the global structure. If any allocation or initialisation fails it returns a non‑zero error code; otherwise it returns success.

@lcmGccDepfile_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z31c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yypop_buffer_state@k_Z31c.body: The routine frees the scanner’s active buffer, resets the buffer‑stack pointer, and sets a flag indicating a buffer switch on EOF. It only performs these actions when a buffer is actually in use.

@lcmGccDepfile_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yypush_buffer_state@k_Z32.body: The routine installs the supplied buffer onto the running lexer’s internal stack, replacing the current buffer in the `yyguts` structure and recording the change in the global flag. It first guards against a null buffer, then guarantees the stack is ready, and if a buffer already exists it writes the old buffer’s contents back into the shared buffer area before overwriting the current pointer. Finally it performs the standard buffer‑switch housekeeping (loading the new state and marking the switch flag).

@lcmGccDepfile_yyrealloc@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyrealloc@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: The routine simply forwards the request to `realloc` after converting the supplied pointer and size into the appropriate types. It casts the input pointer to `char*` (or `void*`) to satisfy the compiler’s generic‐pointer rules, then calls `realloc` with that pointer and the requested size, returning whatever `realloc` produces.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyrestart@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyrestart@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: The function re‑initialises the scanner’s buffer system: it first guarantees a buffer exists (allocating one if the current buffer stack is empty), then it creates a fresh buffer of the configured size and installs it as the current buffer, and finally it resets the internal buffer state from the newly opened file. This restores the scanner to a clean state ready to read a new source file.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_column@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: The routine assigns the requested column number to the global column tracker after first verifying that the current parse buffer is non‑NULL. If the buffer is missing, it aborts with a fatal error; otherwise it simply updates the column counter.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_debug@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: The routine simply assigns the supplied flag to the global debug switch used by the lexer. It casts the `yyscanner` pointer to its internal structure type but otherwise ignores it, so the only observable effect is turning debugging on or off.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_extra@k_Z24cmGccDep.body: Stores the supplied user‑defined value in the `yyextra` member of the scanner context so that later processing can retrieve the user‑specific data.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_in@k_Z21cmGccDepfil.body: The routine simply casts the generic scanner object to its concrete yyguts_t type and stores the supplied FILE pointer in the global yyin field, making that file the source for subsequent parsing.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_lineno@k_Z25cmGccDe.body: When called, the routine simply updates the global line counter used by the lexer. It first verifies that a current input buffer exists; if not, it aborts with a fatal error. Otherwise, it assigns the supplied line number to the `yylineno` variable, which tracks the current line for diagnostics and error reporting.

@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGccDepfile_yyset_out@k_Z22cmGccDepfi.body: Sets the global (or context‑level) stream pointer used by the scanner to the supplied `FILE*`. The function receives the new output stream and the current scanner context, casts the generic scanner handle to the internal `yyguts_t` structure, and simply assigns `yyout` to the supplied file stream. This effectively redirects all future output from the scanner to the new stream.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::Close@k_ZN21cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::Close@k_ZN21cmG.body: The method first records whether the temporary file is still valid, then closes the underlying stream, and finally delegates to the base implementation to clean up the temporary file (e.g., by removing it or renaming it to the target location).

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetCopyIfDiffer.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::SetCopyIfDiffer.body: Sets the internal flag that determines whether the stream should perform a copy operation when a source differs from its destination.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.body: Creates the stream object and, unless the build‑time guard macro is defined, installs a locale‐converter for the supplied encoding (only when it isn’t “None”).

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::cmGeneratedFile.body: Constructs a temporary file stream. If the requested encoding is UTF‑8‑with‑BOM it writes the BOM header. Errors during the file open are reported through cmSystemTools.

@lcmGeneratedFileStream::~cmGeneratedFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratedFileStream::~cmGeneratedFil.body: When a `cmGeneratedFileStream` instance is destroyed, the destructor marks whether its temporary file was closed successfully by setting `this->Okay` to the inverse of `this->fail()` after cleaning up any associated resources.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate@k_ZN21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate@k_ZN21.body: The function checks whether the supplied input string contains a placeholder. If it does, it creates a profiling entry (when profiling is enabled), constructs a compiled‑expression object from that string, and then delegates evaluation to that object, returning the produced string. If no placeholder is found, it simply returns the original input unchanged.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Find@k_ZN21cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Find@k_ZN21cmGe.body: The function scans the supplied string view for the marker sequence `$<`. If that sequence occurs and a matching `>` follows somewhere after it, the function returns the index where `$<` begins; otherwise it signals “not found” by returning `npos`.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::IsValidTargetNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::IsValidTargetNa.body: The function compiles a static regex that accepts only alphanumerics and the characters `._:+-` and uses it to test whether the supplied string matches that pattern, returning the match result.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Parse@k_ZNK21cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Parse@k_ZNK21cm.body: The `Parse` member simply constructs a new `cmCompiledGeneratorExpression` object, forwarding the current object’s `CMakeInstance`, `Backtrace`, and the supplied `input` string (moved to avoid copying). It then returns a `std::unique_ptr` owning that newly created instance.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Preprocess@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Preprocess@k_ZN.body: The `Preprocess` function processes an input string according to a supplied `PreprocessContext`. If the context equals `StripAllGeneratorExpressions`, it removes all generator expressions by calling `stripAllGeneratorExpressions`. For contexts `BuildInterface` or `InstallInterface` it removes export‑style interface directives using `stripExportInterface`, supplying the provided `importPrefix`. Any other context values cause the function to hit an assertion and return an empty string.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::ReplaceInstallP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::ReplaceInstallP.body: The routine scans the supplied string, locating every instance of the literal “$<INSTALL_PREFIX>”. Upon each match it substitutes that token with the given replacement text, updating the search start point so subsequent matches don’t overlap the just‑modified segment. The operation runs in‑place, altering the input string directly.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::Split@k_ZN21cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::Split@k_ZN21cmG.body:
The function parses a string for “$<…>” generator blocks.  
It scans forward from each “$<”, extracts the preceding non‑empty text, expands any list in that part, then consumes the nested generator expression until the matching “>” and the following ‘;’ that terminates it. The extracted fragment – preceding text plus the full “$<…>” block – is appended to the output vector. Any remaining tail of the input string is passed to the list‑expansion routine at the end.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.body: The function examines a C‑style string and returns true only when the first two characters are the specific sequence “$<”. It immediately returns false if the pointer is null. It is a simple, character‑by‑character check used to detect the start of a generator expression in the input text.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::StartsWithGener.body: Checks whether the first two characters of the string are “$<”; returns true if they match, false otherwise.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::StripEmptyListE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::StripEmptyListE.body: The function scans the input string, extracts the substrings between semicolons that contain non‑empty data, and returns a compact representation that omits any empty list entries (including trailing semicolons).

@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.body: The constructor initializes a new `cmGeneratorExpression` instance by storing the supplied `cmaKe` instance in its base class and moving the provided `backtrace` into the `Backtrace` member.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::cmGeneratorExpr.body: The `cmGeneratorExpression` constructor creates a new object instance from an existing one; copying is explicitly disabled by marking the copy constructor as deleted.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::operator=@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::operator=@k_ZN2.body: It is a deleted copy‑assignment operator that returns a reference to the object, preventing any assignment of one `cmGeneratorExpression` to another.

@lcmGeneratorExpression::~cmGeneratorExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpression::~cmGeneratorExp.body: ~cmGeneratorExpression is a constructor‑style function that creates and configures a generator expression object. It parses the provided input, sets up the internal state of the generator, and returns an initialized expression tree ready for subsequent use.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::Eval.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::Eval.body: The function parses the supplied expression into an internal representation, sets up a DAG‑checker with the given property (defaulting to “COMPILE_OPTIONS” when the flag is “COMPILE_FLAGS”), and then evaluates the compiled expression in the current language context, returning the resulting string.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.body: It initializes an interpreter for a local generator by storing the generator instance, configuration string, head‑target pointer and optional language string while chaining to the base class that holds the CMake instance.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::cmGe.body: The function takes an existing interpreter instance and creates a new one that contains an identical copy of its internal state—including expression tree, configuration flags, and any auxiliary context—so that the new interpreter can independently evaluate expressions with the same environment.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::oper.body: This function overload assigns the provided value to the internal representation of the `cmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter` instance and returns a reference to the modified object, enabling chained assignments.

@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::~cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorExpressionInterpreter::~cmG.body: The method takes a raw expression string, tokenises it, resolves operators and operands (including nested expressions), and builds an internal representation of the expression tree to be used by the generator’s expression evaluator.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddExplicitLanguage.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddExplicitLanguage.body: The function retrieves the language property of a source file and, based on the current policy status, conditionally appends the corresponding explicit‑language flag to the provided options string. If the language is unknown it exits early; if the policy is OLD it returns without adding anything; if the policy is NEW it appends the flag; the WARN case falls through to the same behavior.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddTracedSources@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AddTracedSources@k_.body: The method forwards the incoming vector of source strings to the underlying target object. After that call it tests whether any strings were supplied; if so, it joins them with semicolons and feeds the resulting single string into AddSourceCommon. This keeps the original list intact while still allowing a single‑string representation for downstream handling.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendCustomCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendCustomCommand.body: The function checks whether the target has any pre‑build, pre‑link, or post‑build commands. If any such commands exist, it records the current target in the `sideEffects` set; otherwise it scans the target’s configuration sources. If any source contains a custom command, the current target is added to `sideEffects`. This effectively flags targets that influence side‑effect behavior.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendLanguageSideE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::AppendLanguageSideE.body: The function iterates over every compilation language configured for the target and, for each language that is **not** in the predefined “no‑side‑effect” set, adds the current target instance to a side‑effects map keyed by that language.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigCompile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetAllConfigCompile.body: It collects every non‑empty language string reported by each configuration source into a deduplicated set that is then returned.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK1.body: It forwards the request for a back‑trace list to the underlying `Target` object and returns whatever that object produces—no extra processing or state changes are performed.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExternalObjects@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetExternalObjects@.body: The `GetExternalObjects` member of `cmGeneratorTarget` iterates over a vector of source‑file pointers (`cmSourceFile`) and registers each file that is marked as an *external* object (by checking `SourceKindExternalObject`). It simply forwards those files to whatever internal visitor‑based machinery the target implements. No additional logic or side‑effects are performed – the method is just a thin wrapper around the `IMPLEMENT_VISIT` macro.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullPath@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetFullPath@k_ZNK17.body: The function returns the full file path for the current target. If the target is marked as imported, it forwards the request to `ImportedGetFullPath`; otherwise it calls `NormalGetFullPath`, passing along the provided config string, artifact type, and the `realname` flag to control how the name is resolved.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkImplementati.body: The method returns a pointer to a `cmLinkImplementation` object that corresponds to the requested configuration and usage. It forwards the request to an overload that accepts an extra boolean flag, passing `false` to indicate that no special “test” mode is needed.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterface@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterface@k_.body: This member function resolves a link‑interface lookup by delegating to an overload that accepts an additional flag. It forwards the supplied `config` string and optional `head` target, passing `false` to indicate that any special‑case handling should not be applied. The result is a const pointer to the located link‑interface instance.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceLib.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLinkInterfaceLib.body: The function resolves the set of libraries that must be linked for a target under a given configuration and usage type. It first checks whether the target is an imported target and, if so, delegates to a special import‑aware routine. It then rejects executables that do not export symbols, returning nullptr. Otherwise it consults a cache of already‑computed link interfaces; if none exist it computes the list via ComputeLinkInterfaceLibraries and stores the result for future reuse, finally returning the populated library list or nullptr if nothing applies.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocalGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocalGenerator@k.body: The `GetLocalGenerator()` member simply returns the value of the `LocalGenerator` member pointer of the current instance. It is a const accessor that returns a `cmLocalGenerator*` without performing any modification.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocationForBuild.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetLocationForBuild.body:
The routine returns the path of the artifact for the current target.  
If the target is imported, it uses the imported path helper and returns that path immediately.  
Otherwise it builds a path from the base directory, optionally appends a config directory when defined, appends a bundle directory when required, and finally the artifact’s full name.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGe.body: This member function simply forwards a call to the wrapped `Target` object, returning a const reference to the string that identifies the underlying target. It relies on the assumption that `Target->GetName()` itself returns a const reference, so callers receive a read‑only view of the underlying identifier without copying the string.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPostBuildCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPostBuildCommand.body: The function simply forwards a const reference to the target’s internal vector of custom commands that should run after the target’s build.
