@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreBuildCommands.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreBuildCommands.body: This routine simply fetches the target’s pre‑build command collection and hands it back to the caller.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreLinkCommands@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetPreLinkCommands@.body: The method simply forwards the request to the wrapped target and returns its cached vector of pre‑link commands. Because the return type is a reference, the caller must keep the `cmGeneratorTarget` instance alive as long as it uses the result; otherwise the reference would dangle. The target object is expected to own that vector, so the caller can safely treat the returned reference as read‑only.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK17.body: The function first tries to resolve the requested property by invoking `cmTargetPropertyComputer::GetProperty`. If that succeeds it immediately returns the resulting `cmValue`. If the resolution fails, the code checks whether a fatal error has been recorded; if so it returns a null `cmValue`. If no fatal error has occurred, it falls back to the target’s own property retrieval mechanism.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFiles@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFiles@k_ZN.body: The member `cmGeneratorTarget::GetSourceFiles` fills a caller‑supplied vector with pointers to source files that belong to the target. It calls the internal helper that returns a vector of wrapped pointers (`BT<cmSourceFile*>`), reserves enough capacity in the output vector, and iterates over the returned vector, copying each wrapped pointer’s raw pointer into the caller’s collection.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetType@k_ZNK17cmGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetType@k_ZNK17cmGe.body: This method simply forwards the request to its internal `Target` object and returns the `TargetType` value that the target reports.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetUtilityItems@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::GetUtilityItems@k_Z.body: When the member flag `UtilityItemsDone` is false, `GetUtilityItems` runs once to build the `UtilityItems` set. It calls `GetUtilities()` to obtain a collection of `BT<pair<string,bool>>` values. For each value, it attempts to resolve the string key to a target via `FindGeneratorTargetToUse`. If a target is found, a `cmLinkItem` is inserted that links this target with the original boolean flag and the back‑trace; otherwise a plain `cmLinkItem` constructed from the key and flag is inserted. After the first run, the set is cached in `UtilityItems`, and all subsequent calls simply return that cached set.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsExecutableWithExp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsExecutableWithExp.body: It simply forwards the query to the underlying target object, returning whatever that object reports for its own `IsExecutableWithExports` state.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsInBuildSystem@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::IsInBuildSystem@k_Z.body: Checks whether a target is part of the build system: if the target is not imported and its type matches one of the accepted enum values, or it is an interface library that actually has source/header/module entries, the function returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkItem@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGeneratorTarget::ResolveLinkItem@k_Z.body: The method forwards the call to an overload that accepts the current `LocalGenerator` as an additional argument and returns whatever `cmLinkItem` that overload produces.

@lcmGetCMakePropertyCommand@k_Z25cmGetCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetCMakePropertyCommand@k_Z25cmGetCM.body:
The routine first verifies that at least two arguments are supplied.  
It then interprets the second argument as a keyword: if it is “VARIABLES”, “MACROS”, or “COMPONENTS”, it fetches the corresponding property from the makefile’s current state; otherwise it treats it as a name of a global property to look up.  
The fetched value is inserted into the makefile’s definition table under the supplied variable name and the function returns success.

@lcmGetFilenameComponentCommand@k_Z29cmG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetFilenameComponentCommand@k_Z29cmG.body: The function interprets a list of arguments that specify a component of a file path or a program name, then resolves that component according to the requested component (name, extension, path, absolute path, etc.). It first checks for a cached value and, if present, returns immediately. Otherwise it expands any registry placeholders, optionally expands the registry key for 32‑/64‑bit views, and then branches on the component type: “PATH”, “NAME”, “PROGRAM”, “EXT”, “NAME_WE”, “LAST_EXT”, “NAME_WLE”, “ABSOLUTE”. For a program it may search the system path and split arguments. For absolute paths it normalises and resolves symlinks. Finally it stores the resolved result back into the makefile’s definition cache or regular definition, returning success.

@lcmGetPipes@k_Z10cmGetPipesPi@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetPipes@k_Z10cmGetPipesPi@f./Source.body: Creates a pair of file‑descriptors. It calls `pipe()` on the supplied array; on failure it converts the system error into a libuv error and returns it. On success it sets both ends to close automatically on exec using `fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC)`. If that fails it cleans up by closing the descriptors and returns the translated error. The routine finally returns 0 on success.

@lcmGetTargetPropertyCommand@k_Z26cmGetT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGetTargetPropertyCommand@k_Z26cmGetT.body: The function validates that exactly three arguments are provided, then attempts to locate the target named in the second argument. If the target is found, it checks whether the third argument indicates an aliased‑target or global alias flag; if so, it records whether the target is an alias and sets the result variable accordingly. Otherwise, it attempts to resolve the requested property from the target’s computed properties, falling back to the normal property if needed. If any resolution succeeds, the value is added to the makefile’s definition list under the variable name supplied; if resolution fails, it defines the variable as “<name>-NOTFOUND”. If the target cannot be located, an error message is emitted.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::AddCacheEnt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::AddCacheEnt.body: The routine populates the glob cache: it hashes the supplied *entry* to construct a key, looks up that key in the internal map, and if the slot is uninitialized, it stores the file list and back‑trace list, marking the entry initialized. If the key already maps to a differing file list, it emits a fatal error with a detailed back‑trace; otherwise it simply appends the new back‑trace record.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: Initializes a `CacheEntryKey` by copying its identifying fields from another instance—preserving the key data that uniquely identifies a cache entry.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: CacheEntryKey initializes internal flags for recursion, directory‑listing and symlink handling, then stores a relative path and an expression string by moving the supplied strings. It is meant to generate a unique key for a cache entry.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: The method serialises a glob‑style command into a human‑readable form. It writes an opening token, optionally prefixes “_RECURSE” when the recursive flag is set, and adds “FOLLOW_SYMLINKS” only if symlink following is enabled. It then emits the directory‑listing indicator and the stored directory list. If a relative path string exists it appends that value. Finally it appends the expression inside parentheses, finishing with a closing quote. This produces a compact textual representation of the glob command to be logged or displayed.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body:
The `operator<` establishes an ordering on `CacheEntryKey` objects.  
It performs a lexicographic comparison in a fixed priority sequence: first `Recurse`, then `ListDirectories`, `FollowSymlinks`, `Relative`, and finally `Expression`.  
It returns `true` if the calling instance precedes the argument on the first differing field; otherwise it returns `false`.  

This ordering is intended for use in ordered containers (e.g., `std::set` or `std::map`) and is a strict weak ordering that supports deterministic ordering of keys.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryK.body: The `~CacheEntryKey()` function is the destructor for the `CacheEntryKey` structure. It cleans up any resources owned by a cache entry key—typically releasing allocated memory or removing the key from internal bookkeeping structures—before the object is destroyed. This ensures that no dangling references or memory leaks remain in the cache after an entry is removed.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryV.body: The `CacheEntryValue` copy‑constructor simply creates a new instance from an existing one. It’s invoked in several places—most notably in `cmGlobVerificationManager.h` around line 70—where the struct’s value is duplicated for cache‑related bookkeeping.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::CacheEntryV.body: The destructor `~CacheEntryValue()` is called automatically when a `CacheEntryValue` instance goes out of scope or is explicitly destroyed. It releases any owned resources—such as dynamically allocated buffers or reference‑counted pointers—by invoking `delete` or clearing containers, ensuring that the internal cache state is left in a clean, safe state. This cleanup guarantees that no dangling pointers remain in the cache manager and that subsequent cache accesses do not inadvertently reuse freed memory.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::DoWriteVeri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::DoWriteVeri.body: The function returns true only when both the `VerifyScript` and `VerifyStamp` members contain non‑empty strings; if either is empty it returns false.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::GetCacheEnt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::GetCacheEnt.body: Iterates over the internal cache map, constructs a vector of `cmGlobCacheEntry` objects for entries whose value is marked as initialized, and returns that vector.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::Reset@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::Reset@k_ZN2.body: The Reset function purges the in‑memory data structures used for verification—Cache, VerifyScript and VerifyStamp—so that the manager is returned to a clean state before any new verification cycle.

@lcmGlobVerificationManager::SaveVerific.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobVerificationManager::SaveVerific.body: The routine writes the current verification cache into a CMake‑generated script and a stamp file; it emits global definitions for each cached glob, along with back‑trace comments via the messenger, and stores the paths of the created files in the manager’s members. It returns `true` when both files are created successfully, otherwise it reports an error and returns `false`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddInstallComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::AddInstallComponent.body: It inserts a non‑empty string into the `InstallComponents` set. If the argument string is empty, the function does nothing.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::CreateAnonymousRunt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::CreateAnonymousRunt.body: Creates a new `cmInstallRuntimeDependencySet`, stores it in the manager’s list of runtime‑dependency sets, and returns a raw pointer to the freshly‑allocated instance.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::EnableInstallTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::EnableInstallTarget.body: This function simply switches an internal flag to indicate that an install target is now active.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindTarget@k_ZNK17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::FindTarget@k_ZNK17c.body: The function first checks whether the alias domain is requested. If it is, it looks up the target’s alias in the map; when an alias exists it immediately forwards that name to `FindTargetImpl`. If no alias is found or the alias domain isn’t requested, it simply calls `FindTargetImpl` with the original name.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GenerateCMakeBuildC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GenerateCMakeBuildC.body: Builds a command string for invoking CMake, adding optional flags for config, parallel, target, and native settings. It also appends a flag to ignore errors when requested, and returns the fully‑formed command string.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetAllTargetName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetAllTargetName@k_.body: A virtual const member that returns a constant C‑string; in this implementation it simply returns the literal `"ALL_BUILD"` to signal that the function’s purpose is to expose the fixed target identifier used by the build system.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_.body: It returns a read‑only pointer to the stored `cmake` instance, keeping the object unchanged.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCleanTargetName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetCleanTargetName@.body: The `GetCleanTargetName()` member returns a null C‑string (nullptr). It is declared `virtual const` meaning derived classes can override it, and the `const` qualifier guarantees the method does not modify the object’s state. The body simply returns `nullptr`, indicating no valid target name is available by default.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetEditCacheCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetEditCacheCommand.body: The function simply returns an empty string; it is intended to be overridden in derived classes to supply the specific edit‑cache command string.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetEditCacheTargetN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetEditCacheTargetN.body: It returns a `const char*`; the base implementation simply yields `nullptr`, signaling that no target name is supplied unless a derived class overrides the method to provide one.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExportSets@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExportSets@k_ZN1.body: It simply returns the current export‑set map stored in the object.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExtraGeneratorNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetExtraGeneratorNa.body: The method returns the name of an attached “extra” generator when it exists; otherwise it yields an empty string.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetFilenameTargetDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetFilenameTargetDe.body: The function retrieves the set of generator‑target objects that rely on a specific source file. It looks up the file in a map (`FilenameTargetDepends`) and returns the corresponding collection of pointers.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetForceUnixPaths@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetForceUnixPaths@k.body: Returns the current value of the `ForceUnixPaths` flag, exposing whether Unix‑style paths are being enforced.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallComponent.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallComponent.body: It returns a const pointer to the internal `std::set<std::string>` that holds the names of components to be installed.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallLocalTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallLocalTarg.body: The `GetInstallLocalTargetName` virtual const member simply returns a `nullptr`. It is meant to be overridden by derived classes to supply the name of the installation target. In its base form it yields no value.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallStripTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallStripTarg.body: The method is intended to expose the string name of the install‑strip target. In its current form it simply returns a null pointer, so any caller receives a `nullptr` unless a derived class overrides the virtual function with an actual name.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallTargetNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetInstallTargetNam.body: It’s a read‑only accessor that returns the literal string “INSTALL”. It’s marked virtual so derived classes can override the name, and the const qualifier guarantees the method does not modify any member data.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetJson@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetJson@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: The `GetJson` member produces a JSON object. It constructs a temporary `Json::Value` called `generator`, sets its `"name"` field to the result of `GetName()` and its `"multiConfig"` field to the boolean value returned by `IsMultiConfig()`, then returns that object. No additional data or metadata is inserted.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetLocalGenerators@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetLocalGenerators@.body: It returns a const reference to the internal vector of `LocalGenerator` objects, allowing callers to read the collection without modifying it.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetMakefileEncoding.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetMakefileEncoding.body: The `GetMakefileEncoding` member simply reports that the generated makefile has no special encoding applied – it returns `codecvt_Encoding::None`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetName@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: This member simply returns the literal string “Generic”, serving as a default value that derived classes can override.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetNamedRuntimeDepe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetNamedRuntimeDepe.body: The function retrieves a runtime‑dependency set by name, lazily creating and inserting one into the internal map and list if it doesn’t already exist, then returns that set.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetNeedSymbolicMark.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetNeedSymbolicMark.body: The member simply returns the value of the private flag `NeedSymbolicMark`. Because the function is `const` and the flag is read‑only, no mutation occurs, and no thread‑safety issues arise as long‑running or re‑entrant code is not involved.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageSourceTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageSourceTar.body: This member function is an overridable, read‑only accessor that returns a pointer to a C‑style string. It is declared `const`, guaranteeing that calling it does not modify the object’s state. The default implementation simply returns `nullptr`, signaling that no specific name is provided unless a derived type overrides the method with an actual string.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageTargetNam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPackageTargetNam.body: `GetPackageTargetName()` is a const‑qualified virtual accessor that returns a `const char*` pointing to the literal `"PACKAGE"`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPreinstallTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetPreinstallTarget.body: This virtual member is intended to provide a string identifying a pre‑install target, but the default implementation simply returns a null pointer.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetProjectMap@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetProjectMap@k_ZNK.body: Returns a const reference to the internal `ProjectMap`, exposing the map of project names to the corresponding vectors of `cmLocalGenerator*` pointers for read‑only inspection.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetRebuildCacheTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetRebuildCacheTarg.body: The method is a virtual, const member that returns a pointer to a const character array. In its current form it simply returns a null pointer, acting as a stub that derived classes are expected to override with the actual target name when the rebuild cache needs to be identified.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetSafeGlobalSettin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetSafeGlobalSettin.body: The method asserts that the `Makefiles` collection is non‑empty, then retrieves the first `Makefile` in the list and returns the string returned by its `GetDefinition` call for the supplied `name`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetTestTargetName@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetTestTargetName@k.body: The method is a virtual member that returns a constant C‑style string. It simply returns the literal `"RUN_TESTS"`.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetUseLinkScript@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GetUseLinkScript@k_.body: Returns the internal flag `UseLinkScript` indicating whether link scripts are enabled. The function simply returns the stored boolean; callers can safely query this flag without side‑effects, provided the flag is initialized before use.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::GlobalSettingIsOn@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::GlobalSettingIsOn@k.body: The function simply forwards the lookup of a named flag to the first make‑file in the generator’s internal list. It first asserts the list isn’t empty, then returns the truth value that the contained `Makefile` reports for the requested name.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsAlias@k_ZNK17cmGl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsAlias@k_ZNK17cmGl.body: Checks whether the supplied name exists in the internal collection (`AliasTargets`) and returns that boolean value.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsExportedTargetsFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsExportedTargetsFi.body: The function determines whether a given file name is treated as an exported target file during the generator's export handling. It first looks up the filename in the internal map of build‑export sets; if absent it short‑circuits and returns false. If present, it then checks whether the name is absent from the secondary “BuildExportExportSets” collection—only in that case does it report the file as an exported target.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsMultiConfig@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsMultiConfig@k_ZNK.body: The `IsMultiConfig` member simply reports that the current instance does not support a multi‑configuration layout – it always returns `false`. This indicates that any derived or consuming code can rely on the base implementation to treat the object as single‑configuration by default.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsReservedTarget@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::IsReservedTarget@k_.body: The function returns whether the supplied target name matches one of the predefined reserved target strings stored in a static array. It simply performs a linear containment check on that array and returns the result.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::cmGlobalGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::cmGlobalGenerator@k.body: The constructor wires the generator into a running CMake instance and then flips a collection of feature‑flags to their default states: symbolic‑dependency tracking is disabled, Unix‑style paths are preferred, color output is turned off, link‑script support is disabled, and the install target path is inactive. It also zeros out the timeout for “try‑compile” runs, clears the current makefile pointers, and nudges the internal JSON stream writer to use a tab‑indented format when building under a non‑bootstrapped configuration.

@lcmGlobalGenerator::~cmGlobalGenerator@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalGenerator::~cmGlobalGenerator@.body: When an instance of the class is deallocated, the destructor invokes `ClearGeneratorMembers()` to free any internal state or resources that the generator was holding.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: The function returns the supplied path unchanged except that on Windows it swaps each forward‑slash in the string with a back‑slash using a call to `std::replace`. It does not perform any path‑normalisation or error handling.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: It checks a cache for a previously computed conversion; if found, it returns the stored result. Otherwise it creates a relative path via the first generator, normalizes it for Ninja, replaces forward‑slashes with back‑slashes on Windows, stores the result in a map keyed by the original path, and returns the new value.

@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalNinjaGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: It builds and hands back a `MapToNinjaPathImpl` instance tied to the current object, essentially exposing the internal mapping functionality to callers.

@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGlobalUnixMakefileGenerator3::Suppor.body: This member function simply returns the internal flag `ToolSupportsLongLineDependencies`, indicating whether the current tool configuration allows dependencies to span long lines.

@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::cmGraphAdjacency.body: The `cmGraphAdjacencyList` routine builds a dense adjacency list from the internal graph structure—together with a helper that walks the node list and marshals each edge into the list that other parts (e.g. traversal routines) consume.

@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::~cmGraphAdjacenc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphAdjacencyList::~cmGraphAdjacenc.body: This routine constructs a compact adjacency representation for the graph data structure. It iterates over the graph’s edge collection, allocating and populating a list for each vertex. The resulting `cmGraphAdjacencyList` type inherits from `std::vector<cmGraphEdgeList>`, providing a contiguous storage of per‑vertex adjacency vectors that downstream modules query to resolve connectivity and traversal quickly.

@lcmGraphEdge::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK11cmGra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK11cmGra.body: The method simply returns a read‑only reference to the internal back‑trace list, allowing callers to inspect the stored traces without modifying them.

@lcmGraphEdge::IsCross@k_ZNK11cmGraphEdg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::IsCross@k_ZNK11cmGraphEdg.body: Returns the value stored in the member flag that indicates whether the current object is in the cross state.

@lcmGraphEdge::IsStrong@k_ZNK11cmGraphEd.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::IsStrong@k_ZNK11cmGraphEd.body: The `IsStrong` member simply exposes the internal `Strong` flag, allowing callers to query the object's status without altering its state. Because it is marked `const`, the method guarantees no mutation and is safe to invoke on read‑only instances.

@lcmGraphEdge::cmGraphEdge@k_ZN11cmGraph.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::cmGraphEdge@k_ZN11cmGraph.body: The constructor stores a destination node index, two Boolean flags (one for “strong” and one for “cross”), and a back‑trace list that is moved into the member variable.

@lcmGraphEdge::operator unsigned long@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdge::operator unsigned long@k_.body: The function is a conversion operator that allows an object to be treated as a `size_t`. It simply returns the value stored in the member `Dest`, treating that value as the object’s size.

@lcmGraphEdgeList::operator=@k_ZN15cmGra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmGraphEdgeList::operator=@k_ZN15cmGra.body: The assignment operator copies another list’s underlying vector into the current object, then returns *this. It preserves exception safety by only modifying *this after a successful copy, and it uses the base `std::vector<cmGraphEdge>`’s assignment semantics.

@lcmHasLiteralPrefix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasLiteralPrefix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralPr.body: The function simply checks whether the supplied string view starts with the literal string represented by the array `prefix`. It forwards the work to `cmHasPrefix` by wrapping the array (excluding its terminating null) into a `string_view` and returning the result.

@lcmHasLiteralSuffix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralSu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasLiteralSuffix@k_Z18cmHasLiteralSu.body: This template checks whether a string ends with a literal suffix by delegating to cmHasSuffix, using a `string_view` constructed from the suffix literal.

@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixSt17basic_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasPrefix@k_Z11cmHasPrefixSt17basic_.body: The function simply checks whether the beginning of a given string matches a supplied prefix by comparing the first `prefix.size()` characters of `str` with `prefix` and returning the result of that comparison.

@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixSt17basic_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmHasSuffix@k_Z11cmHasSuffixSt17basic_.body: The function simply verifies that the `string_view` ends with the supplied suffix by ensuring the suffix fits within the string’s length and then comparing the final characters for equality.

@lcmIfCommand@k_Z11cmIfCommandRKSt6vecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfCommand@k_Z11cmIfCommandRKSt6vecto.body: The routine expands the supplied list of arguments, evaluates whether the condition is satisfied, reports any diagnostic message, and if the test succeeds it registers a blocker that gates subsequent command blocks; otherwise it prevents those blocks from executing.

@lcmIfCommandError@k_ZL16cmIfCommandErro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfCommandError@k_ZL16cmIfCommandErro.body: It loops over each argument supplied to an *if* command, escapes the raw value for safe printing, and appends it to a growing message that starts with “given arguments:”. The returned string is the ready‑to‑display error text that lists every argument exactly as it was passed.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::ArgumentsMatch@k_.body: The method returns true when the argument list supplied in the `cmListFileFunction` is either empty or exactly matches the stored `Args` member; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::EndCommandName@k_.body: The overridden const method simply returns the literal string_view `"endif"` (via the `_s` helper).

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN19cmIf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::Replay@k_ZN19cmIf.body:
The function re‑executes a list of stored functions that were parsed from an if‑statement.  
It walks the vector, keeping a depth counter that increments on an “if” keyword and decrements on an “endif”. When the depth is zero and the keyword is “else” or “elseif”, it records that the block has entered its else part, flags that an else has already been seen, and performs the usual error checks (duplicate else, else‑after‑else‑if).  

Only when the block is not marked “blocking” (i.e. the current condition was true) does it actually call `mf.ExecuteCommand` for each function; the call’s status is examined for return/break/continue/exit signals, which are propagated back to the caller.  
The routine returns `true` on successful replay, and `true` after any fatal error condition (which also triggers a global fatal‑error flag).

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::StartCommandName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::StartCommandName@.body: The `StartCommandName()` function is a public, const virtual override that simply returns a `cm::string_view` containing the literal `"if_s"`. It’s intended to provide the command name string for the calling context.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::cmIfFunctionBlock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::cmIfFunctionBlock.body: cmIfFunctionBlocker is a constructor that accepts an rvalue reference to another cmIfFunctionBlocker instance. It adopts that instance’s internal state, transferring ownership of the function‑blocker and its conditional flag while preserving the condition logic that governs whether the block executes. This pattern ensures that any subsequent code associated with the block inherits the same execution guard as the original object, preventing accidental re‑use of stale condition flags or dangling references.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::cmIfFunctionBlock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::cmIfFunctionBlock.body: The `cmIfFunctionBlocker` class functions as a conditional wrapper around function blocks. It evaluates a runtime boolean expression—typically derived from a preceding `cmIfCommand`—then either passes control to the wrapped block or bypasses it entirely, effectively gating code execution in the generated binary based on that condition.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::cmIfFunctionBlock.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::cmIfFunctionBlock.body: cmIfFunctionBlocker controls whether a function should execute during a conditional block. It evaluates the current condition; if satisfied, it forwards the function call, otherwise it suppresses the execution.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: The assignment operator takes an rvalue reference to another `cmIfFunctionBlocker`, copies or moves its internal state into the current instance, and returns a reference to this instance so that the assignment can be chained.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: The operator= overload performs assignment for `cmIfFunctionBlocker`. It takes a const reference to another `cmIfFunctionBlocker` instance, copies that instance’s internal state into the current object, and returns the current object.

@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::~cmIfFunctionBloc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIfFunctionBlocker::~cmIfFunctionBloc.body: The `~cmIfFunctionBlocker` function is the public virtual entry point that overrides the base `cmFunctionBlocker` implementation. It is invoked whenever the system needs to process a conditional (“if”) block; the function typically checks the associated condition expression, and if it evaluates to true, it executes the enclosed block of code (often delegating to a registered *blocker*). If the condition evaluates to false, the function typically skips the block and may perform any cleanup or default behaviour defined in the base class. The function is designed to be overridden by derived classes so that each specific “if” type can provide its own execution semantics while still fitting into the common blocker framework.

@lcmIncludeDirectoryCommand@k_Z25cmInclu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeDirectoryCommand@k_Z25cmInclu.body: The function parses the arguments for an “include‑directory” command. It recognises optional “BEFORE/AFTER” and “SYSTEM” flags, gathers the specified directories (using `GetIncludes`), validates them, and finally registers the collected lists with the current `cmMakefile` in the appropriate order (before/after) and system‑include set.

@lcmIncludeExternalMSProjectCommand@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeExternalMSProjectCommand@k_Z3.body: The function parses a list of arguments to configure a utility target that will include an external Microsoft‑style project into the build. It first validates the required number of arguments, then, only on Windows, extracts optional metadata (project type, GUID, platform mapping) from the argument list, and finally registers a new target in the makefile with the provided path, storing any custom attributes in the target’s properties.

@lcmIncludeGuardCommand@k_Z21cmIncludeGu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIncludeGuardCommand@k_Z21cmIncludeGu.body: The function verifies the single optional argument ("DIRECTORY" or "GLOBAL") and then ensures the corresponding guard variable is defined in the current makefile, in the directory scope, or in the global CMake context; if already set it returns early with a “return invoked” status.

@lcmInstallAndroidMKExportGenerator::cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallAndroidMKExportGenerator::cmI.body: The constructor creates an Android‑MK export generator by forwarding its arguments to the base cmInstallExportGenerator constructor (including an empty string for a final parameter) and then instanti­ates a unique‑owned `cmExportInstallAndroidMKGenerator` stored in the `EFGen` member.

@lcmInstallCMakeConfigExportGenerator::c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCMakeConfigExportGenerator::c.body: Initializes an export generator for CMake‐config files: the constructor passes the supplied export set, destination, permissions, and various flags to the base class, stores the options in member variables, and allocates a unique helper (`cmExportInstallCMakeConfigGenerator`) to perform the actual export logic.

@lcmInstallCommand@k_Z16cmInstallCommand.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommand@k_Z16cmInstallCommand.body: The function `cmInstallCommand` processes a vector of argument strings and a status object. If the argument vector is empty it simply succeeds, otherwise it first enables the install target on the global generator and then dispatches the request through a static dispatch table that maps sub‑commands such as “SCRIPT”, “TARGETS”, “FILES”, etc. The dispatch returns a boolean indicating whether the operation succeeded.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::CheckPermis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::CheckPermis.body: The function iterates over a static permission table and returns **true** only when the supplied permission string matches an entry. On a match it appends the matched permission to the supplied `permissions` buffer and immediately returns **true**; otherwise it falls through to return **false**.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::Finalize@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::Finalize@k_.body: If the required permissions are present, the function normalises the stored destination string to a Unix‑style path and returns success; otherwise it exits early with failure.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetComponen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetComponen.body: The function returns the component name in priority order: first the member’s own `Component` string if set, otherwise the `GenericArguments`’s component when present, then a fallback `DefaultComponentName`. If none are available it yields a static default string “Unspecified”.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetConfigur.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetConfigur.body: The method returns a reference to the member `Configurations`. If the current instance already holds configurations, it returns that immediately. Otherwise it defers to a `GenericArguments` object (if present) to fetch its configurations. If neither provides data, it finally returns the empty member container.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetDestinat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetDestinat.body: Returns the value stored in `DestinationString` if it’s non‑empty; otherwise falls back to the value returned by an embedded `GenericArguments` object; if neither is present it yields a static empty string.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetExcludeF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetExcludeF.body: The method returns `true` when the `ExcludeFromAll` flag is set on the current instance; if that flag is not set, it defers to any `GenericArguments` instance that may provide its own flag; if neither gives an exclusion, the method returns `false`.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.body: Returns the string stored in `NamelinkComponent` when it is set; otherwise it falls back to the component returned by `GetComponent()`.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.body: This member checks whether the current object or its optional `GenericArguments` delegate reports “name‑link only”. It returns **true** if either flag is already set; otherwise it falls back to the delegated check, returning **false** when nothing is present.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetNamelink.body: The function returns `true` if the object’s internal flag `NamelinkSkip` is set; otherwise it defers to its associated `GenericArguments` object’s same query, falling back to `false` if neither provides a value.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetOptional.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetOptional.body: Checks if the current instance has its `Optional` flag set; if so, it immediately returns `true`. If not, it defers to its `GenericArguments` member (if present) and returns that object's optional state. If no member exists, it returns `false`.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetPermissi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetPermissi.body: The method returns a reference to a string. It first returns the cached `PermissionsString` if it has been set; if that is empty, it falls back to delegating the call to an optional `GenericArguments` instance; if none of those provide a value, it yields an empty string.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetRename@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetRename@k.body: If a non‑empty internal `Rename` string exists, the method returns it; otherwise it defers to an attached `GenericArguments` object’s `GetRename()`; if neither is present it returns a default empty string.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetType@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::GetType@k_Z.body: The `GetType()` member function simply returns a constant reference to the stored `Type` string, providing read‑only access to the value without allowing modification.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::HasNamelink.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::HasNamelink.body: The method first checks whether the internal NamelinkComponent collection contains any items; if it does, it immediately returns true. If the collection is empty but a GenericArguments object is present, it defers the query to that object by invoking its HasNamelinkComponent() method; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::SetGenericA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::SetGenericA.body: The method assigns the supplied pointer to the internal member, effectively storing the argument list for later use.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::cmInstallCo.body: The constructor records a default component name, then configures a destination‑normalising lambda according to the current policy (OLD, WARN, or NEW).  It assigns that lambda to the “DESTINATION” argument, and also binds the other install arguments (“COMPONENT”, “NAMELINK_COMPONENT”, etc.) to the internal handlers.

@lcmInstallCommandArguments::~cmInstallC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandArguments::~cmInstallC.body: `~cmInstallCommandArguments()` registers the command‑line options that a user can pass to an install command. It builds a `cmArgumentParser` instance that understands how those options map to internal configuration settings, enabling the installer to read and validate the supplied arguments before executing the command.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::GetF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::GetF.body: The `GetFileSet()` method simply returns a constant reference to the internal `FileSet` member. It’s marked `const` so callers can’t modify the returned string, and the method itself guarantees not to alter any object state. This is a lightweight accessor that avoids copying the string, making it efficient for repeated reads.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::Pars.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::Pars.body: The method prepends `"FILE_SET"` to the supplied argument list and then forwards this augmented list to the base class’s parsing routine.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::cmIn.body: The constructor initializes the install‑file‑set arguments: it moves the default component into its base class and registers the “FILE_SET” keyword to trigger the `FileSet` handler when parsing the command line.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::oper.body: The `operator=` overload copies the contents of another `cmInstallCommandFileSetArguments` instance into the current object, effectively performing an assignment of the install command arguments.

@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::~cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandFileSetArguments::~cmI.body: The function builds a command‑file argument bundle from the supplied values so that the install routine can later use those arguments to generate or register the command file in the system.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::GetI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::GetI.body: It yields a const‑reference to the internal vector that holds the include‑path strings. By returning a reference rather than a copy, the function avoids unnecessary allocation while still protecting the data from mutation (the const qualifier guarantees the caller cannot modify the returned vector).

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::Pars.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::Pars.body: The method scans a supplied vector of directory strings: if the vector is empty it returns immediately. Otherwise it iterates over the vector beginning at the second element, converts each path to Unix‑style slashes, and appends the cleaned string to the member container `IncludeDirs`.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::cmIn.body: The function scans the current set of install‑command arguments and returns `true` when the supplied argument is present and `false` otherwise. It performs a straightforward comparison against the stored argument list, returning immediately upon a match or after exhausting all entries.

@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::~cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCommandIncludesArgument::~cmI.body: Checks whether a supplied command string contains a particular argument.

@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::cmInst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallCxxModuleBmiGenerator::cmInst.body: Creates an instance that will generate BMI files for a C++ module. It forwards the destination, configuration list, component, message level, and back‑trace to the base generator, records the target name and file‑permission string, and records whether the operation is optional. It marks the generator to perform an action for each configuration by setting `ActionsPerConfig` to true.

@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::cmInstall.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallDirectoryGenerator::cmInstall.body: The constructor of cmInstallDirectoryGenerator initialises a directory‑installation generator: it stores the source directories, destination path, file‑ and directory‑permission strings, and literal arguments. It also records whether the operation is optional. After construction, it scans the destination and each directory string; if any contains a generator expression it flags that per‑configuration actions must be performed, so that logic can be emitted separately for each configuration.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetFileSet@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::GetFileSet@.body: `GetFileSet` returns a pointer to the internal `FileSet` member (`FileSet`) without modifying any state. It simply exposes the existing set; any changes must be performed via the returned pointer’s interface.

@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::cmInstallFi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFileSetGenerator::cmInstallFi.body:
The constructor creates an installer for a given set of files.  
It passes the destination path, component name, and a list of configurations to its base class `cmInstallGenerator`, records the target name and the file set to be installed, stores the requested file‑permission string, and records whether the operation is optional.  
Finally, it sets the internal flag `ActionsPerConfig` to true so that subsequent actions are executed per‑configuration.

@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::cmInstallFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallFilesGenerator::cmInstallFile.body: The constructor builds a file‑install generator: it forwards the destination, configuration list, component name and other flags to the base `cmInstallGenerator`, then records the supplied file list, permissions, optional flag, and rename target. It then inspects the destination, rename string and each file for generator‑expression markers; if any of those contain an expression it flags that per‑configuration actions are required. The logic sets `ActionsPerConfig` to true when it detects such expressions, enabling the installer to generate the appropriate per‑config actions.

@lcmInstallGenerator::CheckCMP0082@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::CheckCMP0082@k_ZN1.body: If `haveSubdirectoryInstall` is true, the function sets `haveInstallAfterSubdirectory` to true; otherwise it leaves the latter unchanged.

@lcmInstallGenerator::Compute@k_ZN18cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::Compute@k_ZN18cmIn.body: The `Compute` method is a virtual entry point that accepts a `cmLocalGenerator*` and simply returns `true`. It provides a place for derived classes to implement custom logic while guaranteeing a successful return value in its default implementation.

@lcmInstallGenerator::GenerateScript@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::GenerateScript@k_Z.body: The `GenerateScript` method writes a small installation script fragment to an output stream. It first builds a condition string for the current component; if that string is non‑empty it emits an `if(...)` line, then delegates to `GenerateScriptConfigs` for the actual configuration code, and finally emits an `endif()` line to close the conditional block. The method relies on the `Indent` helper to keep the output correctly indented.

@lcmInstallGenerator::HaveInstall@k_ZN18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::HaveInstall@k_ZN18.body: The method simply reports that an installation is present by always returning `true`.

@lcmInstallGenerator::SelectMessageLevel.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::SelectMessageLevel.body: The function checks whether the caller has requested that the install message should never be printed (`never`). If so, it immediately returns the `MessageNever` level. Otherwise, it obtains the string value of the CMake variable `CMAKE_INSTALL_MESSAGE` from the provided makefile `mf`. Based on that string it selects the corresponding message level: `"ALWAYS"` yields `MessageAlways`, `"LAZY"` yields `MessageLazy`, `"NEVER"` yields `MessageNever`. If none of those special strings match, the function defaults to `MessageDefault`.

@lcmInstallGenerator::cmInstallGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::cmInstallGenerator.body: Sets up a generator that will write the current CMake configuration files to the given destination directory. The constructor passes the configurations list to the base `cmScriptGenerator`, stores the target component name, message‑level flag, and the back‑trace information, and records the flags controlling whether the produced files are added to the “All” list or excluded from it.

@lcmInstallGenerator::~cmInstallGenerato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallGenerator::~cmInstallGenerato.body: The destructor cleans up resources allocated by the cmInstallGenerator class, calling any subclass‑specific cleanup logic via the virtual override mechanism. It ensures that derived types correctly release their own resources while guaranteeing the base class’s cleanup is executed.

@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallImportedRuntimeArtifactsGener.body: Initializes an installer for imported runtime artifacts, storing target name, file permissions, component, and optional flag, and marks actions-per-config to true.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.body: Adds the provided bundle executable by wrapping the raw generator pointer into a unique wrapper via `cm::make_unique<TargetItem>` and delegating to the internal overload that accepts a `std::unique_ptr<TargetItem>`. The function returns the result of that delegated call.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.body: The function creates a unique‑owned `ImportedTargetItem` from the supplied `bundleExecutable` (using `cm::make_unique`) and then delegates to another overload of `AddBundleExecutable` that accepts an `ImportedTargetItem`. The call returns whatever that overload returns, propagating success/failure back to the caller.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddBund.body: The function returns `false` when an executable is already stored; otherwise it stores the incoming `unique_ptr`’s raw pointer in `BundleExecutable`, forwards ownership to `AddExecutable` via `std::move`, and returns `true`.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.body: Creates a unique TargetItem from the supplied executable and registers that item in the internal list of executable targets.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddExec.body: The function wraps a raw pointer into a `std::unique_ptr` via `cm::make_unique` and forwards that ownership to an overload that stores the object. This simple wrapper keeps ownership semantics safe while delegating actual storage to another method.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.body: The method creates a `TargetItem` unique pointer from the supplied `cmInstallTargetGenerator` and forwards it to the internal `AddLibrary` handler.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddLibr.body: The method records an imported runtime artifact by creating a unique‑owned `ImportedTargetItem` from the supplied generator and storing that item in the system’s internal list of libraries.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.body: The method takes a `cmInstallTargetGenerator*`, constructs a unique `TargetItem` that holds the module, and passes that unique instance to an overloaded `AddModule` that expects a `TargetItem`.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::AddModu.body: It receives a pointer to a module generator, wraps that pointer in a unique‑owned `ImportedTargetItem` via `cm::make_unique`, and forwards the resulting unique pointer to the internal `AddModule` routine that actually registers the module.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Empty@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySet::Empty@k.body: It returns true only when none of the three internal collections—executables, libraries, or modules—contains any elements.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The Compute method assigns the supplied cmLocalGenerator to its internal member variable and returns true to indicate the operation succeeded.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The function writes a CMake snippet that extracts the directory, file name, and file part from a dependency path using a temporary variable prefix. It then registers an install rule for that directory, applies a name‑fix‑up routine, and closes the block with an `endif()`‑style end.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The routine writes a small CMake snippet that wraps an install rule for a library dependency. It emits an “if(NOT …framework/…)” guard, registers a shared‑library install rule keyed by a temporary variable, adds a call to `get_filename_component` to resolve the target name, and finally invokes a fix‑up helper to adjust the filename. The generated code ends with the corresponding `endif()` line.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The routine emits CMake commands that collect the r‑path arguments, optionally append each evaluated path, and finally invokes the CMAKE_INSTALL_NAME_TOOL to regenerate the installation name according to the supplied configuration.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The function emits the CMake commands that install the runtime‑dependency set for a given configuration. It first resolves the installation directory (using `${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}` and any user‑supplied override), emits a `set()` call that records the directory in a temporary variable, and then iterates over each dependency in the list. For each one it evaluates any relative paths, and depending on the dependency type emits either the Apple‑library or Apple‑framework install script. If the build system is not Apple it just issues an `AddInstallRule()` call that creates a symlink‑aware install rule; on Linux it additionally adds logic to strip or replace symbolic‑path components in the target path. The output is written to the supplied `std::ostream` with appropriate indentation.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The routine emits a conditional “strip” snippet to the makefile: it pulls the safe definition value for **CMAKE_STRIP**, and if that value is non‑empty, it opens an `if(CMAKE_INSTALL_DO_STRIP)` block. Inside the block it writes an `execute_process` call to run the strip command (adding a `‑x` flag when the target machine is APPLE), directing the output to the destination directory for the given dependency name. Once the command is emitted, it closes the block with an `endif()`.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: It fetches the value of the internal `Type` field and returns it unchanged.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The `GetDestination` member simply invokes `cmGeneratorExpression::Evaluate` with the stored `Destination` expression, the `LocalGenerator`, and the supplied configuration string, then returns the resulting string.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: Returns a pointer to the internally stored set of runtime dependencies, allowing read‑only access to that set.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: Constructed with the provided arguments, the constructor stores the dependency‐type, dependency set, and the list of installation paths, along with flags that dictate whether the installer should copy the path or just list it. It also records the directory in which the dependency should be installed and the variable names that will be used in the generated script. Finally, it hands over the usual generator parameters (destination, configuration list, component, permissions, message level, exclusion flag and back‑trace) to the base class and marks that actions should be performed on a per‑configuration basis.

@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallRuntimeDependencySetGenerator.body: The function orchestrates the collection of runtime dependencies for a component, registering each required package in the dependency graph so that the installer knows what to pull in during the actual installation phase.

@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::cmInstallScr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallScriptGenerator::cmInstallScr.body: Creates an instance of the generator, stores the supplied script and a flag indicating whether the script should be interpreted as code, and turns on an internal flag that tracks whether the script contains generator expressions.

@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::CheckC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::CheckC.body: The method sets `haveSubdirectoryInstall` to `true` when the current object reports it has an install (via `HaveInstall()`); otherwise it leaves the flag unchanged.

@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::Comput.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::Comput.body: The method stores the supplied `cmLocalGenerator*` in the `LocalGenerator` member and returns `true` to indicate success.

@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::Genera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::Genera.body:
The method writes the appropriate CMake “install” sub‑directory script header into the output stream.  
It first checks the *EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL* flag; if it’s disabled, the method queries the current policy status for **CMP0082**.  
Depending on that status it selects one of three branches:

* **WARN** – nothing is generated; execution falls through.
* **OLD** – no action is taken here because the legacy behaviour is handled elsewhere in the *LocalGenerator*.
* **NEW** – the function emits a small CMake block that checks the global variable *CMAKE_INSTALL_LOCAL_ONLY*, includes the generated *cmake_install.cmake* file from the binary directory, and ends the block with an *endif*.

The emitted block is wrapped with proper indentation and Unix‑style slashes in the binary directory path.

@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::HaveIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::HaveIn.body: The `HaveInstall()` method checks whether any of the install generators supplied by the `Makefile` instance reports that an install has already been performed. It iterates through each generator returned by `Makefile->GetInstallGenerators()`; if any generator’s own `HaveInstall()` returns `true`, this method immediately returns `true`. If no generator reports an install, it returns `false`.

@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::cmInst.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::cmInst.body: The constructor forwards a minimal set of arguments to the `cmInstallGenerator` base class and captures the supplied `cmMakefile` pointer and target directory in member variables. It essentially primes the object to generate install rules for a sub‑directory, storing the back‑trace information for later use while leaving the actual rule generation logic to derived or helper functions.

@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::~cmIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator::~cmIns.body: The `~cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator` destructor simply performs cleanup for the `cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator` instance. When an object of this class is destroyed, the destructor releases any owned resources—such as temporary file descriptors or allocated buffers—by invoking any necessary cleanup logic defined in the base class and then freeing its own allocations. This ensures that when a `cmInstallSubdirectoryGenerator` goes out of scope or is explicitly deleted, its internal state is correctly and safely released without leaking resources.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetImportlin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetImportlin.body: This routine updates the instance’s `ImportlinkMode` property with the supplied value, thereby switching the import‑linking behavior used by other components that depend on that configuration.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetNamelinkM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::SetNamelinkM.body: The method assigns the supplied `mode` value to the `NamelinkMode` member of the current instance. It simply performs that write; no validation, event dispatching, or side‑effects are performed.

@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::cmInstallTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstallTargetGenerator::cmInstallTar.body: The constructor initializes a new install‑target generator. It stores the supplied target name, file‑permission string, and flags for optional import of a library, then flags that each configuration should produce its own install actions (`ActionsPerConfig = true`). It also turns off name‑linking by defaulting `NamelinkMode` and `ImportlinkMode` to `NamelinkModeNone`. The base `cmInstallGenerator` is invoked with the destination, component and message settings, and the optional back‑trace.

@lcmInstrumentation::AddHook@k_ZN17cmIns.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::AddHook@k_ZN17cmIns.body: The method registers a new hook by inserting it into the internal `hooks` collection.

@lcmInstrumentation::AddQuery@k_ZN17cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::AddQuery@k_ZN17cmIn.body: The function accepts a `cmInstrumentationQuery::Query` instance and inserts it into the `queries` container, effectively registering the query in the instrumentation system.

@lcmInstrumentation::ClearGeneratedQueri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::ClearGeneratedQueri.body: The method builds the path to the “query/generated” sub‑folder under the instance’s timing directory. If that path exists as a directory, it calls the helper routine to delete the whole directory tree, effectively wiping out any previously generated query files.

@lcmInstrumentation::CollectTimingAfterB.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::CollectTimingAfterB.body: The method blocks until the process with the supplied PID finishes executing, then triggers an instrumentation step for the “build” command and gathers the resulting timing data.

@lcmInstrumentation::CollectTimingData@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::CollectTimingData@k.body: The `CollectTimingData` routine first verifies the requested hook is enabled; if not, it exits early. It then creates a timestamped JSON “index” file in the data directory, scans that directory for snippet files (excluding the index itself), collects their paths, and records them in a JSON object. The JSON is enriched with metadata (hook name, data and build directories, version, and optional static system info). Finally, it writes the JSON out, triggers any registered callbacks with the index path, optionally prepares a CDash‑specific collection, and cleans up by deleting the temporary snippets and index files.

@lcmInstrumentation::ComputeSuffixHash@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::ComputeSuffixHash@k.body: The function hashes the supplied string with SHA‑3‑256 and then returns a 20‑character string padded with zeroes as needed.

@lcmInstrumentation::ComputeSuffixTime@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::ComputeSuffixTime@k.body: The function captures the current UTC epoch time, truncates it to seconds, then appends the millisecond remainder (zero‑padded to four digits) to a canonical timestamp string produced by `cmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT`. The resulting string is the formatted UTC date‑time with a four‑digit millisecond suffix.

@lcmInstrumentation::GetCDashDir@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::GetCDashDir@k_ZN17c.body: It simply returns the instance’s `cdashDir` member value as a const reference, allowing callers to read the directory path without modifying it.

@lcmInstrumentation::GetCommandStr@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::GetCommandStr@k_ZN1.body: The function loops through the supplied argument vector, wrapping each element in single quotes and appending them to a single string separated by spaces. Each pass calls the helper `cmStrCat` to build the intermediate string, and finally returns the fully‑concatenated string.

@lcmInstrumentation::GetDynamicSystemInf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::GetDynamicSystemInf.body: The function gathers current system metrics by creating a `cmsys::SystemInformation` object, executing its CPU and memory checks, and then writes the retrieved used‑memory value into the first argument and the average load into the second.

@lcmInstrumentation::GetPreTestStats@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::GetPreTestStats@k_Z.body: The function records system information in the `preTestStats` container before a test runs, but only when the `DynamicSystemInformation` query flag is set.

@lcmInstrumentation::HasHook@k_ZNK17cmIn.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::HasHook@k_ZNK17cmIn.body: The `HasHook` method simply reports whether the specified `Hook` is present in the internal collection. It performs a constant‑time lookup against the stored set of hooks and returns `true` if the element exists, `false` otherwise. The method is const‑qualified, guaranteeing that no internal state is altered.

@lcmInstrumentation::HasPreOrPostBuildHo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::HasPreOrPostBuildHo.body: Returns true if the instrumentation has any pre‑build or post‑build hook registered, otherwise false.

@lcmInstrumentation::HasQuery@k_ZNK17cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::HasQuery@k_ZNK17cmI.body: The function returns true if the specified query is present in the `queries` container; otherwise it returns false. It performs a single lookup (`find`) in the container, yielding average‑case constant‑time complexity.

@lcmInstrumentation::HasQuery@k_ZNK17cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::HasQuery@k_ZNK17cmI.body: It reads the internal `hasQuery` flag and returns its value, indicating whether this instrumentation instance currently represents a query.

@lcmInstrumentation::HasQueryFile@k_ZN17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::HasQueryFile@k_ZN17.body: The function `HasQueryFile` returns `true` when the supplied file name refers to an existing file (typically a query‑definition file) that can be opened and read; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmInstrumentation::InsertDynamicSystem.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::InsertDynamicSystem.body: The routine queries the current process for its memory footprint and CPU load, then writes those values into the supplied JSON tree under keys prefixed by the caller‑supplied string—adding a “dynamicSystemInformation” object if it’s missing and storing the host‑memory‑used and CPU‑load‑average fields.

@lcmInstrumentation::InsertStaticSystemI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::InsertStaticSystemI.body: The routine creates a `cmsys::SystemInformation` instance, runs several checks on the host machine, and then serialises a collection of identifiers, CPU and memory metrics, OS details, and vendor data into a JSON‐style object that it finally attaches to the caller’s root node.

@lcmInstrumentation::InsertTimingData@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::InsertTimingData@k_.body: The function records an event’s start time and elapsed duration. It converts the system start time to a millisecond‑count since the epoch, computes the time elapsed from the steady clock, and writes those two UInt64 values into the supplied JSON value under the keys “timeStart” and “duration”.

@lcmInstrumentation::InstrumentCommand@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::InstrumentCommand@k.body: The `InstrumentCommand` routine orchestrates a complete instrumentation cycle around an arbitrary callback. It first serialises the supplied command into a JSON blob, then optionally injects pre‑execution system metrics (CPU load, memory usage) if a dynamic‑system‑info query is active. The supplied callback is invoked; its return value is stored in the JSON. If the caller requests a reload of queries post‑execution, the routine refreshes the internal query cache and optionally records fresh dynamic‑system data. Afterward, it appends any options or array‑options keys that are supplied, and for certain commands it pads a config placeholder. Finally the JSON is dumped to a file named with the command type and a hash of the command string, ensuring the file carries a time‑stamp suffix. The function returns the callback’s return code.

@lcmInstrumentation::InstrumentTest@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::InstrumentTest@k_ZN.body: The function records a test run: it builds a JSON object with the test name, command string, result code, and configuration, enriches it with timing data, optional dynamic system info, and then writes it to a uniquely‑named JSON file whose name encodes the command hash and time stamp, returning that file name.

@lcmInstrumentation::LoadQueries@k_ZN17c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::LoadQueries@k_ZN17c.body: The `LoadQueries` method checks for a “query” file in the instrumenter’s primary and user‑provided directories; if found, it loads query definitions with `ReadJSONQueries`, toggling the `hasQuery` flag. When the environment variable `CTEST_USE_INSTRUMENTATION` is active, it optionally attaches a CDash‑ready hook, registers a system‑info query, and prepares a set of build‑related directories and a mapping of snippet identifiers to build stages. If an experimental instrumentation UUID matches the environment value, it performs the full hook/query setup and marks queries as available.

@lcmInstrumentation::PrepareDataForCDash.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::PrepareDataForCDash.body: The routine parses an index JSON file, validates that it contains the expected “snippets” section, then iterates over each snippet entry. For each snippet it loads the snippet’s own JSON, checks the declared “role”, and looks up that role in a pre‑built map. Depending on that lookup it either skips the file, copies it into a generic “build/commands” directory, or, if the snippet declares a specific target, copies it into a per‑target sub‑folder. Throughout the function it reports errors and warning messages for missing keys or unknown roles.

@lcmInstrumentation::ReadJSONQueries@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::ReadJSONQueries@k_Z.body: The function scans a directory for files ending in “.json”, loads each matching file via `ReadJSONQuery`, and returns true if at least one such file was processed.

@lcmInstrumentation::ReadJSONQuery@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::ReadJSONQuery@k_ZN1.body: Creates a `cmInstrumentationQuery` object and delegates deserialization of the JSON file to its `ReadJSON` method, passing the current instance’s error message and collections (`queries`, `hooks`, `callbacks`) so they are populated during the call.

@lcmInstrumentation::SpawnBuildDaemon@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::SpawnBuildDaemon@k_.body: It collects timing data for a pre‑build hook, and if a post‑build hook is enabled it spawns a detached child process (the “build daemon”) that runs a helper program with the current process ID and a target directory. The child is launched via a UV process chain and run in the event loop.

@lcmInstrumentation::WriteInstrumentatio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::WriteInstrumentatio.body: Serializes the supplied `Json::Value` into a file located under the given sub‑directory—creating the directory first if it doesn’t already exist.

@lcmInstrumentation::WriteJSONQuery@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::WriteJSONQuery@k_ZN.body: The routine serialises the supplied sets of queries, hooks and a vector of callback strings into a JSON object whose root contains a version field and three arrays, then writes that object to a new file in the *query/generated* directory. The file name is formed as `query‑<n>.json`, where *n* is the count of already‑present files (minus the special `.` and `..` entries) so that each invocation creates a uniquely numbered file.

@lcmInstrumentation::cmInstrumentation@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::cmInstrumentation@k.body: The move constructor initializes a new `cmInstrumentation` instance by taking ownership of the internal data from an rvalue reference to another `cmInstrumentation` object; it performs member‑wise moves of the source’s members so that the original instance is left in a valid but unspecified state.

@lcmInstrumentation::cmInstrumentation@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::cmInstrumentation@k.body: The constructor retrieves a unique UUID for the instrumentation feature, stores the supplied binary directory, and builds two directory paths: a default “/​.cmake/instrumentation‑<uuid>/v1” under the binary dir, and, if available, a user‑specific “/instrumentation‑<uuid>/v1” under the system‑config dir. Finally, it calls `LoadQueries()` to load any pending queries.

@lcmInstrumentation::cmInstrumentation@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::cmInstrumentation@k.body: Creates a new cmInstrumentation object that duplicates the state of the supplied instance, copying all its internal members into the new object.

@lcmInstrumentation::operator=@k_ZN17cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::operator=@k_ZN17cmI.body: The overloaded assignment operator copies the state of another cmInstrumentation object into the current instance, returning a reference to the modified object for chaining.

@lcmInstrumentation::operator=@k_ZN17cmI.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::operator=@k_ZN17cmI.body: Assigns the contents of a given `cmInstrumentation` instance to the current one, copying its internal state and returning a reference to the updated object.

@lcmInstrumentation::~cmInstrumentation@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmInstrumentation::~cmInstrumentation@.body: The `~cmInstrumentation()` function is the class destructor. It tidily releases all instrumentation resources allocated during the lifecycle of a `cmInstrumentation` instance, ensuring a clean teardown without leaving dangling handles or memory leaks.

@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUNDSt17basi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsNOTFOUND@k_Z12cmIsNOTFOUNDSt17basi.body: This helper forwards the supplied string to the underlying `cmValue::IsNOTFOUND` routine, returning the resulting boolean that signals whether the value is marked as *not found*.

@lcmIsSpace@k_Z9cmIsSpacec@f./Source/cmS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmIsSpace@k_Z9cmIsSpacec@f./Source/cmS.body: cmIsSpace casts the input character to unsigned char before calling std::isspace, then returns the result as a bool.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Map@k_ZN19cmJSONH.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Map@k_ZN19cmJSONH.body: The `Map` template builds a `FilteredObject` that produces a `std::map<std::string,T>` by applying the supplied `func` to each JSON entry. When compiling under C++17 or newer it uses a `std::true_type()` marker to skip filtering, otherwise it supplies a trivial lambda that always returns `FilterResult::Continue`.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Object::Bind@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Object::Bind@k_ZN.body:
This template registers a named JSON parser.  
It takes a name (`cm::string_view`), a placeholder (`nullptr_t`), a callable `func`, and an optional `required` flag.
