Inside, it forwards to `BindPrivate`, wrapping `func` in a lambda that creates a temporary of type `M` and forwards that temporary, the JSON value and state to `func`. The lambda then returns the Boolean result of `func`. The method returns a reference to the `Object` on which it was invoked, enabling fluent chaining.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Object::Bind@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Object::Bind@k_ZN.body: This function registers a member value of an object in JSON deserialization logic. It accepts a member pointer `U M::*`, a parsing callback `func`, and an optional `required` flag. Internally it forwards a lambda that captures the callback and member pointer, invoking `func(out.*member, value, state)` on the target object `out`. The returned reference is that of the `Object` being bound.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Object::Bind@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Object::Bind@k_ZN.body: The `Bind` function is a convenience wrapper that takes a name (as a `cm::string_view`), a callable `func`, and an optional flag indicating whether the binding is mandatory. It creates a `MemberFunction` object from `func` and forwards everything to an internal helper (`BindPrivate`). This helper typically registers the callable under the supplied name and returns a reference to the object for fluent usage.

@lcmJSONHelperBuilder::Object::Object@k_.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmList::transform_error::operator=@k_Z.body: operator= overloads the assignment operator for transform_error. It takes an rvalue reference of transform_error and returns a reference to the object, enabling assignment of error instances.

@lcmList::transform_error::operator=@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::transform_error::operator=@k_Z.body: The `operator=` in `transform_error` copies the internal error message from another `transform_error` instance, effectively performing a copy assignment. It returns a reference to the current object for chaining.

@lcmList::transform_error::transform_err.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::transform_error::transform_err.body: The `transform_error` function is a small helper that produces a new `transform_error` instance from an existing one. It takes an rvalue reference to a `transform_error` (allowing move‑semantics), copies or forwards the underlying exception message, and returns the freshly constructed object. This pattern simplifies propagating a transform‑related exception through different layers of the code, avoiding unnecessary copies while preserving the original error details.

@lcmList::transform_error::transform_err.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::transform_error::transform_err.body: The `transform_error` constructor forwards a given message string to the standard `std::runtime_error` base class, enabling the derived exception to carry that text when thrown.

@lcmList::transform_error::transform_err.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::transform_error::transform_err.body: Creates a runtime‑error object that records a failure occurring while attempting to transform data.

@lcmList::transform_error::~transform_er.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::transform_error::~transform_er.body: The destructor `~transform_error()` cleans up a custom exception instance derived from `std::runtime_error`. It releases any held resources (e.g., allocated buffers or state flags) and may emit diagnostic information before the object is discarded.

@lcmList::~cmList@k_ZN6cmListD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmList::~cmList@k_ZN6cmListD1Ev.body: The defaulted destructor `~cmList()` automatically destroys the `cmList` object and frees any resources it holds. It runs during object destruction, ensuring proper cleanup without custom logic.

@lcmListCommand@k_Z13cmListCommandRKSt6v.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListCommand@k_Z13cmListCommandRKSt6v.body: The function receives a vector of command arguments and a status object, verifies there are enough arguments, then uses a static map of sub‑commands (e.g. “LENGTH”, “GET”, “APPEND”, etc.) to dispatch to the corresponding handler function and returns the result of that handler.

@lcmListFileBacktrace::cmListFileBacktra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileBacktrace::cmListFileBacktra.body: The `cmListFileBacktrace` public method is the entry point for retrieving the back‑trace of a list file operation. It orchestrates the logic that walks the current list‑file context, collects the relevant back‑trace information (usually a stack of file operations), and returns it to the caller for diagnostic or logging purposes.

@lcmListFileBacktrace::cmListFileBacktra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileBacktrace::cmListFileBacktra.body: The function takes a `cmListFileBacktrace` instance (by const reference) and uses it to populate internal bookkeeping about which files were opened, closed, or inspected during a run. It walks the supplied object’s trace data, feeds it into the cache’s tracking structure, and ultimately returns a status indicating whether the back‑trace reconstruction succeeded.

@lcmListFileBacktrace::cmListFileBacktra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileBacktrace::cmListFileBacktra.body: cmListFileBacktrace is used to create a *link item* that represents a back‑trace of a file’s dependencies. When called in the dependency‑generation code, it produces a backtrace object that the system can insert into the emitted dependency list (see the several `emitted.insert` calls). The function itself returns this back‑trace structure; it does not perform any heavy computation beyond that – it simply builds and hands back the data needed to track a file’s link chain.

@lcmListFileBacktrace::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileBacktrace::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: `operator=` moves the contents of the right‑hand side into the current object: it frees any previously held resources, copies over all internal state (including file descriptors, internal lists, etc.) and leaves the source object in a valid, though “empty”, state. This allows efficient reassignment of `cmListFileBacktrace` objects.

@lcmListFileBacktrace::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileBacktrace::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: The operator= overload copies the state of a cmListFileBacktrace instance into the target object and returns a reference to that object for chaining.

@lcmListFileBacktrace::~cmListFileBacktr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileBacktrace::~cmListFileBacktr.body: The `~cmListFileBacktrace()` function pulls back‑trace data from the cached file list: it walks the in‑memory structure of list entries in reverse order, extracts any stored back‑trace metadata and packages that into the response. It’s the routine that translates the internal back‑trace records into a consumable structure for callers.

@lcmListFileContext::cmListFileContext@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileContext::cmListFileContext@k.body: Initializes a context record for a file, storing its identifier, path and line number to be queried or sorted later during file‑listing operations.

@lcmListFileContext::cmListFileContext@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileContext::cmListFileContext@k.body: The copy constructor simply creates a new `cmListFileContext` instance that is an exact copy of the source instance. Since it is marked `= default`, the compiler generates the standard member‑wise copy logic; no custom code runs during construction.

@lcmListFileFunction::Arguments@k_ZNK18c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileFunction::Arguments@k_ZNK18c.body: Returns a const reference to the internally‑stored vector of `cmListFileArgument` objects, exposing the underlying `Impl->Arguments` collection without copying or modifying it.

@lcmListFileFunction::Line@k_ZNK18cmList.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileFunction::Line@k_ZNK18cmList.body: Returns the line number stored in the object’s implementation, returning it unchanged as a long value without modifying the instance.

@lcmListFileFunction::LowerCaseName@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileFunction::LowerCaseName@k_ZN.body: The method is a const, noexcept member function that simply returns a constant reference to the `LowerCaseName` string stored inside the implementation object (`Impl`). It guarantees no state change and no exception will be thrown, yielding a direct reference to the underlying value.

@lcmListFileFunction::OriginalName@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmListFileFunction::OriginalName@k_ZNK.body: The member returns a constant reference to the `OriginalName` member inside the implementation object, guaranteeing it can be accessed safely and without exception overhead.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::ComputeObjectF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::ComputeObjectF.body: It iterates through the mapping of source files, calling `GetObjectFileNameWithoutTarget` for each entry. The function supplies the source file, the target’s object directory, a flag for whether the source extension is preserved, and any custom extension returned by the target. The resulting filename string is written back into the mapping’s value.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetConfigNames.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetConfigNames.body: Returns a const reference to the internal vector holding the configuration names, giving callers read‑only access to the stored list.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetTargetFortr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetTargetFortr.body: The function builds a string of compiler flags for a Fortran target. It first adds a module‑output flag if the target needs it, then determines the module directory: it uses the target’s own directory if available, otherwise falls back to a default. That directory string is appended as a “‑mod‑dir” flag and, where required, an explicit include‑path flag. Finally, if the build system defines a separate module‑path flag, the function duplicates each include directory into a flag prefixed with that flag. The composed string of all these flags is returned.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetWorkingDire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::GetWorkingDire.body: It returns a reference to the string that represents the current binary directory stored in the generator’s internal snapshot.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.body: Initialises the generator by calling the base `cmLocalGenerator` constructor and then decides which configuration set to expose. If the global generator is in multi‑config mode and there is at least one makefile, it uses that makefile’s name; otherwise it falls back to the current makefile’s name, and finally retrieves the corresponding generator configurations.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::cmLocalCommonG.body: The constructor copies the configuration from a supplied `cmLocalCommonGenerator` instance, forwarding any required setup to the base `cmLocalGenerator` class to ensure a new generator is properly wired up.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::operator=@k_ZN.body: The operator overload copies the contents of the right‑hand side instance into the current object and returns a reference to the object.

@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::~cmLocalCommon.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalCommonGenerator::~cmLocalCommon.body: The destructor `~cmLocalCommonGenerator()` is overridden to guarantee that any resources allocated by the `cmLocalCommonGenerator` object are properly released when the object is destroyed, and to propagate the cleanup to its base classes before the instance is de‑allocated.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendCompileOptions.body: The method short‑circuits when `options_list` is empty, otherwise it parses that string into a `cmList` and forwards the request to an overloaded `AppendCompileOptions` that works with that list and an optional regex.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDefines@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendDefines@k_ZNK1.body: The function takes an input string list, expands it into a collection of identifiers (via `cmExpandListWithBacktrace`), then iterates over the resulting set adding each identifier into the supplied `defines` set.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlags@k_ZNK16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendFlags@k_ZNK16c.body: The function appends `newFlags` to `flags` only when `newFlags` is non‑empty and contains at least one non‑space character; if `flags` already has content it inserts a preceding space before the new text.

@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIncludeDirecto.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::AppendIncludeDirecto.body: The function first checks whether the incoming include list string is empty; if it is, the function exits immediately because there is nothing to add. Otherwise it parses the string into a list of paths (using the helper constructor), then delegates to the overloaded implementation that actually performs the appending logic, passing along the target vector and the parsed list. This helper effectively expands a single string of include directories into the internal vector representation used by the rest of the generator.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeObjectFilenam.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ComputeObjectFilenam.body: This virtual method is meant to be overridden by derived classes to generate object‑file names during the build process. In its current form it simply receives a map and a target context but performs no actions.

@lcmLocalGenerator::ConvertToIncludeRefe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::ConvertToIncludeRefe.body: Converts a filesystem path into an include‑reference string by delegating to the base‑class helper `ConvertToOutputForExisting`. The routine accepts a `std::string` path and an `OutputFormat` enum and returns the formatted include string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateRulePlaceholde.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateRulePlaceholde.body: Creates a cmRulePlaceholderExpander that holds the compiler‑specific flag mappings for a given build step. If the step is Link and the target is an executable, shared, or module library, it collects the appropriate flag variable (e.g. `CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_CREATE_<LANG>_FLAGS`) and registers it in the mapping; otherwise it defers to the base implementation.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateRulePlaceholde.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateRulePlaceholde.body: The `CreateRulePlaceholderExpander` helper constructs a new `cmRulePlaceholderExpander` instance using the current build context. It pulls in the `Compilers`, `VariableMappings`, and the system‑root directories (`CompilerSysroot` and `LinkerSysroot`) from the owning `cmLocalGenerator` object, and hands them along with the supplied `buildStep`. The function simply returns a `std::unique_ptr` to the freshly‑created expander.

@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateUtilityOutput@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::CreateUtilityOutput@.body: Creates a path string pointing into the build‑generated CMakeFiles directory, looks up (or creates) a source file for that path, tags the file as symbolic if found, and returns the full path string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::FindGeneratorTargetT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::FindGeneratorTargetT.body: The method resolves a target name in the current context: it first checks for an imported target; if none, it resolves an alias; if still none, it checks for a non‑alias local target; if none, it falls back to the global generator, returning a pointer (or nullptr if no match).

@lcmLocalGenerator::Generate@k_ZN16cmLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::Generate@k_ZN16cmLoc.body: The `Generate` method is a virtual hook that does nothing in its base implementation; derived classes are expected to override it to perform custom generation logic.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetBinaryDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetBinaryDirectory@k.body: The function simply forwards the request for the current build’s binary‑output directory to the underlying CMake instance. It reads the current instance’s output path via `GetCMakeInstance()` and returns that string unchanged.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCMakeInstance@k_Z.body: The method retrieves the CMake instance that the global generator holds and returns it unchanged.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCurrentBinaryDire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetCurrentBinaryDire.body: It returns a reference to the current binary‑directory string stored in the state snapshot, without creating a copy.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGeneratorTargets@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGeneratorTargets@.body: It returns the vector of generator targets held by the object, exposing it as a read‑only reference so callers can read the data without copying or allowing modification.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGlobalGenerator@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetGlobalGenerator@k.body: It returns the internal `GlobalGenerator` pointer held by the object, exposing that reference to callers.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeDirectorie.body: The function simply delegates to the internal helper `GetIncludeDirectoriesImplicit`, passing along the target, language, and configuration arguments to populate the supplied vector with the directories that should be added to a target’s include search path.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeFlags@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetIncludeFlags@k_ZN.body: The routine assembles a space‑separated list of compiler‑include flags from a list of directories. It consults the target’s language to pull the proper flag tokens, optionally quoting paths and handling system/framework include directories specially. The resulting string is trimmed of trailing separators before being returned.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetLinkDependencyFil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetLinkDependencyFil.body: The `GetLinkDependencyFile` function simply returns the fixed string `"link.d"`. It is marked `const` and does not make use of either the `target` or `config` parameters, which are deliberately omitted from the body.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetMakefile@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetMakefile@k_ZN16cm.body: The function simply returns the internal `Makefile` pointer stored in the current object. It exposes the stored `Makefile` instance without any modification.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZN.body: The method simply forwards a request for a policy’s current state to the underlying `Makefile` object and returns the result it receives.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetProjectName@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetProjectName@k_ZNK.body: Retrieves the project name from the internal `StateSnapshot` without modifying any state.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourceDirectory@k.body: The method returns a const reference to the string that represents the source‑root directory. It simply forwards the request to the internal CMake instance’s `GetHomeDirectory()` call, guaranteeing the returned reference cannot be modified by the caller.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourcesWithOutput.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetSourcesWithOutput.body:
The method first determines whether the supplied name is a full path.  
If it isn’t, it performs a linear lookup: it fills a `cmSourcesWithOutput` struct with the target found by `LinearGetTargetWithOutput` and the associated source file obtained via `LinearGetSourceFileWithOutput`.  
If the name is already a full path, it falls back to the pre‑built `OutputToSource` map and returns the cached `Sources` value when present. If no entry exists, it returns an empty structure.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetCompileFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetCompileFlag.body: The function builds a list of compiler flag strings for a specific target by first adding language‑specific flags, then conditionally appending flags for features such as IPO, Fortran, or Swift compile modes (handling the three Swift modes), and finally merging any feature, visibility, color‑diagnostics, framework, and custom options from the target’s makefile before returning the assembled vector.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDefines@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDefines@k_Z.body: Invokes an internal overload that returns a set of BT\<std::string> objects; for each element it pulls the underlying string value and inserts that value into the supplied `defines` set.

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetDirectory@k.body: The method is a virtual const member that simply logs an error via `cmSystemTools::Error` and then returns an empty string (the `cmGeneratorTarget` argument is ignored).

@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFortranFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::GetTargetFortranFlag.body: The method supplies the Fortran‑specific compiler flags for a target. In the base implementation it simply returns an empty string; derived generator classes override it to provide the actual flag string.

@lcmLocalGenerator::IssueMessage@k_ZNK16.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::IssueMessage@k_ZNK16.body: Sends the supplied message type and text to the CMake instance associated with the generator, attaching the stored back‑trace information for context.

@lcmLocalGenerator::JoinDefines@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::JoinDefines@k_ZN16cm.body:
Collects the supplied set of compiler‑define names into a single command‑line string.  
For each entry it prefixes the compiler‑specific flag (default “‑D”, overridden by the “CMAKE_<lang>_DEFINE_FLAG” value), escapes any special characters required by the chosen compiler (Watcom or standard), and appends the escaped token to the output string, separating tokens with spaces.

@lcmLocalGenerator::MakeCustomCommandGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::MakeCustomCommandGen.body: The function creates a single `cmCustomCommandGenerator` instance by constructing it with the supplied `cmCustomCommand` and configuration string, adding that instance to a vector, and then returning the vector containing the newly created generator.

@lcmLocalGenerator::~cmLocalGenerator@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalGenerator::~cmLocalGenerator@k_.body: The virtual destructor `~cmLocalGenerator()` is declared in the header and defined in the `.cxx` source. It guarantees the base class’s cleanup logic runs when a `cmLocalGenerator` instance goes out of scope, properly invoking any derived‑class destructors via the C++ virtual‑destructor mechanism.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AddCustomComman.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AddCustomComman.body: The method registers a custom command and its associated target. It inserts the command into a map keyed by the command pointer; if the command is new, it also records the command in a list. Finally, it adds the target to the command’s set of targets.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AdditionalClean.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AdditionalClean.body: It pulls an “ADDITIONAL_CLEAN_FILES” property, evaluates each listed path against the current binary directory, and registers the resolved file paths with the global Ninja generator for cleanup.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.body: The routine walks through the list of dependency names that a custom command declares. For each name it calls `GetRealDependency` to turn the logical dependency into a concrete path that applies to the current build configuration. If that resolution succeeds, the resulting path is converted into the Ninja‑style file path (via `ConvertToNinjaPath`) and appended to the `cmNinjaDeps` vector that will later be emitted into the Ninja build graph.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendCustomCom.body:
The function builds a sequence of shell commands that will run the custom commands supplied by the user.  
It first ensures the build runs in the appropriate directory by inserting a `cd …` line when the custom command has a working directory.  
Then it generates a launcher prefix (via `MakeCustomLauncher`) and appends each custom command string, formatting each one appropriately (shell‑style or Ninjamulti‑style) and appending any command‑specific arguments via `AppendArguments`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetDep.body: The method simply forwards the supplied target, output list, configuration strings and dependency flags to the global Ninja generator to register the target’s dependencies.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetOut.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::AppendTargetOut.body: The function forwards a target’s output dependencies to the global Ninja generator. It calls the singleton’s `AppendTargetOutputs` method, passing the target, the collected outputs, the supplied configuration string, and a flag (`DependOnTargetArtifact`) that indicates the outputs should be considered dependencies in the Ninja build script.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::BuildCommandLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::BuildCommandLin.body: BuildCommandLine collects an array of command fragments into one executable shell line. If no fragments are supplied it simply returns a no‑op placeholder. When a custom step is supplied it checks whether the total length of the fragments would exceed the system‑defined limit; if so, it writes the fragments to a temporary script, appends a hash of that script for cache‑busting, and returns a command that invokes that script. On non‑Windows systems the fragments are concatenated with “&&” separators, adding parentheses around any fragment containing “||” so precedence is preserved. On Windows a special wrapper is used and an extra quote is added around the whole command. This logic guarantees a single, deterministic command string that can be safely cached or rerun‑ed by the Ninja build system.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToInclud.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::ConvertToInclud.body: The function takes a file path and an output format flag, then delegates to the `ConvertToOutputFormat` routine to produce the appropriately formatted include‑reference string.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateRulePlace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateRulePlace.body: Creates a placeholder expander for the supplied build step and target, then configures the target implementation library before returning the new object.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateRulePlace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateRulePlace.body: The function delegates to the base generator to create a rule‑placeholder expander object for the given build step, then configures that expander with the special target‑implib placeholder string (“$TARGET_IMPLIB”) before returning it wrapped in a unique‑pointer. This placeholder string is later replaced during rule expansion so the rule can reference the implementation library that will be generated.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateUtilityOu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::CreateUtilityOu.body: When called, the function first checks whether the build is in a multi‑configuration mode and whether the supplied by‑products are unique for the current backtrace. If either condition fails, it simply defers to the base implementation. Otherwise it builds a base path in the output directory, creates a symbolic source file entry for each configuration (tagged with the “SYMBOLIC” property), registers the target with the global Ninja generator, and finally returns a path string that contains a `$<CONFIG>` placeholder to be expanded later.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::Generate@k_ZN21.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::Generate@k_ZN21.body: The function resolves the output directory relative to the top‑level build directory, then sequentially emits the common, per‑configuration, and global make files. For each target that is part of the build system it creates a Ninja build definition. It handles multi‑configuration builds by generating phony‑alias rules for every configuration, appending the necessary dependencies, and finally writing the aggregate build file. This orchestration ensures that all targets—both global and per‑configuration—receive the appropriate dependency and output declarations in the generated Ninja scripts.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.body: The `GetCMakeInstance` method is a thin wrapper that simply returns the CMake instance managed by the global generator. It calls `GetGlobalGenerator()` to obtain the singleton global generator object, then forwards the call to that object's `GetCMakeInstance()` method, returning the resulting `cmake*`. No additional logic or state changes occur; the method merely delegates the request to the global generator.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCMakeInstanc.body: The `GetCMakeInstance()` member is a straightforward const accessor that delegates to the global generator. It retrieves the global generator instance via `GetGlobalGenerator()` and then returns whatever that instance exposes through its own `GetCMakeInstance()` call. This keeps the local generator lightweight—no new objects are created, and the function simply forwards the call.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCommonFileSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetCommonFileSt.body: The method retrieves a reference to the shared `cmGeneratedFileStream` that belongs to the global Ninja generator instance. By delegating to `GetGlobalNinjaGenerator()->GetCommonFileStream()`, it guarantees that every local generator shares the same stream object while keeping the logic centralized in one place.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.body: The function retrieves the singleton global generator by calling the base class’s `GetGlobalGenerator()` and casting the returned pointer to `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator*`. This yields a pointer to the shared global instance used by all local generators.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetGlobalNinjaG.body: Returns a pointer to the global ninja generator by static‑casting the base generator returned by `GetGlobalGenerator()` to `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator const*`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetHomeRelative.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetHomeRelative.body: Returns the value stored in the member variable `HomeRelativeOutputPath`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetImplFileStre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetImplFileStre.body: The function forwards a request to the shared, globally‑constructed Ninja generator. By taking the supplied *config* string, it calls `GetImplFileStream` on the singleton generator returned by `GetGlobalNinjaGenerator()`, and returns the resulting `cmGeneratedFileStream` reference. Thus it simply proxies the call to the central generator instance, ensuring that all file‑stream creation logic resides in that single source.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetLinkDependen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetLinkDependen.body: The function constructs the full path to the link‑dependency file for a target by concatenating the target’s support directory with the global N‑inja generator’s configuration directory and the fixed suffix “/link.d”.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetRulesFileStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetRulesFileStr.body: The `GetRulesFileStream` method simply forwards a request for the rules‑file stream to the global generator: it calls `GetGlobalNinjaGenerator()->GetRulesFileStream()` and returns that reference directly.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetTargetDirect.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetTargetDirect.body: Returns a string that starts with “CMakeFiles/”, appends the target’s name, and finally adds either “_dir” (when the compiler macro __VMS is defined) or “.dir” (otherwise). The result is returned to the caller.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetWorkingDirec.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::GetWorkingDirec.body: The method returns a const reference to the current binary directory obtained from the state object.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::HasUniqueByprod.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::HasUniqueByprod.body: The routine walks the supplied *byproducts* list, parses each entry into a generator expression, expands that expression for every available config, and verifies that no expanded output path is repeated. If any duplicate path appears, the function immediately returns `false`; otherwise it returns `true`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomComma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomComma.body: The function builds a list of custom‑command generators for a given command and output file. It first determines whether the command requires a dep‑file transformation by inspecting the command’s status. It then creates the base generator, and if the global generator permits cross‑configuration builds, it adds generators for each alternate configuration. Finally, it verifies that all outputs/by‑products use generator expressions and that each configuration’s outputs are distinct; if not, it removes the cross‑configured generators so the returned list contains only unique, valid generators.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomLaunc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MakeCustomLaunc.body: The function retrieves the `RULE_LAUNCH_CUSTOM` property from the current makefile; if that property is empty it returns an empty string. Otherwise it builds a comma‑separated list of each output path (converting them to an appropriate shell format), assigns that string to a placeholder variable `Output`, plus the command role into `Role`, creates a rule‑placeholder expander, and expands the retrieved property string with these placeholders. The resulting expanded string is returned.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MaybeRelativeTo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::MaybeRelativeTo.body: The method forwards the supplied file path through the top‑level binary‑directory resolution logic of the global Ninja generator: it first normalises the path via `MaybeRelativeToTopBinDir`, then asks the shared Ninja generator to compute the final output location with `NinjaOutputPath`, returning that fully resolved path.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuildFileT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteBuildFileT.body: The function emits the top section of a Ninja build file. It writes the common header first, then for each build configuration it inserts the required Ninja version, a configuration‑specific variable, and the list of files that belong to that configuration. After that, it appends the common file list and work‑directory declaration, and finally writes the header for the auxiliary rules file.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCommandScr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCommandScr.body: The function produces a shell or batch script from a list of commands, placing it in the target‑specific output directory (or the current binary directory if no target). It appends the config identifier, creates the directory if needed, writes a header that turns off echo or enables `-e`, writes each command line with any `$` token unescaped, and on Windows appends a failure label and exit handling. The path of the created script is returned.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.body: It gathers the outputs, by‑products, and order‑only dependencies for a given custom command, hashes the main output to produce a unique target name (appending a short SHA‑256 fragment), and writes the corresponding Ninja rule—emitting either a phony rule when no command lines exist or a full command rule that records outputs, dependencies, and optional dep‑file handling.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteCustomComm.body: Iterates over each custom command stored in the generator’s data structure and emits a corresponding build‑statement line into the target file. For each command it looks up the target information in the internal map and delegates the actual formatting to `WriteCustomCommandBuildStatement`.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaConfi.body: The method registers the supplied configuration string as the value of a predefined variable name. It defers to the shared helper that emits the appropriate declaration line in the Ninja build file, annotating it with the given help‑text.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.body: The routine emits a divider line, writes a comment marking the inclusion of auxiliary files, retrieves the global ninja generator instance, encodes the path to the rules file, and emits a single include directive that references that encoded path with a brief description.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaFiles.body: The routine writes a divider comment, then inserts a comment‑labeled include line for the global “common” Ninja file into the output stream. It obtains the global generator, encodes the path, and calls `WriteInclude` to emit the actual include directive.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaRequi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaRequi.body: The routine picks the lowest Ninja version that still supports the generator’s features (console‑pool and manifest‑restart) and emits a comment line stating that version as the required‑ninja‑version directive in the generated .ninja file.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaWorkD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteNinjaWorkD.body: The function writes a comment that explains the logical path to the build‑output working directory, normalises that path (removing any “ninja‑” prefix and ensuring a trailing slash), encodes it safely for shell usage, and finally emits a line that assigns the variable `cmake_ninja_workdir` to the encoded path.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WritePools@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WritePools@k_ZN.body: The `WritePools` routine writes a “pools” section into the generated Ninja file. It first tries to fetch a global `JOB_POOLS` property; if that isn’t defined it falls back to a makefile‑specific definition. Once a list is obtained it emits a comment line and iterates over each pool string, expecting the form `poolName=number`. For each entry it emits a block that declares the pool name and its depth. If a string cannot be parsed into the expected `<name>=<depth>` format, it reports an error.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProcessedM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProcessedM.body: The `WriteProcessedMakefile` helper writes a header block into the generated Makefile. It first emits a divider line, then emits a comment line that names the current CMakeLists source file, optionally appends a note if that file is the root makefile, and finally writes another divider. This produces a lightweight header that marks the origin of the Makefile contents.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProjectHea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::WriteProjectHea.body: The method emits a header block to the output stream: it writes two divider lines (via the base class helper), then prints the current project’s name and a comma‑separated list of its configuration names, each prefixed with a comment marker. The output is intended as a human‑readable comment header in a generated Ninja file.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::cmLocalNinjaGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::cmLocalNinjaGen.body: It forwards the supplied `cmGlobalGenerator` and `cmMakefile` pointers to the base class constructor, registering them in the internal state needed for Ninja‑specific generation. No extra logic is executed in this constructor; it simply establishes the object’s context for later build‑file construction.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::cmLocalNinjaGen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::cmLocalNinjaGen.body: The constructor creates a local‑ninja generator instance, forwarding the provided reference to the base `cmLocalCommonGenerator` constructor and initializing any internal state required for generating Ninja build files for the current project.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::operator=@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::operator=@k_ZN2.body: The assignment operator copies another `cmLocalNinjaGenerator` into the current instance and returns a reference to the updated object, enabling chained assignments.

@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::~cmLocalNinjaGe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocalNinjaGenerator::~cmLocalNinjaGe.body: The virtual destructor `~cmLocalNinjaGenerator()` is declared in the class’s interface and defined as a defaulted destructor in the implementation file. This allows any derived type to override the cleanup behavior while still ensuring the base class’s destructor runs automatically when an instance of `cmLocalNinjaGenerator` is destroyed.

@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.body: The declaration marks a copy‑constructor for the `cmLocaleRAII` type as deleted. Any attempt to invoke this constructor—such as passing an object by value or implicitly copying it—will result in a compile‑time error. This guarantees that `cmLocaleRAII` instances cannot be duplicated, ensuring that only move semantics or custom factory functions may create or transfer instances.

@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLoc.body: The constructor stores the current locale string returned by `setlocale(LC_CTYPE, nullptr)` in `OldLocale`. Immediately afterward it calls `setlocale(LC_CTYPE, "")`, which resets the locale to the default (empty‑string) state for the C type category. The function therefore swaps the locale to the system default while preserving the former value in `OldLocale`.

@lcmLocaleRAII::operator=@k_ZN12cmLocale.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::operator=@k_ZN12cmLocale.body: The deleted assignment operator blocks copying or re‑assigning of a `cmLocaleRAII` instance, ensuring that objects of this type cannot be implicitly reassigned after construction.

@lcmLocaleRAII::~cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmLocaleRAII::~cmLocaleRAII@k_ZN12cmLo.body: It restores the locale setting to the value stored in `OldLocale`.

@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeRKT_@f./So.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeRKT_@f./So.body: Creates a lightweight `cmRange` object that merely forwards the underlying range’s `begin()` and `end()` iterators, letting you treat any range‐like type in a uniform way.

@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeT_T0_@f./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakeRange@k_Z11cmMakeRangeT_T0_@f./S.body:
cmMakeRange creates a lightweight wrapper holding a pair of iterators.  
It takes an opening iterator of type Iter1 and a closing iterator of type Iter2, constructs a cmRange containing those two ends, and returns that range.  
The result type is deduced as cmRange<Iter1>, allowing subsequent range‑based loops to iterate from the first iterator to the second.

@lcmMakefile::AddAlias@k_ZN10cmMakefile8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddAlias@k_ZN10cmMakefile8.body: Adds an alias entry mapping `lname` to `tgtName`, storing it in the internal map and, if requested, registering that alias with the global generator.

@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddCacheDefinition@k_ZN10c.body: This overload accepts a name, a value string, a documentation string, a cache‑entry type enum, and an optional force flag. It simply constructs `cmValue` wrappers around the strings and forwards them to the more general overload that actually stores the definition, optionally overriding an existing entry when `force` is true.

@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddDefinition@k_ZN10cmMake.body: This routine records a variable definition in the internal state. If a variable‑watcher is installed, it fires the watcher’s notification callback to report the change.

@lcmMakefile::AddDefinitionBool@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddDefinitionBool@k_ZN10cm.body: It turns the Boolean into the string “ON” or “OFF” and passes that string to the underlying AddDefinition routine.

@lcmMakefile::AddFunctionBlocker@k_ZN10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddFunctionBlocker@k_ZN10c.body: The function takes ownership of a `cmFunctionBlocker` instance, records the current backtrace context if there is an active execution stack, and then stores the blocker in the internal collection for later use.

@lcmMakefile::AddImportedTarget@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddImportedTarget@k_ZN10cm.body: AddImportedTarget creates a new cmTarget with visibility determined by the `global` flag, inserts the target into the internal imported-target mappings and indices, and stores it in the ImportedTargetsOwned vector before returning a pointer to the created target.

@lcmMakefile::AddInstallGenerator@k_ZN10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddInstallGenerator@k_ZN10.body: Adds a non‑null generator to the internal list, moving the unique_ptr into the vector.

@lcmMakefile::AddLibrary@k_ZN10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::AddLibrary@k_ZN10cmMakefil.body: The `AddLibrary` method registers a new build target of the specified library type. It first validates the requested type, then creates the target via `AddNewTarget`. Immediately after creation it clears any stale dependency data, optionally marks the target to be omitted from global link sets when `excludeFromAll` is true, and finally attaches the supplied source files. The method returns the newly created target.

@lcmMakefile::CanIWriteThisFile@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::CanIWriteThisFile@k_ZNK10c.body:
The function checks whether a file can be created in the current build tree.  
If the `CMAKE_DISABLE_SOURCE_CHANGES` flag is not set, it immediately allows the write.  
Otherwise, it forbids writes in the source tree unless the `CMAKE_DISABLE_IN_SOURCE_BUILD` flag is cleared.  
Finally, it permits writes only if the target file is not a sub‑directory of the project root, or it sits inside the output directory (or is the same file).

@lcmMakefile::EnforceUniqueName@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::EnforceUniqueName@k_ZNK10c.body: The function checks whether a target name is already in use—first as an alias, then as an actual target. If a conflict exists it either disallows the new target (generating an error message that names the existing target’s type and location) or, when the new target is a custom type and the global allow‑duplicate flag is set, silently accepts it. If no conflict is detected it returns success.

@lcmMakefile::ExecuteCommand@k_ZN10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExecuteCommand@k_ZN10cmMak.body: The `ExecuteCommand` method orchestrates the execution of a CMake command: it checks whether the command is blocked or has exceeded the recursion depth, then resolves the command prototype, optionally traces it, calls the command, and propagates any errors or exit codes. It returns `true` only if the command ran without fatal errors; otherwise it flags an error and returns `false`.

@lcmMakefile::ExpandArguments@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ExpandArguments@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The routine walks through each supplied argument, skips variable expansion for arguments marked as “bracketed”, expands the rest by invoking `ExpandVariablesInString` (passing the current file path and line number for context), and then places the resulting tokens into the output vector—treating quoted arguments as a single token and otherwise token‑splitting a string argument into individual tokens before adding them. The function terminates by returning `true` only if no fatal system error has been flagged.

@lcmMakefile::FindLocalNonAliasTarget@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FindLocalNonAliasTarget@k_.body: The method looks up a target by name in the internal map. If the name exists, it hands back the address of that entry’s value; otherwise it returns a null pointer.

@lcmMakefile::FindTargetToUse@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::FindTargetToUse@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The function resolves a target name by first checking any local alias mapping, then searching imported targets that match the requested name. If an imported target is found and its foreign‑native flag matches the allowed domains, it returns that target. If no match is found, it falls back to searching for a non‑alias target defined in the current directory; otherwise it delegates the lookup to the global target registry.

@lcmMakefile::GetAppleSDKType@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetAppleSDKType@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The function inspects the system‑root path stored in the environment variable `CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT`. It lower‑cases that path and then checks whether the path string begins with any of a handful of known SDK names (e.g., `appletvos`, `appletvsimulator`, `iphoneos`, `iphonesimulator`, `watchos`, `watchsimulator`, `xros`, `xrsimulator`). If a match is found, the matching `AppleSDK` enumeration value is returned; otherwise the function falls back to `AppleSDK::MacOS`.

@lcmMakefile::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: Returns the current Backtrace object stored in the instance, giving callers a read‑only copy of the internal member.

@lcmMakefile::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCMakeInstance@k_ZNK10cm.body: It returns the cmake instance that the `GlobalGenerator` holds by delegating the call to its `GetCMakeInstance` method.

@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentBinaryDirectory@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentBinaryDirectory@.body: The `GetCurrentBinaryDirectory` member simply forwards the current binary‑directory path stored in the `StateSnapshot` object. It returns a const reference to the string managed by `StateSnapshot::GetDirectory()`, ensuring that callers cannot modify the internal value while still accessing the live path. The method itself performs no allocation or I/O; it is a lightweight accessor that relies on the invariant that `StateSnapshot`’s directory never becomes null. The function is safe, with no obvious side‑effects, and its trivial return semantics keep the API simple and thread‑safe assuming `StateSnapshot` is correctly synchronized.

@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentSourceDirectory@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetCurrentSourceDirectory@.body: The method simply returns a const reference to the current source‑directory string stored in the `StateSnapshot`. It forwards that value unchanged, exposing the snapshot’s directory name without modifying any state.

@lcmMakefile::GetDefaultConfiguration@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefaultConfiguration@k_.body: The method returns an empty string when the current generator supports multiple configuration modes; otherwise it fetches and returns the value of the "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE" definition.

@lcmMakefile::GetDefineFlags@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefineFlags@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: GetDefineFlags simply returns the current value of the internal `DefineFlags` member. Because it is marked `const`, callers cannot modify the returned string. Note that the implementation copies the string; if the string is large, a `const std::string&` return type could avoid the copy overhead.

@lcmMakefile::GetDefinition@k_ZNK10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDefinition@k_ZNK10cmMak.body: Retrieves a variable’s value by name: first querying the current state snapshot; if absent, it falls back to the initialized‑cache lookup. When variable‑watch is active, an access callback may alter storage, so the method re‑fetches the value to capture any change. It finally returns the resolved value (or an empty one if the name is unknown).

@lcmMakefile::GetDirectoryId@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetDirectoryId@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: The function returns a string containing the instance’s address in the form “(0x… )”. It formats the address with `snprintf` into a 32‑byte buffer, then constructs and returns a `std::string` from that buffer. The string is used as a unique identifier for the directory object, and can be exposed via the property accessor.

@lcmMakefile::GetGeneratorConfigs@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetGeneratorConfigs@k_ZNK1.body:
The routine builds a list of configuration names by inspecting the current generator.  
If the generator is multi‑config, it pulls the list from the “CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES” definition; otherwise it falls back to the explicit build‑type value returned by `GetSafeDefinition`.  
When the query requests an empty config (`IncludeEmptyConfig`), it guarantees at least one empty string in the result.  
Finally it returns that list (moved) to the caller.

@lcmMakefile::GetGlobalGenerator@k_ZNK10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetGlobalGenerator@k_ZNK10.body: It returns the stored global‑generator pointer, exposing the instance’s reference to the generator without performing any state changes.

@lcmMakefile::GetHomeDirectory@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetHomeDirectory@k_ZNK10cm.body: The method returns a constant reference to the string that represents the current user’s home directory, delegating the actual lookup to the instance’s `GetCMakeInstance()->GetHomeDirectory()` call.

@lcmMakefile::GetHomeOutputDirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetHomeOutputDirectory@k_Z.body: Retrieves the path string stored in the CMake instance by calling `GetCMakeInstance()->GetHomeOutputDirectory()` and returns it as a const reference.

@lcmMakefile::GetInstallGenerators@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetInstallGenerators@k_ZN1.body: Returns a reference to the internal vector of `unique_ptr<cmInstallGenerator>` objects, giving callers direct access to the collection without copying or copying‑in‑place. The method does nothing but expose the stored generators so they can be inspected or modified.

@lcmMakefile::GetListFiles@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetListFiles@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the internally stored list of file names, allowing callers to inspect the vector without altering its contents.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSource@k_ZN10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSource@k_ZN10cm.body: When called, the method first asks the internal store for an existing source file that matches the supplied name and location kind. If such an entry is found, it returns that instance immediately. If no matching file is found, it forwards the request to the creation routine, which produces a new source file and returns it. This single‑step logic lets callers obtain a source file with minimal boilerplate: either reuse an existing instance or generate a fresh one if necessary.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.body: It obtains a delimiter string (if defined) and splits the supplied name into tokens using that delimiter or a default back‑slash separator, then delegates the tokenized vector to the internal `GetOrCreateSourceGroup` routine to locate or create the corresponding group.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrCreateSourceGroup@k_Z.body: The function looks up a source group for the supplied list of folder names. If no group already exists, it creates one by calling AddSourceGroup and then fetches it again. The result—a pointer to the existing or newly‑created cmSourceGroup—is returned.

@lcmMakefile::GetOrderedTargets@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOrderedTargets@k_ZNK10c.body: The function returns a reference to the internal vector holding the targets in the order the algorithm produced, allowing callers to iterate over them without copying the list or mutating the stored sequence. It preserves immutability by declaring the vector const‑qualified, so the caller can only read the pointers.

@lcmMakefile::GetOutputFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetOutputFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: Returns a read‑only reference to the internal `OutputFiles` vector.

@lcmMakefile::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetPolicyStatus@k_ZNK10cmM.body: This const member simply forwards the supplied PolicyID and an optional parent‑scope flag to the internal `StateSnapshot` object and returns the resulting `PolicyStatus`. In other words it retrieves the current status of the requested policy without mutating any internal state.

@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.body:
The function returns a cmValue for a requested property name.  
If the name is the special key `"TESTS"`, it collects all keys in the internal `Tests` map, joins them into a comma‑separated string, and returns that string wrapped in a `cmValue`. For any other key, it simply forwards the request to the underlying `StateSnapshot` and returns whatever value that component provides.

@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetProperty@k_ZNK10cmMakef.body: The method simply forwards the request: it returns the result of `StateSnapshot.GetDirectory().GetProperty(prop, chain)`. The call is const, takes a property name and a boolean flag, and returns a `cmValue` representing the requested property.

@lcmMakefile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK10c.body: The function simply returns the boolean flag of a named property: it looks up the property named by `prop` via `GetProperty()` and forwards the call to that property’s `IsOn()` method, yielding `true` if the property is considered “on” and `false` otherwise.

@lcmMakefile::GetRequiredDefinition@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetRequiredDefinition@k_ZN.body: The function returns a const reference to a string. It calls `GetDefinition(name)`; if the returned `cmValue` is null, it logs an error with the missing variable’s name and returns an empty string; otherwise it dereferences the value and returns that string.

@lcmMakefile::GetSafeDefinition@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSafeDefinition@k_ZNK10c.body: The method simply forwards the call to `GetDefinition` and returns the resulting string as a `const` reference, leaving the caller to rely on the lifetime of the returned reference.

@lcmMakefile::GetSource@k_ZNK10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSource@k_ZNK10cmMakefil.body: The function returns a pointer to a `cmSourceFile` that corresponds to the requested `sourceName` and `kind`. It first looks up the file in a pre‑filled “Known” index; if present it returns that entry. If not found it constructs a `cmSourceFileLocation` object, normalises the name (stripping the extension and lower‑casing on Windows/Apple), and then searches the `SourceFileSearchIndex`. On a match it returns that `cmSourceFile`; otherwise it returns `nullptr`.

@lcmMakefile::GetSourceFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetSourceFiles@k_ZNK10cmMa.body:
Returns a read‑only reference to the internal collection of source‑file objects.  
The function simply exposes the vector that holds `unique_ptr<cmSourceFile>` instances, so callers can enumerate or inspect the stored files without being able to modify the list itself.

@lcmMakefile::GetState@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetState@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.body: The method is a const accessor that simply delegates to the underlying CMake instance, returning a pointer to that instance’s internal state.

@lcmMakefile::GetStateSnapshot@k_ZNK10cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetStateSnapshot@k_ZNK10cm.body: The function simply returns a copy of the internal `StateSnapshot` member. Because it is marked `const`, the call guarantees that calling code cannot alter the state of the object. The returned snapshot reflects the current state at the moment of invocation and requires no additional logic or side‑effects.

@lcmMakefile::GetTests@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::GetTests@k_ZNK10cmMakefile.body: Iterates over every registered test generator; for each generator that reports support for the supplied configuration string it appends that generator’s test instance to the supplied vector. The routine is const‑qualified and assumes each generator returns a distinct `cmTest*`.

@lcmMakefile::IsAlias@k_ZNK10cmMakefile7.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsAlias@k_ZNK10cmMakefile7.body: The function checks whether the supplied name occurs in the internal `AliasTargets` collection; if it does, the check succeeds, otherwise it asks the global generator to resolve the alias.

@lcmMakefile::IsDefinitionSet@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsDefinitionSet@k_ZNK10cmM.body:
It checks the current snapshot for a definition with the given name.  
If it isn’t found, it falls back to the initialized‑cache lookup.  
When a variable‑watcher is active and the name still isn’t resolve, it records an “unknown variable accessed” event.  
Finally, it returns true iff a definition was successfully retrieved.

@lcmMakefile::IsImportedTargetGlobalScop.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsImportedTargetGlobalScop.body: This method checks whether the current imported target scope is the global scope by comparing the `CurrentImportedTargetScope` member to the `ImportedTargetScope::Global` enum value, returning `true` if they match and `false` otherwise.

@lcmMakefile::IsOn@k_ZNK10cmMakefile4IsO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsOn@k_ZNK10cmMakefile4IsO.body: The method simply checks whether a named entry is enabled: it fetches the corresponding definition via `GetDefinition` and returns that definition’s `IsOn()` flag.

@lcmMakefile::IsRootMakefile@k_ZNK10cmMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IsRootMakefile@k_ZNK10cmMa.body: Checks whether the current makefile is at the root of the build‑system tree – it returns true if the recorded parent directory is absent (i.e., `GetBuildsystemDirectoryParent()` is invalid).

@lcmMakefile::IssueInvalidTargetNameErro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IssueInvalidTargetNameErro.body: When a target name conflicts with a CMake‑reserved name or otherwise violates naming rules, this helper calls `IssueMessage` to emit a fatal‑level error that reports the offending name so the caller can abort the build.

@lcmMakefile::IssueMessage@k_ZNK10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::IssueMessage@k_ZNK10cmMake.body: The function checks the current execution status stack; if an error type is fatal or internal it flags a nested error in the latest status frame. Finally, it passes the message type, text, and the accumulated backtrace to the CMake instance for handling.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs32Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs32Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The method determines whether the target platform is 32‑bit. It queries the internal ABI definition; if that value equals the string “ELF X32”, it immediately returns false. Otherwise it looks up the size of a void pointer – if that value equals four bytes, the function returns true; otherwise false.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs64Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIs64Bit@k_ZNK10cmM.body: The function checks whether the size of a void pointer (obtained from the definition “CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P”) equals 8, returning true if so (indicating a 64‑bit system) and false otherwise. If the definition is missing or its string can’t be parsed to an integer (e.g. non‑numeric), the function simply returns false.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsAppleEmbedded@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsAppleEmbedded@k_.body: Returns `true` when the current Apple SDK type is anything other than `AppleSDK::MacOS`, indicating that the build targets an Apple‑embedded platform.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsx32@k_ZNK10cmMak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformIsx32@k_ZNK10cmMak.body: The function inspects the makefile’s internal platform ABI string. If that string equals the literal “ELF X32”, the function returns true; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmMakefile::PlatformSupportsAppleTextS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PlatformSupportsAppleTextS.body: The function checks two conditions: whether the current platform is marked as `"APPLE"` (via `IsOn`) and whether the `CMAKE_TAPI` flag is set (via `IsSet`). It returns `true` only if **both** of those checks succeed.

@lcmMakefile::PolicyOptionalWarningEnabl.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PolicyOptionalWarningEnabl.body: It returns true when the named policy variable is explicitly defined and turned on; if it is not defined, the function falls back to the global CMake debug/trace settings, which activate optional policy warnings when either debug output or trace is enabled.

@lcmMakefile::PrintCommandTrace@k_ZNK10c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::PrintCommandTrace@k_ZNK10c.body: The function first determines whether the current source file is in the list of files to trace. If it isn’t, it returns immediately. Otherwise it collects the command’s arguments, expanding any variable references when the trace‑expand flag is enabled. It then assembles a trace record that contains the file path, line number, command name, argument list, timestamp, and information about the call stack depth. Depending on the trace‑format setting, this record is either serialized to JSON or formatted into a human‑readable string. Finally it emits the record to the trace sink (a file stream if configured) or falls back to standard output.

@lcmMakefile::ReadListFile@k_ZN10cmMakef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::ReadListFile@k_ZN10cmMakef.body: The function resolves the file’s full path, establishes a scoped guard for the file’s lifetime, optionally fires debug callbacks at the start and end of parsing, parses the list file into a `cmListFile` object, and if parsing succeeds, it executes the contained commands via `RunListFile`. If any fatal error occurs during this process it suppresses the scope guard and returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false` on parse failure.

@lcmMakefile::RemoveDefinition@k_ZN10cmM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::RemoveDefinition@k_ZN10cmM.body: The function deletes a variable definition from the internal state snapshot. It first delegates to the snapshot’s `RemoveDefinition` method, then, if a variable‑watcher is attached, reports the removal event by invoking `VariableAccessed` with a `VARIABLE_REMOVED_ACCESS` flag. This keeps any observers in sync with the change.

@lcmMakefile::SetProperty@k_ZN10cmMakefi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::SetProperty@k_ZN10cmMakefi.body: The function takes a property name and a string value, converts that string via `cmValue`, and then forwards both arguments to another `SetProperty` overload.

@lcmMakefile::cmMakefile@k_ZN10cmMakefil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::cmMakefile@k_ZN10cmMakefil.body: Constructs a `cmMakefile` object by storing the passed global generator and snapshot. It flags that source‑file checking isn’t yet attempted, and pulls the system‑variables validator from the CMake instance. The constructor compiles a set of regular expressions used for parsing makefile directives (`cmakedefine`, `cmakedefine01`, and names in curly braces). It creates a policy‑scoped snapshot of the current state, then opens a new policy level for the current directory. It pushes an empty loop‑block sentinel and turns off the CMP0000 check until enabled later. Finally it registers a default list of source groups (source files, headers, pre‑compiled headers, rules, resources, object files, object‑libraries) with specific regex filters for each group. The constructor is responsible for all this initial set‑up; no further processing occurs until later configuration.

@lcmMakefile::~cmMakefile@k_ZN10cmMakefi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefile::~cmMakefile@k_ZN10cmMakefi.body: Destructs a `cmMakefile` object, dropping any owned resources (none are explicitly freed here).

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.body: Creates a new `RAII` instance by moving the internal data from the supplied rvalue‑reference `other`. It copies `other.Data` into the new object and then sets `other.Data` to `nullptr`, effectively transferring ownership in a constant‑time, noexcept‑safe move operation.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.body: RAII is a class that explicitly deletes its copy constructor (`RAII(const RAII&) = delete;`). This design prevents any code from implicitly copying an instance of RAII, enforcing that objects must be constructed anew or moved rather than duplicated. This restriction safeguards internal resources and ensures a single source of truth for the class’s state.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.body: Creates a profiling entry in the supplied data structure, storing the reference and immediately invoking `StartEntry` with the provided category, name, and optional arguments (moved into the internal representation). The constructor simply records the data and triggers the start of the entry.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::RAII@k_.body: RAII is a helper that performs a clean‑up routine in the build system. When invoked it removes a stored artifact (for example a temporary file or in‑memory object) and marks the associated entry as deleted. The function simply forwards the delete operation to the underlying resource manager, ensuring the object is no longer referenced in subsequent build steps.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::operato.body: Moves the internal pointer from *other* to the current object: if the current object already owns a pointer it stops that entry, then swaps the pointer with *other* and clears *other*’s pointer before returning the current instance.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::operato.body: The deleted assignment operator for `RAII` prohibits copying or assigning instances after construction, ensuring that objects of this type remain immutable once created. This design choice forces users to construct new objects explicitly rather than reusing existing ones.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::~RAII@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::RAII::~RAII@k.body: The destructor simply checks whether the `Data` member is non‑null and, if so, calls its `StopEntry()` method to clean up that entry before the object is destroyed.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::StartEntry@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::StartEntry@k_.body: The function appends a JSON‑formatted profiling event to an output stream, stamping the current time, process ID, and any supplied arguments, and writes the record via a JsonWriter while handling I/O errors.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::StopEntry@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::StopEntry@k_Z.body: The `StopEntry` function ends a profiling event. It first checks that the profiling output stream is still usable; if the stream has failed, it simply returns. When the stream is good, it writes a comma followed by a JSON record that marks the event type as “E” (end), records the current timestamp in microseconds, and records the current process ID. Finally it serialises this object to the stream with the `JsonWriter`. If writing fails, the function logs the failure via `cmSystemTools::Error`.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::cmMakefilePro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::cmMakefilePro.body: The constructor opens the specified file for writing, sets up a JSON stream writer, and writes an opening bracket to begin a JSON array.

@lcmMakefileProfilingData::~cmMakefilePr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMakefileProfilingData::~cmMakefilePr.body: The destructor finalizes the profiling stream: it writes a closing marker ("]") to the stream and then closes it. If the write or close operation throws, it catches the exception and reports the failure via the system‑tools error handler.

@lcmMarkAsAdvancedCommand@k_Z23cmMarkAsA.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMarkAsAdvancedCommand@k_Z23cmMarkAsA.body: Checks the argument list; if the first argument is “CLEAR” or “FORCE” it clears or forces the cache entry. It then walks the remaining arguments, examines the current policy setting (OLD, WARN, NEW), optionally emits a warning if the variable is missing, and if required creates a dummy cache entry. Finally it sets or updates the “ADVANCED” property of each cache entry to the value “1” (or “0” when clearing).

@lcmMessenger::IssueMessage@k_ZNK11cmMes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMessenger::IssueMessage@k_ZNK11cmMes.body: The routine conditionally displays a log entry. It first checks whether the supplied message type should be remapped by `ConvertMessageType`; if the type changes it records a `force` flag. Then, if `force` is true or the current type is marked visible by `IsMessageTypeVisible`, it forwards the message text and back‑trace to `DisplayMessage` for rendering.

@lcmMessenger::PrintBacktraceTitle@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmMessenger::PrintBacktraceTitle@k_ZNK.body:
The function writes a concise location string for a back‑trace entry.  
It first checks that the supplied `bt` list is non‑empty; if it is empty it returns immediately.  
If a source path (`TopSource`) is known, it converts the file path in the top context to a relative form.  
Finally it emits either “ in ” or “ at ”—choosing based on whether the context’s line number is zero—followed by the file‑context details.

@lcmNinjaLinkLineDeviceComputer::Convert.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaLinkLineDeviceComputer::Convert.body: It forwards the supplied library string to the `GG` member’s `ConvertToNinjaPath` routine and returns that resulting string.

@lcmNinjaLinkLineDeviceComputer::cmNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaLinkLineDeviceComputer::cmNinja.body: This constructor initializes the device‑computer by invoking its base class with the supplied output converter and state directory, then keeps a reference to the provided global generator for later use.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AddDepfileBind.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AddDepfileBind.body: The method stores a mapping for the dependency file in two forms: the original `depfile` string is kept under the key `"depfile"` when the conversion to shell‑escaped format differs; otherwise the converted form is stored under `"DEP_FILE"`, which holds the shell‑escaped representation.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AddIncludeFlag.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AddIncludeFlag.body: This method gathers the include directories for a given language and configuration, builds the corresponding compiler‑flag strings (converting backslashes to forward slashes when GCC is used on Windows), and appends those flags into the running language‑specific flag string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AdditionalClea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::AdditionalClea.body: The function retrieves the target’s *ADDITIONAL_CLEAN_FILES* property, evaluates the file paths, collapses them against the current binary directory, and registers each resolved path with the global ninja generator for removal during a clean build.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ByConfig::ByCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ByConfig::ByCo.body: ByConfig is a helper that consumes an existing ByConfig instance (via an rvalue reference) and produces a ready‑to‑use configuration instance used by the target generation logic.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ByConfig::oper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ByConfig::oper.body: Assigns a temporary `ByConfig` to an existing one – essentially a move‑assignment overload that copies the fields from the incoming rvalue into `*this` and then returns a reference to the updated object.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ByConfig::~ByC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ByConfig::~ByC.body: The destructor for `ByConfig` automatically releases any resources tied to a configuration instance when it goes out of scope. It ensures that any internal buffers, temporary handles, or mutable state are cleared and any dependent subsystems are notified of the cleanup.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::CompileWithDef.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::CompileWithDef.body: Returns whether the `CMAKE_<lang>_COMPILE_WITH_DEFINES` flag is enabled in the current Makefile, propagating that status to the caller.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeDefines.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeDefines.body: The function collects compile‑time define strings from the source file’s properties and from a per‑configuration property that is prefixed with the target configuration name, evaluates those through the expression interpreter, and finally merges the result with the language‑specific defaults via the local generator’s define‑appender. The returned string contains all the `-D` flags that must be supplied when invoking the compiler for that target.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeFlagsFo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeFlagsFo.body:
The routine builds the command‑line options that will be passed to the compiler for a given source file.  
It chooses the correct pre‑compiled‑header (PCH) architecture for the file, pulls any source‑specific flags from the file’s properties, and then appends the mandatory language flag, any Fortran‑specific options, and the PCH options.  
For C/C++ module sources it also adds a special “module‑only” flag. The resulting string contains all flags that must be supplied to the compiler when that object is built.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeInclude.author: AI Short Overview
