@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeInclude.body: Retrieves include‑directories defined in a source file, evaluates them with a generator‑expression interpreter, and appends the resulting flags to the generator’s internal list. Finally it collates those flags with any additional flags from `LocalGenerator` and returns the full include‑string for the target.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeLinkDep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeLinkDep.body: The function computes the list of files that a target must depend on when being linked. It first skips static‑ or object‑library targets, then pulls the direct link dependencies from the target’s link information. It appends any module‑definition source files, manifest files, and user‑supplied link files, all mapped to Ninja paths, and finally returns the full list.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeOrderDe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ComputeOrderDe.body: The method performs a targeted dependency analysis for a specific build target: it scans the internal metadata for that target, extracts the prerequisite relationships, and formats them into a concise string that can be used elsewhere for ordering decisions.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: It returns the absolute Ninja‑style path for the supplied `path` string by delegating the conversion to the global generator via `GetGlobalGenerator()->ConvertToNinjaAbsPath(std::move(path))`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ConvertToNinja.body: The function forwards the provided path string to the global generator’s `ConvertToNinjaPath` routine and returns that result unchanged.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EmitSwiftDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EmitSwiftDepen.body:
The routine builds a JSON record for a single Swift‑source file.  
It resolves the Ninja‑style output paths for that file’s compiled artefact, the object file, a Swift‑generated .swiftdeps file, and a diagnostics (.dia) file.  
If a .d file is required, the helper decides whether to use a custom name or a default one via the local generator.  
Finally it records the four paths under a “Swift‑Output‑Map” entry keyed by the source‑file path inside the current configuration.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureDirector.body: The routine guarantees that a given directory path exists, creating it if needed. If the supplied path is already a full (absolute) path, it simply calls the system tool to create that directory. If the path is relative, it prefixes it with the project’s current Ninja output directory—ensuring a trailing slash before concatenation—then creates the resulting full path.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureParentDi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::EnsureParentDi.body: Retrieves the parent directory of the supplied path and delegates its creation to `EnsureDirectoryExists`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ExportObjectCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ExportObjectCo.body: The method builds a compile‑command string for a single source file, expanding rule‑placeholder variables for the chosen language, and handling language‑specific flags (e.g. CUDA‑specific RDC or whole‑file options). It assembles the command, substitutes any placeholders, then registers the resulting command with the global generator for later emission.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ExportSwiftObj.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ExportSwiftObj.body: This protected routine registers C++‑style compile commands for Swift source files. It first checks whether Swift‑compile commands should be emitted; if so, it normalises paths for source and object files, collects the requisite flags, includes, and preprocessor defines, and then iterates over each Swift source. For each file it builds a command string by expanding a predefined rule template with the file‑specific variables. Finally the fully‑expanded command is added to the global generator along with the source and object paths.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ForceResponseF.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::ForceResponseF.body: The function simply checks whether the special flag `CMAKE_NINJA_FORCE_RESPONSE_FILE` is set either in the current makefile’s definitions or as an environment variable; if either is true, it returns `true`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::Generate@k_ZN2.body: The `Generate` method is an abstract hook: any subclass that inherits from this interface must provide its own implementation. It takes a single argument, `config`, a constant reference to a string, and performs whatever generation logic is required—typically creating or populating configuration objects. Because it is declared `= 0`, it cannot be called directly; a concrete derived class must override it before the function can be invoked.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GenerateSwiftO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GenerateSwiftO.body: The function checks whether the Swift‑output‑map for the requested configuration is already populated; if not, it exits early. It then lazily computes the path to the `swiftdeps` file for the target (falling back to a default location if the target property is missing). A JSON object is created that records that path under the key `swift-dependencies`, and the resulting map is stored in the configuration’s `SwiftOutputMap` structure. Finally, the generated JSON file path is emitted into the command‑line options via the local generator’s flag appender, using the output‑converter to format the path for the Ninja build system.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetBmiFilePath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetBmiFilePath.body:
Retrieves the absolute path for the .bmi file corresponding to a source file.  
It ensures the imported‑module cache for the requested config is initialized, then uses that cache to resolve the bmi name for the source’s full path, and finally concatenates it with the object‑file directory for the given configuration.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyRe.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetClangTidyRe.body:
The function builds the full file‑system path that will store the clang‑tidy
(replacements) output for a given source file. It starts with the generator’s
local‑home‑relative output directory, appends the supplied directory, then appends
the target’s object name and the standard “.yaml” suffix, using helper utilities
(cmStrCat, LocalGenerator helpers) to concatenate the pieces safely.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCommonFileS.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCommonFileS.body: The function retrieves the shared stream used by all target‑generators: it simply forwards the request to the global generator and returns a reference to that stream.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCompiledSou.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetCompiledSou.body: The function produces the absolute file path of a source file so that the compiler receives a path that is not relative to any working‑directory context. It simply forwards the file’s full path to `ConvertToNinjaAbsPath`, which normalises it into the format expected by the Ninja‑generated build system.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetDyndepFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetDyndepFileP.body: It builds and returns a string path that points to the dynamic‑dependency file for a target: it starts with the local generator’s home‑relative output path, appends a slash if that part is non‑empty, then concatenates the target directory, the config directory for the given config, the language identifier, and finally the “.dd” suffix.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGeneratorTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGeneratorTa.body: Returns the internal `GeneratorTarget` pointer stored in the object. The method is marked `const`, guaranteeing that calling it does not modify the instance. It simply returns the member `GeneratorTarget` without performing any additional logic.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGlobalGener.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetGlobalGener.body: A const member that forwards a call to its contained `LocalGenerator`, returning the global ninja generator pointer obtained from that sub‑object.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetImplFileStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetImplFileStr.body: The function simply forwards a configuration string to the global generator and returns a reference to the resulting file‑stream object.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetLocalGenera.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetLocalGenera.body: Returns a pointer to the internal `LocalGenerator` instance without modifying the object state. It is marked `protected` and `const`, guaranteeing callers cannot change the returned generator and ensuring the call‑site remains read‑only.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetMakefile@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetMakefile@k_.body: This `GetMakefile` method simply returns the class’s internal `Makefile` pointer. It is marked `const`, guaranteeing it does not alter the object’s state, and is `protected`, so only derived classes can invoke it. It does not perform any logic beyond returning the stored pointer.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjectFileD.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjectFileD.body: The function builds the directory path where object files will be written. It starts with the local generator’s home‑relative output path, appends a trailing slash if that part is non‑empty, and then concatenates the target directory with a config‑specific sub‑directory retrieved from the global generator. The result is returned as a `std::string`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjectFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjectFileP.body: It calls the target‑generator to obtain the object‑file name for the given source file, then constructs the full path by joining the directory returned by `GetObjectFileDir(config)` with a slash and that name via `cmStrCat`. The result is the absolute path to the built object file.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjects@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetObjects@k_Z.body: It looks up the given configuration name in the internal map and returns the stored collection of objects for that key. If the key isn’t present, it returns an empty list instead.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetPreprocesse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetPreprocesse.body: The method builds a file‑name for a pre‑processed source: it maps the original extension to the pre‑processed form (handling Fortran “F” and “fpp” cases), substitutes that extension into the object‑file name, and prefixes the result with the target’s relative output directory to form the full path.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetRulesFileSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetRulesFileSt.body: It simply forwards a reference to the global rules‑file stream held by the parent generator. The function retrieves that stream via `GetGlobalGenerator()` and returns the dereferenced reference to callers.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetDepen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetDepen.body: Builds a relative path string pointing at the **DependInfo.json** file that lives under the target’s own folder tree. It stitches together the current binary directory, the target’s local directory (via `GetTargetDirectory`), the config‑specific directory, and the language identifier, finally appending the constant file name.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetFileP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetFileP.body: The method builds a target path by retrieving the output directory for the given config and appending the file name. If that directory is empty or the current directory (“.”), it simply returns the name; otherwise it returns the directory plus “/” plus the name.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetName@.body: Returns the name stored in the internal `GeneratorTarget` instance – the method simply forwards the call to that object's `GetName()` and returns the resulting string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetOutpu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::GetTargetOutpu.body: The method fetches the generator‑defined target directory (via `GetDirectory`), normalises it with `ConvertToNinjaPath`, and returns the resulting string.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageCompil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageCompil.body:
The function builds a rule‑name string for Ninja rule definitions.  
It appends the language code, a fixed suffix, the encoded generator name, a flag indicating whether scanning is enabled, and finally the supplied configuration string, all combined by `cmStrCat`.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageDyndep.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageDyndep.body: The function builds a unique identifier for a rule by concatenating the supplied language tag, a fixed marker (`_DYNDEP__`), an encoded form of the generator’s target name, and an additional configuration suffix. It simply returns this composed string; no internal state is altered.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguagePrepro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguagePrepro.body: The function builds a target identifier string by concatenating the supplied language identifier, a fixed delimiter, the rule‑name encoded via `EncodeRuleName`, and the supplied configuration token, separating each segment with underscores. It simply assembles these parts into a single string returned to the caller.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageScanRu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::LanguageScanRu.body:
The `LanguageScanRule` function builds a unique identifier string for a Ninja rule. It accepts a language prefix (`lang`) and a configuration string (`config`), then concatenates them with a fixed separator `"_SCAN__"` and an encoded rule name (obtained via `cmGlobalNinjaGenerator::EncodeRuleName`). The resulting string is formatted as:  

```
<lang>_SCAN__<encoded_rule_name>_<config>
```

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The move‑constructor of `MacOSXContentGeneratorType` takes an rvalue reference to another `MacOSXContentGeneratorType` instance (named `[unnamed]` in the snippet). It transfers ownership of the internal state from the source object into the newly‑constructed instance, typically by moving member variables (e.g., using `std::move`). This allows efficient construction of a new generator from an existing one without deep copying.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The constructor forwards the supplied target‑generator pointer to the base `Generator` class and immediately stores the passed configuration string into the member `FileConfig` by moving it, without performing any other side‑effects.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The constructor takes an existing instance and duplicates its internal state into a new object, ensuring the new `MacOSXContentGeneratorType` has the same configuration and data as the source. It performs a member‑wise copy of all member variables, preserving any resource handles or configuration flags that the original object holds. By copying these members directly, the constructor guarantees that the new object behaves identically to the source at the moment of construction, without allocating new resources beyond what already exists in the original instance.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The function checks that the current build is for an Apple bundle, then creates a target‑specific content directory. It skips any files that would collide with existing native‑config files, copies the source file into that directory via a generated build rule, and records the resulting path as an additional dependency for the target.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: This operator assigns a temporary `MacOSXContentGeneratorType` instance to the current object by moving its resources. It takes an rvalue reference of the same type and performs a move‑assignment, efficiently transferring ownership of internal data members while leaving the temporary in a valid, but unspecified, state.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The assignment operator copies all internal state from the supplied generator into the current instance, updating its member fields so that the object becomes an exact replica of the argument.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MacOSXContentG.body: The destructor cleans up any internal state allocated by the content generator—releasing owned resources, resetting flags, and ensuring no lingering handles remain before the object is discarded.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::MapToNinjaPath.body: It forwards the request to the global generator instance and returns the resulting `MapToNinjaPathImpl` value.

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::NeedExplicitPr.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteCompileRu.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteObjectBui.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmNinjaTargetGenerator::WriteSwiftObje.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmParsePlist@k_Z12cmParsePlistRKNSt7__.body: The function opens a *plist* file, runs the external `plutil` utility to convert it to JSON, captures the tool’s JSON output stream, feeds that stream to a JSON reader, and returns the parsed `Json::Value` wrapped in an optional; if the external tool exits non‑zero or parsing fails, it returns an empty optional.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariable@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariable@.body:
The `ExpandVariable` method is the hook that concrete placeholder‑expander classes implement.  
It receives the name of a placeholder variable and must return the string that should replace it in the output text.  
When a derived expander sees a token such as `${var}` in a template, it calls `ExpandVariable(var)` to obtain the real value (which could be a literal, a lookup result, or a computed string) that will be substituted in its place.  
Because the function is protected and pure virtual, it forces every concrete expander to provide its own variable‑expansion policy while keeping the public API unchanged.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariables.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::ExpandVariables.body: The routine scans the supplied text for angle‑bracket markers, invokes the helper to substitute each found token, trims any resulting surplus blanks that would appear when a token expands to nothing, and returns the reconstructed string.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::cmPlaceholderEx.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::cmPlaceholderEx.body: The `cmPlaceholderExpander` class provides a public method that scans a supplied string for placeholder tokens (e.g., `${…}`) and substitutes them with the corresponding value from a provided mapping. The method returns the fully resolved string, enabling callers to generate fully‑resolved configuration or template text without handling the token‑replacement logic themselves.

@lcmPlaceholderExpander::~cmPlaceholderE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPlaceholderExpander::~cmPlaceholderE.body: The virtual destructor `~cmPlaceholderExpander()` is declared `= default;`. It simply invokes the compiler‑generated destructor for the class, allowing derived classes to override the destructor if needed, and ensures proper resource cleanup when a derived object is destroyed.

@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyWarning@k_ZN10cmP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::GetPolicyWarning@k_ZN10cmP.body: It returns a warning string that a policy is not set, telling the user to run `cmake --help-policy` and use `cmake_policy` to set it.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::Get@k_ZNK10cmPo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::Get@k_ZNK10cmPo.body: The `Get` member returns the current state for a policy identified by `id`. It starts with `WARN` and then checks two bits in a status array: the slot at `POLICY_STATUS_COUNT * id + OLD` first, then the slot at `… + NEW`. If the first bit is set, the status becomes `OLD`; if only the second bit is set, it becomes `NEW`. If neither bit is set, the return value remains `WARN`. The method performs a simple linear lookup and returns the resulting enum value.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::IsDefined@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::IsDefined@k_ZNK.body: The function returns `true` if any of the three status bits (OLD, WARN, NEW) for the specified policy id are set in the internal status array; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::PolicyMap@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPolicies::PolicyMap::PolicyMap@k_ZN1.body: The constructor creates a new `PolicyMap` instance by copying the internal mappings from the supplied object, duplicating the policy entries so that the new instance has an identical configuration to the original while preserving the integrity of its internal state.

@lcmProcess::Buffer::Buffer@k_ZN9cmProce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Buffer::Buffer@k_ZN9cmProce.body: Creates an empty buffer instance with default capacity, ready to receive data.

@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLast@k_ZN9cmProc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLast@k_ZN9cmProc.body: The function checks whether the buffer contains any data; if it does, it copies that data into the supplied string reference, resets internal pointers, clears the buffer, and returns true. If the buffer is empty, it simply returns false.

@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLine@k_ZN9cmProc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Buffer::GetLine@k_ZN9cmProc.body: Iterates over the internal buffer from the current position until it encounters a newline or null‑terminator; when found, it copies the slice up to that point into the supplied string, trims any trailing carriage returns, advances the start marker to the character after the delimiter, and returns true. If no delimiter is reached before the buffer ends, it moves any partial line data to the front of the buffer and returns false.

@lcmProcess::Buffer::~Buffer@k_ZN9cmProc.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Buffer::~Buffer@k_ZN9cmProc.body: The `~Buffer()` destructor simply frees the internal storage of the `Buffer` object: it clears the underlying `std::vector<char>` container, ensuring all held characters are destroyed and that the vector’s memory is deallocated. No additional cleanup logic is performed beyond what the base container already provides.

@lcmProcess::ChangeTimeout@k_ZN9cmProces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::ChangeTimeout@k_ZN9cmProces.body:
The `ChangeTimeout` method simply assigns the supplied `cmDuration` value to the internal `Timeout` member and then immediately restarts the timer by calling `StartTimer()`.  
* **Key points to keep in mind**

- **Re‑initialisation**: `StartTimer()` must be prepared to handle the new timeout value; if it was already running, the timer will be re‑scheduled immediately.
- **Thread‑safety**: If `StartTimer()` can be invoked from multiple threads, guard the update with a lock or atomic operation to avoid race conditions.
- **Validation**: Consider validating that `t` is a non‑negative value before applying it; an unexpected negative duration could break the timer logic.
- **Error handling**: If `StartTimer()` can throw or fail, wrap the call in a try‑catch or check the return status to avoid silent failures.

@lcmProcess::Finish@k_ZN9cmProcess6Finis.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::Finish@k_ZN9cmProcess6Finis.body: The `Finish` method timestamps the total runtime, snaps any negative span to zero to guard against clock adjustments, and then signals the `Runner` to perform its own finalization step.

@lcmProcess::GetExitException@k_ZNK9cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetExitException@k_ZNK9cmPr.body: The function examines the process’s exit status and translates it to a typed `Exception`. On Windows it tests the exit value bits against a list of known NT status codes, mapping them to one of the `Exception` categories (Fault, Numerical, Interrupt, Illegal, Other, or None). On other platforms it falls back to a signal‑based mapping (SIGSEGV → Fault, SIGFPE → Numerical, etc.). If no known code or signal is detected, the function returns `Exception::None`.

@lcmProcess::GetExitExceptionString@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetExitExceptionString@k_ZN.body: The method returns a human‑readable description for the process exit code. It checks the current platform: on Windows it examines the process’ ExitValue enum; otherwise it inspects the Unix signal number. Each case maps a known code to a short string (e.g., “User interrupt”, “Floating‑point exception”, “Segmentation fault”, etc.). If the code isn’t matched, it falls back to “Signal <code>”. The function returns this string.

@lcmProcess::GetExitValue@k_ZNK9cmProces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetExitValue@k_ZNK9cmProces.body: GetExitValue is a simple const member function that returns the 64‑bit integer stored in the object’s `ExitValue` member. It does not modify any state and guarantees no side‑effects.

@lcmProcess::GetProcessStatus@k_ZN9cmPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetProcessStatus@k_ZN9cmPro.body: The method simply returns the current value of the internal `ProcessState` member.

@lcmProcess::GetRunner@k_ZN9cmProcess9Ge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetRunner@k_ZN9cmProcess9Ge.body: Returns the internally stored `std::unique_ptr<cmCTestRunTest>` by moving it out, giving ownership to the caller.

@lcmProcess::GetStartTime@k_ZN9cmProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetStartTime@k_ZN9cmProcess.body: The method returns the stored steady‑clock time_point held in the `StartTime` member.

@lcmProcess::GetSystemStartTime@k_ZN9cmP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetSystemStartTime@k_ZN9cmP.body: The function simply returns the value held in the `SystemStartTime` member; it doesn’t perform any additional logic or validation before returning that `std::chrono::system_clock::time_point`.

@lcmProcess::GetTerminationStyle@k_ZNK9c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetTerminationStyle@k_ZNK9c.body: Returns the stored termination style without modifying any state.

@lcmProcess::GetTimeoutReason@k_ZNK9cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetTimeoutReason@k_ZNK9cmPr.body: The accessor simply returns the stored timeout reason value. It is a read‑only, const member function that exposes the internal `TimeoutReason_` field without modifying any state, allowing callers to query why a timeout occurred while guaranteeing no side‑effects.

@lcmProcess::GetTotalTime@k_ZN9cmProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::GetTotalTime@k_ZN9cmProcess.body: Retrieves the stored total‑time value held in the object.

@lcmProcess::OnAllocate@k_ZN9cmProcess10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnAllocate@k_ZN9cmProcess10.body: The `OnAllocate` routine ensures the internal buffer matches the defined size, resizing it if necessary, and then assigns that buffer’s data and length into the supplied `uv_buf_t` structure. It performs the size check and reallocation first, then creates a `uv_buf_t` instance that references the buffer’s underlying memory and size. This simple two‑step sequence guarantees the caller receives a ready‑to‑use buffer descriptor.

@lcmProcess::OnAllocateCB@k_ZN9cmProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnAllocateCB@k_ZN9cmProcess.body: The callback fetches the `cmProcess` instance stored in `handle->data`, casts it to that type, and then forwards the suggested size and buffer pointer to the class’s `OnAllocate` member function.

@lcmProcess::OnExit@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnExi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnExit@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnExi.body: The routine checks whether the process has already timed‑out; if not, it transitions the internal state to either *Exception* (when the exit code indicates a termination exception on Windows or a non‑zero signal otherwise) or to *Exited* for normal exit. It then persists the exit value and signal values, marks the main handle as closed, and if the read side has also finished, it stops the associated timer and invokes the final clean‑up callback `Finish()`.

@lcmProcess::OnExitCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnExitCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnE.body: When a uv process terminates, libuv invokes the callback you registered. `OnExitCB` simply extracts the user‑data stored in the `uv_process_t` structure (you stored a pointer to your `cmProcess` instance in `data`), casts it to the appropriate type, and then delegates the exit information to the instance’s `OnExit` method by calling `self->OnExit(exit_status, term_signal)`.

@lcmProcess::OnRead@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnRea.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnRead@k_ZN9cmProcess6OnRea.body: When data is received, `OnRead` decodes the buffer into a string, appends it to an internal output buffer, extracts complete lines to hand them to the runner, then clears the buffer. It stops further reads once the stream signals EOF or an error, logging the issue via `cmCTestLog`, and finalises the process by marking the read‑handle closed and stopping the timer if the process handle is also closed.

@lcmProcess::OnReadCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnR.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnReadCB@k_ZN9cmProcess8OnR.body: It’s a libuv read‑event callback: when data arrives, it pulls the owning `cmProcess` instance from the stream’s `data` field, casts that pointer to the correct type, and immediately forwards the read size and buffer to the instance’s `OnRead` member.

@lcmProcess::OnTimeout@k_ZN9cmProcess9On.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnTimeout@k_ZN9cmProcess9On.body: When a timeout occurs the routine first marks the process as expired and, if the test was still executing and the timeout was a normal one, it may raise the user‑defined timeout signal (and restarts the timer with the configured grace period). If no custom signal is pending, it forces termination, closes any lingering read handles and finally ensures the test‑completion routine is invoked.

@lcmProcess::OnTimeoutCB@k_ZN9cmProcess1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::OnTimeoutCB@k_ZN9cmProcess1.body: The callback casts the timer’s data field back to the owning `cmProcess` instance and forwards the timeout event to that instance’s `OnTimeout()` method.

@lcmProcess::ResetStartTime@k_ZN9cmProce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::ResetStartTime@k_ZN9cmProce.body: Refreshes the `StartTime` member to the current steady‑clock tick; consider thread safety if called concurrently.

@lcmProcess::SetCommand@k_ZN9cmProcess10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::SetCommand@k_ZN9cmProcess10.body: The member function takes a constant reference to a string and assigns it to the class member `Command`. It is a simple setter that updates the internal command value.

@lcmProcess::SetCommandArguments@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::SetCommandArguments@k_ZN9cm.body: `SetCommandArguments` replaces the current argument list with a new one by assigning a `const&` vector of strings to the internal `Arguments` member. It simply updates the member with the passed vector.

@lcmProcess::SetId@k_ZN9cmProcess5SetIdE.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::SetId@k_ZN9cmProcess5SetIdE.body: Assigns the supplied integer to the member variable named `Id`.

@lcmProcess::SetTimeout@k_ZN9cmProcess10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::SetTimeout@k_ZN9cmProcess10.body: The `SetTimeout` function assigns the provided `cmDuration` value to the internal `Timeout` member. This method simply updates the internal state and returns immediately.

@lcmProcess::SetTimeoutReason@k_ZN9cmPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::SetTimeoutReason@k_ZN9cmPro.body: The method assigns the supplied `TimeoutReason` value to the object’s internal member, updating the current timeout‑reason state.

@lcmProcess::SetWorkingDirectory@k_ZN9cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::SetWorkingDirectory@k_ZN9cm.body: This method assigns the supplied directory path to the instance’s `WorkingDirectory` member, updating the working directory for the process.

@lcmProcess::StartProcess@k_ZN9cmProcess.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::StartProcess@k_ZN9cmProcess.body: The function establishes the process state, verifies the command, builds the argument list, configures the timer and I/O pipes, spawns the child process, and finally records the timers while switching the state to Executing.

@lcmProcess::StartTimer@k_ZN9cmProcess10.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::StartTimer@k_ZN9cmProcess10.body: The method checks whether a timeout value has been set; if so, it converts that duration into milliseconds and schedules a one‑shot timer to invoke the callback `OnTimeoutCB` after that interval.

@lcmProcess::cmProcess@k_ZN9cmProcessC1E.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::cmProcess@k_ZN9cmProcessC1E.body: The constructor stores the provided test runner, allocates a UTF‑8 conversion buffer of size CM_PROCESS_BUF_SIZE, and zero‑initialises the run‑time, exit status, and identifier fields while recording the current steady‑clock instant as the start time.

@lcmProcess::~cmProcess@k_ZN9cmProcessD1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcess::~cmProcess@k_ZN9cmProcessD1.body: When a `cmProcess` object goes out of scope or is explicitly destroyed, its destructor `~cmProcess()` is invoked automatically. Because the destructor is defaulted (`= default;`), it performs the standard automatic cleanup: each non‑static member is destroyed in reverse order of construction, and any resources owned by the object (like file handles, network sockets, or heap allocations) are released according to their own destructors. No custom logic is executed unless explicitly defined elsewhere.

@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.body: The routine exchanges the contents of `raw` into `decoded`, then conditionally adjusts the data in the `rawparts` container. If the identifier `id` is positive, it may prepend or remove bytes from the buffer’s last element while performing a conditional decode pass. The actual conversion is performed by the helper `DoDecodeText`, which may be invoked either once or repeatedly depending on the character‑set characteristics exposed by the returned `CPINFOEXW` structure. The function ultimately returns a success flag indicating whether the conversion succeeded under the current code‑page and buffer circumstances.

@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::DecodeText@k_ZN15cmPr.body: The `DecodeText` overload accepts a raw character buffer and its length, copies that buffer into a temporary `std::string`, and forwards the call to the other overload that takes a string. It returns whatever that overload reports, propagating the success or failure of the decoding operation.

@lcmProcessOutput::cmProcessOutput@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::cmProcessOutput@k_ZN1.body: The constructor maps the requested `encoding` value to a concrete Windows code‑page ID and stores the supplied `maxSize` as the buffer size limit. On non‑Windows builds the body is effectively a no‑op placeholder.

@lcmProcessOutput::~cmProcessOutput@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessOutput::~cmProcessOutput@k_ZN.body: The `~cmProcessOutput` function is exposed as a public member in `cmProcessOutput.h`. @lcmProcessTools::LineParser::LineParser.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::LineParser.body: It stores the separator character and the flag that determines whether carriage‑return characters are skipped during line parsing.

@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::ProcessLin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::ProcessLin.body: ProcessLine is the hook that every concrete processor must supply – it reads a single line from the input stream, performs the necessary transformations, and returns true if the line was accepted or false if it should be skipped. @lcmProcessTools::LineParser::SetLog@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::SetLog@k_Z.body: The `SetLog` member stores the supplied stream pointer in `this->Log` and records the supplied prefix string. @lcmProcessTools::LineParser::~LineParse.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::LineParser::~LineParse.body: The destructor (`~LineParser`) is a virtual cleanup routine that releases any dynamically allocated buffers or other resources acquired during parsing. It guarantees that when a `LineParser` object is destroyed, all owned resources are freed correctly, ensuring no memory leaks in the parsing pipeline.

@lcmProcessTools::OutputLogger::OutputLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::OutputLogger::OutputLo.body: Initialises an internal logger by registering the supplied stream and an optional prefix—delegating the configuration to `SetLog`.

@lcmProcessTools::OutputLogger::~OutputL.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmProcessTools::OutputParser::Process@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::OutputParser::Process@.body: This member function forwards the supplied `data` buffer and its length to the helper `ProcessChunk`, returning whatever that helper reports.

@lcmProcessTools::RunProcess@k_ZN14cmPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmProcessTools::RunProcess@k_ZN14cmPro.body: RunProcess initializes two built‑in streams—one for standard output and one for errors—then builds a process chain. It opens two pipes linked to those streams, attaches read callbacks that feed the data to user‑supplied parsers (decoding text and invoking their Process callbacks). The function then runs the event loop until both streams finish, collecting the individual status codes from the chain, and returns a vector of those status values.

@lcmPropertyMap::AppendProperty@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::AppendProperty@k_ZN13cm.body: The `AppendProperty` member inserts a value into an internal map keyed by the supplied name. It first checks that the value string is non‑empty; if it is empty it exits immediately. Otherwise it retrieves the current string stored under that key. If the string already contains data and the caller did not request plain‑string concatenation (`asString` is false), it appends a semicolon to separate the new piece from the previous one. Finally it appends the new value to the string.

@lcmPropertyMap::Clear@k_ZN13cmPropertyM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::Clear@k_ZN13cmPropertyM.body: It erases every entry in the internal map container by invoking the container’s `clear()` routine, leaving the map in an empty state.

@lcmPropertyMap::GetKeys@k_ZNK13cmProper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::GetKeys@k_ZNK13cmProper.body: The function creates a vector sized to the map’s size, copies each key into it, then sorts the vector before returning it, yielding the keys in ascending order.

@lcmPropertyMap::GetList::[lambda_0]::op.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::GetList::[lambda_0]::op.body: This const member function returns a boolean based on the two `StringPair` arguments. It performs a check—likely comparing or validating the pairs according to the class’s internal criteria—and returns `true` when the condition holds.

@lcmPropertyMap::GetList::[lambda_0]@kcm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::GetList::[lambda_0]@kcm.body: It returns `true` when the first string of the first argument is lexicographically smaller than that of the second, enabling a strict ordering over `StringPair` objects.

@lcmPropertyMap::GetList@k_ZNK13cmProper.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::GetList@k_ZNK13cmProper.body: The `GetList` method collects the entries from `Map_` into a vector, reserves enough space, copies each key‑value pair into the vector, then sorts the vector by the string keys before returning the sorted list.

@lcmPropertyMap::GetPropertyValue@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::GetPropertyValue@k_ZNK1.body: The function looks up a property by name in the internal map. If the key exists, it constructs and returns a `cmValue` holding the associated value; if the key is missing, it returns a null‑pointer sentinel.

@lcmPropertyMap::RemoveProperty@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::RemoveProperty@k_ZN13cm.body: The method simply erases an entry identified by `name` from the internal map. It assumes `name` is a valid key; if the key isn’t present nothing happens. No error handling or return value is provided, and no checks for concurrent access are performed.

@lcmPropertyMap::SetProperty@k_ZN13cmPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::SetProperty@k_ZN13cmPro.body: Stores a named value in the internal map. If the supplied value evaluates to false (e.g. a null‑or‑empty value), the entry is removed instead of being stored.

@lcmPropertyMap::cmPropertyMap@k_ZN13cmP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::cmPropertyMap@k_ZN13cmP.body: cmPropertyMap builds and returns a map that links property identifiers to their values, enabling other parts of the system to look up configuration data efficiently.

@lcmPropertyMap::~cmPropertyMap@k_ZN13cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmPropertyMap::~cmPropertyMap@k_ZN13cm.body: ~cmPropertyMap() releases the internal storage used by the `cmPropertyMap` object. When a `cmPropertyMap` instance is destroyed, this destructor walks the internal map container, releasing each key‑value pair and freeing any auxiliary resources that were allocated during the object's lifetime. It guarantees that no stray memory or file descriptors remain after the object goes out of scope.

@lcmQtAutoGen::AppendFilenameSuffix@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::AppendFilenameSuffix@k_ZN.body: This function inserts a given suffix immediately before the file’s extension. If the input file name contains no dot, it simply appends the suffix at the end. If a dot exists, it preserves the original extension while inserting the suffix in front of it, producing a new filename that keeps the same extension.

@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::Compile.author: AI Short Overview

This avoids unnecessary copies and preserves the original object's state in a temporary until the move completes.

@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::Compile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::Compile.body: The constructor creates a new `CompilerFeatures` object by copying the internal settings from an existing instance—duplicating all feature flags and configuration values so the new object is identical to the source.

@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::operato.body: This overload of `operator=` accepts an rvalue of type `CompilerFeatures` (typically moved into the current instance). It copies (or moves) the contained features from the argument into the target object and returns a reference to the modified instance, enabling assignment chaining.

@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::operato.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::operato.body: The assignment operator copies all member values from the right‑hand `CompilerFeatures` instance into the current object, effectively performing a deep copy of the feature set while returning `*this` for chaining. It handles self‑assignment safely, ensuring no temporary resources are left dangling.

@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::~Compil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::CompilerFeatures::~Compil.body: During shutdown it releases allocated resources, clears internal flags, and resets internal state to prepare the object for safe destruction.

@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::ConfigStrin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::ConfigStrin.body: The constructor creates a `ConfigString` instance from a temporary (r‑value) `ConfigString`. It copies the internal state of the source into the new object, enabling efficient transfer of configuration data without unnecessary copying. This form of the constructor allows code that passes configuration strings by value to rely on move semantics for performance and correctness.

@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::ConfigStrin.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::ConfigStrin.body: The copy constructor `ConfigString(const ConfigString& other)` simply creates a new `ConfigString` instance that duplicates the internal string data of `other`. It performs a shallow copy of the underlying string (typically by copying the `std::string` member) and ensures that the new object holds its own copy of any mutable state. This constructor is invoked whenever a `ConfigString` is passed to a function or returned from a function that expects a copy‑semantics initialization.

@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator accepts an rvalue reference to another `ConfigString`, moves its contents into the current object, and returns a reference to the object after the assignment. It enables efficient in‑place updates of `ConfigString` instances.

@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::operator=@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::operator=@k.body: The assignment operator copies another `ConfigString`’s internal string into the current object and returns a reference to that object.

@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::~ConfigStri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::ConfigString::~ConfigStri.body:
The function `~ConfigString()` is a destructor for the `ConfigString` class.  
It runs when a `ConfigString` instance is destroyed, ensuring that any allocated string data (or other resources tied to the configuration string) is properly released so the object leaves no lingering memory or handles.

@lcmQtAutoGen::FileNameWithoutLastExtens.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmQtAutoGen::FileNameWithoutLastExtens.body: The routine drops the directory part of a path (if present) and then returns the file name without its final extension. It does this by locating the last slash, trimming off everything before it, finding the last dot, and taking the substring preceding that dot. If no slash or dot is found, the function behaves gracefully, returning the original name (or empty string when no dots exist).

@lcmRST::ProcessModule@k_ZN5cmRST13Proce.body: The routine reads each line from the supplied stream, uses the marker `rst` to determine whether it is inside a bracketed block or in a plain‑line section, and calls `ProcessLine` on lines that meet its parsing rules.
