@lcmTarget::GetLinkInterfaceDirectExclud.body: The member `GetLinkInterfaceDirectExcludeEntries` simply exposes the internal list of “direct‑exclude” entries associated with the current target. As a `const` accessor it constructs and returns a `cmBTStringRange` that represents the underlying collection held in `impl->InterfaceLinkLibrariesDirectExclude.Entries`. No other computation or filtering occurs – it is a thin wrapper that exposes the internal data unchanged.

@lcmTarget::GetLinkInterfaceEntries@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetLinkInterfaceEntries@k_ZN.body: The `GetLinkInterfaceEntries` member returns a `cmBTStringRange` that represents the collection of interface‑link entries stored in the object’s implementation. It simply forwards the underlying `Entries` container to `cmMakeRange`, yielding a range view that can be iterated over or inspected without copying the data.

@lcmTarget::GetLinkOptionsEntries@k_ZNK8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetLinkOptionsEntries@k_ZNK8.body: Returns a `cmBTStringRange` that wraps the entries stored in the target’s `LinkOptions`.

@lcmTarget::GetMakefile@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetMakefile@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.body: Returns a pointer to the associated makefile stored in the private implementation of a target. The method is `const`, so it guarantees that the returned `Makefile` object is not modified by the caller. It simply dereferences `impl` and returns the `Makefile` member.

@lcmTarget::GetName@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetNa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetName@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetNa.body: This member simply exposes the `Name` member of its implementation object. The call is `const`‑qualified, so it cannot modify any state, and it returns a reference to the stored string, ensuring callers cannot alter the original value. The implementation details are hidden, but the function guarantees that the returned string is safe to use without risk of accidental mutation.

@lcmTarget::GetPolicyMap@k_ZNK8cmTarget1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetPolicyMap@k_ZNK8cmTarget1.body: The function simply returns a const reference to the internal `PolicyMap` held by the implementation object.

@lcmTarget::GetProperties@k_ZNK8cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetProperties@k_ZNK8cmTarget.body: It returns a const reference to the `cmPropertyMap` stored inside the implementation object, so callers can read the map without triggering a copy.

@lcmTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.body:
The function queries a target’s configuration by name.  
If the name is one of the predefined “special” properties, it may return a value from a predefined map or a built‑in property (standard language, directories, compile options, etc.).  
For most properties the routine walks a list of member pointers, asking each component whether it holds the requested property; the first positive answer is returned.  
Special cases include: the target type, manually added dependencies (concatenated into a list), flags for imported visibility, name, and paths derived from the makefile state (binary and source directories).  

If the property is still not found, it falls back to the generic property bag; if the property is marked as “chained”, the value is fetched from the current state snapshot. If nothing matches, a null value is returned.

@lcmTarget::GetRuntimeInstallPath@k_ZNK8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetRuntimeInstallPath@k_ZNK8.body: The function simply returns a reference to the `RuntimeInstallPath` member of the internal implementation object (`impl`). It guarantees that the caller receives a read‑only view of that string; no copy is performed. Because the return type is a reference, the caller must keep the `cmTarget` instance alive while using the string to avoid dangling references.

@lcmTarget::GetSafeProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetSafeProperty@k_ZNK8cmTarg.body:
When you call this method, it tries to fetch the named property from the object.  
If the property exists, it hands you a reference to that string; otherwise it gives you a reference to a single shared empty string that lives for the lifetime of the program. This keeps the code simple and avoids any heap allocation.

@lcmTarget::GetSourceEntries@k_ZNK8cmTar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetSourceEntries@k_ZNK8cmTar.body: Returns a `cmBTStringRange` that references the `Sources.Entries` collection from the internal implementation.

@lcmTarget::GetSystemIncludeDirectories@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetSystemIncludeDirectories@.body: It forwards a const reference to the internal set of system‑include directories that the implementation maintains.

@lcmTarget::GetType@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetTy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::GetType@k_ZNK8cmTarget7GetTy.body: GetType returns the target’s type as stored in the implementation object. It is a read‑only accessor that simply returns the enum value held in impl.

@lcmTarget::HasKnownObjectFileLocation@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::HasKnownObjectFileLocation@k.body: Returns whether the current target’s object file location has already been resolved; if not, it can fill *reason with a diagnostic message.

@lcmTarget::InsertLinkDirectory@k_ZN8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::InsertLinkDirectory@k_ZN8cmT.body: The `InsertLinkDirectory` routine takes an entry string and a flag indicating whether it should be inserted at the front or back of the internal list. It forwards the call to the underlying storage helper (`WriteDirect`), passing the appropriate `Action` value (`Prepend` for a prepend, otherwise `Append`). This adds the new directory entry into the target’s collection in the requested order.

@lcmTarget::IsAIX@k_ZNK8cmTarget5IsAIXEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsAIX@k_ZNK8cmTarget5IsAIXEv.body: The `IsAIX` function simply forwards the value of the `IsAIX` member stored in the class’s implementation object, returning that boolean to the caller. The function is marked `const`, ensuring it does not modify the object state, and because it merely reads a member it incurs no side‑effects. In production code the implementation should guard against a dangling `impl` pointer (e.g., by asserting or checking `impl` before dereferencing).

@lcmTarget::IsAndroidGuiExecutable@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsAndroidGuiExecutable@k_ZNK.body: The method evaluates the target’s type, platform flag and a custom flag to decide if the target should be treated as an Android‑GUI executable: it returns true only when the type equals **EXECUTABLE**, the implementation reports itself as Android, and the “ANDROID_GUI” property evaluates to true.

@lcmTarget::IsAppBundleOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsAppBundleOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.body: Checks that the target is an executable, flagged as an Apple build, and that the `MACOSX_BUNDLE` property is set to true.

@lcmTarget::IsDLLPlatform@k_ZNK8cmTarget.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsDLLPlatform@k_ZNK8cmTarget.body: Returns the flag stored in the implementation object, indicating whether the current target represents a DLL platform.

@lcmTarget::IsExecutableWithExports@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsExecutableWithExports@k_ZN.body: It returns true when the instance’s type is marked as `EXECUTABLE` and the `ENABLE_EXPORTS` flag is set, and false otherwise.

@lcmTarget::IsFrameworkOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsFrameworkOnApple@k_ZNK8cmT.body: Checks whether the target is an Apple‑style framework by ensuring that its type is a shared or static library, that it reports being on Apple, and that it carries the FRAMEWORK property flag.

@lcmTarget::IsImported@k_ZNK8cmTarget10I.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsImported@k_ZNK8cmTarget10I.body: Returns the result of its implementation’s IsImported() – a simple delegation that reports whether the target has been imported.

@lcmTarget::IsImportedGloballyVisible@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsImportedGloballyVisible@k_.body: Checks whether the target’s visibility flag equals `ImportedGlobally` and returns that Boolean value.

@lcmTarget::IsPerConfig@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsPerConfig@k_ZNK8cmTarget11.body: The `IsPerConfig()` member simply returns the value of the `PerConfig` flag stored in the target’s implementation object, indicating whether the target is in the “per‑config” state.

@lcmTarget::IsSharedLibraryWithExports@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::IsSharedLibraryWithExports@k.body: Determines whether the current target is a shared library with export support enabled.

@lcmTarget::SetHaveInstallRule@k_ZN8cmTa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTarget::SetHaveInstallRule@k_ZN8cmTa.body: The `SetHaveInstallRule` method simply updates the internal flag that indicates whether the target should enforce its install rule. It assigns the supplied Boolean (`hir`) to the `HaveInstallRule` member of the target’s implementation object. This change affects how the target behaves during subsequent operations that rely on that flag.

@lcmTargetCompileDefinitionsCommand@k_Z3.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetCompileDefinitionsCommand@k_Z3.body: The function creates a `TargetCompileDefinitionsImpl` instance and uses its `HandleArguments` method to process the supplied argument vector under the command name `COMPILE_DEFINITIONS`, propagating the resulting status.

@lcmTargetCompileFeaturesCommand@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetCompileFeaturesCommand@k_Z30cm.body: The function accepts a list of string arguments and a reference to a status object. It delegates the work to `TargetCompileFeaturesImpl(status)`, invoking its `HandleArguments` method with the arguments and the literal `"COMPILE_FEATURES"`. It returns whatever boolean value that helper method produces.

@lcmTargetDepend::SetBacktrace@k_ZNK14cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::SetBacktrace@k_ZNK14cm.body: The method assigns the supplied back‑trace list to the object’s internal `Backtrace` member, replacing any prior value with the new reference.

@lcmTargetDepend::SetCross@k_ZNK14cmTarg.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::SetCross@k_ZNK14cmTarg.body: The function assigns the supplied boolean to the member `Cross`. Because it is declared `const`, the member must be marked `mutable` (or the function should not be `const`) to allow modification. It simply stores the flag in the object.

@lcmTargetDepend::SetType@k_ZNK14cmTarge.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::SetType@k_ZNK14cmTarge.body: The `SetType` member merely flips a single flag: it turns on `Util` when the `strong` argument is true and turns on `Link` otherwise. Because the method is declared `const`, the implementation implicitly relies on mutable members or `const_cast`; otherwise the compiler would reject modifying `Util` or `Link`. It also never clears any previously set flag, so consecutive calls simply toggle the chosen flag without resetting the other.

@lcmTargetDepend::cmTargetDepend@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetDepend::cmTargetDepend@k_ZN14c.body: Constructs a *cmTargetDepend* instance by forwarding a pointer to its base class `Target` via the initializer list. It simply delegates construction to the base; no additional work is performed in the body.

@lcmTargetExport::cmTargetExport@k_ZN14c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetExport::cmTargetExport@k_ZN14c.body: The `cmTargetExport()` function serializes the current target’s configuration data and writes it out (usually to a file or stream) so that downstream tools or frameworks can consume that exported representation. It is the routine invoked when a target’s state needs to be persisted or shared with other components.

@lcmTargetLinkDirectoriesCommand@k_Z30cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetLinkDirectoriesCommand@k_Z30cm.body: The command simply forwards the supplied argument list and status object to a `TargetLinkDirectoriesImpl` instance, invoking its `HandleArguments` routine with the predefined command string and processing flag.

@lcmTargetPrecompileHeadersCommand@k_Z32.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPrecompileHeadersCommand@k_Z32.body: The function runs the pre‑compile‑headers step for a target: it feeds the provided arguments into `TargetPrecompileHeadersImpl`, invoking `HandleArguments` with the `"PRECOMPILE_HEADERS"` command token and the `PROCESS_REUSE_FROM` flag, and returns the success status of that call.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleArgumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleArgumen.body: The function parses a list of command‑line arguments for a target‑property command. It first validates that enough arguments were supplied, resolves the target name (including alias handling), confirms the target is a type that can have the requested property, and processes optional modifiers such as `SYSTEM`, `BEFORE`, `AFTER`, and `REUSE_FROM`. Finally, it delegates the remaining arguments to a helper that stores the property values on the target, returning success or failure accordingly.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleDirectC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleDirectC.body: The `HandleDirectContent` function is a virtual method that takes a pointer to a `cmTarget` object and returns a `bool`. It processes the target directly—typically performing an operation on the target and signaling success/failure via the return value. This routine is invoked from several places in the codebase (e.g., in `cmTargetPropCommandBase.h` around line 49) where different command implementations need to handle content without routing through a full command‑execution path.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleMissing.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::HandleMissing.body: When a target name cannot be resolved, the `HandleMissingTarget` override should react—typically by throwing an exception or logging the error and returning an error code. The base declares it as a pure‑virtual, so every concrete subclass must provide its own handling logic.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::Join@k_ZN23cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::Join@k_ZN23cm.body: The `Join` member builds a single string by flattening a list of strings—essentially it concatenates the supplied vector of string objects into one string that is then used when building a command‑line value. The function is pure virtual, so any concrete derived class implements the specific joining logic (e.g., joining with a delimiter or building a quoted list).

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.body: Constructs an object that stores a reference to the global *Makefile* extracted from the supplied `cmExecutionStatus` instance and keeps a reference to that status so that subsequent members can query or modify the current build state.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropC.body:
The public member `cmTargetPropCommandBase::cmTargetPropCommandBase()` initializes a new target‑property command.  
It accepts the target name, the property to modify, and the new value, stores these values, and registers the command in the builder so that the target receives the change when the build graph is later materialised.

@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::~cmTargetProp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropCommandBase::~cmTargetProp.body: The function is a virtual destructor, marked `= default`, ensuring that derived classes are correctly destroyed without custom cleanup.

@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::IssueLocatio.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetPropertyComputer::IssueLocatio.body: It emits a fatal error message telling the build system that the LOCATION property of a target cannot be resolved. The message explicitly recommends either passing the target name directly to add_custom_command or using the generator syntax $\<TARGET_FILE>. The function simply formats and forwards this error string to the make‑file’s IssueMessage routine with a FATAL_ERROR severity.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.body: The routine walks through every generator configuration that can generate a custom command. For each utility referenced in a command line it records the utility in the target’s dependency set; if the utility is a code‑generation tool it is added as a code‑generation dependency. It also aggregates the file‑level dependencies emitted by the command generator and, for each such file that isn’t a built‑in utility, places it in a queue for later processing; otherwise the file is treated as a code‑generation dependency.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::CheckCustom.body: The function iterates over every `cmCustomCommand` in the supplied vector and delegates each item to the member function `CheckCustomCommand`, effectively validating each custom command individually.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowName@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowName@.body: When called, FollowName searches the internal map for the supplied name. If it is missing, it asks the local generator to locate any target or source that can produce that file—potentially adjusting a relative path if needed. Once found, it records the dependency in the current entry and queues that source for later processing. If the result is a utility target, it also registers that target with the generator.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowNames.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::FollowNames.body: The method simply iterates over the provided list of names and forwards each one to the class’s dedicated `FollowName` routine, effectively delegating the name‑processing logic to that helper for every element in the vector.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::IsUtility@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::IsUtility@k.body: The function examines a dependency string, strips any trailing “.exe” and then resolves it to a target name. It looks up that name in the current generator’s target list; if a matching target is found and the path matches the expected build location, it records the target as a utility dependency (marking it with a flag indicating whether the original name was a full path). If no such target exists, the function returns false.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::QueueSource.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::QueueSource.body: The method adds a source file to the internal structures: it first inserts the pointer into a set of queued sources; if the insertion succeeds, it pushes the file onto the internal queue and stores its resolved path in a list of new sources.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::Trace@k_ZN2.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::Trace@k_ZN2.body: The `Trace` routine consumes the source‑file queue until it is empty, setting `CurrentEntry` to the `SourceDepends` entry for each popped file. For every file it pulls any extra dependencies from its `OBJECT_DEPENDS` property, normalises any full paths, and enqueues those names. It also follows the file’s own declared dependencies (`GetDepends`) and, if a custom command is present, verifies that command’s prerequisites. Once all sources in the current batch have been resolved, the gathered set of newly traced sources is passed to `AddTracedSources`.

@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTargetTraceDependencies::cmTargetTra.body: Initializes internal queues and checks for dependency loops before scheduling commands. It gathers source files, checks for circular dependencies, and enqueues pre‑/post‑build custom commands.

@lcmTest::AppendProperty@k_ZN6cmTest14Ap.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::AppendProperty@k_ZN6cmTest14Ap.body: The method simply forwards the supplied property name, value and string‑flag to the internal `Properties` helper, allowing callers to add a key‑value pair to the test’s configuration.

@lcmTest::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK6cmTest12Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetBacktrace@k_ZNK6cmTest12Get.body: The member function simply returns a reference to the internal `Backtrace` member. Because the function is marked `const`, the returned reference is read‑only (i.e., a `const` reference), ensuring callers cannot modify the underlying data. This allows callers to inspect or iterate over the backtrace information without risking accidental mutation of the internal state.

@lcmTest::GetCMP0158IsNew@k_ZNK6cmTest15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetCMP0158IsNew@k_ZNK6cmTest15.body: Returns true if the policy status flag for CMP0158 is set to the NEW enum value.

@lcmTest::GetCMP0178@k_ZNK6cmTest10GetCM.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetCMP0178@k_ZNK6cmTest10GetCM.body: Returns the current status of the CMP0178 policy.

@lcmTest::GetCommand@k_ZNK6cmTest10GetCo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetCommand@k_ZNK6cmTest10GetCo.body: The method returns a reference to the internal `Command` vector, exposing it in a read‑only (const) way so callers can inspect the stored strings without copying or modifying them.

@lcmTest::GetCommandExpandLists@k_ZNK6cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetCommandExpandLists@k_ZNK6cm.body: Returns the current value of the `CommandExpandLists` flag—a simple, read‑only query that lets callers check whether the list‑expansion feature is active.

@lcmTest::GetMakefile@k_ZN6cmTest11GetMa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetMakefile@k_ZN6cmTest11GetMa.body:
This function simply returns a pointer to the internal `Makefile` member.  
It provides read‑only access to the `cmMakefile` instance stored inside the object.

@lcmTest::GetOldStyle@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetO.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetOldStyle@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetO.body: The function provides read‑only access to the class’s `OldStyle` flag, returning its current Boolean value.

@lcmTest::GetProperties@k_ZN6cmTest13Get.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetProperties@k_ZN6cmTest13Get.body: The `GetProperties()` member simply returns a reference to the internal `Properties` map. It returns the map directly, so callers obtain a live view of the object’s state and can mutate it. This eliminates copy overhead but also exposes the internal structure to external modification and bypasses any encapsulation boundary; in a multithreaded context it may also break thread‑safety if the map is accessed concurrently without proper synchronization.

@lcmTest::GetProperty@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetProperty@k_ZNK6cmTest11GetP.body: The method returns a value for the requested property. It first looks up the property in the object’s own `Properties` collection. If that lookup fails, it checks whether the property is marked as “chained” in the associated state; if so, it tries to fetch the value from the linked `Makefile` via `GetProperty`. If that succeeds, it returns the chained value; otherwise it returns `nullptr`. If the initial lookup succeeds, the value is returned immediately.

@lcmTest::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK6cmTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::GetPropertyAsBool@k_ZNK6cmTest.body: Retrieves the named property via `GetProperty` and returns whether that property reports itself as “on”. If the property is marked on, the function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmTest::SetCommand@k_ZN6cmTest10SetCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetCommand@k_ZN6cmTest10SetCom.body: The `SetCommand` method simply assigns the supplied vector of strings to the class’s internal `Command` member, replacing its current contents with a copy of the argument.

@lcmTest::SetCommandExpandLists@k_ZN6cmT.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetCommandExpandLists@k_ZN6cmT.body: This routine simply assigns the supplied boolean to the internal flag `CommandExpandLists`, turning command‑expansion on or off for the test instance.

@lcmTest::SetName@k_ZN6cmTest7SetNameERK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetName@k_ZN6cmTest7SetNameERK.body: Assigns the supplied string to the internal `Name` member, taking the argument by const reference to avoid unnecessary copies.

@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::SetProperty@k_ZN6cmTest11SetPr.body: The method forwards the supplied key/value pair to the internal `Properties` collection, delegating the actual storage and validation logic to that helper.

@lcmTest::cmTest@k_ZN6cmTestC1EP10cmMake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::cmTest@k_ZN6cmTestC1EP10cmMake.body: The constructor reads the back‑trace and policy flags from the supplied `cmMakefile` and stores them in its member variables. It also keeps a pointer to that makefile and flips the `OldStyle` flag to true so the object knows it’s running in legacy mode.

@lcmTest::~cmTest@k_ZN6cmTestD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTest::~cmTest@k_ZN6cmTestD1Ev.body: The destructor is declared default, so the compiler generates a trivial destructor that automatically destroys all member subobjects in the order they were constructed, performing no additional cleanup beyond the default semantics.

@lcmTestGenerator::Compute@k_ZN15cmTestG.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::Compute@k_ZN15cmTestG.body: Stores the passed `cmLocalGenerator` pointer in the instance’s `LG` member.

@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.body: The function `operator()` is a public, `const` member that accepts a `const std::string&` argument and returns a new `std::string` value. It operates without modifying the object that owns the function, and its body is expected to perform a simple transformation or lookup on the supplied string before producing the resulting string. The implementation should be careful to avoid unnecessary allocations and should guard against empty or excessively long inputs to keep both performance and exception safety in check.

@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.body: The lambda receives each argument string, parses it into an expression object, and then evaluates that expression using the current instance’s `LG` context and the supplied configuration.

@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::EvaluateCommandLineAr.body: The function takes a list of command‑line strings, feeds each one through the `ge.Parse()` parser to obtain an expression, evaluates that expression with the current logic graph and the supplied `config` string, and finally returns a new vector containing the resulting evaluated strings.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateInternalPrope.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateInternalPrope.body:
Collects a test’s back‑trace and serialises it to the output stream.  
If the trace list is empty it returns immediately.  
Otherwise it writes a prefixed header, then iterates over each trace element, emitting “FilePath;Line;Name” pairs separated by semicolons, and finally closes the string.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateOldStyle@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateOldStyle@k_ZN.body: The routine writes an old‑style test entry into a CMake build file. It first flags the test as generated, then decides if the test name needs quoting (using “==…==” delimiters). It emits an `add_test(...)` line, escaping quotes in each argument. Finally it emits a `set_tests_properties(...)` line with the test’s properties and any internal properties.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptActions.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptActions.body: The routine checks whether the current generator should emit actions per configuration. If the flag is set, it defers to the base class’s per‑configuration implementation. Otherwise it falls back to the legacy path by invoking the legacy‐style routine for a single configuration.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptConfigs.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptConfigs.body: The function simply forwards the call to its base implementation. It passes the supplied output stream and indentation level to `cmScriptGenerator::GenerateScriptConfigs`, which then emits the appropriate configuration scripts. The method itself performs no additional processing beyond invoking the inherited routine.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptForConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptForConf.body: The lambda fetches a property from a target, parses it into a list of command‑line arguments, silently drops any empty elements (issuing a warning if the policy is WARN), builds the command string with proper escaping, and finally writes it to the supplied stream.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptForConf.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptForConf.body: The function emits a CMake‑style test definition: it emits an `add_test` line that may be quoted or plain, followed by a list of arguments that may include an expanded target executable. If the executable is a target of type EXECUTABLE, its full path and any declared launcher properties are inserted. The command line is escaped for CMake, and finally the test’s properties are written with `set_tests_properties`, including any internal properties.

@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptNoConfi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GenerateScriptNoConfi.body: The routine emits a test‑definition line into the output stream: it decides whether the test name needs quoting, builds the required number of “=” characters for the quoting syntax, and then writes either a quoted form or a plain form of the call `add_test(... NOT_AVAILABLE)` with the appropriate indentation.

@lcmTestGenerator::GetTest@k_ZNK15cmTest.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::GetTest@k_ZNK15cmTest.body: It simply returns the stored pointer to the test object held in the generator. The method is const‑qualified and does no further processing.

@lcmTestGenerator::NeedsScriptNoConfig@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::NeedsScriptNoConfig@k.body: The function evaluates whether a test script must be created when no concrete configurations exist but the test is still sensitive to configuration types. It returns true only when a test has already been generated, the test’s actions are configured per‑config, there are no configuration objects present, yet configuration types are defined.

@lcmTestGenerator::TestsForConfig@k_ZN15.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::TestsForConfig@k_ZN15.body: The method simply forwards the supplied configuration string to the internal `GeneratesForConfig` routine and returns that routine’s boolean result, indicating whether the test generation succeeded for that configuration.

@lcmTestGenerator::cmTestGenerator@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::cmTestGenerator@k_ZN1.body: The constructor initializes a `cmTestGenerator` instance by calling the base `cmScriptGenerator` constructor with the configuration type `"CTEST_CONFIGURATION_TYPE"` and the supplied configurations vector. It then stores the supplied `cmTest` pointer in the member `Test`, sets the flag `ActionsPerConfig` according to whether the test uses the old style (`!test->GetOldStyle()`), and initializes `TestGenerated` to `false` and `LG` to `nullptr`.

@lcmTestGenerator::~cmTestGenerator@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTestGenerator::~cmTestGenerator@k_ZN.body: The `~cmTestGenerator()` destructor is responsible for cleaning up when a `cmTestGenerator` instance is destroyed. It will automatically invoke any base‑class destructors and clean resources (e.g., memory, file handles, threads) that the class owns. If the class holds no special resources, the default implementation (`= default;`) suffices; otherwise override might be required.

@lcmTimestamp::AddTimestampComponent@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::AddTimestampComponent@k_Z.body: The function builds a formatted string fragment for a timestamp string based on a format flag. It switches on the flag character and returns a string fragment that represents that component of the date‑time (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond, UTC offset, etc.). If the flag is unrecognised it simply returns the format character itself. The routine handles a handful of special cases (e.g. “%”, “%a”, “%Z”, “%z”, “%s”, “%f”) and falls back to the standard library’s `strftime` for the rest. When compiled on a few older platforms it applies platform‑specific work‑arounds such as setting `XPG_SUS_ENV` on AIX or using a custom loader for MinGW. The function is marked `private const` to keep it internal and immutable; it never mutates the caller’s state.

@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.body: The method forwards the call to a more detailed overload, passing the supplied `time_t` value, a zero‑offset, the `formatString` moved into the call, and the same `utcFlag`. This keeps the public interface simple while deferring all formatting logic to the underlying implementation.

@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CreateTimestampFromTimeT@.body: The routine produces a formatted timestamp string. It accepts a time value, optional microseconds, a format mask, and a flag indicating UTC. When the mask is empty it defaults to "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S" and appends “Z” for UTC. It converts the time into a `struct tm` using `gmtime` or `localtime`, then walks the format string, replacing each format token (e.g. %Y, %m) by calling `AddTimestampComponent`. The final string is returned.

@lcmTimestamp::CreateUtcTimeTFromTm@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CreateUtcTimeTFromTm@k_ZN.body: Creates a UTC‑time value from a `struct tm` argument by temporarily setting the `TZ` environment variable to “UTC”, calling `tzset()` and `mktime()`, then restoring the original `TZ` setting before returning the resulting `time_t`.

@lcmTimestamp::CurrentTime@k_ZNK11cmTime.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::CurrentTime@k_ZNK11cmTime.body: The routine first queries the current time‑point (seconds and micro‑second parts) via libuv, then checks if the build was supplied a `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` override; if present it replaces the time value (and zero‑pads microseconds). Finally it forwards the resolved epoch and micro‑second values, together with the requested format string and UTC flag, to `CreateTimestampFromTimeT` to construct the string to return. If the system reports an invalid time (i.e. a returned -1), an empty string is returned.

@lcmTimestamp::FileModificationTime@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::FileModificationTime@k_ZN.body: The function resolves a given file path, verifies the file exists, then uses libuv’s stat call to pull the modification time and its microsecond part. It truncates the nanosecond field to microseconds for consistency, and finally formats the timestamp into a string according to the supplied format string and UTC flag.

@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTimestamp::cmTimestamp@k_ZN11cmTimes.body: The `cmTimestamp()` routine fetches the system’s current time, normalizes it to the project’s epoch convention, and emits it in the unified format adopted across the code base. It runs in constant time, avoiding heavy allocations, and only returns the time representation—no side‑effects or state mutations are performed.

@lcmTokenize@k_Z10cmTokenizeB5cxx11St17b.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTokenize@k_Z10cmTokenizeB5cxx11St17b.body: The function tokenizes a string view into a sequence of string tokens. It accepts a separator type of template parameter `Sep` (defaulting to `char`) and a tokenization mode that selects the algorithm variant. Internally it forwards the string view, separator, and mode to a lower‑level helper `cmTokenize` that inserts each token into a container via a `back_inserter`. The resulting `std::vector<std::string>` holds the split substrings.

@lcmTrimWhitespace@k_Z16cmTrimWhitespace.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmTrimWhitespace@k_Z16cmTrimWhitespace.body: It copies the substring of the input that excludes leading and trailing whitespace characters into a freshly‑allocated std::string.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::Connect@k_ZN19cmU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::Connect@k_ZN19cmU.body: The `Connect` static function attempts to create a new POSIX‐based `cmUVJobServerClient` instance. It first constructs an `ImplPosix` object tied to the supplied event loop, checks that it is in a connected state, then stores the supplied callbacks (`onToken`, `onDisconnect`) into that implementation before returning a wrapped client object. If the implementation cannot connect (or on Windows where it’s unimplemented), it simply returns a null option.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::GetHeldTokens@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::GetHeldTokens@k_Z.body: Returns the value of the `HeldTokens` member field from the `Impl_` object. The method is marked `const`, guaranteeing it does not modify any observable state. Because it simply reads and returns that integer, it incurs no side effects and can be safely called by any code that holds a reference to a `cmUVJobServerClient` instance.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::GetNeedTokens@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::GetNeedTokens@k_Z.body: The `GetNeedTokens()` method simply returns the current value of the `NeedTokens` member stored in the implementation object (`Impl_`). It does not perform any computation or state mutation—its purpose is to expose the token count that the client requires.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::ReleaseToken@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::ReleaseToken@k_ZN.body: The method simply forwards a token‑release request to the underlying implementation object (`Impl_`). It delegates the actual release logic to `Impl_->ReleaseToken()` so that component can perform the required cleanup or cleanup‑related work.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::RequestToken@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::RequestToken@k_ZN.body: Requests a fresh authentication token from the server and stores it locally for subsequent authenticated requests.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::cmUVJobServerClie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::cmUVJobServerClie.body: The public constructor `cmUVJobServerClient(cmUVJobServerClient&&) noexcept` is a move‑constructor that efficiently transfers ownership of the client’s internal resources (e.g., network sockets, buffers, thread handles) from a temporary instance into a new instance without throwing exceptions. It’s marked `noexcept` to guarantee that the move operation cannot propagate exceptions, and is employed whenever an existing `cmUVJobServerClient` object needs to be moved into a new context (as shown in the various usage points throughout the codebase).

@lcmUVJobServerClient::cmUVJobServerClie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::cmUVJobServerClie.body: The declaration removes the default copy constructor, so any attempt to copy a `cmUVJobServerClient` object will be a compile‑time error—effectively making instances immutable after creation.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::cmUVJobServerClie.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::cmUVJobServerClie.body: It moves the supplied `std::unique_ptr<Impl>` into the member `Impl_`, initializing the object with that implementation instance.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: This function implements the move‑assignment operator for `cmUVJobServerClient`. It takes an rvalue reference to another client, transfers that object’s internal resources into the current instance, and returns a reference to the instance. It is declared `noexcept` to guarantee no exception is thrown.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::operator=@k_ZN19c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::operator=@k_ZN19c.body: The deleted assignment operator prevents the client object from being reassigned after construction, ensuring that any copy‑assignment attempts are caught at compile time and that the object remains immutable once created.

@lcmUVJobServerClient::~cmUVJobServerCli.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVJobServerClient::~cmUVJobServerCli.body: The destructor releases any resources acquired by the `cmUVJobServerClient`. It shuts down networking sockets, joins background threads, and frees allocated buffers or memory before the object is destroyed. It guarantees that no stray handles or memory leaks remain when a client instance is discarded.

@lcmUVProcessChain::ErrorStream@k_ZN16cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::ErrorStream@k_ZN16cm.body: The method simply returns the integer value stored in the `BuiltInStream` member of the object’s `ErrorStreamData`. It accesses that field through the internal `Data` pointer and returns it unchanged.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Finished@k_ZNK16cmUV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Finished@k_ZNK16cmUV.body: Returns `true` when the number of processes that have finished matches or exceeds the total number of processes in the chain, and `false` otherwise.

@lcmUVProcessChain::GetLoop@k_ZN16cmUVPr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::GetLoop@k_ZN16cmUVPr.body: It returns a reference to the underlying `uv_loop_t` instance stored in the `Data` member of the current object – essentially a thin getter that dereferences `Data->Loop` and returns that reference.

@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.body: The function returns a read‑only reference to the status of the requested process in the internal chain. It simply looks up the process at the supplied index in the `Data->Processes` collection and hands back its `ProcessStatus` member, without altering any state. It relies on the caller to ensure the index is valid; an out‑of‑range index would lead to undefined behaviour.

@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::GetStatus@k_ZNK16cmU.body: The method creates a vector sized to the number of processes, fills each slot with the address of the result of `GetStatus(i)`, and returns that vector.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Finish.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Finish.body: The `Finish` routine clears temporary output and error buffers and flags the internal data structure as successfully processed by setting `Valid` to `true`.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Intern.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Intern.body: The function creates a new `InternalData` instance by moving the contents of an existing `InternalData` object that is passed as an rvalue reference. It transfers the internal state of the source object into the new instance, avoiding copying of the underlying data.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Intern.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Intern.body: InternalData constructs and returns an `InternalData` instance that packages the UV‑processing state—essentially a lightweight container of context‑specific flags and pointers used by the UV chain to coordinate subsequent steps.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Prepar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Prepar.body:
The `Prepare` method configures the process chain’s standard‑in/out/error streams according to the supplied `builder`.  
It assigns stream descriptors (or built‑in pipes) to each stream slot (input, error, output), sets appropriate flags (`UV_IGNORE`, `UV_INHERIT_FD`), and creates the inter‑process pipes that chain each process’s output to the next process’s input.  
While setting up these connections it populates a `ProcessData` instance per process, initializes its I/O pipe handles, and returns `false` immediately whenever any pipe creation or handle opening fails; otherwise it returns `true` after all data objects have been initialized.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.body: The method flags the internal finished flag as true and bumps the counter for completed processes, indicating that the processing chain has reached its conclusion.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.body: ProcessData orchestrates the data handling pipeline by validating, transforming, and persisting incoming data objects while coordinating downstream actions.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.body: ProcessData gathers input payloads, validates them against schema rules, and populates a ProcessData struct instance before dispatching the enriched payload to downstream consumers. It acts as the single entry point that normalises and enriches data for further routing in the UV processing pipeline.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Proces.body: ~ProcessData is a public entry point that receives a `ProcessData` structure, executes a predefined series of transformations (often involving validation, mapping, or aggregation), and emits a resulting status or transformed output for the surrounding processing chain.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.body: The lambda receives a termination signal, casts the handler’s data to a `ProcessData` pointer, writes the exit status and signal into the process status structure, and then calls `Finish()` to clean‑up and end the process.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::SpawnP.body: The method configures a `uv_process_options_t` structure with the executable path from `config.Arguments[0]`, appends a NULL‑terminated argument list, sets the appropriate `UV_PROCESS_*` flags depending on the builder’s detached flag and UV version, and wires up the three stdio streams. It attaches an exit callback that records the exit status and signal in the surrounding `ProcessData` before calling `uv_spawn`. If the spawn fails it marks the process as finished; otherwise, when detached, it unreferences the process handle. Finally it clears the input/output pipe references used during the spawn.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.body: `StreamData` is a move constructor that accepts an rvalue reference to a `StreamData` instance, initializing the new object by transferring ownership of the underlying stream buffer and related metadata from the source instance.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.body: Creates a new instance with the same values as the passed reference, effectively copying all member data.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.body: The `StreamData` function builds and returns a lightweight structure that packages the key stream‑level information required by the UV‑processing pipeline—specifically the codec type, stream resolution, frame‑rate, and any time‑stamp markers that downstream components need to correlate frames to processing windows.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.body: The `operator=` function is a move‑assignment operator for `StreamData`. It takes an rvalue reference to a temporary `StreamData` instance, copies its internal state into the current object (typically by moving members or resetting them to a valid state), and returns `*this`. This allows `StreamData` objects to be assigned efficiently without copying expensive resources.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.body: The assignment operator copies all member data from the right‑hand `StreamData` into the current object and returns a reference to that object, enabling chained assignments.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::Stream.body: ~StreamData releases any dynamically allocated resources associated with a `StreamData` instance, ensuring internal buffers and streams are properly closed and memory freed. It performs any necessary bookkeeping before the object is destroyed.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::operat.body: Accepts an rvalue reference to `InternalData`, moves that internal state into the current object, and returns a reference to the updated instance.

@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::~Inter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::InternalData::~Inter.body: It returns the internal data structure used by the processing chain.

@lcmUVProcessChain::OutputStream@k_ZN16c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::OutputStream@k_ZN16c.body: This member function is a simple accessor that returns the value of the `BuiltinStream` member stored in the `OutputStreamData` sub‑object of the process chain’s `Data` pointer. It performs no validation or side‑effects; it simply dereferences the pointer hierarchy and returns the integer. If any part of the chain (`Data`, `OutputStreamData`, or `BuiltinStream`) is null, the call will result in a crash or undefined behaviour. The function’s sole purpose is to expose the stored builtin stream identifier.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Status::GetException.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Status::GetException.body:
The `GetException()` routine converts a child‑process exit status into a user‑friendly error pair.  
It first checks whether a spawn‑time error (`SpawnResult`) occurred; if so, it returns an `ExceptionCode::Spawn` pair with the system‑error string.  

For a finished process, on Windows it examines the exit code against a long list of predefined status values (e.g. `STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT`, `STATUS_FLOAT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO`, etc.) and maps each to the appropriate `ExceptionCode` (e.g. `Interrupt`, `Numerical`, `Fault`, `Illegal`, `Other`). If none of the cases match, it returns the raw code in a generic “Other” message.  

On non‑Windows builds it does the same mapping for termination signals (`SIGSEGV`, `SIGILL`, `SIGINT`, etc.), again producing a corresponding `ExceptionCode` and message.  

Finally, if no special condition applies, it returns `(ExceptionCode::None, “”)`.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Status::operator=@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Status::operator=@k_.body: This overload copies all fields from the right‑hand operand into the current object and then returns *this*, allowing chained assignments.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Valid@k_ZNK16cmUVPro.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Valid@k_ZNK16cmUVPro.body: Returns the Boolean flag stored inside the `Data` member of the instance.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait::[lambda_0]@kcm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait::[lambda_0]@kcm.body: It treats the `uv_timer_t` passed to the callback as a pointer to a `bool` flag stored in its `data` field, and flips that flag to `true` when the timer expires.

@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait@k_ZN16cmUVProce.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::Wait@k_ZN16cmUVProce.body: The function starts a timer that will set a `timeout` flag after the requested number of milliseconds. It then spins in a loop, calling `uv_run()` until either the timeout flag becomes true or all queued processes finish. It returns `true` only if the timeout flag was never set—i.e., the processes completed before the timeout elapsed.

@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.body: The constructor forwards the internal `Data` member from `other` with a noexcept guarantee, leaving the body empty.

@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::cmUVProcessChain@k_Z.body: Creates an instance of `cmUVProcessChain`, allocating and storing its private `InternalData` instance via `cm::make_unique`.

@lcmUVProcessChain::operator=@k_ZN16cmUV.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::operator=@k_ZN16cmUV.body: This constructor‑like move operator swaps the internal `Data` member from another `cmUVProcessChain` instance into the current object and returns a reference to the modified object.

@lcmUVProcessChain::~cmUVProcessChain@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChain::~cmUVProcessChain@k_.body: The destructor `~cmUVProcessChain()` is marked `default`, so its behavior is the compiler‑generated cleanup of all non‑static member variables. When an object of `cmUVProcessChain` goes out of scope or is explicitly destroyed, this function is called automatically; it simply destroys the class’s members in reverse construction order. No explicit code is required because the default destructor handles all member destructors.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::AddCommand@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::AddCommand@k_.body: Adds a new command to the internal list only when the supplied argument list isn’t empty—moving the arguments into the new entry—then returns the builder instance for chaining.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::GetLoop@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::GetLoop@k_ZNK.body: The function simply exposes the internal event‑loop handle. When called, it returns the member `Loop` stored in the object, yielding a pointer of type `uv_loop_t*`. No additional logic or side‑effects occur.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetBuiltinLoo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetBuiltinLoo.body: It clears the internal `Loop` pointer (resetting it to `nullptr`) and then returns the current `cmUVProcessChainBuilder` instance, allowing further method calls on the same builder.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetBuiltinStr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetBuiltinStr.body: The method registers the supplied stream as an internal built‑in stream only for the OUTPUT and ERROR cases. It fetches the corresponding stream record, tags its type as Builtin, and leaves the INPUT case untouched, after which it returns the current builder instance for further chaining.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetDetached@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetDetached@k.body: The `SetDetached()` method simply toggles the internal `Detached` flag on the `cmUVProcessChainBuilder` instance to `true` and returns a reference to the same builder. This indicates that subsequent calls should not attach the built chain to any existing process chain, allowing the builder to operate in isolation.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalLo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalLo.body: The method assigns the supplied `uv_loop_t` instance to the internal `Loop` member and returns the builder instance (`*this`) to allow fluent chaining of subsequent builder calls.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.body: The `SetExternalStream` method attaches a standard‑I/O stream to the processing chain. It calls `cm_fileno` on the supplied `FILE*`; if the result is a non‑negative file descriptor it forwards that descriptor to the internal overload that accepts a descriptor. If `cm_fileno` fails (returns –1), the method falls back to the no‑stream variant, ensuring the chain remains in a sane state. The function returns a reference to the builder so calls can be chained fluently.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetExternalSt.body: The `SetExternalStream` method assigns a file descriptor to one of the three standard streams (input, output, or error). It updates the corresponding internal `Stdio` entry’s `Type` to `External` and records the supplied file descriptor, then returns a reference to the builder for fluent chaining.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetMergedBuil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetMergedBuil.body: The method flips the `MergedBuiltinStreams` flag to true and then chains two stream setups: it first calls `SetBuiltinStream(Stream_OUTPUT)` and immediately after that, `SetBuiltinStream(Stream_ERROR)` on the returned object. The call sequence returns the current builder instance so the caller can continue configuring the chain.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetNoStream@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetNoStream@k.body: The method clears the stream type for the specified stream index by setting the stored type to `None`. After updating the internal record, it returns the current builder instance for chaining.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetWorkingDir.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::SetWorkingDir.body: The method assigns the supplied path to the builder’s internal `WorkingDirectory` member by moving the string (so the caller’s string is transferred without copying) and then returns a reference to the builder itself. In effect, it lets a caller chain further configuration calls on the same object after setting the working directory.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::Start@k_ZNK23.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::Start@k_ZNK23.body: Creates a `cmUVProcessChain`, prepares it via `Prepare`, spawns each registered process in order (marking first and last), finalises it with `Finish()`, and returns the fully‑built chain.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::cmUVProcessCh.body: Initializes the internal state that a process‑chain instance requires—setting up the builder’s context and registering the default nodes that will later be linked together into a chain.

@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::~cmUVProcessC.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVProcessChainBuilder::~cmUVProcessC.body: The function `~cmUVProcessChainBuilder()` creates a new instance of `cmUVProcessChainBuilder`. It initializes the builder with any context or configuration required by the surrounding code (e.g., registering a process chain with a UV processing system) and returns that instance for subsequent use in building or executing a UV process chain.

@lcmUVStreamRead@k_Z14cmUVStreamReadP11u.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmUVStreamRead@k_Z14cmUVStreamReadP11u.body: The template registers the supplied `onRead` and `onFinish` callbacks on a `uv_stream_t`, starts an asynchronous read with `uv_read_start`, and returns a handle object that keeps the callbacks alive until the read operation completes.

@lcmValue::IsOff@k_ZNK7cmValue5IsOffEv@f.author: AI Short Overview

It returns the logical conjunction of these two conditions, signalling whether the value is considered active.

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1EDn@f./.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1EPKNSt7.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1ERKNSt7.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmValue::cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueC1ERKS_.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmValue::operator bool@k_ZNK7cmValuecv.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmValue::operator=@k_ZN7cmValueaSERKS_.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmValue::~cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmValue::~cmValue@k_ZN7cmValueD1Ev.body: The destructor `~cmValue()` cleans up the resources held by a `cmValue` object, ensuring any dynamically allocated members are released before the instance is discarded.

@lcmVersion::GetCMakeVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmVersion::GetMajorVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmVersion::GetMinorVersion@k_ZN9cmVers.author: AI Short Overview

@lcmWhileCommand@k_Z14cmWhileCommandRKSt.author: AI Short Overview
