On non‑Windows builds it simply verifies unsupported syntax and returns the original expression unchanged.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::FromView@k_ZN17cmWi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::FromView@k_ZN17cmWi.body: Converts a `View` enum value to its string representation using a lookup table. It returns the corresponding `cm::string_view` from a statically‑built `unordered_map`; if the value isn’t present in the map, it returns an empty view.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetLastError@k_ZNK1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetLastError@k_ZNK1.body: The `GetLastError` member simply returns the value stored in the `LastError` member variable. It’s a `const` getter that produces a `string_view` over that internal string without copying it.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetSubKeys@k_ZN17cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetSubKeys@k_ZN17cm.body: The function opens a registry key under each view supplied by `ComputeViews`, merges the returned sub‑key lists, removes duplicates, sorts them, clears any previous error if at least one query succeeded, and returns an `optional` containing the unique sorted list (or `nullopt` if the code is not compiled for Windows).

@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetValueNames@k_ZN1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::GetValueNames@k_ZN1.body: Retrieves all value names under a given key across the requested registry views, aggregates the unique names, sorts them, and returns the list; any view that throws a registry_error is skipped, and if at least one view succeeds the error field is cleared before returning.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::ReadValue@k_ZN17cmW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::ReadValue@k_ZN17cmW.body: Accepts a key, optional separator, and view flag, then forwards the call to a more complete overload passing an empty string as a separator argument.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::ReadValue@k_ZN17cmW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::ReadValue@k_ZN17cmW.body: The function searches the registry views obtained from `ComputeViews`. For each view it clears any previous error, opens the key with `KeyHandler::OpenKey`, and tries to read the named value (treating `"(default)"` as the default key and using the provided separator). If a read succeeds it returns the value; on failure it records the error and continues. If none of the views provide the value, the function returns `nullopt`.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::ToView@k_ZN17cmWind.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::ToView@k_ZN17cmWind.body: The function performs a lookup of the supplied view name in a static `unordered_map` of known definitions and returns the matching `View` value wrapped in an `optional`; if the name isn’t present, it returns an empty optional.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.body: The function is a move‑constructor for `cmWindowsRegistry`. It takes an rvalue reference to another `cmWindowsRegistry` instance and transfers the internal registry data into the new object, performing a member‑wise move of the entries.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.body: The constructor initializes a `cmWindowsRegistry` instance only on Windows platforms. It stores the set of supported value types and, if a `CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P` definition is present in the supplied makefile, determines whether the target architecture is 32‑ or 64‑bit (by comparing the string to `"8"`). On non‑Windows builds it immediately records an error message indicating the registry is unavailable.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::cmWindowsRegistry@k.body: The constructor copies all registry entries from the source object into the new instance, setting up the internal mapping data structures that back the registry’s in‑memory representation. It performs no complex logic beyond copying and initializing member containers.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::operator=@k_ZN17cmW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::operator=@k_ZN17cmW.body: Moves the contents of another registry into this instance and returns a reference to the current object.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::operator=@k_ZN17cmW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::operator=@k_ZN17cmW.body: The operator= copies the internal registry state from the supplied source instance to the current object, performing a deep copy of the stored entries and returning a reference to the destination object for chaining.

@lcmWindowsRegistry::~cmWindowsRegistry@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWindowsRegistry::~cmWindowsRegistry@.body: ~cmWindowsRegistry loads a Windows registry helper object that parses a specified registry path, populates a map of key‑value pairs, and exposes utility helpers for querying, writing, and deleting those entries. It is the single entry point used throughout the code base to safely read‑and‑write the registry without leaking direct Windows API calls.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::Failed@k_ZNK18cmWo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::Failed@k_ZNK18cmWo.body: It reports whether the internal error string contains any text – returning true if the string is non‑empty and false otherwise. This const method performs a single emptiness test.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::GetError@k_ZNK18cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::GetError@k_ZNK18cm.body: Returns a const reference to the `Error` member, allowing callers to read the stored error string without copying it or modifying the underlying data.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::cmWorkingDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::cmWorkingDirectory.body: The constructor remembers the current working directory in `OldDir` by calling `cmSystemTools::GetLogicalWorkingDirectory()` and then immediately changes the working directory to the supplied `newdir` via `SetDirectory(newdir)`. The effect is to temporarily switch the working directory while preserving the original value for later restoration.

@lcmWorkingDirectory::~cmWorkingDirector.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWorkingDirectory::~cmWorkingDirector.body: When an instance of `cmWorkingDirectory` is destroyed, the destructor calls `Pop()` to remove that object from its owning structure.

@lcmWriteFileCommand@k_Z18cmWriteFileCom.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmWriteFileCommand@k_Z18cmWriteFileCom.body: The routine parses the supplied command arguments, assembles the text to be written, and writes it to the specified file—creating any missing directories and adjusting permissions so the file can be opened for writing. It honours an “APPEND” flag to append rather than overwrite, and signals errors through the status object.

@lcmXMLParser::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLPar.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLPar.body: The `EndElement` method is invoked whenever the parser finishes processing an XML element. It prints a simple status line—“End element: <element‑name>”—to the console and can be overridden in derived classes to perform custom cleanup or state updates at element termination.

@lcmXMLParser::ParseFile@k_ZN11cmXMLPars.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::ParseFile@k_ZN11cmXMLPars.body: The `ParseFile` routine first validates the input pointer, returning a failure code immediately if `file` is null. It then opens the file using `cmsys::ifstream`; if the stream fails to open, it again returns zero. When the file is successfully opened it reads the entire buffer into a `std::ostringstream` via `rdbuf()` and forwards the resulting C‑string to the class’s `Parse` method. The function has no explicit error reporting beyond the `int` return value, and it relies on the underlying `Parse` implementation for content validation. The implementation is straightforward but lacks explicit resource‑cleaning or exception safety; it also allocates a potentially large string in memory that could be avoided by streaming or buffered parsing in the future.

@lcmXMLParser::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLP.body:
The function writes a line to the console that contains the element name.  
The `atts` argument is present in the signature but is not used inside the implementation.

@lcmXMLParser::cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLPa.body: Initialises internal state: sets Parser and callback pointers to nullptr and resets ParseError to 0.

@lcmXMLParser::~cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLP.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLParser::~cmXMLParser@k_ZN11cmXMLP.body: This destructor checks whether the parser instance was created; if so, it calls `CleanupParser()` to release resources.

@lcmXMLWriter::Attribute@k_ZN11cmXMLWrit.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Attribute@k_ZN11cmXMLWrit.body: The `Attribute` method emits an attribute name/value pair into the output stream: it calls a pre‑attribute hook, then streams the name, an equals sign, and the value escaped by `SafeAttribute`.

@lcmXMLWriter::Content@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Content@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.body: Processes the supplied argument through a pre‑processing hook and then writes it into the output stream using the `SafeContent` escape routine.

@lcmXMLWriter::Element@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::Element@k_ZN11cmXMLWriter.body: This function writes a named element containing the provided value. It calls `StartElement` with the element’s name, passes the value to `Content`, then calls `EndElement`. The template accepts any type that can be rendered by `Content`.

@lcmXMLWriter::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLWri.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::EndElement@k_ZN11cmXMLWri.body: It removes the current element from the stack, writes either an empty‐element close (`/>`) or a full end tag (`</name>`), and updates indentation and line‑break state accordingly.

@lcmXMLWriter::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::StartElement@k_ZN11cmXMLW.body: The method finalizes any pending start‑tag, emits a line break if needed, writes the opening `<name>` tag, records the element name on the internal stack, bumps the indentation counter, and marks the element as opened with the appropriate flags (`ElementOpen=true`, `BreakAttrib=false`).

@lcmXMLWriter::cmXMLWriter@k_ZN11cmXMLWr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::cmXMLWriter@k_ZN11cmXMLWr.body: The constructor simply stores the supplied output stream and indentation level. It also creates a helper object that represents the current indentation string—by defaulting it to one tab character. No additional logic occurs.

@lcmXMLWriter::~cmXMLWriter@k_ZN11cmXMLW.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmXMLWriter::~cmXMLWriter@k_ZN11cmXMLW.body: The destructor checks that the writer’s indentation level is zero before object cleanup, guarding against unfinished or nested output streams.

@lcm_fileno@k_Z9cm_filenoP8_IO_FILE@f./S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_fileno@k_Z9cm_filenoP8_IO_FILE@f./S.body: The routine forwards the supplied `FILE*` to `fileno()` and returns the resulting integer file descriptor.

@lcm_utf8_decode_character@kcm_utf8_deco.author: AI Short Overview
@lcm_utf8_decode_character@kcm_utf8_deco.body: Decodes a UTF‑8 byte sequence: it reads the first byte, determines how many continuation bytes are required by checking the leading‑bit pattern, validates each continuation byte, and assembles the Unicode scalar value into *pc. On success it returns a pointer to the byte following the decoded character; on failure it returns 0.

@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::AddCacheEntry@k_ZN5cmake13AddCa.body: Adds a cache entry with the supplied key, value, and help string, then removes the key from the unused‑cli list. If the key matches a special string it updates the messenger’s warning‑or‑error flags accordingly—turning off or on the relevant deprecation/ developer‑warning settings.

@lcmake::CreateGlobalGenerator@k_ZN5cmak.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::CreateGlobalGenerator@k_ZN5cmak.body: The function first produces an auxiliary external‑generator via `createExtraGenerator`. It then loops through the stored generator objects, invoking each one's `CreateGlobalGenerator` method until one succeeds. Once a global generator is obtained, it attaches the external generator instance to it and finally returns the configured global generator.

@lcmake::GetCacheDefinition@k_ZNK5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetCacheDefinition@k_ZNK5cmake1.body: The function simply retrieves a cache entry that was previously initialized. It forwards the request to the internal state object and returns the resulting `cmValue` unchanged.

@lcmake::GetCheckInProgressMessages@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetCheckInProgressMessages@k_ZN.body: It returns a read‑only reference to the internal vector that holds the queued “check‑in‑in‑progress” strings, letting callers inspect the list without modifying it.

@lcmake::GetCurrentSnapshot@k_ZNK5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetCurrentSnapshot@k_ZNK5cmake1.body: The function merely returns the stored snapshot value. Because it’s declared `const`, it guarantees no modification of the object state during the call. The returned `cmStateSnapshot` is a copy of the internal `CurrentSnapshot` member, so callers receive a snapshot that cannot be altered back into the owning instance.

@lcmake::GetFileAPI@k_ZNK5cmake10GetFile.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetFileAPI@k_ZNK5cmake10GetFile.body: Returns a pointer to the internal `FileAPI` instance, so callers can invoke file‑related operations while preserving the constness of the containing object.

@lcmake::GetGlobCacheEntries@k_ZNK5cmake.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetGlobCacheEntries@k_ZNK5cmake.body: The function returns a copy of the global cache entries by delegating to the underlying state object; it is a const member that simply forwards the request to State->GetGlobCacheEntries() and returns the resulting vector.

@lcmake::GetGlobalGenerator@k_ZN5cmake18.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetGlobalGenerator@k_ZN5cmake18.body: Retrieves the singleton instance of the global generator; returns a pointer to the cmGlobalGenerator currently stored in the GlobalGenerator member.

@lcmake::GetHomeDirectory@k_ZNK5cmake16G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetHomeDirectory@k_ZNK5cmake16G.body: The `GetHomeDirectory` function simply returns a reference to the source‑directory string stored in the internal state object—no additional computation or side‑effects.

@lcmake::GetHomeOutputDirectory@k_ZNK5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetHomeOutputDirectory@k_ZNK5cm.body: The method simply returns a reference to the string returned by `State->GetBinaryDirectory()`. Because it returns a `const std::string&`, no copy of the string is performed; it just forwards the reference held inside the `State` object. This accessor is marked `const`, guaranteeing that calling it does not modify any internal state. It therefore provides a lightweight read‑only view of the binary directory without side‑effects or allocation overhead.

@lcmake::GetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11GetProp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11GetProp.body: GetProperty retrieves a global property value by delegating to the State object's GetGlobalProperty method and returns the retrieved value.

@lcmake::GetState@k_ZNK5cmake8GetStateEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetState@k_ZNK5cmake8GetStateEv.body: Returns a pointer to the internal state by invoking the `State` member’s `get` method, preserving const‑ness.

@lcmake::GetTrace@k_ZNK5cmake8GetTraceEv.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::GetTrace@k_ZNK5cmake8GetTraceEv.body: It returns the value of the internal `Trace` flag, exposing the current trace status without affecting any state.

@lcmake::HasCheckInProgress@k_ZNK5cmake1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::HasCheckInProgress@k_ZNK5cmake1.body: Checks whether there are any pending messages in the collection and returns that boolean result.

@lcmake::IsACLikeSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IsACLikeSourceExtension@k_ZNK5c.body: The method returns whether the supplied extension string appears in the set of known source‑file extensions. It forwards the check to `CLikeSourceFileExtensions.Test(ext)`, which performs the lookup and returns a Boolean result.

@lcmake::IssueMessage@k_ZNK5cmake12Issue.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::IssueMessage@k_ZNK5cmake12Issue.body: The function simply forwards the provided message type, text, and backtrace to the Messenger instance’s own IssueMessage method.

@lcmake::ReportVersionJson@k_ZNK5cmake17.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::ReportVersionJson@k_ZNK5cmake17.body: Creates and returns a JSON object containing the build‑time version data: the string identifier, major/minor numbers, optional suffix, a boolean flag for a dirty build, and the patch level, all pulled from the CMake_* macros.

@lcmake::SetHomeDirectory@k_ZN5cmake16Se.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetHomeDirectory@k_ZN5cmake16Se.body: The routine registers the supplied path as the project’s source directory, records it in the snapshot definition if a valid snapshot is already in place, and finally informs the messenger about the top‑level source root—using the “Normal” project kind to trigger the messenger’s top‑source switch, otherwise clearing it.

@lcmake::SetHomeOutputDirectory@k_ZN5cma.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetHomeOutputDirectory@k_ZN5cma.body: It assigns the supplied directory string to the internal state’s binary‑directory field and, if the current snapshot is still valid, records the new value under the key “CMAKE_BINARY_DIR” in that snapshot.

@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::SetProperty@k_ZN5cmake11SetProp.body: The function forwards the given property name and value to an overload of SetProperty that expects a cmValue. It simply wraps the string value in a cmValue and delegates the call, providing a convenient entry point for callers that supply raw string arguments.

@lcmake::cmake@k_ZN5cmakeC1ENS_4RoleEN7c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::cmake@k_ZN5cmakeC1ENS_4RoleEN7c.body: The constructor establishes the CMake instance by configuring its working directory, initializing the internal state and messenger objects, and registering the default and extra generators. It attaches scripting or project commands as appropriate, and if required, loads environment presets. Finally, it populates the source‑and‑header‑extension maps and enables console output for build‑tool diagnostics.

@lcmake::~cmake@k_ZN5cmakeD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmake::~cmake@k_ZN5cmakeD1Ev.body: The `~cmake()` call destroys a `cmake` instance. It runs the class’s destructor, which is declared `default`. This function is implicitly invoked whenever an object of type `cmake` goes out of scope (or when `delete` is called on a heap‑allocated instance), and it releases whatever resources the class holds.

@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::Directory@k_ZN5cmsys.body: Creates a fresh `DirectoryInternals` object and stores the pointer in the `Directory` instance, so that internal data structure is ready for use.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetFile@k_ZNK5cmsys9.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetFile@k_ZNK5cmsys9.body: The function fetches the name of a file stored in the private `Internal` container. It takes an unsigned index, looks up the corresponding element in the internal vector, and returns a C‑style string pointing at that file’s name. Because the function is marked `const`, it guarantees that no mutable state is changed during the call. However, callers should ensure the supplied index is within bounds; otherwise the dereference of `Internal->Files[dindex]` would be undefined behavior.

@lcmsys::Directory::GetNumberOfFiles@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::GetNumberOfFiles@k_Z.body: The method casts the size of the internal file list to `unsigned long` and returns it, giving the number of files in the directory. It does not modify any state and merely forwards the stored count.

@lcmsys::Directory::Load@k_ZN5cmsys9Dire.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::Load@k_ZN5cmsys9Dire.body: The method clears the current directory state, attempts to open the directory named `name` using `opendir`. If opening fails it reports the `errno` in `errorMessage` and returns a failure status. On success it iterates through the directory entries with `readdir`, appending each entry name to the internal file list. If any read error occurs it again propagates that error. Finally it stores the directory path, closes the directory descriptor, and returns success.

@lcmsys::Directory::~Directory@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Directory::~Directory@k_ZN5cmsy.body:
The destructor releases the dynamically allocated `Internal` object.  

*If `Internal` was allocated elsewhere, ensure it was not already freed—otherwise `delete this->Internal` will crash.  
*If `Internal` is a raw pointer owned by `Directory`, make sure it is never null before deletion to avoid a crash.  
*Because `delete this` would be undefined behavior, this code **must** be called only when the object is already safely removed from any owning containers.

@lcmsys::FStream::ReadBOM@k_ZN5cmsys7FSt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::FStream::ReadBOM@k_ZN5cmsys7FSt.body: Probes the stream’s initial bytes to detect a UTF‑8, UTF‑16 (big‑endian or little‑endian) or UTF‑32 BOM; returns the matching enum value or a “none” flag, resetting the stream position when no marker is found.

@lcmsys::Glob::FindFiles@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::FindFiles@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.body: The function first clears its internal expression and file lists, then normalizes the supplied path: if the argument isn’t an absolute path it is prefixed with the current working directory. It scans the path string, looking for the first “/” that is not escaped, and keeps track of that position to later drop the initial prefix (e.g. drive letter or network‑share). It then splits the remaining path into components separated by “/”, building a string for each component and storing them via `AddExpression`. Finally it calls `ProcessDirectory` for each component—recursively exploring directories—before returning true.

@lcmsys::Glob::GetFiles@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob8.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::GetFiles@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob8.body: The function returns a reference to the internal vector that stores file names.

@lcmsys::Glob::Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobC1Ev@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobC1Ev@.body: Creates a new `GlobInternals` instance, sets the recursion and symlink‑handling flags to their defaults (`Recurse` = false, `RecurseThroughSymlinks` = true, `RecurseListDirs` = false), and initializes counters and path strings (`FollowedSymlinkCount` = 0, `Relative` = `""`). It also enables the default directory‑listing behavior (`ListDirs` = true).

@lcmsys::Glob::PatternToRegex@k_ZN5cmsys.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::PatternToRegex@k_ZN5cmsys.body: The function converts a glob‑style pattern into a regex string. It walks the pattern once, translating '*', '?' and bracket expressions into their regex counterparts while escaping non‑alphanumeric characters. Optionally it prefixes the pattern with `^` and suffixes `$` to force a full‑string match, and it supports case‑insensitive matching when requested. The routine handles edge cases such as unmatched brackets or empty bracket lists, and escapes backslashes inside bracket expressions.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOff@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOff@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.body: RecurseOff clears any recursion flags and disables further recursive processing in the running context.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOn@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseOn@k_ZN5cmsys4Glob.body: Recursively walks a data structure, invoking itself on each sub‑element until the terminating condition is satisfied.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOff.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOff.body: The function turns off recursive traversal of symbolic links, ensuring that any subsequent symlink‑resolution stops at the first link it encounters instead of following it blindly.

@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOn@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::RecurseThroughSymlinksOn@.body: RecurseThroughSymlinksOn walks a directory tree, following each symbolic link it encounters and recursing into the referenced target until it reaches a stopping condition, while guarding against cycles and marking visited nodes.

@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurse@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::SetRecurse@k_ZN5cmsys4Glo.body: SetRecurse receives a single Boolean argument that determines whether the system should perform recursive operations. Internally it flips a flag that downstream modules consult to enable or skip any recursive logic during processing.

@lcmsys::Glob::~Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobD1Ev.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Glob::~Glob@k_ZN5cmsys4GlobD1Ev.body: The destructor simply calls `delete` on the `Internals` member; you must ensure that this pointer is either `nullptr` or was allocated with `new` and that no other part of the program will keep a dangling reference to it after deletion. If `Internals` is `nullptr`, the call to `delete` is harmless, but if a later operation still touches that memory after the destructor runs, it will lead to undefined behavior. Also consider adopting smart pointers (e.g., `std::unique_ptr`) to avoid manual deletion and the risk of double‑deletion.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.body: The function accepts a C‑style string and returns a ready‑to‑use regex representation built from that pattern.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.body: The function takes a string that represents a regular‑expression pattern and produces a compiled regex object (or its equivalent representation) that can be applied to input strings for matching.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::RegularExpre.body: `RegularExpression()` is the entry point for creating a regular‑expression object that is subsequently consumed by other parts of the code. It typically returns a fully‑parsed regex instance (or a string representing it) that callers use to match or substitute text.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.body: The compile function validates the supplied pattern string, parses it into an internal byte‑code representation, allocates a program buffer to store the compiled instructions, and fills that buffer with the generated bytecode. It performs size checks to reject overly large patterns, initializes the internal state (including start‑anchor and literal‑match information), and returns `true` on success or `false` on failure.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::compile@k_ZN.body: The function returns `true` when the compilation succeeds and `false` otherwise.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::end@k_ZNK5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::end@k_ZNK5cm.body: Returns the index marking the end of the current token, used to slice substrings in parsing routines.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.body: The `find` function scans a null‑terminated C‑string up to a given length for a particular character and returns `true` if that character occurs within that range, otherwise `false`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZN5cm.body: The `find` function performs a substring search on a supplied string. It receives the target string, a search pattern, an index offset, and a maximum search length, and returns `true` when the pattern is located within those bounds, otherwise `false`.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZNK5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::find@k_ZNK5c.body: The `find` method runs a compiled regular‑expression program against a supplied C‑string starting at a given offset. It first clears any previous match data, verifies that the program is non‑null and not corrupted, and if a “must‑appear” substring is known, confirms that substring occurs somewhere after the offset. It then constructs a `RegExpFind` helper, sets its `regbol` and `regreject` pointers based on the options flag, and finally attempts to match. If the expression is anchored it performs a single anchored try; otherwise it scans ahead for the first character that matches the expression’s start character and invokes `regtry` on each potential position until a match is found or the string ends. If a match succeeds the method returns true and fills `rmatch` with the start and end pointers; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::match@k_ZNK5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::match@k_ZNK5.body: The `match` function processes the supplied integer argument and returns a string that represents a specific regex match result. It is called when populating `DoFile` parameters, supplying a string that identifies the file category (e.g., `Updated`, `Modified`, `Conflicting`, or a removal type) depending on the integer passed.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::start@k_ZNK5.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::start@k_ZNK5.body: The `start` function simply returns the index at which a particular element or pattern begins in a string. It is used throughout the code to obtain the starting position of a parsed token or flag before further processing.

@lcmsys::RegularExpression::~RegularExpr.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpression::~RegularExpr.body: The function `~RegularExpression()` constructs and returns a compiled representation of a regular‑expression pattern. Internally it parses a pattern string—checking that it adheres to the language’s syntax, flagging errors for malformed forms—then builds an internal automaton (often a deterministic finite‑state machine) that can efficiently test strings against the pattern. The public API is simply “call this function and receive a ready‑to‑use expression object that you can query for matches.”

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::Regular.body: The function performs the standard regex‑matching logic: it compiles the provided pattern into a parsing tree, walks the target string token‑by‑token, and reports whether the pattern matches (along with any captured groups).

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::match@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::match@k.body: The `match` function is a simple accessor that receives an integer index and returns the corresponding string value from an internal lookup table. It is invoked by various tool modules to pull out specific dependency strings (e.g., a library name or a path token) that is later split or appended to a list. The function does no complex processing beyond fetching the stored string for the supplied index.

@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::~Regula.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::RegularExpressionMatch::~Regula.body: Matches a given string against a regular‑expression pattern and returns a simple Boolean result (or a minimal match object). It is invoked in several parts of the codebase to validate user inputs or to gate‑keep further processing until a pattern succeeds; the implementation relies on the underlying regex engine to report whether the entire source string satisfies the supplied expression.

@lcmsys::Status::GetString@k_ZNK5cmsys6S.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::GetString@k_ZNK5cmsys6S.body: Retrieves the textual description corresponding to the stored error kind: a plain “Success” text for Kind::Success; the POSIX code uses strerror() for POSIX; and on Windows uses FormatMessageW() to fetch the system message, converts it to a narrow string and frees the buffer before returning it.

@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.body: It takes an rvalue reference of the same type and initializes the new instance by transferring the internal state of the argument, avoiding any deep copy of its members.

@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Statu.body: Status() retrieves and returns the current system status, typically as a struct or enum indicating whether operations are active, idle, or in error.

@lcmsys::Status::operator bool@k_ZNK5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::operator bool@k_ZNK5cms.body:
The `operator bool()` const member simply lets an instance of the class be used in Boolean contexts.  
It evaluates the object’s internal state and returns `true` or `false` accordingly, enabling statements such as `if (obj) { … }` or logical expressions that rely on the object’s truth value.  
This conversion operator is invoked implicitly wherever the code tests conditions—e.g., evaluating the status of a file, a directory, or a custom flag—by casting the object to a `bool`.

@lcmsys::Status::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys6St.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::operator=@k_ZN5cmsys6St.body:
It overloads the move‑assignment operator for `Status`.  
When invoked, it transfers the internal state of the temporary `Status` instance into the current object, leaving the source in a valid (typically empty) state, and finally returns a reference to the updated object.

@lcmsys::Status::~Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Stat.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::Status::~Status@k_ZN5cmsys6Stat.body: The `~Status` function is a public entry point that simply returns a status value (often an enum or error code) indicating the result of an operation. It’s typically invoked from other parts of the code to query or report the current state without side‑effects.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.body: The function forwards the supplied path string to an internal helper (`CollapseFullPathImpl`), passing `nullptr` for its optional parameter. It returns whatever that helper produces.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath@k.body: This function simply forwards the arguments to `CollapseFullPathImpl`, delegating the actual path‑normalising logic to that helper implementation.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToUnixSlash.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ConvertToUnixSlash.body: Converts a file‑path string to a canonical Unix form: it normalises slashes, preserves a leading “//” when present, expands a leading `~` to the user’s home directory (or another user’s if the tilde is followed by a user name), and trims an extraneous trailing slash except when the path is the root or a Windows‑style drive root. It performs these changes in‑place on the supplied string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileAlways@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::CopyFileAlways@k_Z.body: The function CopyFileAlways copies a file or directory from a source path to a destination path. It first creates any missing destination directory, then copies the file contents—preferring a fast clone operation and falling back to a blockwise copy if cloning fails. After copying it updates the destination’s permissions to match the source and returns a status object that reports whether the operation succeeded or, if not, the reason for failure.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Delay@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Delay@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: The function implements a millisecond‑level pause by delegating to OS primitives. On Windows it simply calls Sleep( msec ) – which has a 1‑ms resolution. On other systems it falls back to the standard C library functions: the routine splits large waits into whole‑second chunks using sleep() and finer‑microsecond waits via usleep(). If msec is ≥ 1000 it first sleeps for the whole seconds and then sleeps for the remaining microseconds; otherwise it sleeps only for the requested time. The implementation ensures the call returns after the requested delay, but it relies on the operating system’s timing granularity and may lose precision for very small values (e.g. sub‑millisecond ranges).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.body: The FileExists function checks whether a given path refers to an existing file on the current system. On Windows it first queries the file’s attributes; if the file is a reparse point it attempts to open the target as a backup‑semantics file and, if that fails, reads the reparse point data to confirm that the target is an executable alias. On non‑Windows systems it simply tests the file’s accessibility with the appropriate system call.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileExists@k_ZN5cm.body: The method checks whether a path refers to an existing file and, if the caller wants to exclude directories, it rejects them by returning false for any directory. The logic is implemented via a recursive call to FileExists followed by a test against FileIsDirectory to decide the final return value.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsDirectory@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsDirectory@k_.body: `FileIsDirectory` normalizes the supplied path (removing trailing slashes) and then, depending on the platform, checks the file attributes: on Windows it queries `GetFileAttributesW` on other systems it calls `stat`. It returns `true` only if the path refers to a directory; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.body: The function simply forwards the input string to the internal static helper, supplying a flag that indicates whether the string starts with one or two path‑separator characters (it returns 0 if empty, 1 if it starts with a single separator, 2 otherwise).

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsFullPath@k_Z.body: This function forwards the provided string’s C‑string pointer and length to a helper that validates whether the string represents a full path, returning that Boolean result.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsSymlink@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FileIsSymlink@k_ZN.body: It normalises the supplied path string to the platform‑specific format and then checks the file’s attributes: on Windows it queries the Win32 API (`GetFileAttributesW`) via a helper, while on POSIX it calls `lstat` and tests the `S_ISLNK` bit in `st_mode`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FilesDiffer@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FilesDiffer@k_ZN5c.body: The routine first obtains file attributes (or stat structs) to quickly reject mismatches when file sizes differ or an I/O error occurs. It then opens each file in binary mode and sequentially reads fixed‑size buffers, comparing the data blocks with a single memcmp per chunk; a single mismatch immediately signals difference. If the entire streams match byte‑by‑byte, the function returns false, indicating no change.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.body: The wrapper checks for a null or empty name and forwards the request to the more general overload, returning an empty string when the input is invalid.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::FindProgram@k_ZN5c.body: The function searches for an executable file named *name*. First it checks whether the file already has a recognized extension; on Windows it tries adding `.com` and `.exe` before calling `FileIsExecutable`. If that fails, it expands the search to each directory supplied in *userPaths* (and optionally the system PATH). It normalizes each directory by ensuring a trailing slash and stripping stray quotes on Windows, then concatenates the program name and attempts to open it. When an executable is found, it returns the fully‑resolved path; if none are found, it returns an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Fopen@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Fopen@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: The `Fopen` routine opens a file for use in a cross‑platform utility. On Windows it converts the requested path and mode string to wide‑character forms, strips any trailing “e” characters that Windows treats as illegal in extended‑path strings, then forwards the wide strings to the native `_wfopen`. On other systems it simply forwards the plain `fopen` call. The code is intended to provide a single entry point that abstracts the path‑encoding and mode‑normalization differences between Unix‑style paths and Windows’ extended‑path API.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetActualCaseForPa.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetActualCaseForPa.body: The function resolves a path’s real‑case name. On Windows it delegates to `SystemToolsStatic::GetCasePathName`; otherwise it returns the input unchanged.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: GetEnv retrieves the value of an environment variable named by `key`. It returns `true` if the variable is found and copies its value into `result`; otherwise it returns `false`. On Windows it performs a UTF‑16 conversion of the key, calls `GetEnvironmentVariableW`, and converts the wide‑character string back to a narrow string for the output. On other platforms it simply uses the standard `getenv` call.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameExtensi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameExtensi.body: The function returns the part of a filename after the last period. It locates the final ‘.’, erases everything preceding it, and returns the remaining string; if no period is found, it returns an empty string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameLastExt.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameLastExt.body: The routine extracts the suffix that follows the final period in a filename. It first isolates the filename component (without path) via `GetFilenameName`, then searches for the last dot. If a dot exists, the substring following it is returned; otherwise an empty string signals that no extension is present.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameName@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameName@k_.body: The function scans the input path for the last directory separator ("/" or "\\" on Windows) and returns the substring after that separator; if no separator is found it simply returns the original string. It contains a few bugs: the separator variable is incorrectly typed, the separator string literal isn’t escape correctly, and the code calls a non‑existent `find_last_of` method instead of `find_last_of`/`rfind`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenamePath@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenamePath@k_.body: The routine trims a file name to its directory part: after normalising slashes it locates the last separator, then returns the string up to that point. If the separator is at the very beginning it returns “/”, and if the path starts with a drive letter it keeps the “C:/” prefix. When no separator is found the result is an empty string. The algorithm simply shrinks the string to the position just before the final separator.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.body: The function strips the file extension by first locating the initial dot in the name returned from `GetFilenameName`. If a dot exists, it truncates the string at that position, effectively returning the filename without its extension.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetFilenameWithout.body: The function removes the portion of the file name that follows the last period in the file name part of a path. It first isolates the file name via `GetFilenameName`, then locates the final dot with `rfind('.')` and truncates the string to that position using `resize`. If no dot is found, it returns the original file name unchanged.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetLineFromStream@.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetLineFromStream@.body:
The routine clears the output string, checks whether the supplied stream is in a good state, then reads one line with `std::getline`.  
If the line ends with a carriage‑return character it removes that trailing `'\r'`.  
If a size limit is supplied it truncates the result to that length.  
Finally it sets the provided boolean flag to indicate whether the read ended at the stream’s end‑of‑file, and returns whether any data was actually obtained.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetParentDirectory.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetParentDirectory.body: The method forwards the given path to `SystemTools::GetFilenamePath`, returning that result.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPermissions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::GetPermissions@k_Z.body: The function first checks whether the supplied file path is non‑null; if the pointer is null it returns a POSIX‑style error status. Otherwise it forwards the call to the string‑based overload of `GetPermissions`, which performs the actual permission lookup.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::IsSubDirectory@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::IsSubDirectory@k_Z.body: The function normalises both path strings to Unix‑style slashes, checks that the first string is longer than the second, then verifies that the second string occurs as a prefix of the first followed by a slash at the expected position, and finally compares the two normalised strings for equality.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::LowerCase@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::LowerCase@k_ZN5cms.body: The function creates a new string of the same length as the input, iterates over each character, casts the result of `tolower` into the string’s value type, assigns it to the new string, and finally returns that string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeCidentifier@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeCidentifier@k_.body: The function normalizes a supplied string into a legal C identifier. It prefixes an underscore when the first character is a digit, then walks through the string, replacing any character that is not a letter, digit, or underscore with an underscore, and finally returns the cleaned string.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeDirectory@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::MakeDirectory@k_ZN.body: The function validates the supplied path string, ensures that the target path is not already an existing file, and then iteratively constructs each missing component of the path using a native `mkdir` call. It returns a status value indicating success or the specific POSIX error that occurred.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::PutEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::PutEnv@k_ZN5cmsys1.body: The function parses a string in the form “NAME=value”, splits it around the ‘=’, and uses the resulting parts to call the system setenv API. If the split succeeds it returns true when that call succeeds; otherwise it delegates to kwsysUnPutEnv and returns its Boolean result.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveADirectory@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveADirectory@k.body: The routine first ensures the target directory has read‑write rights (setting the appropriate flags for the platform in question), loads its contents via the helper `Directory` class, then iterates over every entry except “.” and “..”. For each entry it builds the full path, checks whether it is a sub‑directory (excluding symlinks), recursing into `RemoveADirectory` if true, otherwise it deletes the file via `RemoveFile`. When all contents are cleared it calls `rmdir` on the directory itself, and propagates any failure via a `Status` return. If any step fails (`Load`, recursive delete, or final `rmdir` call), the function returns the error status immediately.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveFile@k_ZN5cm.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::RemoveFile@k_ZN5cm.body: RemoveFile tries to delete a file specified by its path. On Windows it converts the path to an extended‑path string, attempts to delete the file, and if the file is read‑only it temporarily changes the file’s permissions to allow write access. It then checks if the file is actually a directory or a reparse point and tries to remove it as such. On success it returns a success status; otherwise it returns the Windows error code that was encountered. On POSIX it simply calls unlink and returns success or the system error.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceString@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::ReplaceString@k_ZN.body: It replaces every occurrence of the given substring in the source string with another substring, skipping the operation when the substring to replace is empty. The heavy lifting is delegated to a static helper that performs the actual string substitution.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SameFile@k_ZN5cmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SameFile@k_ZN5cmsy.body:
The function takes two file paths and returns `true` only if the two paths refer to the same underlying file.  
On Windows it opens each file, reads the `BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION` records, and compares the volume‑serial number and the high/low parts of the file index.  
On non‑Windows builds it calls `stat()` on each path and compares the device number, inode, and file size. If all those values match, the function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SetPermissions@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SetPermissions@k_Z.body: This public static helper verifies the input pointer isn’t null; if it is, it returns a POSIX error status. Otherwise, it delegates the call to the overload that accepts a `std::string`, returning whatever status that overload produces.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::Split@k_ZN5cmsys11.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::Split@k_ZN5cmsys11.body: The routine walks through the input string, pulls out segments ending at newline characters (removing an adjacent carriage‑return if present), pushes each fragment into the supplied vector, and returns true only if the string ends in a newline; otherwise it returns false.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitString@k_ZN5c.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::SplitString@k_ZN5c.body: The `SplitString` routine splits a given string by a specified separator character, optionally treating a leading slash as a separate element when the `isPath` flag is true. It returns a `std::vector<std::string>` containing each piece between separator occurrences, preserving the original order.

@lcmsys::SystemTools::UpperCase@k_ZN5cms.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsys::SystemTools::UpperCase@k_ZN5cms.body: The function takes a string reference, creates a new string of identical length, copies each character after converting it to its uppercase form with `toupper`, and finally returns that new string.

@lcmsysEncoding_DupToNarrow@kcmsysEncodi.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysEncoding_DupToNarrow@kcmsysEncodi.body: Converts a wide‑character string to a null‑terminated narrow string, allocating a buffer sized by the wcstombs length and returning the pointer (or NULL on allocation failure).

@lcmsysEncoding_DupToWide@kcmsysEncoding.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysEncoding_DupToWide@kcmsysEncoding.body: The routine allocates a buffer sized to the wide‑char length of *str*, zero‑initialises it, copies the string into that buffer with `kwsysEncoding_mbstowcs`, and returns the newly‑allocated wide string (or `NULL` on allocation failure).

@lcmsysEncoding_mbstowcs@kcmsysEncoding_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysEncoding_mbstowcs@kcmsysEncoding_.body: This function converts a multibyte string into a wide‑character string. It checks for a NULL input and returns `(size_t)-1` if the source string is null. On Windows it calls `MultiByteToWideChar` with the default code‑page; on other platforms it calls `mbstowcs`. The return value is the number of characters that were written into the destination buffer.

@lcmsysEncoding_wcstombs@kcmsysEncoding_.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysEncoding_wcstombs@kcmsysEncoding_.body: The routine converts a wide‑character string to a multibyte string, returning the number of bytes written or a failure code. It checks for a null source, then on Windows it calls `WideCharToMultiByte` with the default code page; otherwise it simply forwards to `wcstombs`. The caller must ensure the destination buffer is large enough to hold the resulting bytes.

@lcmsysProcess_KillPID@kcmsysProcess_Kil.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysProcess_KillPID@kcmsysProcess_Kil.body: The function simply casts the supplied `process_id` to a `pid_t` and forwards it to `kwsysProcessKill`, delegating the termination request to the underlying system call.

@lcmsysString_strcasecmp@kcmsysString_st.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysString_strcasecmp@kcmsysString_st.body: The routine performs a case‑insensitive string comparison that returns 0 when the two arguments match, a negative value if the first differs earlier, or a positive value otherwise. It first checks whether the build‑time macro defines an available native routine (_stricmp or strcasecmp); if neither is available it falls back to a hand‑rolled routine that normalises each byte via a static lower‑case table and walks the strings byte‑by‑byte until a non‑equal pair is found or a null byte is reached.

@lcmsysSystem_Parse_CommandForUnix@kcmsy.author: AI Short Overview
@lcmsysSystem_Parse_CommandForUnix@kcmsy.body: The routine is a thin wrapper that verifies that the supplied flag mask is zero; otherwise it aborts by returning NULL. When the flag check passes it simply delegates to the internal parser implementation (`kwsysSystem__ParseUnixCommand`) and forwards whatever `char**` array that routine produces. This design keeps the public API concise while entrusting detailed parsing logic to a dedicated helper.

@lcountMaxConsecutiveEqualSigns::[lambda.author: AI Short Overview
@lcountMaxConsecutiveEqualSigns::[lambda.body: The operator() member simply takes a single character argument and returns a `bool`. In practice it’s used as a small, read‑only helper (likely an overload of some operator) that reports a true/false condition based on the supplied character.

@lcountMaxConsecutiveEqualSigns::[lambda.author: AI Short Overview
@lcountMaxConsecutiveEqualSigns::[lambda.body: The lambda simply checks whether a character equals `'='`. In the call, `find_if_not` will scan the string from `startIt + 1` until it finds that character, and return an iterator pointing at it. This allows the surrounding code to locate the first `'='` after a given position.

@lcountMaxConsecutiveEqualSigns@k_ZN12_G.author: AI Short Overview
@lcountMaxConsecutiveEqualSigns@k_ZN12_G.body: The routine scans the string for stretches of ‘=’ characters, keeps a running maximum of the lengths seen, and returns that maximum when the scan completes.

@lctrl@k_Z4ctrli@f./Source/CursesDialog/.author: AI Short Overview
@lctrl@k_Z4ctrli@f./Source/CursesDialog/.body: The function performs a bitwise AND operation between the input integer and the octal literal 037 (decimal 31), returning the result.

@lcurrent_field@kcurrent_field@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@lcurrent_field@kcurrent_field@f./Source.body: This function normalizes a `FORM` instance and then returns the field that is marked as the current one in that normalized form.

@lcurses_move@k_Z11curses_movejj@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lcurses_move@k_Z11curses_movejj@f./Sour.body: Moves the cursor to the specified column and row by invoking the underlying `move()` routine with the supplied coordinates.

@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::BasicTypeInfo@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::BasicTypeInfo@k_ZN.body: Receives a string by rvalue reference and extracts the core type metadata, returning the resulting type info object.

@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::deserialize@k_ZNK3.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::deserialize@k_ZNK3.body: The `deserialize` method reads serialized data through the supplied `Deserializer` into the object’s fields and returns `true` when all required data is correctly populated; otherwise it returns `false`.

@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::serialize@k_ZNK3da.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::serialize@k_ZNK3da.body:
The function is a member of a class that provides a binary‑serialization interface.  
When called, it receives a pointer to a `Serializer` helper and a pointer to the data object to be serialized.  
It returns a `bool` that indicates whether the serialization succeeded.  
Because the function is marked `const`, it promises not to modify the owning object’s internal state, though the helper may still write to external buffers.  
Typical implementations will:

* Query the `Serializer` to identify the target stream or buffer  
* Marshal the object’s fields in a predefined layout (often in little‑endian order)  
* Handle any failures (e.g. stream errors, insufficient memory) by returning `false` and ensuring resources are left in a safe state

Key pitfalls to watch for are:

1. **Null‑pointer handling** – the function should immediately return `false` if either argument is null.  
2. **Memory ownership** – if the helper owns the buffer, the caller must not free it until after serialization completes.  
3. **Exception safety** – be sure no uncaught exceptions leave the object in an inconsistent state; guard with `try‑catch` or use RAII.  
4. **Thread‑safety** – if the serializer uses shared resources, it should synchronize access or document that the function is not thread‑safe.

These points give a quick snapshot of what the function’s contract and typical responsibilities look like.

@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::~BasicTypeInfo@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::~BasicTypeInfo@k_Z.body: The function supplies a lightweight descriptor of a type—typically its name, size, alignment and any flags needed for downstream reflection or serialization tasks. This information is then consumed by other parts of the system that require type metadata at runtime.

@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::~BasicTypeInfo@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::~BasicTypeInfo@k_Z.body: Releases any resources tied to a BasicTypeInfo instance, ensuring proper cleanup when the object is destroyed.

@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::~BasicTypeInfo@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::BasicTypeInfo::~BasicTypeInfo@k_Z.body: ~BasicTypeInfo() acts as a virtual destructor for the base type‑info class, automatically releasing any resources tied to a derived instance and ensuring proper cleanup when an object of that type hierarchy is destroyed.

@ldap::CMakeInitializeRequest::CMakeInit.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::CMakeInitializeRequest::CMakeInit.body: `CMakeInitializeRequest` constructs a new request object by moving the supplied instance. The function accepts an rvalue reference to a `CMakeInitializeRequest` object, effectively transferring ownership of its internal state without copying. This is used when creating a new request during the CMake protocol initialization phase, ensuring that the request’s resources are transferred efficiently and safely.

@ldap::CMakeInitializeRequest::CMakeInit.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::CMakeInitializeRequest::CMakeInit.body: CMakeInitializeRequest constructs a request object by copying fields from an existing request instance, registering it with the protocol handler, and setting up any internal state required for processing the new request.

@ldap::CMakeInitializeRequest::CMakeInit.author: AI Short Overview
