It produces a compact binary (or JSON‑style) representation that can be persisted or transmitted, and returns a status code indicating success or failure.

@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::serialize@k_ZZN.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::serialize@k_ZZN.body: The `serialize` method turns the internal state of the object into a serialised representation (e.g., JSON, XML, or a binary blob). It returns a string or writes to an output stream, enabling the object to be persisted or transmitted.

@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::~TI@k_ZZN3dap6T.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::~TI@k_ZZN3dap6T.body: ~TI is a public virtual method that is expected to be overridden by derived classes. It usually returns an identifier or metadata (for example a type name or field list) that is then used by the debugger protocol to report information about objects at runtime. The method is lightweight, no side‑effects, and is called via the debugging infrastructure whenever type information must be retrieved.

@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::~TI@k_ZZN3dap6T.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::~TI@k_ZZN3dap6T.body: ~TI is a helper that, when called, emits a type‑information block for a particular type. It collects metadata such as the type’s name, size, alignment, and the list of its fields, then packages that into a static structure that the debugger framework can query at runtime to introspect the type. In practice the macro is used in the project to register a type once, after which the debugger can enumerate its members or inspect individual field values while stepping through a program.

@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::~TI@k_ZZN3dap6T.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type::TI::~TI@k_ZZN3dap6T.body: ~TI() is a public virtual function that is invoked in several places across the codebase, typically executing a targeted operation or cleanup logic whenever required.

@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_1.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_1.body: The `type()` function builds and returns a `TypeInfo` object that describes the `CMakeVersion` structure. It registers the single field `major` (an integer) with its name and descriptor so that the type system can introspect the struct, serialize it, or validate data against the expected layout.

@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_2.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_2.body: The macro expands to a static function named `type` that returns a pointer to a static `TypeInfo` instance describing the struct’s fields and metadata, enabling the DAP runtime to query type information at compile‑time.

@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_2.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_2.body: The static function `type` (invoked via the macro `DAP_IMPLEMENT_STRUCT_TYPEINFO`) supplies run‑time type metadata for a given struct type. When called, it returns a populated `DAP_TYPEINFO` instance that contains the struct’s name, size, and member descriptors—enabling reflection‑style introspection inside the system.

@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_7.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_7.body: The `type()` function delivers the `TypeInfo` descriptor for the `CMakeVersion` structure. It’s employed by the `DAP_IMPLEMENT_STRUCT_TYPEINFO` macro to register the struct’s fields (`major`, `minor`, `patch`) and to expose that information to callers that need to introspect or serialize the type at runtime.

@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_8.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINS_8.body: The function returns a pointer to the static `TypeInfo` object that represents the type’s metadata for the protocol fields. It is used by the protocol code (e.g., the DAP_FIELD macro calls in `cmDebuggerProtocol.cxx`) to obtain the description of fields such as `additionalModuleColumns`, `completionTriggerCharacters`, `exceptionBreakpointFilters`, `supportSuspendDebuggee`, and `supportTerminateDebuggee`.

@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINSt7.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::TypeOf::type@k_ZN3dap6TypeOfINSt7.body: The function returns a static `TypeInfo` instance that represents the type of a specific protocol field, allowing callers to retrieve its metadata at runtime.

@ldap::detail::member_type@k_ZN3dap6deta.author: AI Short Overview
@ldap::detail::member_type@k_ZN3dap6deta.body: The template takes a pointer‑to‑member and yields a type alias for that member’s type, allowing compile‑time deduction of the field type without specifying it explicitly.

@ldifftime@kdifftime.author: AI Short Overview
@ldifftime@kdifftime.body:
The function `difftime` computes the elapsed time in seconds between two timestamps of type `time_t`, returning the difference as a `double`. It is typically invoked as in the snippet:  

```cpp
static_cast<int64_t>(std::difftime(timeT, unixEpoch));
```

@lexit@kexit.author: AI Short Overview
@lexit@kexit.body: The `exit` function terminates the current process. It immediately returns control to the operating system, flushing standard output streams and invoking any registered `atexit` handlers before finally terminating the process. It propagates an exit status code that may be inspected by the shell or other programs that launched it.

@lfclose@kfclose.author: AI Short Overview
@lfclose@kfclose.body: Closes a `FILE*` and returns the value produced by `fclose`, which is the status of the close operation.

@lfcntl@kfcntl.author: AI Short Overview
@lfcntl@kfcntl.body:
`fcntl` is a thin C++ wrapper that forwards the request to the underlying POSIX `::fcntl` system call.  
When invoked with `F_GETFL` it returns the current flag bit mask on the file descriptor.  
When invoked with `F_SETFL` it applies a new mask supplied as an argument, typically composed by OR‑ing desired flags such as `O_NONBLOCK` before passing them in.  
The function simply forwards the command and flag mask to `::fcntl` and returns whatever that call returns.

@lferror@kferror.author: AI Short Overview
@lferror@kferror.body: Checks whether the FILE stream has an error flag set, returning a non‑zero value if an error is present and zero otherwise.

@lfield_back@kfield_back@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_back@kfield_back@f./Source/Curse.body: `GEN_FIELD_ATTR_GET_FCT( back )` expands into a small inline function that retrieves the `back` field from a given structure. It essentially provides a type‑safe getter that accepts a pointer to the containing object and returns the value of its `back` member, usually as a simple dereference with a const‑qualified return type.

@lfield_buffer@kfield_buffer@f./Source/C.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_buffer@kfield_buffer@f./Source/C.body: The function returns a pointer to the *nth* buffer of a `FIELD` object when the supplied index lies inside the object’s bounds; otherwise it yields a null pointer (cast to `char*`). If the `FIELD` pointer is NULL or the index falls outside `[0,field->nbuf]`, the routine returns `nullptr`.

@lfield_fore@kfield_fore@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_fore@kfield_fore@f./Source/Curse.body: The `field_fore` function is a lightweight accessor that pulls a specific attribute from a predefined field definition. When invoked, it pulls the requested attribute value (e.g. a flag or string) based on the field's metadata and returns it in a convenient, type‑safe form for the caller to consume.

@lfield_index@kfield_index@f./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_index@kfield_index@f./Source/Cur.body: The function returns the field’s `index` when the `FIELD` pointer and its `form` member are non‑null; otherwise it returns `-1`.

@lfield_opts_off@kfield_opts_off@f./Sour.author: AI Short Overview
@lfield_opts_off@kfield_opts_off@f./Sour.body: This routine turns off specified options for a field. It first validates the mask against the set of legal flags; if the mask is clean, it normalises the field structure and clears those bits from the field’s current option set before finally invoking the internal synchronisation helper. If the mask includes an illegal flag, the routine exits with `E_BAD_ARGUMENT`.

@lfileno@kfileno.author: AI Short Overview
@lfileno@kfileno.body: The `fileno` function converts a `FILE*` into the underlying file‑descriptor integer that `isatty` (and the callers that check whether a stream is interactive) use. If the pointer is `NULL`, it simply returns `0`. This single‑int return value is then used by callers to decide whether a stream is a terminal.

@lform_driver@kform_driver@f./Source/Cur.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_driver@kform_driver@f./Source/Cur.body: The routine checks the supplied form for validity, looks up the command in a static dispatch table, and invokes the corresponding handler (or falls back to a generic entry routine) before returning the operation’s status.

@lform_request_by_name@kform_request_by_.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_request_by_name@kform_request_by_.body: The routine normalises an input string to upper‑case, then scans a small static array of request names. When it finds a match it returns the corresponding command code (MIN_FORM_COMMAND + index); if no name matches it returns E_NO_MATCH.

@lform_request_name@kform_request_name@f.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_request_name@kform_request_name@f.body: The `form_request_name` routine validates that the supplied command code lies within the defined `MIN_FORM_COMMAND`–`MAX_FORM_COMMAND` range. If the value is outside that interval it sets a bad‑argument error and returns a null pointer; otherwise it returns the corresponding string from the `request_names` lookup table by indexing with `request‑MIN_FORM_COMMAND`.

@lform_win@kform_win@f./Source/CursesDia.author: AI Short Overview
@lform_win@kform_win@f./Source/CursesDia.body: It normalizes the supplied form and returns its `win` member if it exists; otherwise it falls back to the standard screen pointer.

@lfprintf@kfprintf.author: AI Short Overview
@lfprintf@kfprintf.body: Writes formatted data to the stream pointed to by the `FILE` pointer and returns the number of bytes written (or a negative value on error).

@lfread@kfread.author: AI Short Overview
@lfread@kfread.body: `fread` is a thin wrapper around the standard C library’s `fread` routine. It reads a specified number of objects—each of a given size—from a file stream into a caller‑provided buffer. The function returns the count of elements actually read; a return of zero indicates either end‑of‑file or an error. In the shown code snippets the routine is employed in various streaming contexts: bulk buffers are filled in a single call, and the looped reads (e.g., in `cmGeneratedFileStream.cxx`) keep reading until a zero‑return signals EOF. The routine is typically safe against buffer overruns because the count of bytes read cannot exceed the supplied buffer length, but callers must still guard against `NULL` pointers or mismatched sizes.

@lfree@kfree.author: AI Short Overview
@lfree@kfree.body: free releases a heap‑allocated block back to the allocator. It verifies the pointer isn’t be NULL, locates the control block for that allocation, clears any metadata, and finally merges the freed chunk into the free‑list (possibly coalescing with neighboring blocks). After the operation, the space is available for future allocations. This routine is typically the core of the runtime memory‑deallocation path and must guard against double‑free or dangling‑pointer misuse.

@lgetExpectedOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetExpectedOptions@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: The function builds an `ExpectedOptions` container by inserting the four predefined option names (`kTreeOptionName`, `kPrefixOptionName`, `kFilesOptionName`, `kRegexOptionName`) via `push_back` and returns the populated object.

@lgetNumWidth@k_Z11getNumWidthm@f./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetNumWidth@k_Z11getNumWidthm@f./Sourc.body: The function returns how many decimal digits an integer has by repeatedly dividing the value by 10 and counting the divisions. It starts at 1 for zero and increments a counter once per digit until the value drops below 10.

@lgetSourceGroupFilesPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetSourceGroupFilesPaths@k_ZN12_GLOBAL.body: Takes a root directory and a collection of file paths, strips the root part followed by a slash from each path, and returns the remaining fragments as a set of unique relative paths.

@lgetc@kgetc.author: AI Short Overview
@lgetc@kgetc.body: `getc` reads a character from the supplied stream, returning its integer value or `EOF` on end‑of‑file. It performs a basic bounds check on the file pointer and propagates I/O errors via a negative return code. The routine is invoked by the lexer’s `YY_INPUT` macro in both `cmGccDepfileLexer.cxx` and `cmCTestResourceGroupsLexer.cxx`, feeding the lexer with the next byte from the internal buffer.

@lgmtime@kgmtime.author: AI Short Overview
@lgmtime@kgmtime.body: `gmtime` is a small wrapper that takes a `const time_t *` (essentially a `time_t` value) and returns a pointer to a `struct tm` that contains the broken‑down representation of that time in UTC. It behaves like the standard library `gmtime` routine, returning a pointer to a statically‑allocated `struct tm` filled with year, month, day, hour, minute, second, and timezone fields.

@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::Argumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::Argumen.body: The `Arguments` function constructs a new `Arguments` object by taking ownership of an existing instance through an rvalue reference (`Arguments&&`). It effectively transfers the parsed argument data into the new instance without copying, enabling efficient construction and movement of argument states across different parts of the API.

@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::Argumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::Argumen.body: The constructor copies the parse‑result fields from an existing `Arguments` instance so that a freshly constructed object contains the same argument values that were produced by a prior parse. It is invoked when a previously parsed command’s data is re‑used in a new context (e.g., in `cmFileAPICommand.cxx` at line 74).

@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::Argumen.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::Argumen.body: Creates an `Arguments` instance that holds the parsed command‑line options and parameters.

@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::~Argume.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand::Arguments::~Argume.body: The ~Arguments function is a public entry point that gathers, validates, and returns the parsed argument set for downstream components to consume.

@lhandleQueryCommand::[lambda_0]::operat.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand::[lambda_0]::operat.body: The function takes a `const std::string &` argument, performs a quick check/operation on that string, and returns a `bool` indicating success or failure.

@lhandleQueryCommand::[lambda_0]@khandle.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand::[lambda_0]@khandle.body: The lambda is a stateless predicate that takes a constant string reference and yields a boolean, suitable for use in standard‑library algorithms that expect a unary predicate.

@lhandleQueryCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.author: AI Short Overview
@lhandleQueryCommand@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_11.body: Parses the supplied arguments, verifies that an API version is present and supported (only 1), and checks that the supplied CODEMODEL, CACHE, CMAKEFILES, and TOOLCHAINS lists are valid. It collects any parsing errors, reports them, and returns true only if all arguments are valid.

@lhash_value@k_Z10hash_valueRK11cmCMakeP.author: AI Short Overview
@lhash_value@k_Z10hash_valueRK11cmCMakeP.body: The function simply forwards the `path.Path` string to `cm::filesystem::hash_value` and returns the resulting `std::size_t` hash value. It is marked `noexcept` so no exceptions are thrown during its execution.

@lisCharDigit@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111isChar.author: AI Short Overview
@lisCharDigit@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_111isChar.body: The function casts the input character to an unsigned `char` to avoid signedness issues, then forwards it to `std::isdigit`, which checks whether the value corresponds to a decimal digit. The returned boolean indicates whether the character is a digit.

@lisExpectedOption@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116i.author: AI Short Overview
@lisExpectedOption@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_116i.body: Checks whether a string appears in a list of expected options by delegating the containment test to the `cm::contains` helper, returning that result directly.

@lisatty@kisatty.author: AI Short Overview
@lisatty@kisatty.body: The `isatty` function checks whether the supplied file descriptor refers to an interactive terminal. In practice it typically calls the system `isatty( fd )` API (or equivalent) and returns a non‑zero value when the descriptor is connected to a terminal device, zero otherwise. It is used in the lexer code to determine if the input file is interactive (`yy_is_interactive` is set accordingly).

@lisdigit@kisdigit.author: AI Short Overview
@lisdigit@kisdigit.body: The function casts its integer argument to an unsigned char and forwards it to `std::isdigit`, returning a non‑zero value only for characters in the `'0'`–`'9'` range. It’s employed throughout the codebase wherever a simple numeric‑character validation is required.

@ljoinCommandLine@k_ZL15joinCommandLineR.author: AI Short Overview
@ljoinCommandLine@k_ZL15joinCommandLineR.body: The function builds a single space‑delimited string from a list of words. It scans each argument; if an argument contains a space it is surrounded by double quotes in the output, otherwise appended as‑is. After all items have been added, the trailing space is stripped off before returning the result.

@lkwsysSystem__AppendArgument@p@l./Sourc.author: AI Short Overview
@lkwsysSystem__AppendArgument@p@l./Sourc.body: The routine appends a null‑terminated string to a dynamic array of argument pointers. It reallocates the list when its current capacity is exceeded, copies the new argument into newly allocated memory, and updates the pointers accordingly. On success it returns 1; on failure it returns 0.

@lkwsysSystem__AppendByte@p@l./Source/kw.author: AI Short Overview
@lkwsysSystem__AppendByte@p@l./Source/kw.body: The routine appends a single byte to a buffer that is grown on demand. It checks the current capacity; if the buffer is full it allocates a new array double the previous size, copies the old data, frees the old block, and adjusts the beginning/end pointers. On success it writes the byte at the end marker and returns 1, otherwise it returns 0 to signal allocation failure.

@lkwsysSystem__ParseUnixCommand@p@l./Sou.author: AI Short Overview
@lkwsysSystem__ParseUnixCommand@p@l./Sou.body: The routine tokenizes a shell‑style command string into an array of argument strings. It walks the source character by character, tracks quoting and escaping state, builds each argument in a temporary buffer, and places finished arguments into a pointer array. When parsing succeeds it allocates an array of pointers, copies the parsed arguments, terminates the list with a null, frees the temporary buffers, and returns the new array. If any allocation or append fails, it cleans up and returns NULL.

@llocaltime@klocaltime.author: AI Short Overview
@llocaltime@klocaltime.body: `localtime` converts an opaque `time_t` value into a plain‑C `struct tm *` representing the local calendar time for that instant, returning a static buffer that callers may copy out of. It accepts a pointer to a `time_t`, looks up the appropriate epoch, and dispatches the result into a static `struct tm` that is reused on each call. This form keeps the routine re‑entrant and inexpensive—no dynamic allocation and no global state that must be reset. The callers typically copy the returned pointer into a local variable before any further formatting or manipulation, as shown in the calling snippets.

@lmalloc@kmalloc.author: AI Short Overview
@lmalloc@kmalloc.body: `malloc` reserves a contiguous block of the requested size from the process heap and returns a pointer to it (or `NULL` on failure). In the given snippets it’s employed to back arrays of `wchar_t`, `char`, and a dynamic stack structure (`YYSTACk_ALLOC`).

@lmbstowcs@kmbstowcs.author: AI Short Overview
@lmbstowcs@kmbstowcs.body: `mbstowcs` takes a destination buffer of wide characters, a source multibyte string, and a maximum length. It copies up to that many wide‑characters into the buffer, stops at a null byte, and returns the number of wide characters written.

@lmemcpy@kmemcpy.author: AI Short Overview
@lmemcpy@kmemcpy.body: The `memcpy` routine accepts a destination pointer, a source pointer, and a size count. It performs a byte‑wise copy of `n` bytes from the source buffer to the destination buffer, returning the destination pointer. The call site expects the buffers to be distinct and of sufficient size; otherwise, a buffer overrun or undefined behavior may ensue.

@lmemset@kmemset.author: AI Short Overview
@lmemset@kmemset.body: Copies the byte value `c` into the first `n` bytes beginning at the address pointed to by `s` and returns that pointer. The function performs no argument validation—invalid pointers or lengths result in undefined behaviour.

@lmktime@kmktime.author: AI Short Overview
@lmktime@kmktime.body: The function `mktime` takes a pointer to a `struct tm` and returns a `time_t` value, typically representing the number of seconds since the Unix epoch. It interprets the `tm` fields—year, month, day, hour, minute, second—normalizing them if necessary (e.g., handling daylight‑saving offsets) before computing the final timestamp.

@lmove_field@kmove_field@f./Source/Curse.author: AI Short Overview
@lmove_field@kmove_field@f./Source/Curse.body: The function first validates that the supplied field pointer and new row/column indices are non‑null and non‑negative. If the field already belongs to a form, it returns an error; otherwise it writes the new coordinates to the field and reports success.

@lneedToQuoteTestName@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.author: AI Short Overview
@lneedToQuoteTestName@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_1.body: This function determines whether a test name needs quoting when added. It checks the CMP0110 policy: if the policy is WARN, it issues a warning when a forbidden character appears in the name; otherwise, when the policy is NEW it returns true, and when the policy is OLD it returns false.

@loperator new@k_Znwm.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator new@k_Znwm.body: Allocates a buffer of the requested size and returns a void‑pointer to that memory. It is called whenever a caller needs raw storage (e.g., for a newly constructed object or a temporary buffer) and is typically paired with a matching delete or free to avoid leaks.

@loperator!=@k_ZneRK11cmCMakePathS1_@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator!=@k_ZneRK11cmCMakePathS1_@f./.body: The overload performs an inequality comparison by delegating to the internal `Compare` method; it returns true when the comparison result is non‑zero, indicating the paths differ.

@loperator!=@k_ZneRK6cmListS1_@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator!=@k_ZneRK6cmListS1_@f./Source.body: Returns `true` when the two lists contain different elements; otherwise `false`. The comparison is performed by the underlying `Values` containers, and the function guarantees no exceptions are thrown.

@loperator!=@k_ZneRKN11cmCMakePath8itera.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator!=@k_ZneRKN11cmCMakePath8itera.body: The `operator!=` simply inverts the result of `operator==`; it returns `true` when the two `cmCMakePath::iterator` objects are not equal and `false` otherwise.

@loperator!=@k_ZneRKN9cmFileAPI6ObjectES.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator!=@k_ZneRKN9cmFileAPI6ObjectES.body: This overload implements the `!=` comparison by delegating to the `==` operator and simply returns the negated result.

@loperator+=@k_ZpLRSt6vectorINSt7__cxx11.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator+=@k_ZpLRSt6vectorINSt7__cxx11.body: The `operator+=` function appends all elements from a `cmList&&` r into a `std::vector<std::string>& l`. It uses `std::move` and `std::back_inserter` to transfer elements by value, clears `r`, and finally returns `l`. This provides a move‑based, noexcept‑safe way to merge two containers.

@loperator+=@k_ZpLRSt6vectorINSt7__cxx11.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator+=@k_ZpLRSt6vectorINSt7__cxx11.body: The function overloads the `+=` operator for a `std::vector<std::string>`. It appends every string from the `cmList` argument `r` to the end of the vector `l` by using `vector::insert`. After performing the insertion, it returns a reference to the modified vector `l`.

@loperator/@k_ZdvRK11cmCMakePathS1_@sope.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator/@k_ZdvRK11cmCMakePathS1_@sope.body: Creates a new `cmCMakePath` by invoking the existing division operator on a copy of the left‐hand operand, then returns that result.

@loperator<<@k_ZlsRSo23cmScriptGenerator.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator<<@k_ZlsRSo23cmScriptGenerator.body: The overload writes an `cmScriptGeneratorIndent` object to the stream by invoking its `Write` method, then returns the stream to allow further chaining of output operations.

@loperator<<@k_ZlsRSoRK17cmListFileConte.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator<<@k_ZlsRSoRK17cmListFileConte.body: Formats a `cmListFileContext` for streaming: the file path is printed, followed by a colon and the line number if positive, optionally appending the name in parentheses, and a special “:DEFERRED” label when the line value matches the placeholder sentinel.

@loperator<@k_ZltRK15cmStandardLevelS1_@.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator<@k_ZltRK15cmStandardLevelS1_@.body: The overload lets you compare two `cmStandardLevel` objects directly. It simply returns whether the left‑hand side’s internal `index_` is smaller than the right‑hand side’s.

@loperator<@k_ZltRKN9cmFileAPI6ObjectES2.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator<@k_ZltRKN9cmFileAPI6ObjectES2.body: It implements a strict ordering: first it compares the `Kind` values, and if they’re equal it falls back to comparing the `Version` field. This gives a deterministic, total order useful for containers that rely on ordering semantics.

@loperator==@k_ZeqRK11cmCMakePathS1_@f./.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator==@k_ZeqRK11cmCMakePathS1_@f./.body: The operator compares two `cmCMakePath` objects by delegating to `Compare`. It returns `true` only when `Compare` reports equality (zero result), otherwise `false`. The function is marked `noexcept` and declared `friend`, so it has access to private members for the comparison but does not modify either argument.

@loperator==@k_ZeqRK6cmListS1_@f./Source.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator==@k_ZeqRK6cmListS1_@f./Source.body: The function is a friend comparison operator that takes two `cmList` objects by const reference and returns `true` if the underlying containers `Values` are equal (using that container’s own `operator==`). It is marked `noexcept` so no exceptions are thrown during the comparison.

@loperator==@k_ZeqRK7cmRangeIT_ERKS_IT0_.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator==@k_ZeqRK7cmRangeIT_ERKS_IT0_.body: The operator checks that both ranges have the same number of elements and then uses `std::equal` to verify every element pairwise matches. It returns true only if the lengths coincide and all corresponding values are equal.

@loperator==@k_ZeqRKN11cmCMakePath8itera.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator==@k_ZeqRKN11cmCMakePath8itera.body: This operator checks whether two `cmCMakePath::iterator` objects refer to the same underlying path and point to the same position in that path. It returns true only when both the `Path` pointers and the internal `Iterator` pointers match.

@loperator==@k_ZeqRKN9cmFileAPI6ObjectES.author: AI Short Overview
@loperator==@k_ZeqRKN9cmFileAPI6ObjectES.body: The `operator==` overload compares two `Object` instances by checking that both their `Kind` and `Version` members are equal, returning `true` only when both fields match.

@lparseArguments@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114par.author: AI Short Overview
@lparseArguments@k_ZN12_GLOBAL__N_114par.body: The routine walks through a command‑line argument list, first determining whether the first token is an option. If it’s not an expected flag it records that token as the source‑group name. Then it loops over the remaining tokens, treating each expected flag as a key and collecting every following token that isn’t another flag into the vector mapped to that key. * **Usage in the codebase** – in `cmConfigureLog.cxx` it is used to emit a single byte in hex form (`"\x%02x"`); in `cmFileCommand.cxx` it prefixes a file‑size field (`"[%" KWIML_INT_PRIu64 " bytes data]\n"`); and in `cmStringAlgorithms.cxx` it formats a pattern‑based string. @lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::find_first.body: find_first_not_of scans a character sequence (e.g., a C‑style string or a std::string) until it encounters a character that is not contained in a given set of delimiter characters and returns the index of that position. If every character matches the set, the function returns the length of the string (i.e., the sentinel value that indicates “no match”). The algorithm operates in linear time proportional to the length of the examined string.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::find_first.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::find_first.body: find_first_not_of returns the smallest index `i` ≥ `pos` such that the character at position `i` in the string is **not** present in the supplied pattern string. If every remaining character belongs to that pattern set, the function yields `npos`. The operation runs in linear time relative to the remaining string length.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::find_first.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::find_first.body: The `find_first_of` function scans a string from a given position (default 0) and returns the index of the first character that matches any character in a supplied search set; if none are found, it returns the string’s length. It essentially implements a substring‑search that checks each character of the search string against every character in the source string until a match is reached, then returns that position.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::find_first.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::find_first.body: The `find_first_of` member function scans a character buffer for the first occurrence of any of the supplied characters, returning the offset of that match or `npos` if none is found. It accepts an optional starting offset, enabling partial scans from a specific point. The function is widely used for locating delimiters (`=`, `:`, `-`) across various modules, simplifying string parsing logic and keeping code paths consistent.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::front@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::front@k_ZN.body: The `front()` function returns the first element of an underlying container (e.g., a string or vector). It is used in the code to pass a reference to the first element of `path` to `MakeTempDirectory`. The implementation is typically a thin wrapper that forwards to the container’s native `front()` or similar accessor, ensuring the container is not empty before dereferencing.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::length@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::length@k_Z.body: The `length()` function returns the number of characters in a string or container. It’s used to compare sizes, cut off trailing data, or determine offsets in the code shown. The calls simply check that a string contains enough characters or that a buffer hasn’t been fully consumed.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator s.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator s.body: The operator converts a `std::basic_string_view` into a view over a contiguous character buffer, enabling the surrounding code (e.g., `cmHasLiteralPrefix` and `cmExpandList`) to treat a `std::basic_string_view` as a lightweight string slice without allocating new storage. It merely forwards the underlying data pointer and length, so the caller can employ it in string‑matching and argument parsing without creating copies or touching the underlying buffer.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator+=.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator+=.body: The operator+= for basic_string appends a null‑terminated sequence of characters to the existing string, resizing the internal buffer as necessary and updating the length. It returns a reference to the modified string so calls can be chained.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator+=.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator+=.body: The operator performs an in‑place concatenation: it appends the supplied string to the current instance and returns a reference to the modified object.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator+=.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator+=.body: The `operator+=` appends a single character to the string’s internal buffer and returns a reference to the modified string. It operates on a `basic_string` instantiated with a particular character type, traits and allocator.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.body: The move‑assignment operator for `basic_string` replaces the current string’s contents with the contents of the rvalue operand. It releases the existing buffer (or, if the allocators propagate, re‑allocates), then takes ownership of the source’s internal buffer without copying individual characters, leaving the source in an empty state. The function returns a reference to the modified string for chaining.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.body: Assigns a `basic_string` from a C‑style string literal or pointer. The operator takes a `const _CharT*` (a null‑terminated array) and copies that sequence into the string, reallocating and copying characters as needed. It returns a reference to the modified string, enabling chained assignments. This overload is what callers use when writing code like `str = "foo";` or `str = somePointer;`.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.body: The assignment operator copies the contents of the right‑hand string into the current string, deallocating any storage that is no longer needed, updating the internal size and capacity fields, and then returns a reference to the modified object. It handles self‑assignment safely and works for any character type, traits, and allocator provided by the template parameters.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator=@.body: Assigns the contents of the right‑hand operand to the current string instance and returns a reference to the modified string.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator[].author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator[].body: `operator[]` is a const overload that simply returns a `const_reference` (typically a reference to the stored element) for the element at the given `size_type` index. It performs any necessary bounds checking (or relies on a pre‑condition) and guarantees no mutation of the underlying container.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator[].author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::operator[].body: Returns a reference to the element at the requested index (typically after bounds‑checking).

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::push_back@.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::push_back@.body: push_back inserts a new element at the logical tail of the internal sequence, adjusting internal bookkeeping (like size counters and capacity markers) and triggering any necessary reallocation logic while keeping the data structure coherent for subsequent iterations.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::replace@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::replace@k_.body: This overload replaces a subrange of the string—specified by the start and length arguments—with the supplied string and returns a reference to the modified string.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::reserve@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::reserve@k_.body: The `reserve` function takes a `size_type` argument and ensures the container has at least that many elements of space reserved. It typically performs a reallocation if the current capacity is insufficient, preserving existing elements while extending the internal storage to the requested capacity. This is commonly used to pre‑allocate memory before a known number of push‑backs to avoid repeated reallocations.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::reserve@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::reserve@k_.body: The reserve function pre‑allocates the necessary storage or resources for upcoming operations, marking the relevant slot or buffer as occupied and ensuring the required capacity is available.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::resize@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::resize@k_Z.body: The `resize` function takes a single argument, `size_type`, which specifies the new size to which the underlying data structure should be adjusted. It internally updates the stored size value, reallocates or truncates the internal buffer if necessary, and ensures that all elements are preserved or zero‑filled according to the implementation’s policy. During the operation it guards against out‑of‑range or null inputs, performs bounds‑checking, and triggers a re‑allocation when the new size exceeds the current capacity.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::resize@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::resize@k_Z.body: Resizes the internal buffer to the requested length, reallocating memory and copying existing elements if needed, and ensures the new size is within valid bounds before returning.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::rfind@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::rfind@k_ZN.body: The `rfind` helper performs a reverse lookup in a C‑style string: it scans a `const _CharT*` buffer from the end toward the beginning and returns the index where a particular search pattern first appears. If the pattern is not present, it returns `std::string::npos`. The function is intentionally side‑effect‑free, making it safe to use in constant contexts such as the debug‑helper calls shown.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::rfind@k_ZN.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::rfind@k_ZN.body: `rfind` is a `const` member of the string‐like class that returns the **index of the rightmost occurrence** of a supplied character (or substring). It scans the string from the end towards the beginning, and if the character is found it returns its position; otherwise it returns `string::npos`. The optional second argument can be used to specify a starting point (or offset) for the search.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::size@k_ZNK.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::size@k_ZNK.body: The `size()` member simply returns the internal `size_type` value that tracks how many elements are stored in the associated collection; it is a `const` accessor that never mutates the object. It is called in many conditional checks throughout the codebase – for example, to guard string‑like operations in the debugger helper, to test line length before indexing in the RST parser, and to provide the byte count when a file is written.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::substr@k_Z.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::substr@k_Z.body: It copies a contiguous block of characters from the original string into a new string object and returns that copy. The original string stays unchanged while the returned string contains only the requested segment.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::~basic_str.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_string::~basic_str.body: ~basic_string() is a public helper that simply generates and returns a base string representation—typically used wherever a plain string value is needed in the surrounding code.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_stringstream::basi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_stringstream::basi.body: Creates and returns a string‑based stream object that reads input characters sequentially, exposing them through standard stream interfaces. It also performs the necessary cleanup of any temporary buffers when the stream is destroyed.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_stringstream::rdbu.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_stringstream::rdbu.body: `rdbuf()` supplies a reusable string buffer that the rest of the code uses to construct temporary string values. It is a const helper that hands back a pointer to a pre‑allocated buffer, ensuring that functions that build small strings avoid allocating new memory for each call. The returned buffer typically lives for the duration of the calling scope, allowing callers to write into it before passing the final string to other routines. This design keeps string construction fast and keeps the buffer isolated from the rest of the program’s state.

@lstd::__cxx11::basic_stringstream::~bas.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::basic_stringstream::~bas.body: Creates a string‑stream object that wraps a string buffer so callers can read from or write to a string as if it were a file. It initializes the internal buffer and returns the stream ready for use.

@lstd::__cxx11::stoi@k_ZNSt7__cxx114stoi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::stoi@k_ZNSt7__cxx114stoi.body: `stoi` converts a string (or string view) into an integer. It accepts an optional pointer that receives the index of the first character that was not part of the parsed number; if `nullptr` is supplied, the index is ignored. The function parses an optional leading sign, optional base prefix (`0x` for hex, `0` for octal, decimal otherwise), and then interprets digits according to the given base (default 10). If the input is malformed or the resulting value would overflow, it throws `std::invalid_argument` or `std::out_of_range` as appropriate. The implementation follows the semantics of the standard library’s `std::stoi`, ensuring that trailing non‑numeric characters do not alter the parsed value.

@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.body: Utility function that turns an integer value into its textual representation, typically used when composing formatted strings in various helper modules (e.g. variable listings, test indices, and status messages). It delegates to the standard library’s conversion routine so that every call produces a consistent string form.

@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.body: Converts an unsigned integer into its decimal string representation, returning a std::string that can be inserted into textual output.

@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.body: Converts a `long` value into its decimal string representation, typically used to prepare string values for storage or display.

@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__cxx11::to_string@k_ZNSt7__cxx11.body: `to_string` converts an unsigned long value into its textual string form, providing a consistent stringified representation for use in debugger‑output routines.

@lstd::__detail::_Node_const_iterator::o.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__detail::_Node_const_iterator::o.body: The operator* returns a read‑only reference to the object’s internal value, letting callers treat the instance like a dereferenced pointer while preserving encapsulation.

@lstd::__detail::_Node_const_iterator::o.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__detail::_Node_iterator::operato.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__detail::_Node_iterator::operato.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__detail::operator!=@k_ZNSt8__det.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::__detail::operator==@k_ZNSt8__det.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__detail::operator==@k_ZNSt8__det.body: The `operator==` for `_Node_iterator_base` performs a structural comparison: it returns `true` when the two iterators refer to the same underlying node – typically by comparing the internal pointer (or internal index) that identifies the node. If either iterator is at the end sentinel, the comparison still succeeds only if both are at the same sentinel. It gracefully handles `nullptr`‑style values by treating them as equal only to each other null iterator. This operator does **not** dereference the node; it merely checks identity, so no runtime side‑effects occur.

@lstd::__shared_ptr_access::operator->@k.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::__shared_ptr_access::operator->@k.body: Returns a pointer to the underlying element_type, enabling member‑access through a pointer‑like interface.

@lstd::advance@k_ZSt7advanceRSt19istream.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::advance@k_ZSt7advanceRT_T0_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::advance@k_ZSt7advanceRT_T0_.body: The template increments an input iterator by a given distance in a type‑safe, compile‑time‑checked manner. It relies on the iterator’s category to dispatch the appropriate specialization: for random‑access iterators it performs a direct pointer arithmetic, while for bidirectional or forward iterators it loops via the increment operation. The function returns the iterator positioned after the movement, enabling chaining or assignment in algorithms that process sequences.

@lstd::all_of@k_ZSt6all_ofOT_T0_S1_T1_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::all_of@k_ZSt6all_ofOT_T0_S1_T1_.body: The template implements a forward‑iterator‑based `all_of` that evaluates a predicate over a range. @lstd::all_of@k_ZSt6all_ofT_S_T0_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::all_of@k_ZSt6all_ofT_S_T0_.body: The template `all_of` accepts a begin and end iterator pair and a predicate functor; it scans the range and returns `true` only if every element satisfies the predicate. @lstd::any_of@k_ZSt6any_ofOT_T0_S1_T1_.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::any_of@k_ZSt6any_ofT_S_T0_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::any_of@k_ZSt6any_ofT_S_T0_.body: It scans a contiguous range of elements and reports whether at least one element fulfills a supplied predicate, returning `true` if a match is found and `false` otherwise.

@lstd::array::array@k_ZNSt5arrayI20uv_st.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::array::begin@k_ZNSt5array5beginEv.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::array::data@k_ZNSt5array4dataEv.author: AI Short Overview

@lstd::array::operator[]@k_ZNSt5arrayixE.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::array::operator[]@k_ZNSt5arrayixE.body: `operator[]` returns a reference to the element at the given index, allowing direct read/write access. It usually performs a bounds check (or asserts) and then returns the internal element in constant time.

@lstd::back_inserter@k_ZSt13back_inserte.author: AI Short Overview

`back_inserter` is a template that produces an iterator adaptor.  
Given a container reference, it returns an object that behaves like an output iterator: on each assignment it appends the supplied element to the container’s back (via `push_back`/`push_back`‑like operation).  
The returned iterator can be used in standard algorithms such as `std::move` or `std::copy` to efficiently append ranges.  
This helper is employed throughout the code base to construct containers by streaming elements into them instead of constructing temporary intermediate collections.

@lstd::basic_ifstream::basic_ifstream@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ifstream::basic_ifstream@k_.body: basic_ifstream creates a new input stream object from a filename and requested open mode. It opens the file in the specified mode, handles any failure by throwing an exception, and returns a pointer/reference to the initialized stream for the caller to use. The function is exposed publicly and is employed throughout the code to supply file‑based input streams to various components.

@lstd::basic_ifstream::basic_ifstream@k_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ifstream::basic_ifstream@k_.body: The `basic_ifstream` function initializes an input file stream by opening a file with a given path and optional mode flags, handling any errors during the open operation.

@lstd::basic_ifstream::close@k_ZNSt14bas.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ifstream::close@k_ZNSt14bas.body: The `close` function performs the necessary cleanup for the object: it shuts down any active network or file descriptors, releases any allocated buffers, and marks the instance as no longer usable so that subsequent operations will be rejected. @lstd::basic_ifstream::open@k_ZNSt14basi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ifstream::open@k_ZNSt14basi.body: The `open` function accepts a file‑path and an `openmode` flag, then locates the target file, allocates the stream’s internal buffers, and establishes the requested access mode (read, write, append, etc.). It performs the necessary system calls to open the file, reporting any failure through an exception or an error flag, and guarantees that resources are properly cleaned up on error paths.

@lstd::basic_ifstream::rdbuf@k_ZNKSt14ba.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ifstream::rdbuf@k_ZNKSt14ba.body: The `rdbuf()` function returns a pointer to a `__filebuf_type` instance that holds the in‑memory buffer used by the program. @lstd::basic_ios::clear@k_ZNSt9basic_ios.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ios::clear@k_ZNSt9basic_ios.body: The `clear` function accepts an `iostate` object and resets its internal contents—flushing any pending buffers or resetting status flags—so that the object is left in a pristine, ready‑to‑reuse state.

@lstd::basic_ios::eof@k_ZNKSt9basic_ios3.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ios::eof@k_ZNKSt9basic_ios3.body: `eof` is a public function that returns a `bool`. It reports whether the input stream has reached its end – i.e., there is no further data to read.  The function is invoked in the code to guard subsequent reads: for example, before attempting to read a line it checks `if (!eof())` to avoid trying to consume beyond the available data.

@lstd::basic_ios::fail@k_ZNKSt9basic_ios.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ios::fail@k_ZNKSt9basic_ios.body: The `fail()` function reports whether the object is in a failure state. It returns `true` when a failure condition is present and `false` otherwise. Its invocations are inverted (`!this->fail()`) to test for success in the surrounding code.

@lstd::basic_ios::good@k_ZNKSt9basic_ios.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ios::good@k_ZNKSt9basic_ios.body: It returns a Boolean flag that signals whether the current state satisfies whatever condition the surrounding code expects—**true** when the condition is met, **false** otherwise. The function is `const`, so it does not modify any member data and is safe to call from any context.

@lstd::basic_ios::operator bool@k_ZNKSt9.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ios::operator bool@k_ZNKSt9.body: Converts the object to a boolean value, typically returning true when the internal state satisfies a validity condition (for example, a non‑null pointer or a true flag) and false otherwise. The const qualifier guarantees no modification of internal data during the check, and the operator is usually invoked implicitly in conditional contexts.

@lstd::basic_ios::operator!@k_ZNKSt9basi.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ios::operator!@k_ZNKSt9basi.body: This function returns a Boolean flag indicating whether a specific condition holds true when the operator is invoked. It is deliberately declared const so that it does not alter any internal state of the owning object, and it is public so that callers from other modules can query the condition without mutating the instance. Its body typically performs only a read‑only check against internal data members or external inputs, and then returns true or false accordingly. The surrounding code usually relies on this indicator for decision‑making logic in business‑logic modules, as a quick guard in conditional branches or for early exit from loops that must terminate when the condition fails.

@lstd::basic_ios::setstate@k_ZNSt9basic_.author: AI Short Overview
@lstd::basic_ios::setstate@k_ZNSt9basic_.body: setstate takes an `iostate` argument and applies that value to update the internal state representation.

@lstd::basic_istream::get@k_ZNSt13basic_.author: AI Short Overview
